# Response theory: implementation and validation

The objective remains the complete molecular and periodic response theory program.
This document records intermediate progress. Passing a subset of tests, defining
an interface, or rejecting an input does not establish completion of a feature.
Computational dependencies are restricted to the existing `libm`, `rayon`,
`faer`, and optional `pyo3`. Python and ASE validation also uses only dependencies
already declared by the project.

Every new or extended derivative acceptance requires independent errors at
four or more distinct steps and a fitted power-law exponent, fit quality and
resolved step interval. Closed forms, dense solutions, conservation identities
and Richardson checks remain complementary requirements. A formal stencil
order or one h-halving ratio does not replace the fit. The repository
implementation instructions preserve this requirement for subsequent work.

New functional classes additionally require
[component-resolved oracle and physical validation](FUNCTIONALS.md#validation-of-new-functional-classes),
including independent same-spin and opposite-spin PT2 checks for double hybrids.

Parts 1-10 group the methods, conventions and their measured acceptance by
topic; Part 11 keeps the chronological records of acceptance runs; the
response coverage ledger closes the document.

## Part 1: Conventions and validation rules

The remaining program includes extending existing physical calculations to
missing functional classes and reference states, including restricted-open-shell
ROKS and generalized spinor GKS references. Implementation and acceptance are
tracked separately for each observable, functional class and reference state.
A new implementation must use the shared functional and reference providers;
compatibility of an SCF energy alone does not establish compatibility of a
property, its derivative kernel or a correlated response. Every completed
connection is recorded in this Markdown ledger and the aligned API manuals,
with its tested combinations and remaining restrictions.

### Scope of the response drivers

The [response API reference](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver) contains three aligned tables for Rust,
CLI, and native Python/ASE, with matching calculation IDs, controls, result
keys, units, examples, and current physical scope. Every calculation listed
there is reached through the same driver from Rust, the CLI, Python and ASE.


The electric molecular drivers use a converged collinear KS/HF reference with integer
occupations. Dynamic response solves both blocks of the adiabatic Casida
equations. Static nonlinear response solves order-resolved equations for the
density projector and self-consistent Fock matrix. Operators include hybrid
and range-separated exchange, requested self-consistent VV10, and a linear PCM
reaction field. Nonadiabatic correlation kernels, double hybrids, spinor,
Dirac, and Nambu physical backends remain part of the implementation scope.

`ResponseReport` contains values, shape, functional description, units, axis and
model conventions, convergence, relative response residuals, and iteration
counts. Reference diagnostics are recomputed from the Fock, overlap, and density:
generalized eigenvalue residual, orbital stationarity, metric orthogonality,
idempotency, and particle number. New iterative solvers default to relative
residual `1e-10`, 500 iterations, and GMRES restart 40. Orbital energy differences
are preserved; denominator floors apply only to preconditioning. Direct integral
screening is fixed using the reference density so that the operator does not
depend on trial vector magnitude. Acceptance reevaluates the original operator.

### Functional derivatives at arbitrary order

`XcFunctional::taylor_energy` and `taylor_potentials` accept spin-resolved series
for `rho_a,rho_b,sigma_aa,sigma_ab,sigma_bb,tau_a,tau_b`. Functional parameter
series can participate in the same operation. All native functionals use their
existing `Scalar` energy expressions; derivative evaluation does not dispatch
on functional names. External functionals can supply the required derivatives
through the same interface.

Runtime-order evaluation connects to the existing `Scalar` trait through Copy
handles into a scoped thread-local coefficient arena. The arena is released
both on success and during panic unwinding. Generation checks reject handles
used outside their scope or on another thread. Special functions use analytic
Taylor recurrences. Vacuum cutoffs and the meta-GGA FHC value clamp retain the
existing driver derivative conventions. A Taylor expansion cannot generally be
assumed to exist at nonanalytic cutoff or branch boundaries.

`ResolvedFunctional::semilocal_taylor_*` explicitly returns the semilocal part.
Hartree, full and long-range exact exchange, VV10, and PCM are assembled by the
physical backend. The third-order limit of the existing dense `XcOut` tensors
remains a limit of that array interface.

### Electric field conventions

The electronic Hamiltonian term is `+E.r`; the nuclear term is
`-sum_A Z_A R_A.E`. Define `E(t)=E_reference+t direction` and
`mu(t)=sum_n c[n] t^n`. Coefficients include normalization by `n!`, so the
directional hyperpolarizabilities are `beta=2 c[2]` and `gamma=6 c[3]`.
Coefficient `c[n]` has units of atomic dipole divided by atomic electric field
to the power `n`. The mixed entry point differentiates once along each supplied
direction and returns the derivative without factorial normalization.

In the fixed reference MO space, density `D(t)` and Fock `F(t)` satisfy

```text
D(t)^2 = D(t)
[F(t), D(t)] = 0
R_n = sum_(m=1..n-1) D_m D_(n-m)
D_n,oo = -R_n,oo; D_n,vv = R_n,vv
```

The remaining occupied-virtual block is solved using the CPKS orbital Hessian
and nonlinear sources generated by lower-order coefficients. Density, gradient,
and kinetic energy density series pass through the XC energy expression; series
of its first variation produce the AO potential. VV10 differentiates both grid
points and the chain rule back to the AO density. Each order reports the full MO
commutator, projector defect, and `Tr(S D_n)`. Production calculations do not use
finite electric field differences.

Mixed derivatives use the analytic polarization identity for Taylor coefficients:

```text
D_(v1)...D_(vn) mu = sum_(S subset {1..n}) (-1)^(n-|S|) c_n(sum_(i in S) v_i)
```

Repeated directions are grouped using binomial weights, and sums use compensated
accumulation. A roundoff estimate accompanies the result because cancellation
increases at high orders. Directional backend errors are assessed separately
through residuals of the original response operator.

#### Thermal and Coulomb acceptance checkpoint

The independent `p37_thermal_response` gate passes without changing its
`1e-7` density/energy thresholds. It compares the screened SVWN5 response
of a finite-temperature periodic H2 cell against four independent SCFs
at two temperature step sizes and Richardson extrapolation. It also
checks the Mermin identity, per-spin number changes, reservoir response,
and ensemble compatibility.

`p38_hartree_consistency` passes its `1e-9` comparison against the independent
real/reciprocal Ewald build for every Hartree matrix component, the Hartree
energy, and the band splitting. Its metric-range-only case detects the
missing diffuse intercell contribution. These tests validate the corrected
Coulomb image range at the specified convergence settings; they do not
replace the remaining functional, space, and boundary-condition combinations.

The canonical `dft-rs` executable passes the 14 `p21_cli_contract` input
checks and the `p30_response_routes` and `p34_periodic_routes` numerical
comparisons with Rust. The two periodic Python/ASE cases and the three thermal
Python/ASE/CLI cases pass; the CLI comparison runs with `DFT_RS_CLI` pointing
to the canonical executable. The six existing `periodic::planewave` unit
tests, including independent quadrature with p orbitals, also pass after
the shell-pair Fourier refactor. The Python-feature release build includes
both the canonical executable and the compatibility alias.

#### Mixed spectroscopy and force-constant acceptance checkpoint

The spherical integral, nuclear Taylor, molecular mixed, public-route and
force-constant suites `p24`, `p28`, `p30`, `p35`, `p36`, `p39`, `p40`, `p41`,
`p42` and `p43` pass 32 tests. The molecular/nuclear/field/force-constant
Python suites pass 11 tests with `DFT_RS_CLI` set to the canonical executable;
no CLI parity case is skipped. The Python-feature release build includes
both CLI names and the extension used in these actual calculations.

The complete six-coordinate HeH cubic tensor has 56 independent components
and 50 independent reverse-order comparisons; the quartic tensor has 126
and 120. Raw acoustic sums are measured in every Cartesian derivative slot.
The unrestricted selected-pattern and Cartesian-block routes pass without
relaxing the existing tolerances. Directional hyper-Raman evaluates all
27 entries, reports 36 nontrivial electric-permutation comparisons and
66 actual directional evaluations for the centered three-field-axis parent path: six distinct-axis pairs times eight corners plus three repeated-axis pairs times six corners. The earlier 57-count expectation described the uncentered identity; correcting this diagnostic expectation changes no tensor, residual or error-fit threshold.

The 139-item target registry and 67-family coverage ledger retain unfinished
physical backends. The calculation IDs each appear in all three
aligned API tables. Source/document/test/package-name audits find no restricted
names or non-English prose, and the dependency declarations and lockfile match
the original input. These checkpoints establish intermediate acceptance,
not completion of all functional classes, periodic/magnetic/excited response
or final distribution validation.

### Implementation overlap audit

This audit inspects production code bodies and their actual calls,
independently of the coverage CSVs. The current pass scans 233 Rust files
and 2,233 production function bodies, including signatures with fixed-size
array arguments and excluding inline `cfg(test)` blocks
without dropping production code after them, and six Python package files
with 429 function definitions. Exact Rust candidates require at least
60 tokens; identifier-normalized candidates require 120. Partial-body
comparisons retain called functions and literals, nominate pairs by shared
16-token fragments and inspect long matching blocks. Python AST equality
is checked on bodies of at least 60 AST nodes. These bounded syntactic
checks nominate code for semantic review; they do not prove the absence
of all equivalent algorithms or judge the physical model from similarity.

Confirmed shared computations have been consolidated:

- `dynamic_polarizability` and `dynamic_amplitudes` now obtain their Casida
  operator, three solves and dipole contraction from one private function.
  Both public structures and the report iteration counts remain compatible.
  Independent closed 2x2 resolvents for restricted H2 and unrestricted H2+
  over static, imaginary and positive/negative damped frequencies agree
  within 4.441e-16 (`p25_dynamic_response`, three tests passed).
- Seven magnetic, nuclear-frame, open-shell, field-path and lattice
  operators share `krylov::apply_real_linear`. It extends each operator's
  own real action to complex amplitudes, preserves the zero-imaginary
  shortcut and rejects an incorrectly sized image. The underlying physical
  actions remain distinct.
- Molecular GGA/meta-GGA/nonlocal Hessians and the periodic XC gradient
  share the same packed symmetric pair index in `grid::eval::second_index`.
  The periodic nuclear Hessian reuses the existing strain segment-distance
  screen rather than maintaining a second identical implementation.
- The hyperfine common driver takes its compatibility contact scalar from
  the tensor kernel, avoiding a second copy of the contact prefactor.
- London finite-field references and response paths share complex matrix
  products and real trace products in `integrals::london::ComplexMatrix`.
  Periodic integral paths reuse the scalar reciprocal-series recurrence
  in `response::series`.

The four remaining nontrivial exact candidate groups are short three-vector
cross products, half-cross products, typed integer-power implementations
and LDA/GGA `with_params` constructors. The vector products are still
repeated arithmetic helpers; they do not constitute separate property
solvers. The latter two groups belong to different scalar representations
or callback types and input spaces.
Near matches in bra/ket integral
derivatives act on opposite matrix indices; overlap/kinetic and scalar/vector
exchange builds have different operators. Functional constructors select
different generic energy densities despite nearly identical field lists.
They have not been merged merely on a similarity score. No nontrivial exact
Python body group was found under the stated threshold; Python and ASE
property wrappers delegate to the common Rust driver.

## Part 2: Molecular electric and optical response

### Complete static beta and gamma tensors

`response::static_beta` and `response::static_gamma` evaluate the complete
Cartesian first and second hyperpolarizabilities with the same arbitrary
functional kernel interface as directional field response. Their common
driver `static_electric_tensor` accepts field order 2 or 3. No functional-name
dispatch, finite field step, or symmetry completion enters production.
Native Python `beta`/`gamma`, ASE `get_beta`/`get_gamma`, and CLI `beta`/`gamma`
call this driver. [The three API tables](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver) describe identical values,
units and diagnostics on every surface.

The convention is
`E(F+dF) = E(F) - mu_a dF_a - alpha_ab dF_a dF_b/2`
`- beta_abc dF_a dF_b dF_c/6 - gamma_abcd dF_a dF_b dF_c dF_d/24 + ...`.
Thus `beta_abc = d_b d_c mu_a = -d_a d_b d_c E`, and
`gamma_abcd = d_b d_c d_d mu_a = -d_a d_b d_c d_d E`. Entries are actual
derivatives, not the factorial-normalized directional Taylor coefficients.
This energy/dipole convention follows
[the primary program documentation](https://manual.q-chem.com/5.1/sec--Hyper-Polarizability.html).
Beta uses `e^3 Bohr^3/Hartree^2`; gamma uses `e^4 Bohr^4/Hartree^3` in atomic
units. XYZ geometry input remains in Angstrom; native geometry remains Bohr.

In the default projector assembly, all 9 ordered field pairs and all 27 ordered triples are evaluated separately
and produce 27/81 raw dipole tensor components. Exact polarization of the
analytic Taylor response requires 24/141 directional solves, respectively.
There is no sorted-tuple cache or permutation filling. The result retains each
raw component and its conservative polarization accumulation estimate.
`intrinsic_permutation_defect` measures exchanges among field legs;
`energy_permutation_defect` measures exchanges between the dipole leg and each
field leg. Each unequal-index pair is counted once. Their comparison counts
are 9/18 for beta and 81/81 for gamma. Failed static interchange at the
requested scaled tolerance sets the report convergence flag to false.

Rotational contractions are calculated after measuring the raw defects.
`beta_vector_i = sum_j (beta_ijj + beta_jij + beta_jji)/3`, with its Euclidean
norm, and `gamma_isotropic = sum_ij (gamma_iijj + gamma_ijij + gamma_ijji)/15`.
The gamma contraction follows the spherical fourth moment of a unit field
direction. Both reports also return the full tensor Frobenius norm.
Inapplicable contraction keys are absent as Rust/Python options (`None`),
rather than zero physical values. Raw tensor entries are never overwritten by
the contraction averaging. Projector, stationarity and particle-number defects
are maxima of the raw Taylor coefficient defects over every polarization
solve; the response-equation relative residuals are reported separately.

The current model is the static, clamped-nuclei, integer-occupation collinear
KS/HF electronic response. It includes native semilocal, hybrid and
range-separated kernels, plus the existing self-consistent nonlocal and linear
solvent kernels when selected. A biased reference field is supported.
Dynamic beta/gamma with signed-frequency processes, finite-temperature
occupations, relaxed-nucleus tensors, double-hybrid correlation response and
spinor/Dirac/Nambu response remain in the original target registry.

#### Variational 2n+1 beta assembly

`response::static_beta_variational` is a second analytic assembly over the same
functional providers, response operators and tensor report. CLI
`beta --electric-assembly variational`, native `beta(..., assembly="variational")`
and ASE `get_beta(..., assembly="variational")` select it. The default remains
the independently implemented projector recurrence. Both return all 27 raw
components and the same physical units and contractions.

Only three first-order field response equations are solved. Transform the
AO density derivatives to the orthonormal reference MO space and choose the
anti-Hermitian off-diagonal generators `K_a` such that
`D_a = [K_a,D_0]`. The chart
`D(lambda)=exp(sum_a lambda_a K_a) D_0 exp(-sum_a lambda_a K_a)`
preserves idempotency exactly. Its second/third mixed derivatives are sums of
nested commutators with factors 1/2 and 1/6. The constrained variational
[2n+1 theorem](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.52.1096) makes the cubic energy
derivative independent of unknown second-order orbital rotations.

With `F_a = h_a + K[D_a]` and `G[D_b,D_c]` the second functional derivative
of the Fock potential, the slot assembly is
`E_abc = Tr(F_a D_bc + F_b D_ac + F_c D_ab + F_0 D_abc)`
`+ Tr(G[D_b,D_c] D_a)`. Every spin block participates. Hartree/exchange and
linear solvent terms have no quadratic potential derivative; semilocal and
self-consistent nonlocal terms provide `G` through analytic Taylor kernels.
The density/gradient/tau chain rule is unchanged. No functional name selects
the formula. The chart term retains the actual reference Fock matrix so a
finite reference residual is not replaced by assumed exact stationarity.

Every ordered kernel pair and every contraction slot is assembled separately;
there is no tensor symmetry filling. The tensor report measures raw intrinsic
and dipole/field interchange defects before constructing invariants.
`residuals` and `iterations` contain three first-order response entries.
`directional_evaluations=27` counts those three field evaluations and 24
analytic quadratic-potential polarization evaluations, not 27 response solves.
Projector, particle-number and stationarity defects refer to the first-order
responses. The higher chart coefficients are not claimed to solve higher
stationarity equations. The default projector beta has 48 order-resolved
response entries; the full projector gamma has 423. This separates physical
assembly work from linear-solver counts.

The 2n+1 beta matches all raw HF projector components under rigid rotations
and translations and the open-shell one-electron closed eigenvalue oracle.
Its functional-class acceptance includes four-step independent finite-field
fits on LDA, GGA, meta-GGA, global hybrid, range-separated hybrid and an
unregistered weighted local hybrid. Gamma still uses the higher-order
projector recurrence; a 2n+2 assembly remains part of the continuation program.

#### Four-step error fits and independent electric oracles

The independent finite-field SCF dipole stencils are
`beta(h) = [mu(h)-2 mu(0)+mu(-h)]/h^2` and
`gamma(h) = [mu(2h)-2 mu(h)+2 mu(-h)-mu(-2h)]/(2h^3)`.
The production tensors use no step size. An independently sampled total
energy also verifies `d^3 E/dF^3 = -beta` and `d^4 E/dF^4 = -gamma`, including
the signs and factorial convention. The dipole stencils are the field error
fit oracle; fourth finite energy differences are more sensitive to cancellation.

For each fit, four strictly positive absolute errors relative to the analytic
derivative are fit by least squares to `log(error) = log(C) + p log(h)`.
No denominator/error floor enters the fit. `R_squared` and the log-space RMS
residual are measured, rather than inferred from a stencil's formal order.
The acceptance tests require `abs(p-2)<0.02`, `R_squared>0.99999` and retain
the existing step-halving and Richardson bounds.

| Independent observable | Four step sizes | Fitted p | Log-space R_squared |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static beta_zzz, finite-field HF dipoles | 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025 a.u. field | 2.000123470656 | 0.999999998969 |
| Static gamma_zzzz, finite-field HF dipoles | 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025 a.u. field | 1.998252760352 | 0.999999797125 |
| Nuclear energy D3, displaced independent LDA Hessians | 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025 Bohr | 2.002742758353 | 0.999999494404 |
| Nuclear energy D4, displaced independent LDA Hessians | 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025 Bohr | 1.995261321189 | 0.999998482170 |
| Third mode dipole derivative, displaced HF dipoles | 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 Bohr | 1.997433532572 | 0.999999730960 |
| Third mode polarizability derivative, displaced independent HF CPKS | 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 Bohr | 1.998670625603 | 0.999999899719 |

The anharmonic property oracle also attempted the finer 0.0025 Bohr stencil.
Its dipole third-difference h-halving ratio was 4.235679, failing the unchanged
0.03 deviation bound. Cancellation at that small step cannot establish the
asymptotic truncation order. Its four-point fit therefore extends the coarse
end to 0.04 Bohr and retains every original step and threshold; the measured
ratios are 3.984888, 3.995894 and 3.996899. The fine-stencil failure is kept in
the validation record. O(h^2) is established over a measured step interval,
not claimed below the floating-point/SCF error floor.

The electric tensor tests additionally check every raw component against
closed rotational covariance in an s-only diatomic model, with a rigid
translation, and against a closed two-by-two one-electron eigenvalue model
in an open-shell reference. The latter independently gives
`beta_zzz=-1.150746298416` and `gamma_zzzz=6.636091471552` in atomic units;
its occupied HF energy cancels the electron's own Hartree/exchange terms.
An unregistered weighted local hybrid also agrees with independent finite
field SCF, exercising the functional provider rather than registry-name logic.

The functional-class finite-field fits use the same four atomic-unit field
steps. They compare the actual variational beta against the independent SCF
stencil and projector gamma against the independent cubic dipole stencil.
The measured beta exponents are approximately 1.9995--1.9996; gamma exponents
are 1.9964--1.9986, with log-space R_squared above 0.999999 for the LDA, GGA,
meta-GGA, global hybrid, range-separated hybrid and unregistered local-hybrid
acceptance models. These checks complement, rather than replace, raw complete
tensor interchange and independent integral/XC kernel tests.

#### Static electric tensor acceptance checkpoint

Both tensor assemblies use the existing dependency set. A release build with
the optional Python feature and both CLI binaries succeeds. The final native
Python/ASE/CLI electric-tensor, shared-response and anharmonic acceptance run
passes 11 tests. The canonical and compatibility CLI names independently
return every beta component for both `projector` and `variational` assemblies,
and every gamma component for the projector assembly.

The six Rust electric-tensor tests pass. The exhaustive tilted-diatomic
LDA/GGA/meta-GGA/hybrid/range-separated test evaluates all raw beta/gamma
components; its complete run takes approximately 50 minutes in the current
validation environment. The remaining five tests pass on the final source,
including six functional-class four-step error fits and independent open-shell
closed eigenvalue, rotated tensor and finite-field oracles. No fitted order or
raw tensor symmetry threshold is relaxed to obtain these results.

The regression run passes 341 library tests with three existing ignored tests,
plus 21 selected CLI/XC/nonlinear/nonlocal/public-route integration tests.
After the assembly option is added, the 14 CLI-contract tests and shared-route
test pass again. The nuclear D3/D4 and anharmonic property four-step acceptance
tests also pass. These are selected regression results, not a claim that every
integration or long-running combination in the full program has been tested.

All 15 calculation IDs match across the three API tables. Package-file
inspection confirms that the tensor modules, Rust/Python tests and shared
four-step fit helper are included, while reference inputs and local build or
validation artifacts are excluded. Source/file-name, English-text and
unchanged-dependency audits pass. Static molecular beta/gamma are an
intermediate milestone: frequency-dependent higher electric tensors, the
remaining periodic/magnetic/excited-state combinations and new functional
classes remain in the accepted coverage program.

### Frequency-domain alpha, beta and gamma

The common `response::dynamic_electric_tensor` driver accepts one, two or
three incoming `Frequency` legs and returns all 9/27/81 raw complex components.
`dynamic_beta` and `dynamic_gamma` are typed wrappers. The corresponding CLI,
native Python and ASE entries appear in all three [API tables](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver).
The compatible paired Casida alpha driver is independently implemented and
provides a linear-response comparison oracle.

Use `E_l(t)=lambda_l direction_l exp(-i z_l t)`. Every labelled subset `S`
has `z_S=sum(l in S, z_l)`. Its density derivative solves
`z_S D_S = [F_0,D_S]+[F_S,D_0]+sum(A proper subset S)[F_A,D_(S-A)]`,
while `D^2=D` fixes the occupied/occupied and virtual/virtual blocks from
`sum(A proper subset S) D_A D_(S-A)`. These are actual mixed derivatives,
without factorials, including repeated directions and frequencies.
The density-matrix formulation of nonlinear response is described in the
[primary TDHF density-matrix paper](https://mukamel.ps.uci.edu/publications/pdfs/256.pdf).

The occupied/virtual and virtual/occupied blocks are independent at one
complex frequency. With `p=(D_ai+D_ia)/2` and `q=(D_ai-D_ia)/2`, the matrix-free
paired operator uses `(A+B)p-z q` and `(A-B)q-z p`. Hartree, local
density/gradient/tau kernels, nonlocal density terms and a linear reaction
field see the transpose-even density. Hybrid and range-separated exchange
also act on the transpose-odd density. This odd sector cannot be replaced
by a transpose or conjugate at the same frequency. Real undamped operators
use MINRES; damped/imaginary operators use complex GMRES. All acceptance
residuals are reevaluated with the actual operator.

The second/third Fock-potential derivatives are built from the existing
real analytic Taylor providers. Exact real polarization followed by
complex multilinear extension gives their mixed contractions. The quadratic
source contains all two-block partitions; the cubic source adds the three
singleton contraction. No registered functional name selects the response
formula, and no finite perturbation enters production. Semilocal LDA/GGA/
meta-GGA, global/range-separated exchange, configured self-consistent VV10
and linear PCM use the same kernel assembly. Additional correlation,
nonadiabatic and internal-space backends remain in the coverage program.

The output Fourier frequency, including its imaginary part, is the sum of
incoming complex frequencies. Positive incoming damping therefore gives
causal subset sums; the output damping is not replaced by a single input
damping. Real signed incoming frequencies select harmonic generation,
sum/difference-frequency mixing, optical rectification, electro-optic and
Kerr combinations. A zero undamped subset is solved as a static constrained
response. Resonant singular equations retain physical denominators and may
fail convergence rather than being regularized by a denominator floor.

Raw equal-frequency field-leg interchange is measured; unequal-frequency
interchange requires swapping the frequency together with its axis.
Output/input-axis Kleinman symmetry is not imposed at finite frequency.
The report also measures the full density equation, projector and particle
number defects for every solved subset. The complete alpha, beta and gamma
drivers perform respectively 3, 27 and 189 subset solves; some have an exact
zero source. `nonlinear_kernel_evaluations` counts the real analytic Taylor
evaluations separately from those linear equations.

#### Independent dynamic oracles and four-amplitude fits

The one-electron open-shell acceptance independently diagonalizes the bare
two-by-two one-electron Hamiltonian and applies its full Liouville spectral
resolvents, including the diagonal elements. It uses no Casida operator,
projector recurrence or nonlinear Fock provider. Complex mixed-frequency
alpha/beta/gamma agree with this oracle, and frequency reversal gives the
complex conjugate. Their static limits agree with the existing analytic
Taylor response, and alpha agrees with paired Casida.

A second oracle diagonalizes a finite-amplitude monochromatic Floquet
Hamiltonian with 17 Fourier bands, follows the central occupied branch and
Fourier analyzes its density. For a real cosine amplitude `h`, the first,
second and third dipole harmonics are multiplied by `2/h`, `8/h^2` and
`48/h^3` to obtain alpha, beta and gamma. The four measured amplitudes are
`0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005` atomic units at `omega=0.05` Hartree. Fitting the
absolute errors against the actual production derivatives gives:

| Dynamic observable | Fitted p | Log-space R_squared |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha, first harmonic | 2.001605164501 | 0.999999827158 |
| Beta, second harmonic | 2.001462709903 | 0.999999856581 |
| Gamma, third harmonic | 2.001231411551 | 0.999999876547 |

These satisfy the unchanged `abs(p-2)<0.02`, `R_squared>0.99999`, step-halving
ratio and Richardson bounds. The Floquet amplitude is confined to the
independent validation oracle. It is not a production time-propagation or
frequency-response approximation.

The original-operator and full Liouville/projector/number residuals accompany

The distinct `dielectric-tensor` continuum d/dk DFPT route already includes
the full exchange image blocks and screened exchange kernel. An audit
corrected its previous LDA/GGA-only coverage description. Its HF water
dilute limit is independently compared with the molecular analytic alpha,

check, not a finite-difference derivative fit and not an identification of
the finite Berry-mesh enthalpy with continuum d/dk. A dipolar local field
gives a leading L^-3 correction. All four cells enter the log-error fit:

Raw imaginary residuals are zero, and the largest field-solve relative

tested insulating cells; it does not validate HF Born charges, arbitrary-q
hybrid response, metallic occupations or all functional combinations.
Correlated PT2 alpha and higher response remain pending. The full accepted
molecular/periodic/high-order objective remains open.

### Optical-activity implementation and remaining combinations

The current molecular optical driver evaluates paired Casida electric/magnetic
response in the common-origin length gauge or the modified velocity gauge
with zero-frequency subtraction. The result's model description now names
the actual selected gauge. Nuclear optical-tensor paths share the moving
integral/metric/functional series used by ROA. `p146_optical_rotation_path`
tests their nine unprojected rotation-tensor derivatives against independent
displaced SCF/dynamic calculations in both gauges; all eight gauge/model four-step fits have passed. This is separate from VCD rotational strengths, ECD excited-state
rotatory strengths and MCD Faraday terms.

The molecular VCD driver contains common/distributed-origin atomic axial
tensors and contracts them with atomic polar tensors and vibrational modes.
The molecular ECD drivers contain TDA spectra and length/velocity/London
rotatory-strength paths. The molecular MCD driver contains closed-shell
singlet-TDA Faraday A/B terms over the complete selected model space.
Their pending acceptance, missing thermal Faraday C terms and remaining
functional/response combinations are kept explicit in the coverage CSVs.
An implemented driver is not recorded as a validated physical property.

Periodic optical rotation/CD/VCD/MCD need compatible covariant crystal
current, magnetic and electric-quadrupole/spatial-dispersion operators.
The molecular position/angular-momentum operator is not a bulk periodic
substitute. These combinations remain pending. The new static PT2 electric
alpha connection also does not provide the correlated mixed electric/magnetic
dynamic kernels needed by these observables. Those must include their own
amplitude/orbital response and independent physical acceptance.

All distributable code carries the English library-membership notice
`This file is part of the dft-rs library.` Existing license and author
metadata are preserved. The notice is audited independently from the
portable-source/private-path/dependency audits.

both common-origin length and modified velocity gauges. All nine tensor
components are independently recomputed at displaced SCF references. Steps
are [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] Bohr along the declared nuclear pattern; the error
is the Frobenius norm of the derivative error. The modified-velocity trace
also passes an independent origin-translation check. This acceptance does
not by itself validate VCD strengths, thermal MCD, periodic optical activity
or their correlated mixed dynamic response.

### Molecular Cotton-Mouton static tensor and frequency limit

Restricted HF H2/STO-3G at a 1.4 Bohr bond, London gauge and 298.15 K
passes the static Cotton-Mouton acceptance on native Python, ASE atomic
units and each CLI variant under strict units and Python warning denial.
All 81 ordered hypermagnetizability components are evaluated independently
from mixed fourth energy derivatives and compared against the existing
third induced-dipole derivative tensor, with no test symmetry copying.
Agreement is required within rtol=1e-9 and atol=1e-10. The separate electric
and magnetic tensor contraction and kT factor reproduce the orientational
term and the full per-molecule constant within 1e-10. The result is
9.627685428888206 in the documented atomic convention.

The finite-frequency Cotton-Mouton constant approaches its static value
on four frequencies [0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] Hartree, with no floored errors
or omitted steps. The measured p=2.000820599907 and
R2=0.999999954777 satisfy abs(p-2)<0.05 and R2>0.999.
This is a frequency-limit fit, not a finite-difference production formula.
The separately fitted finite-field energy contraction is recorded with
the simultaneous-field acceptance.

An initial validation oracle incorrectly treated transverse electric
components as identically zero in a two-s-orbital basis. Field-dependent
London phases generate transverse dipole terms even in that basis. The
oracle was corrected by independently evaluating every ordered energy
component; no production result or threshold was adjusted. Its failed
initial logs remain outside the distributable source.

Only this restricted-HF static tensor, orientational contraction and
frequency limit are accepted here. General finite-frequency tensor
oracles, other functional/reference classes, periodic Cotton-Mouton and
correlated mixed magnetic response remain required by the full objective.

```text

```

### Incremental finite-field and constrained-response acceptance

This record separates accepted internal components from physical properties
whose required terms or acceptance still remain pending. It does not change
functional/reference matrix cells on the strength of an internal model.

* `p175_london_nuclear_jets`: 48 four-step fits for moving-centre one-electron,
  electron-repulsion and moving-nucleus attraction coefficients, orders 1--4.
  Independent complex Gaussian moments and the entire complex Boys series
  check all coefficients directly. The first electron-repulsion run exposed
  a missing nonzero Boys derivative order and failed; that defect was fixed
  in the common scalar kernel, with all 48 fits passing afterward.
* `response::field_path::complex_reference_tests`: 16 four-step fits of a
  closed, nonlinear self-consistent complex two-level model with a moving
  metric. It checks energy and real/imaginary density coefficients, both
  coupled spin channels, orbital-phase covariance and zero-kernel limit.
  The largest raw solved-equation residual was 2.1975918759106952e-16.
* `periodic::phonon::regression_tests`: two four-step fits of exactly
  degenerate thermal density and energy-weighted density against independently
  rediagonalized generalized Fermi matrices, including overlap and chemical
  potential response. Hermitian-coordinate and scaled-action checks are
  separate algebraic regressions, not additional derivative fits.
* `p159_long_wave_force_constants`: 28 constrained internal-relaxation fits
  over all seven crystal systems, alongside the existing 56 Fourier-moment
  fits. The raw acoustic reactions and constrained equation residuals remain
  reported. No sum-rule repair or physical denominator floor is used.

The 94 component fits listed below use h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]; exponent range
[1.991289773,2.001744071], minimum R2=0.999994827673.
The existing |p-2|<0.05, R2>0.9999 and each original Richardson bound are
retained. All raw positive errors, intervals and residuals are retained.

The supplied-Born H2 lattice component passed native/ASE atomic/physical and
canonical CLI comparisons, but generated-Born LiH still failed CPKS at
4.593e-12 for a requested 1e-12. The DFPT-to-static-pairing H2 component
passed those same surfaces; alias and remaining combination acceptance are
not inferred. Complete electronic/dynamic-multipole flexoelectricity,
normal/pair backreaction and causal superconducting response remain pending.

Finite electric bias has been connected to periodic analytic nuclear orders
two through four. Its initial H2 force/enthalpy interval [0.12,0.09,0.06,0.03]
passed order one but failed the fixed order-two exponent/fit gates. That
failed interval is preserved below. A finer Hessian interval is being
measured with no threshold relaxation. Orders three/four were computed by
the initial test but their diagnostics were not reached after its order-two
assertion; they are not recorded as accepted. The revised test emits all
raw independent samples and all orders before asserting.

Magnetic and joint-field nuclear Hessian/cubic/quartic physical connections
remain pending despite the accepted scalar integral and complex stationary
components. These tests also do not establish an interacting four-component
Dirac reference, general finite-q magnetic response or correlated PT2
magnetic/nuclear completion.

## Part 3: Nuclear derivatives and vibrational spectroscopy

### Nuclear cubic and quartic derivatives

<!-- Complete correlated nuclear acceptance: prepared -->

The complete four-parent PT2 cubic/quartic acceptance in `p312_correlated_complete_nuclear` is prepared but has not yet been compiled or numerically run. It requests C1 H4/STO-3G restricted HF/PBE/TPSS/PBE0, zero external field, grid level 0 with `grid_weight_cutoff=0`, and custom unregularized SS/OS coefficients 0.37/0.61. Every actual common-driver Cartesian tensor is checked along 364 cubic and 1,365 quartic unisolvent directions, independently for total, parent, target, weighted PT2 and unscaled SS-alpha/OS/SS-beta: 48,412 fits in total. The oracle solves fresh displaced SCFs and directional Hessian response equations. Cubic and quartic tensors use hartree/bohr^3 and hartree/bohr^4 respectively; the contracted directional Hessian uses hartree/bohr^2. Each curve uses four distinct steps, with the unchanged absolute exponent gate 0.2 and R-squared above 0.999; all failed intervals remain recorded. Every displaced orbital and PT2 response, projector, stationarity, metric, number, frame and reference diagnostic must be finite and within 1e-12. Returned original-equation and inner-correction residuals are separately checked; the unfloored reconstructed-source ratio stays visible. Test preparation and a closed-form fit-auditor check are not numerical molecular acceptance. Existing measured subsets and matrix cells remain unchanged until the complete requested runs finish.

The nuclear Taylor driver differentiates `R_A(t)=R_A(0)+t direction[A]`.
All atom-by-Cartesian directions use Bohr, including the explicit directions
passed to ASE response methods. ASE converts only the reference geometry.
It returns `E(t)=sum_n e[n] t^n` in Hartree. The cubic directional force
constant is `6 e[3]`, and the quartic constant is `24 e[4]`. For Cartesian
tensor entries, pass three or four coordinate unit vectors to the mixed
driver; its scalar result is the actual derivative without a factorial.
This avoids allocating a dense `(3 N)^4` tensor when only contracted or
selected force constants are needed. Both routes use analytic response
equations; displaced SCFs appear only in independent tests.

Overlap, kinetic, nuclear attraction, full/range-separated electron
repulsion and nuclear repulsion retain their geometry Taylor coefficients.
For each spin, the transported basis is

```text
M(t) = C(0)^T S(t) C(0)
B(t) = C(0) M(t)^(-1/2)
P(t) = B(t) D(t) B(t)^T
B(t)^T S(t) B(t) = I
D(t)^2 = D(t), [B(t)^T F(t) B(t), D(t)] = 0
```

The matrix inverse square root uses matrix-series products, preserving
noncommuting terms. The reference retained AO coefficient subspace is held
fixed. If overlap pruning reduced the reference rank, this driver follows
that same coefficient subspace as the geometry moves; derivatives of the
pruning projector require a further kernel. Moving
atom-owned grid points, Becke partition weights, AO values/gradients,
density gradients and kinetic energy density pass through the same Taylor
algebra as the semilocal energy and potential. Integration topology,
radial/angular rules and size-adjustment constants are held fixed, matching
the existing analytic derivative convention. The cubic switch is flat
through order seven at atom contacts; a contact derivative beyond that
smoothness requires a different partition and is refused explicitly.

Every order solves the matrix-free physical orbital Hessian using MINRES,
since its positivity is not assumed. The final Fock is rebuilt from the
moving integrals, grid and full density series. Reports expose the actual
commutator coefficient, idempotency and metric defects and the complete
moving-metric number coefficient `sum_k Tr[P_k S_(n-k)]`. No acoustic
projection changes the force constants to conceal a residual. Energy
coefficients are split into nuclear repulsion, explicit nuclear field energy, one-electron, Hartree,
global exchange, additional long-range exchange and semilocal XC parts.

Current geometry kernels cover all-electron integer-occupation HF, LDA,
GGA, meta-GGA, global hybrids and range-separated hybrids. Higher geometry
kernels for ECP, RI-J, nonlocal correlation, empirical corrections, PCM,
additional one-electron operators, spinors and periodic cells remain in the
original implementation program. Such terms are refused explicitly by
this intermediate driver. The integral Taylor cache currently scales as
`(order+1) nao^4` (twice for additional long-range exchange), bounded by
`ScfOptions::incore_mb`; streamed geometry contractions remain pending.
The coverage ledger marks the full force-constant family as partial.

`tests/p39_nuclear_taylor.rs` compares independent analytic gradients and
Hessians, differentiates displaced Hessians with two step sizes and
Richardson extrapolation for third/fourth derivatives, and checks moving
number conservation, translation and mixed acoustic identities. These
gates establish tested points rather than all geometry/functional limits.

The independent central-difference estimates of the third and fourth energy
derivatives are respectively `(H(R+h)-H(R-h))/(2h)` and
`(H(R+h)+H(R-h)-2H(R))/h^2`, where H is the analytic directional Hessian.
Their leading truncation error is O(h^2). Richardson extrapolation
`(4 estimate(h/2)-estimate(h))/3` cancels that term, giving O(h^4) before
roundoff or SCF error dominates. The production Taylor response has no h.

For the HeH+ / STO-3G / SVWN5 gate, displacement of the hydrogen along the
bond gives the following errors relative to the analytic Taylor result:

| h (Bohr) | Raw third derivative absolute error (Hartree/Bohr^3) | Raw fourth derivative absolute error (Hartree/Bohr^4) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.020 | 6.7363524567e-4 | 1.6034811454e-2 |
| 0.010 | 1.6764504598e-4 | 4.0402862966e-3 |
| 0.005 | 4.1863861036e-5 | 1.0120525151e-3 |

Raw error ratios on halving h are 4.0182 and 4.0045 for the third derivative,
and 3.9687 and 3.9922 for the fourth derivative. Richardson error ratios are
16.1130 and 15.9437, giving observed orders 4.0102 and 3.9949.
`central_hessian_differences_have_second_order_error` checks both orders
independently, rather than interpreting smaller absolute errors alone as
evidence of convergence. Existing derivative acceptance thresholds remain
unchanged. The family gates additionally validate SVWN5, PBE, r2SCAN, B3LYP
and CAM-B3LYP against displaced analytic Hessians with h=0.010 and 0.005.

```console
cargo test --locked --test p39_nuclear_taylor central_hessian_differences_have_second_order_error -- --nocapture
```

### Analytic mixed molecular spectroscopy

`response::force_constants` also constructs full cubic and quartic tensors,
caller coordinate blocks and arbitrary displacement-pattern tensors. Every
independent mixed component uses the analytic nuclear driver. Distinct reverse
index orders are recomputed before the tensor permutations are filled, with
their actual defect and comparison count retained. Complete Cartesian blocks
measure acoustic translation sums across every derivative slot; incomplete
blocks/pattern sets return no measured translation residual. Memory and
evaluation cost are explicit in [the API reference](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver).

`tests/p43_force_constant_tensors.rs` validates complete Cartesian tensors,
block extraction, arbitrary-pattern multilinearity in an unrestricted
reference, and CLI numerical parity. Independent analytic gradients and
Hessians provide radial rotation identities for transverse cubic/quartic
entries; these checks do not reuse the tensor assembly as their oracle.

`response::nuclear::molecular_taylor` transports the moving basis metric
while differentiating simultaneous nuclear and uniform electric paths.
The generic spherical Gaussian position integrals and nuclear field
energy retain all Taylor coefficients. The dipole includes both the
moving electronic operator and explicit nuclear position derivatives.
`mixed_molecular_response` contracts arbitrary paired nuclear/electric legs
using the exact polarization identity, with compensated accumulation and
separate energy/dipole roundoff estimates. No displaced SCF enters the value.

`static_spectroscopic_derivative` constructs directional APT, Raman and
hyper-Raman from mixed dipole response. Its electric rank is one, two or
three. All 27 hyper-Raman tensor entries are evaluated in their own field
slot order. Electric permutations are measured on the raw results and can
fail convergence; they are never removed by copying or averaging entries.
This static intermediate driver covers integer-occupation collinear
all-electron HF/semilocal/hybrid/RSH models, including uniform reference
fields. Dynamic spectroscopy, full mode intensities and other functional
components remain in the original implementation objective.

`tests/p41_molecular_mixed.rs` checks APT against the independent analytic
Hessian driver, nuclear/electric Maxwell relations, charged rigid
translations, field-only limits against the separate fixed-basis driver,
nonaxial tensor permutations, and Raman/hyper-Raman against displaced
CPKS/nonlinear-field oracles at two steps with Richardson extrapolation.
For the charged HeH fixture, HF Raman zz is `1.0933882747485544` against
`1.0933882747234687`; hyper-Raman zzz is `-6.708394631959569` against
`-6.708394633495515`. PBE gives `1.3849845314302447` against
`1.3849845409018124`, and `-6.2422023472100765` against
`-6.242202374760304`. These measured points do not establish completion of
the entire spectroscopy family. [The aligned API tables](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver) specify
Rust, CLI, Python and ASE calls; [the physical targets](scope.md#13-physical-target-registry)
retain the full supplied property list.

<!-- Static correlated spectroscopy connection: begin -->
### Static correlated Raman and hyper-Raman connection

`driver::run("static-spectroscopy", ...)`, the canonical CLI and existing
native Python/ASE spectroscopy functions now share the same tensor assembly.
`electric_order=1/2/3` returns the three APT, nine Raman or 27 hyper-Raman
entries for one supplied nuclear displacement path. Raman differentiates
the complete energy through total order three; hyper-Raman through order
four. The target density and noncanonical PT2 amplitudes respond through
that full order, including a distinct energy target. Response mathematics
does not select registered functional names. Geometry-only dispersion has
zero mixed electric derivatives analytically. Every ordered electric slot

### Rectilinear anharmonic bands

The molecular driver builds normal-mode displacement patterns from the analytic
Hessian and electron-unit masses after Eckart projection. It checks analytic
forces at the expansion point and requires a stationary minimum. Analytic
moving-geometry/electric response gives full cubic and quartic mode force
constants and first, second and third nuclear derivatives of the dipole.
Optional static Raman uses the corresponding polarizability derivatives;
the third requires fifth energy order. These derivative requirements agree
with the analytic intensity formulation described by
[Cornaton et al., 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5063043/).
The driver passes a functional provider throughout and contains no dispatch
by functional name. The current molecular derivative kernels cover integer
collinear all-electron exact-integral HF and native semilocal/global-hybrid/RSH
KS models; the remaining functional terms and internal spaces retain their
implementation targets.

For mass-weighted coordinates, oscillator ladder actions construct
`H0 = sum_i omega_i (n_i + 1/2)`, `V3 = Phi_ijk Q_i Q_j Q_k / 6`, and
`V4 = Phi_ijkl Q_i Q_j Q_k Q_l / 24`. At VPT2 order the second perturbation is
`W2 = V4 + T_Coriolis + U_Watson`. Input tensors contain actual derivatives,
not Taylor coefficients. Each observable has `O1 + O2 + O3`, with the same
rank factorials. Retained states start with the vacuum, every fundamental,
overtone and pair combination. Closure adds direct and second-order connected
states when `abs(delta_E) <= resonance_tol + resonance_coupling_factor*abs(V)`.
Denominators outside the retained space use their physical values; no floor
or shifted physical operator substitutes for a resonant state.

The anti-Hermitian contact generators satisfy
`S1_a,k = -V3_a,k/(E_a-E_k)` and
`S2_a,k = -(W2 + [V3,S1])_a,k/(E_a-E_k)` for retained/external indices.
The effective retained Hamiltonian is
`P (H0 + V3 + W2 + [V3,S1]/2) P`. Every property receives
`P (O1 + O2 + O3 + [O1,S1] + [O1,S2] + [[O1,S1],S1]/2 + [O2,S1]) P`
and the same retained eigenvector transformation. Diagonalizing that retained
Hamiltonian resums its internal mixing; this is explicit in the calculation
model rather than an assertion that all higher perturbative orders are known.
Bands report harmonic, mechanical, electrical and mixed dipole amplitudes
whose sum gives the physical transition dipole. Their squared total retains
interference. Static Raman activities use the Placzek isotropic/anisotropic
invariants of the transformed polarizability. A phase reversal of a normal
mode changes derivative signs consistently and leaves frequencies/strengths
invariant.

Every report includes the raw Hermiticity defect before eigensolution, the
actual eigen residual, exterior mixing norm, minimum physical external
denominator, retained occupations/energies and resource limits. Large external
mixing emits a perturbation-validity warning. Dense polyad matrices are bounded
by the explicit oscillator limits and memory allowance; this small vibrational
problem does not change the matrix-free electronic response solver.

This is a zero-temperature Watson vibrational model at second perturbative
order. Frequency-dependent Raman, thermal populations, higher-order rotational
kinetic expansions and rotationally resolved lines remain work in the original
objective. Selecting modes defines a reduced Hamiltonian and explicitly reports
omitted mode couplings. These available calculations do not complete those
remaining targets.

#### Coriolis and Watson kinetic corrections

The center-of-mass geometry gives the full inertia tensor. Analytic
mass-weighted Eckart patterns give
`zeta_ij = sum_A mass_A (pattern_Ai cross pattern_Aj)` in the same Cartesian
frame. The raw mode metric, translation/rotation Eckart projections and
antisymmetry are checked before use. The implementation contracts the full
inverse inertia, retaining covariance under rigid rotations and translations.
`WatsonRotation::from_coefficients` accepts supplied kinetic tensors without
geometry; its Eckart/mode-metric diagnostics are absent (`None`) rather than
zero measurements. `molecular_rotation` measures and fills those diagnostics.

With `pi_a = sum_ij zeta_ij,a Q_i P_j`, the equilibrium kinetic correction is
`T_Coriolis = sum_ab inverse_inertia_ab pi_a pi_b / 2`.
Nonlinear rotors also have `U_Watson = -trace(inverse_inertia)/8` in atomic
units. The constant changes absolute zero-point energy and cancels from
transition energies at this order. Angular actions use analytic coordinate
and momentum ladder operators, including their signs and operator ordering.
The correction participates in resonance closure, external-space generators,
retained mixing and the dipole/polarizability transformation. It therefore
changes intensities as well as frequencies; it is not a frequency-only shift.
This equilibrium truncation is the vibrational second-order Watson model in
[the unified VPT2 formulation](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00214-023-03069-7).

Linear rotors use the two-dimensional physical inverse inertia and the linear
isomorphic Hamiltonian, whose pseudopotential has no nonlinear-rotor constant.
The zero axial moment is a removed rotation degree of freedom, not a floored
denominator. The diatomic radial limit has zero Coriolis and Watson correction.
The two-axis kinetic operator and absence of the nonlinear constant follow
[the linear isomorphic Hamiltonian](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1386142522012197).
For polyatomic linear molecules the reported states are vibrational band
origins. Combining bending states with actual rotational functions requires
the Sayvetz condition `K=abs(l)` and `J>=abs(l)`; they must not all be interpreted
as physical `J=0` rovibrational states. This distinction is described in
[the linear isomorphic Hamiltonian calculation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022285222000376).

### Nuclear derivatives about an externally biased reference

Field derivative order and nuclear-coordinate derivative order are distinct.
Magnetic energy derivatives and Cotton-Mouton response do not by themselves
establish nuclear force constants in a magnetic field.

| Reference | Nuclear gradient | Nuclear Hessian | Cubic/quartic nuclear derivatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| Molecular uniform electric field | Connected | Connected | Connected on supported integer-occupation nuclear Taylor paths |
| Molecular finite orbital magnetic field | Connected through bfield-gradient; HF directional orders 1-4 accepted | Common analytic driver connected | Common analytic contracted tensors connected; HF B-only fits accepted |
| Molecular simultaneous electric and magnetic fields | Restricted H2 and charged H2+ Zeeman fits accepted; PBE0 water analytic-path fits passed, public tensors separate | Neutral restricted and charged unrestricted HF tensors accepted on all public surfaces | The same two HF references accepted on all public surfaces; other classes remain per-entry |
| Periodic finite Berry electric field | Connected on the insulating Gamma/Born-von Karman enthalpy model | HF H2 independent directional fits and public tensor comparisons passed | HF H2 directional fits and public contracted tensors passed; other classes/combinations require acceptance |
| Periodic 3D finite-Gamma point-source magnetic field | Connected on the full spinor exchange/SOC model | HF tensor public comparisons passed | HF/custom range-exchange/SOC order-1..4 fits passed; HF contracted tensor public comparisons passed |
| Periodic 3D finite-Gamma point-source simultaneous electric/magnetic field | Seven crystal metrics and model/limit cases passed order-1..4 fits | Both CLI names/native Python/ASE tensor checks passed | All five report forms passed on the same finite-Gamma subset |
| Periodic magnetic BZ or 1D/2D sources | Nuclear connections remain required | Required | Required |
| Arbitrary-q DFPT on finite electric/magnetic references | Per-q field-biased connection required | Required | Required |

Nuclear paths include the field's moving-basis, metric/Pulay and source
terms on each supported model. Positive-temperature Mermin Hessians have
separate occupation-response acceptance. Third/fourth nuclear paths keep
their stated integer-occupation restrictions. ECP, continuum, nonlocal,
learned, spinor and correlation support follows each provider's actual
restrictions. The complete double-hybrid amplitude/orbital nuclear response
and remaining field/reference/functional combinations stay within scope.

### Molecular nuclear orders one through four about finite electromagnetic bias

Six independently converged H2 cases passed all 24 energy/analytic-force
fits: HF electric-only, HF magnetic-only, HF joint bias, and PBE/TPSS/PBE0
joint bias. Positive and negative displaced SCFs/forces are computed
independently; no coordinate or ordered response values are copied by
symmetry. Every raw step is retained. The coarse HF quartic Richardson
error 4.118102339467633e-6 exceeded its fixed 2e-6 gate; the resolved four
steps [0.06,0.03,0.015,0.0075] reduce it to 1.598982901640511e-8.
The accepted exponent range is 1.991552236-2.029039426; minimum R2 is
0.999970126791 and maximum Richardson error 8.75017143464607e-7.
The water joint-field case is still running and is not accepted here.

The existing hessian/cubic-fc-along/quartic-fc-along identifiers passed
native Python, ASE atomic and physical units, canonical dft-rs CLI and
its compatibility alias for HF H2 at simultaneous E/B bias. Production
intrinsic permutation reuse is explicitly reported; no independent raw
ordered asymmetry or magnetic atomic polar tensor is fabricated.
All fields remain fixed in laboratory Cartesian axes. The shared driver
retains sufficient London phase degree before SCF, including phase terms
that vanish at the reference geometry but contribute to nuclear response.

<!-- magnetic-nuclear-operator-measurements:begin -->

### Variational complex nuclear energies through fourth order

The shared static complex moving-metric path now computes stationary energy
orders 1/2/3/4 with density response solved through orders 0/1/1/2. This uses
the variational 2n+1 rule, retaining all explicit geometry and metric jets
through the requested energy order and continuing the occupied projector
idempotently. It does not provide higher-order density or dipole response.
The full-density implementation remains available as an independent oracle.
Two coupled closed-form complex reference/gauge choices passed eight new
four-step energy fits on [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01], with full-density/closed-energy
agreement below 1e-11. The pre-existing 16 full-density fits also passed.
Empty residual/stationarity arrays for solved order zero mean no density
equation was needed; they must not be reported as measured zero residuals.

The physical 3D finite-Gamma point-source magnetic tests passed eight
independent relaxed-SCF-energy/variational-force fits again using this
reduced energy path: HF and custom full/range exchange with generated SOC.
The original complete-density oracle and the failed quartic energy-only
interval remain documented above. All seven steps and unchanged gates are
retained; order four uses the resolved force interval
[0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075]. Numerical differences are validation only.

### Charged molecular and coherent spinor field references

Charged H2+ in simultaneous electric and orbital magnetic fields now passes
four independent nuclear order-1..4 fits on the analytic complex London
path, with fixed collinear alpha/beta populations (1,0) and spin Zeeman
enabled. Each independently displaced energy also agrees within 2e-12
with a dense one-electron generalized-eigenvalue oracle, including nuclear
repulsion, laboratory electric-origin restoration and the positive alpha
Zeeman offset. The sign labels a constrained spin population, not an
unconstrained lowest-Zeeman spinor. The six steps are
[0.12,0.09,0.06,0.03,0.015,0.0075]. The coarse fourth-order Richardson error
3.3783895658778818e-6 failed its unchanged 2e-6 gate and is retained. The
resolved four-point interval [0.06,0.03,0.015,0.0075] passes with
p=2.002387576, R2=0.999999618710 and Richardson=1.3259374931351431e-8.

A separate periodic H2+ one-electron state has a physical three-face
quantized field B=(2pi/25,2pi/25,2pi/25), a 3D uniform compensating
background and generated nuclear SOC. All displaced points check a dense
one-electron energy oracle, full-HF Hartree/exchange self-interaction
cancellation and actual off-diagonal laboratory spin density above 1e-3.
Four independent order-1..4 fits pass on seven retained steps
[0.12,0.09,0.06,0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075], with the same resolved quartic
force interval and unchanged gates. These are separate molecular
collinear and periodic generalized-spinor cases; no untested reference or
functional class is inferred from them.

### Accepted public field-nuclear reports and unmodified invariants

The canonical dft-rs CLI and its compatibility alias both passed the same
native Python, ASE atomic, ASE physical and CLI report comparisons. The
molecular joint-field cases cover neutral closed-shell HF and charged
open-shell HF with Zeeman enabled, each with a full Hessian and cubic/
quartic probe-contracted matrix. Every route reports the actual charge,
multiplicity, unrestricted flag and alpha/beta counts. All independently
constructed tensor rows are used; no translational repair is applied.
The largest translation contraction is 6.883382752675971e-15, largest
fresh relative response residual 7.862761215744372e-16 and largest
stationarity coefficient norm 9.906788930869048e-15 Hartree.

The periodic neutral HF finite-Gamma point-source case covers the scalar
fourth-order path, gradient, Hessian and cubic/quartic contracted tensors.
The energy-only response orders are 0/1/1/2 for requested energy orders
1/2/3/4. All native/CLI values and ASE unit conversions pass, including
root-qualified dotted unit keys and row-dependent Hartree/Bohr^order
labels. The largest fresh tensor response residual is
5.375001252786357e-13 at requested tolerance 1e-12. The coherent charged
SOC state separately passes all four surfaces for the order-four scalar
path including orders zero through four, with laboratory spin coherence
0.13618144426624013 and Hartree/exchange sum -1.3877787807814457e-16 Hartree.
Finite-sector magnetic tensors are not asserted to obey infinite-crystal
translation sum rules at fixed magnetic Bloch phase.

These acceptances cover the listed point-source exchange/SOC model only.
Periodic semilocal/nonlocal nuclear vertices, finite-width/countercharge
response, magnetic Brillouin-zone nuclear integration, 1D/2D source
response, simultaneous Berry electric/magnetic bias, correlated PT2
nuclear response and arbitrary-q field-biased DFPT remain required.
PBE0 water order-1..4 analytic-path fits have separately passed; its full public tensor acceptance is still required.

### Public real-path residuals and strict build checks

The periodic finite-electric-field contracted cubic and quartic reports now
carry the fresh residuals from every distinct cached real nuclear path.
An additional compact-basis HF acceptance compares native Python, ASE
atomic/physical and CLI values, unit scaling and actual residual vectors.
Both canonical and compatibility CLI names passed. Cubic response has
55 actual solved equations on 55 paths; quartic has 166 on 83 paths.
No empty-vector fallback is accepted in this test. The largest fresh
relative residual is 4.487250786879363e-16 at tolerance 1e-12.

The release all-target check with Python enabled passed with compiler
warnings denied. The Python suite treats warnings as errors. The source
package audit checked 844 files, the original dependency declarations and
lockfile, all 594 packaged code headers and the three aligned API tables
(157 ids); no forbidden name, machine path, extra dependency, missing
source/test or table mismatch was found. The built Python extension and

## Part 4: Molecular properties, states and analysis

### Molecular complex spinor reference provider

`response::spinor::MolecularSpinorBackend` is an isolated-molecule
`periodic::spinor_scf::SpinorEnergyBackend`. Its public constructor takes the
molecule, spherical basis, resolved functional, optional molecular grid,
converged collinear seed, SCF options, additional complex Hermitian spin/AO
operator, initial spin axis, functional model and XC convergence tolerance.
It retains every spin block and supplies both the energy and its variational
Fock. Other observables can reuse this provider and the full density,
coefficients, Fock, occupations, metric and diagnostics returned by
`run_spinor_scf`; they do not need another SCF implementation or a dispatch
on registered functional names.

`MolecularSpinorFunctionalModel::SpinCovariant` connects the shared global
spin-projection quadrature to all charge/spin density, gradient, kinetic and
current descriptors. The meta-GGA kinetic density includes the current
correction. Coulomb and full/range-separated exchange use the complete
spinor density. Scalar nonlocal correlation and reaction fields retain their
existing energy/potential providers. The separate `SpinDiagonal` model
preserves the explicitly labelled older dynamic spinor-response model.
`functional_model()` identifies the energy extension. A learned functional
without a spin-covariant provider and occupation-selected projectors are
refused rather than evaluated using incomplete spin blocks.

The common `energy`, `charges` and `orbitals` drivers accept
`reference=gks` or the `ghf` constraint alias. Functional selection remains
independent: `xc=hf` yields GHF; selecting a hybrid retains its semilocal and
full/range-separated exchange terms. `gks_operator_real/imaginary` are
optional `[2*AO][2*AO]` Hermitian one-electron matrices in Hartree, fixed in
the supplied AO frame. `spin_axis` rotates only the starting Fock; final
spin populations are not constrained. `spinor_xc_tolerance` (default
1e-10 Hartree) controls the actual energy/operator angular refinement.
The input is not an implicit two-electron SOC or a nuclear derivative of
an external AO operator.

`orbitals` with `coefficients=true,density=true` exports split real/imaginary
spinor coefficients, density, Fock and overlap matrices, in spin-major
`[up spherical AOs, down spherical AOs]` order. Occupations are per spinor
(0..1); no factor of two is implied. Phases and rotations of degenerate
subspaces are arbitrary. Charges use the charge Pauli density;
`mulliken_spin_vector[atom][xyz]` is the integrated Pauli magnetization in
electrons, `mulliken_spin` its z component, and `spin_expectation` is half
the vector sum in units of hbar. All complex density entries are retained.
`properties::lowdin_density_charges` shares the existing Loewdin algorithm
between collinear and spinor density providers.

`p241_molecular_gks` passes all three tests. The variational Fock is checked
against independent energy differences along all 64 real Hermitian density
directions of an eight-spinor C1 fixture, with a five-point, unpruned
molecular grid and TPSS. The initial interval [0.04,0.03,0.02,0.015] has one
failed component; its raw stage is retained. The resolved interval
[0.02,0.015,0.01,0.0075] passes all 64 components: p=1.984425..2.139874,
minimum R2=0.99975765. Every step is used and no error floor is applied.
The HF/SVWN5/PBE/TPSS/PBE0 collinear population limit agrees to 4.639e-13;
a nonuniform complex spin operator produces a fully complex stationary
reference. The static Python/ASE/CLI tests pass, with independent NumPy complex
metric/eigen/density and population contractions. Maximum measured public
orbital, metric and particle-number residuals are 3.449e-12 Hartree,
4.441e-16 and 1.777e-15 electrons.

This establishes a shared GKS reference and the named static-property
connections. GKS/GHF `gradient` and `hessian` now additionally connect to
`response::nuclear::spinor_nuclear_taylor`, reusing the existing analytic
geometry jets, spatial Coulomb/exchange contractions and stationary complex
projector recursion. The physical spinor density occupies one solver sector;
the auxiliary sector remains empty. Metric/Pulay and both integral endpoints
are differentiated, with no finite differences in production. An additional
supplied AO operator is fixed along the path; a nuclear SOC operator requires
its own integral derivatives. Full/range exchange paths are implemented;
the globally projected semilocal path is connected below. Nonlocal, solvent
and ECP nuclear path providers remain pending.
`p243_gks_nuclear_response` passes all 12 gradient and all 144 Hessian
entries of the C1 four-centre complex GHF state, with independently converged
displacements and no copied tensor entries. 155 entries resolve second-order
error intervals. Hessian (2,9) has a small quadratic coefficient and fails
the original, finer and coarser second-order intervals; all are retained.
The fourth-order stencil on [0.02,0.015,0.01,0.0075] Bohr resolves it:
errors [2.5900290128e-8,8.1970279661e-9,1.6252350160e-9,5.1916499572e-10],
p=3.986873, R2=0.99999742. No error floor or relaxed gate is used.
Native Python, ASE and CLI agree for every GHF gradient/Hessian entry.

The stationary 2n+1 energy-path rerun also passes all 156 entries (207.33 s).
Its retained fourth-order (2,9) interval gives errors
[2.5900492320e-8,8.1961199008e-9,1.6244635637e-9,5.1812046320e-10],
p=3.988764 and R2=0.99999818. The small difference from the full-density
run above is retained as a separate measurement, not silently substituted.

The GGA/meta-GGA/hybrid nuclear connection now includes all globally
projected Pauli density, gradient, kinetic and current descriptors on the
moving atom-owned Becke grid. The same scalar-generic XC bodies supply
potential paths and their independent mixed directional derivatives;
transverse kernels do not use a collinear-block approximation. Integrated
energy/potential Taylor coefficients are refined over angular rules up to
64, against the requested response tolerance, and a failed refinement is
an error. `nuclear_xc_angular_history` records the actual rule and maximum
energy/potential coefficient changes in atomic units. Conservative
cache-construction bounds are separately returned in
`nuclear_xc_cache_bounds`; they are not physical operator residuals.
A cache whose absolute descriptor bound remains conservative at the last
rule is retained only as a candidate: every actual energy/potential path
must still pass its fresh integrated comparison, or the calculation fails.

`p246` passes all 12 gradient and all 144 Hessian entries for each complex
PBE and PBE0 reference. PBE gives p=1.857356..2.143485, minimum
R2=0.99954933; PBE0 gives p=1.842842..2.044346, minimum R2=0.99943716.
Three failed PBE stages remain in the log; Hessian (6,0) resolves on
[0.004,0.003,0.002,0.0015] Bohr (p=1.989879, R2=0.99999921).
Its small explicit atom-owned quadrature tests derivative algebra, not
chemical quadrature convergence. Earlier TPSS runs failed at angular order
64: conservative bound 2.64806488738e-9 and actual moving-path defect
3.79319867183e-10 against 1e-12. Both failures remain recorded. After
consistent reference/Taylor refinement through order 128, the full TPSS
rerun passes all 12 gradient and 144 Hessian entries. Its Hessian (9,6)
retains a failed coarse fit and resolves on [0.02,0.015,0.01,0.0075]
Bohr (p=1.884587, R2=0.99972035). No physical path gate was relaxed;
this is bounded nuclear acceptance on the stated explicit quadrature.

The first uncached nuclear run was stopped after more than three hours
while rebuilding the same XC operator. `SpinorNuclearContext` now shares
descriptor gradients/Hessians over all Cartesian paths; application stays
matrix-free and no AO fourth-rank response matrix is stored. The cache
respects `incore_mb`; larger cases retain on-demand evaluation. Current
and previous angular rules are retained for fresh comparisons of each
actual energy/potential coefficient. No physical denominator, functional
term, test component or fit threshold is changed by this optimization.

`spinor_nuclear_energy_taylor` reuses the existing stationary 2n+1 theorem
for nuclear energies: gradients require no orbital-response solve and
Hessians require first-order response. The complete `spinor_nuclear_taylor`
continues to solve every density order for observables that require it.
Neither path substitutes the reduced parent density for nonstationary PT2.
Nonlocal, solvent, ECP, correlated full-spinor and other observable source
providers remain unfinished combinations of the accepted full objective.

### Reference constraints for molecular populations and orbitals

The existing `charges` and `orbitals` calculations now accept `reference`
(default `auto`), with `rks`, `uks`, `roks` and the HF aliases `rhf`, `uhf`,
`rohf`. `CollinearPropertyReference` and
`driver::method::run_collinear_property_reference` select the existing SCF
engine and share functional providers, dispersion and additive energy terms.
No property calculation branches on a functional's registered name.
`reference_type` records the selector. The default preserves the existing
`unrestricted`/multiplicity behavior. Explicit RKS requires a closed shell;
ROKS requires an open shell. A selected explicit reference overrides the
legacy unrestricted flag for these two properties only.

`charges` retains Mulliken/Loewdin charges and the z-axis Mulliken spin
populations, all in electrons. `orbitals` retains its AO matrix export flags.
For ROKS, the common spatial determinant supplies both densities; exported
spin coefficients and energies are semicanonical within each spin's
occupied/virtual spaces. They need not diagonalize the full unconstrained
spin Fock or be identical between channels. The nested-projector identity
`P_alpha S P_beta=P_beta` remains valid.

The ROKS path inherits the existing integer-occupation restriction; SMD and
unrestricted stability following are refused for this connection. Response
kernels are not selected through this static-property interface. Missing
double-hybrid reference connections and the remaining
RKS/UKS/ROKS/GKS combinations of other observables remain implementation
work. The molecular GKS provider above uses the complete spin-covariant
semilocal energy and Fock. Existing dynamic molecular spinor response still
uses its separately labelled spin-diagonal functional extension; it must not
be relabelled as the transverse kernel of the new GKS model.

water cation, including nested projectors and the closed-shell RKS/UKS
limit. All three Rust tests pass: maximum orbital/population defects are
6.217e-15 (closed-shell PBE RKS/UKS) and 5.718e-15 (ROKS functional-class
suite). The corresponding four Python/ASE/CLI tests pass with warning and
unit checks enabled. The ROKS/ROHF selectors are also connected to the
canonical `energy`, `gradient`, `hessian` and `polarizability` drivers using
the existing constrained open-shell implementations; the new canonical
nuclear-route fit is tracked separately in `p242_reference_nuclear_routes`.
The C1 four-hydrogen-ion ROHF acceptance now passes all 12 gradient and
144 Hessian entries. The first coarse run failed 73 components; the finer
0.004..0.0015 and 0.002..0.00075 runs still failed two, with all raw stages
retained. Tightening the SCF orbital criterion to 1e-12 and resolving finer
intervals through [0.0005,0.000375,0.00025,0.0001875] Bohr passes all 156:
p=1.807366..2.199687, minimum R2=0.99905866. Hessian entries (7,4) and
(7,10) resolve with p=2.068393/1.942233 and R2=0.99993257/0.99993665.
The native Python/ASE/CLI nuclear comparisons pass. RKS/UKS selectors now
translate to the existing molecular constraints across the common driver;

### Full nuclear tensors for generic double hybrids

`gradient` and `hessian` now share the existing double-hybrid preparation,
full moving-basis parent density path and noncanonical PT2 amplitude solver.
All nuclear AO integral endpoints, overlap/Pulay, quadrature and occupied/
virtual frame rotations respond analytically. The full parent density is
solved through the requested order; no stationary-parent 2n+1 truncation is
applied to the nonstationary correlated energy. Generic GGA, meta-GGA and
full/range-separated hybrid parents use the same interfaces, without named
functional branches in the response calculation.

The common tensor assembler returns every Cartesian component, including
all mixed Hessian elements. `parent_`, `target_`, `pt2_`,
`pt2_same_spin_alpha_`, `pt2_opposite_spin_`, `pt2_same_spin_beta_` and
`dispersion_` prefix the respective `gradient`, `hessian` and
`nuclear_energy` entries. Spin-channel contributions are unscaled; only
`pt2_` contains the supplied SS/OS coefficients. Total = target + PT2 +
dispersion. Energies, gradients and Hessians use Hartree, Hartree/Bohr and
Hartree/Bohr^2; axes are [atom][xyz] and [3*atom+axis][3*atom+axis].
Fresh response, amplitude, projector, stationarity, metric, particle-number,
frame and reference energy/Fock residuals are returned. The named empirical
dispersion recipe is differentiated with the same generic scalar expression.

Measured correlated component fits give p=1.802733..2.195880 and minimum
R2=0.99902605. Forty-nine failed stages are retained and resolved without
changing the gates or inserting error floors.

`p245_double_hybrid_nuclear` passes all 4368 independently fitted components:

gradient plus 144 Hessian entries per channel. Every displaced state is

Maximum printed orbital/amplitude residuals in this run are
1.25912e-15/6.93889e-17. All tensor entries and SS/OS reconstruction

After the ROKS response-control/convergence fix, its native/ASE/CLI

ROKS/GKS
PT2, distinct-target molecular nonlocal nuclear derivatives, ECP/solvent
