### Analytic orbital stability and internal following

The molecular collinear orbital Hessian uses the same production adiabatic
Hartree, semilocal density/gradient/tau, global and range-separated exchange,
configured nonlocal and solvent kernel products as the existing TDDFT/CPKS
reference. Real generators use A+B; imaginary generators use A-B, retaining
the antisymmetric exchange sector. No finite orbital rotations are used to
construct the production Hessian. The stability-channel interpretation follows
[the orbital stability theory](https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.127.1650).

Block Davidson constructs only projected matrices, retains a degeneracy
buffer, adds full-support starting directions and checks fresh full-operator
residuals. Independent Rayleigh descent probes the lowest root when the
Davidson subspace is incomplete. Substantial non-Hermiticity is an error;
unconverged eigenvalues or an overturned lowest root are returned with
warnings and unconverged provenance. Resolution-dependent `indefinite` is
not a stable verdict. A negative physical curvature is independent of
numerical convergence. The detailed channels, defaults, layouts and report
fields are in [all three API tables](rust-api.md#orbital-stability-and-following-conventions).

An independent energy oracle explicitly rotates complex occupied AO
coefficients, forms determinant densities, and sums four-index ERIs for
Hartree, global exchange and long-range exchange, plus the energy-only XC
quadrature. It never applies a response/TDA operator or response Fock kernel.
Restricted normalized generators give `E''=4*lambda`; coupled unrestricted
generators give `E''=2*lambda`. Central energy differences validate every real
and imaginary singlet/triplet curvature for six functional examples. The
accepted angular steps are `0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.00125` radians:

| Functional | Internal real p | External spin p | External complex p | External complex spin p | Minimum log-space R_squared |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hf | 1.999714350993 | 2.000554680803 | 1.995054319856 | 1.995053132046 | 0.999997207354 |
| svwn5 | 2.000377812234 | 2.000700591325 | 2.001744573769 | 2.001746296905 | 0.999998649161 |
| pbe | 2.000168171247 | 2.000015905108 | 1.999977629019 | 1.999978825770 | 0.999999929754 |
| b3lyp | 2.000117337544 | 1.999020590483 | 2.004422120679 | 2.004457139729 | 0.999996100737 |
| cam-b3lyp | 2.000167454252 | 1.999212029261 | 1.991938419696 | 1.991890717134 | 0.999990221625 |
| r2scan | 1.998861312011 | 1.993964730353 | 2.009710056518 | 2.009710997226 | 0.999997114329 |

All 24 fits satisfy unchanged `abs(p-2)<0.02`, `R_squared>0.99999`,
step-halving relative ratio deviation below 0.03, and independent Richardson
agreement within 1e-6 Hartree. Failed broader intervals are retained:
`0.04..0.005` gave SVWN5 external-spin p=2.033942392009 and
R_squared=0.999931747727; `0.02..0.0025` gave r2SCAN external-spin
p=1.980074370775 and R_squared=0.999980006500. Those intervals did not meet
the asymptotic acceptance criteria; the resolved four-point interval above
is used for every channel and functional, with no threshold relaxation.

Additional independent checks include restricted H2 positive/negative spin
curvature across bond stretching, the unrestricted one-electron bare-Hcore
energy-gap limit, an uncoupled negative and degenerate matrix spectrum,

budget, and explicit unresolved-sign/channel/input contracts.

Internal following evaluates the exact orthogonal exponential of the full
occupied-virtual generator, preserves determinant particle numbers and the

Every accepted step lowers energy by at least the requested amount and is

external spin instability is reported without silently changing reference
class. The returned final state is used for downstream CLI molecular
properties. The dedicated native/ASE getter reports the final reference
without replacing another independently generated calculation.

but still need dedicated independent curvature acceptance.

### Relaxed orbital energy and frontier gap gradients

The shared nuclear driver now returns `orthonormal_fock_coefficients[n]`,
the factorial-normalized Taylor coefficient of `B(t)^T F_s(t) B(t)`.
The metric transport satisfies `B(t)^T S(t) B(t)=I` and starts in the
reference MO basis. These coefficients are operator matrices, not orbital
energies. They include integral/grid derivatives, Pulay terms and the
self-consistent density response through the same generic functional provider.
No displaced SCFs or orbital-gap denominator replacements construct them.

For a nondegenerate eigenvalue, its first nuclear derivative is the diagonal
element of the first coefficient. `orbital_energy_gradients` collects these
derivatives for requested Cartesian IDs `3*atom+axis`, preserving request
order. Omitting coordinates requests all `3*N` coordinates. The returned
layout is `[spin alpha,beta][orbital][coordinate]`, in Hartree/Bohr; orbital
energies and the default degeneracy tolerance `1e-8` use Hartree.

Eigenvalues whose total cluster energy span is within the tolerance return
a projected derivative matrix for every coordinate and `None` for their
individual gradients. Grouping limits the entire energy span and does not
chain successive small gaps into a much larger group. Matrices retain raw
Hermiticity diagnostics before any interpretation, their actual reference
energy spread, and the largest coordinate-operator commutator.

At exact degeneracy, eigenvalues of `sum_a direction[a]*D_a` are directional
slopes. Separately sorted slopes for different directions cannot generally
be combined into multivariate orbital branches. In Rust,
`OrbitalCluster::directional_slopes(weights)` provides this spectrum;
`linearized_energies(weights, step)` instead diagonalizes
`diag(reference energies)+step*sum_a weights[a]*D_a`, retaining small
nonzero reference splittings. Python/ASE/CLI return the same matrices and
energies for explicit directional diagonalization. A near-degenerate block
spectrum is not mislabeled as exact individual Cartesian gradients.

`frontier_gap_gradient` reports each spin's neutral-reference `LUMO-HOMO`
orbital gap and the difference of the corresponding relaxed gradients.
It is not a charged-state fundamental gap. A spin without occupied or
virtual orbitals has no frontier gap. If either frontier belongs to a
grouped eigenspace, its unique Cartesian gap gradient is absent and the
full block data remains available.

Projector, stationarity, moving-metric, particle-number, raw Hermiticity,
reference-energy and reference-Fock defects accompany the common report.
Complete Cartesian results at zero field measure the translation sum
for both individual gradients and whole projected blocks. Coordinate
subsets or a nonzero reference field leave that diagnostic absent.

Rust, CLI, native Python and ASE entries are aligned in [the API tables](rust-api.md#common-calculation-driver).
Native positions and reference electric fields use atomic units. ASE
converts geometry from Angstrom and returns the atomic-unit report. Explicit
unrestricted singlet references are available through the request keyword.
All-electron integer-occupation collinear HF, LDA, GGA, meta-GGA, global
hybrid and range-separated hybrid kernels share this driver. Moving ECP,
RI-J, nonlocal/solvent terms, finite-occupation, periodic and spinor/Dirac
versions remain in the original scope and are not claimed complete here.

### Orbital magnetic response and NMR

The common molecular driver computes analytic zero-field orbital response for
restricted and unrestricted collinear references. It uses the actual alpha and
beta occupations, orbitals, energies, exchange and spin meta-GGA current kernels.
The supported all-electron terms are exact exchange, LDA, GGA, global hybrids,
range-separated exchange and gauge-covariant meta-GGA. Functional providers use
their parts, derivatives, family and exchange coefficients; no response branch
uses a registered functional name.

For each Cartesian field component and spin, `dP_s/dB_a = i D_s,a`,
`dS/dB_a = i Shat_a`, with real antisymmetric matrices. The field is the
reduced atomic field entering `(p+A)^2/2`, `A=B cross (r-origin)/2`.
The default London orbitals and the explicit common-origin alternative share
the same contractions. A common-origin finite basis retains origin dependence.
Positions and the explicit origin are in Bohr on Rust/native/Python APIs.
ASE converts its Atoms positions from Angstrom; its explicit origin remains Bohr.

The spin orbital equations include the differentiated metric constraint:

```text
(eps_a,s-eps_i,s) U_a,i,s + (-cx K[D_s]-clr K_lr[D_s]+K_current,s[D_s])_a,i
    = eps_i,s Shat_a,i - Fhat_explicit,s,a,i - G_response[D_occ,s]_a,i
D_s = C_v,s U_s C_o,s^T - transpose - C_o,s Shat_oo,s C_o,s^T
D_s S P_s + P_s S D_s + P_s Shat P_s - D_s = 0
Tr(D_s S + P_s Shat) = 0
```

Antisymmetric imaginary spin densities have zero first-order real density,
gradient and conventional kinetic-density changes at a real current-free
reference. Density Hartree and density/gradient XC kernels therefore vanish.
The explicit London derivatives of the Coulomb, exchange and semilocal Fock
remain. The meta-GGA variable is `tau_s-|j_p,s|^2/(2 rho_s)`; its cached
spin current Hessian and basis current are included. London ERI exchange uses
the exchange density of each spin, without replacing an unrestricted spin
density by half the total density.

MINRES solves the Hermitian magnetic orbital operator without constructing it.
The fresh residual is `||A U-b||_2/||b||_2`, separately for each spin and
field component, including a zero-source result of zero. Defaults are relative
tolerance `1e-10`, at most 500 iterations and the shared configuration's
GMRES restart 40. MINRES does not restart. No energy gap is clipped and no
preconditioner floor changes the physical operator. An invertible indefinite
stationary Hessian has a formal response; a stability analysis is needed to
classify that reference as a minimum. Singular incompatible equations fail
instead of producing an accepted unconverged tensor.

`magnetic_density_response(...,&config)` returns
`ResponseReport<SpinMagneticResponse>`. Its value includes:

- `density_hat[spin][B][AO,AO]`, `overlap_hat[B][AO,AO]` and explicit
  fixed-density `explicit_fock_hat[spin][B][AO,AO]`.
- Actual occupations, gauge, origin and the per-source solver methods.
- Measured differentiated-projector, number and antisymmetry defects.

The report contains the independently recomputed reference stationarity,
eigenvector, metric, projector and particle-number defects, six spin-major
relative response residuals and iteration counts, units, axes, model and warnings.
The legacy `magnetic_response[_with_grid]` returns the sum of the two spin
derivatives in its unchanged result layout; its residual now maximizes the two
fresh relative spin residuals.

`molecular_nmr_response(...,&config)` returns
`ResponseReport<Vec<Shielding>>`. The diamagnetic/mixed operator and the
total spin density response are contracted with the nuclear-moment operators.
Each tensor is `nucleus, nuclear moment axis, external B axis` and has
total, diamagnetic and paramagnetic pieces in ppm, using `alpha_fs^2*1e6`.
This is orbital shielding at fixed spin occupations. Spin Zeeman, hyperfine,
Curie/temperature contributions, spinor/SOC and Dirac response are additional
planned observables; this orbital result does not assert a complete paramagnetic
chemical shift.

The native `magnetic_response(numbers,positions,*,...)` wrapper routes to
the same compiled `_core.nmr(...,density_response=True)` driver. It also
returns the actual zero-field Fock, overlap, density, orbitals and energies for
independent validation. `nmr(...)` retains its shielding dictionary and
adds common response metadata. Both accept `unrestricted=True` and shared
`response_tol/response_max_iter/response_restart` controls. ASE getters are
`get_magnetic_response` and `get_nmr`. The canonical CLI commands
are `dft-rs magnetic-response molecule.xyz` and `dft-rs nmr molecule.xyz`,
with the same executable alias. `--magnetic-gauge` accepts `giao` or
`common_origin`; `--magnetic-origin` accepts three comma-separated
Bohr coordinates. All indexed density/source/metric entries or total and
component shieldings are printed alongside raw diagnostics.

Existing nonlocal London derivatives, ECP magnetic operators, RI-J London
derivatives, embedding/reaction-field London derivatives and a reference already
in an external electric field still need connections. Those inputs raise a
typed incomplete-capability error. They remain in the accepted full objective;
a refusal does not count as completing those combinations.

The implementation follows the London magnetic integral and response theory
described in [DFT NMR shielding](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp9529127), with the
spin current correction described in
[Current-dependent meta-GGA theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.07989).
No new library or external oracle runtime is required.

Acceptance includes the existing 14 NMR tests, including independent full
total/component shielding oracles, atomic Lamb limits, split-valence origin
cancellation and meta-GGA current behavior. The new Rust suite adds open-shell
origin cancellation for six functional classes, the forced-unrestricted closed
shell limit and density/reference contracts. Twelve independent generalized
spectral-projector four-step fits compare the analytic density derivative
against a complex Hermitian generalized eigenproblem in a doubled real space.
The public acceptance uses independent NumPy complex eigendecomposition for
eight more fits and compares actual native, ASE and CLI output entries.

The resolved reduced-field interval is `0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.00125`.
Rust exponents span `1.999297938065..2.000034413243`, with
`R2 >= 0.999999966878`. Public exponents span
`1.999297947406..2.000026902516`, with the same lower fit-quality bound.
All positive errors remain in the logs. Gates remain `|p-2|<0.02`,
`R2>0.99999`, halving ratios within 3% of four and Richardson error below
`1e-8`. The initial `0.04..0.005` open-shell interval passed the
order fit but failed the Richardson gate because the higher-order field
remainder was too large. The Richardson threshold is retained.

### Finite-temperature molecular references

`electronic_temperature` (Kelvin) gives Fermi-Dirac occupations in a
canonical ensemble with each spin channel's electron count fixed. The SCF
then minimizes the Mermin free energy `A = E - T S`,
`S/k_B = -sum_i [f_i ln f_i + (1 - f_i) ln(1 - f_i)]`, and `energy` is `A`.
The analytic gradient uses the occupation-weighted energy density
`W = sum_i f_i e_i C_i C_i^T`; no occupation-response term enters because the
occupations are stationary. Integer-occupation response routes (CPKS,
Hessian, stability) refuse a smeared reference by name; the ensemble
response below carries the occupation response explicitly.

`response::ensemble::EnsembleSolver` solves the static linear response of a
smeared reference: `dP_ij = W_ij (dF_ij - dmu delta_ij)` with
`W_ij = (f_i - f_j)/(e_i - e_j)` (and `df/de` on the diagonal and for
degenerate pairs), `sum_i dP_ii = dN_sigma`, and `dF = V + K[dP]` with the
full Hartree, exchange, XC, VV10 and continuum kernel. The number constraint
fixes `dmu`; the remaining linear problem is solved with GMRES on the original
operator.

### Conceptual DFT

`conceptual-dft` and `spin-conceptual-dft` report the route they used:

* `grand_canonical` (default at positive `electronic_temperature`): per-spin
  chemical potentials are the exact `dA/dN_sigma` (Fermi levels); the hardness
  matrix `d mu_sigma / d N_sigma'` and the Fukui matrices come from the
  ensemble response. `N = N_alpha + N_beta`, `M = N_alpha - N_beta`:
  `mu_N = (mu_a + mu_b)/2`, `mu_S = (mu_a - mu_b)/2`, `eta_NN`, `eta_SS`,
  `eta_NS` and its independently evaluated transpose `eta_SN`.
* `integer` (default at zero temperature): N, N-1 and N+1 integer ground
  states (lowest multiplicity unless `cation_multiplicity`/`anion_multiplicity`
  are given); IP, EA, `mu = -(IP+EA)/2`, `eta = IP - EA`, condensed
  `f+`, `f-`, `f0`, dual descriptor and local softness. These are the
  one-sided derivatives of the piecewise-linear E(N). A negative EA is
  reported with a warning. The spin channel uses fixed-N spin flips
  (`M +/- 2`); charge hardness and coupling are `null` with the reason.
* `koopmans`: frontier orbital energies and condensed frontier densities.

Conventions: `eta = d2E/dN2` without a factor 1/2, `S = 1/eta`,
`omega = mu^2/(2 eta)`; Fukui values are electron-population changes per atom
(`population = mulliken` or `lowdin`).

### Excited states on the common driver

`excitations`, `ecd-spectrum` and `td-state-gradient` route the TDA/RPA
solver and the singlet TDA gradient through the common driver
(`tests/p97_excited_states.rs`, water and twisted hydrogen peroxide in
STO-3G, bent magnesium hydride in LANL2DZ):

- The driver reproduces the library solver to 1e-10 for TDA and RPA.
- The complete RPA spectrum reproduces the analytic CPKS polarizability
  through `alpha_ab = sum_n 2 d_a d_b / omega_n`: largest deviation 4.4e-13
  (HF), 1.3e-13 (SVWN5), 2.6e-14 (PBE), 2.1e-13 (TPSS), 3.5e-12 (B3LYP),
  6.5e-12 (PBE0), 3.9e-13 (CAM-B3LYP), 1.9e-12 (wB97X-D), 2.6e-12 (M06);
  every TDA root lies above its RPA root.
- Broadened spectra integrate to their line strengths (oscillator strengths
  to 1e-5, rotatory strengths to 1e-5 of the summed magnitudes) and the
  mirror image has the same absorption and the opposite circular dichroism,
  for HF, PBE, B3LYP, wB97X-D and M06.
- Analytic excited-state gradient against central differences of
  `E_SCF + omega` with the state followed by its amplitudes (steps 0.02 to
  0.0025 Bohr): HF `p = 2.000084`, `R^2 = 1.00000000` and `p = 1.996417`,
  `R^2 = 0.99999914`; SVWN5 `p = 2.000126` and `p = 1.997404`,
  `R^2 = 0.99999955`; translation residual 3.6e-15. With an effective core
  potential on magnesium: HF `p = 2.000124` and `1.999936`, SVWN5
  `p = 2.000780` and `1.999471`, `R^2` at least `0.99999990`.
- GGA, meta-GGA and hybrid references, external fields, fractional
  occupations and RPA circular dichroism are refused by name.

- Hydrogen atom, STO-3G: the contact density 0.3946941394885 equals the

- Planar methyl radical, STO-3G, unrestricted: the three hydrogen couplings
  agree to 1e-4 for every functional class; carbon and hydrogen couplings in

### Three-body dispersion of molecules

`dispersion = d3abc` (zero damping) and `d3bjabc` (Becke-Johnson damping)
add the Axilrod-Teller-Muto term of every atom triple to the D3 pair energy,
with `C9 = sqrt(C6_ab C6_ac C6_bc)` on the D3 coordination numbers, pair
radii scaled by 4/3 and the damping exponent 16. Gradient and Hessian are
forward duals of the same energy function.

Acceptance (`dispersion::tests`): a carbon-nitrogen-oxygen triangle
reproduces the closed form with explicit angles (1.606907901409e-6 Hartree);
the three-body gradient and Hessian of ethane against central differences
over 0.008 to 0.001 Bohr give `p = 1.999814` to `2.000272`
(`R2 >= 0.99999998`) for both damping models; the periodic lattice sum of a
boxed molecule equals the molecular value to 2e-19.

### Complete collinear hyperfine tensors: measured acceptance

The common `hyperfine` driver now uses
`properties::hyperfine::spin_hyperfine_tensor` for the contact scalar and
the full contact-plus-spin-dipolar tensor. Its dipolar AO operator reuses
`response::spin_spin::field_gradient_operator`, the existing analytic
Hessian of the positive Coulomb potential. The distributional contact
correction `(4 pi/3) rho(R_A) delta_ab` restores the principal-value
dipolar operator without imposing a zero trace afterwards. The provider
is a supplied real collinear spin density, with no functional-name branch.
The result describes that electronic state, not a relativistic effective
spin Hamiltonian or an average over degenerate electronic states.

#### Resolving the open-shell frame comparison

The original independently initialized zero-field PBE OH comparison failed:
the rotated tensors differed by 41.186540689 MHz at the unchanged 1e-6 MHz
gate. The energies differed by 6.940e-8 Hartree and the dipolar eigenvalues
by 5.122e-5 MHz. Tightening all SCF tolerances to energy 1e-12, density
1e-10 and commutator 1e-8 did not converge in 300 iterations, at either
grid level 3 or 5; those failed trials are not accepted measurements.
The independent HF diagnostic resolves the distinction: zero-field
energies agree to 1.422e-14 Hartree and eigenvalues to 9.380e-13 MHz while
the tensor components differ by 64.065 MHz. Different azimuthal states of
the degenerate pi manifold have been selected, so equality of those two
component tensors is not an invariant physical requirement.

The frame test now rotates a state-selecting transverse electric field
`(0.02,0.03,0.01)` a.u. with the molecule. At the original PBE reference
tolerances the energy difference is zero at printed precision, the
eigenvalue difference is 5.116e-13 MHz and the component covariance
defect is 1.053e-9 MHz, passing the same 1e-6 gate. The tight HF comparison
gives 6.274e-10 MHz. The zero-field spherical-atom and raw symmetry/trace
tests are retained. No tensor is rotated, projected or averaged to force
agreement, and electronic-state tracking is not inferred from this test.

conversion. Coarse-mesh raw Hall reciprocity failures are retained with

### Exchange-enhanced thermal spin acceptance

`p129_spin_susceptibility` compares the production static spin response to
independent nonlinear finite-Zeeman-field SCF solutions, each with a common
chemical potential at fixed total number. The nonlinear route calls the
shared Fock evaluator but never the response kernel or its XC derivative.
The H2 cell uses a 9 Bohr cubic lattice, STO-3G, Gamma sampling and 150000 K.
The intentionally high temperature resolves both occupation channels; this
fixture is an operator test, not a low-temperature materials prediction.

At fields [0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01] atomic units:

| Parent | Screened chi per cell | Bare chi | Enhancement | Absolute central-difference errors | Fitted p | R^2 | Richardson defect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SVWN5 | 0.49920025343669683 | 0.45174205337959300 | 1.1050559709950787 | [2.1878503441069563e-4, 5.469884472575348e-5, 1.3674870776581027e-5, 3.4187290837150996e-6] | 1.999971360 | 0.999999999946 | 1.519e-11 |
| PBE | 0.50442427040060644 | 0.45379094459351321 | 1.1115785284178565 | [2.2589031662845205e-4, 5.64781930562086e-5, 1.4119897567721473e-5, 3.529997159690268e-6] | 1.999939909 | 0.999999999759 | 3.036e-11 |

No step was discarded and no error floor was used. The maximum finite-field

### Natural bond orbital analysis

`natural-bond` analyses the SCF one-particle densities and Fock matrices
(`src/properties/natural_bond.rs`, `src/properties/natural_bond/lewis.rs`).
Natural atomic orbitals: component-averaged atomic natural orbitals per atom
and angular momentum; the natural minimal basis takes the core and valence
subshells of the element (`ns np` for main-group elements including Li, Be,
Na and Mg; `ns (n-1)d` for transition metals; `ns (n-1)d (n-2)f` for
lanthanides and actinides; subshells removed by an effective core potential
are dropped); the core set is symmetrically orthogonalized, the valence set
is Schmidt-orthogonalized to it and orthogonalized with occupancy weights
(occupancies below 1e-6 raised to 1e-6), the Rydberg set is
Schmidt-orthogonalized and symmetrically orthogonalized, and the natural
character is restored by atom and angular-momentum block diagonalization.
Natural population analysis, natural electron configurations and Wiberg
indices `2 sum (D^a_mu,nu^2 + D^b_mu,nu^2)` follow in the NAO basis. The
natural Lewis structure takes core NAOs, lone pairs, two-centre bonds (pairs
in descending Wiberg coupling) and optionally three-centre bonds above an
occupancy threshold, depleting the density of every accepted orbital; the
threshold is scanned from 0.95 to 0.75 of the maximum occupancy for the
smallest non-Lewis occupancy among structures with at most the expected
number of Lewis orbitals. Hybrids are symmetrically orthogonalized per atom
and completed by Rydberg hybrids; bonds and antibonds are the eigenvectors
of the density in their hybrids. Degenerate eigenvectors are fixed by the
Fock matrix within their degenerate space. NLMOs come from Jacobi rotations
of the Lewis/non-Lewis density block; second-order donor-acceptor energies
are `q_i F_ij^2/(F_jj - F_ii)`. Open shells get one Lewis structure per spin
with at most one electron per orbital. Assumptions: a full-rank AO metric;
the extensions to correlated densities, periodic cells, natural resonance
theory and the shielding, coupling and energy decompositions are described
in the next subsection.

Measured `p233_natural_bond` (release, strict units, one test thread; six
tests pass in 2.51 s):

- External NAO oracle (`tests/oracle_data/nbo_oracle.json`, generated by
  `tools/oracle/gen_nbo.py`): RHF/UHF water (STO-3G, 6-31G*), ammonia,
  formaldehyde, phosphine (6-31G*), ethylene (STO-3G) and the water cation
  doublet (6-31G*). The oracle's minimal basis differs from this package's
  for s-block elements (valence `ns` only) and lanthanides, so the cases
  contain H, B-Ne and Al-Ar only. Largest deviations over the seven cases:
  energy 5.826e-13 Hartree, natural charges 1.503e-10, natural spin
  populations 5.823e-10, sorted NAO occupancies per atom 1.771e-10, Wiberg

  [-0.96552, 0.48154, 0.48399].
- Lewis structures of HF/6-31G* references at the selected threshold 1.90:

  formaldehyde CR(C), CR(O), 2 LP(O), BD(1) and BD(2) C-O, 2 BD(C-H),
  non-Lewis 0.107356 of 16; ethylene 2 CR, BD(1) and BD(2) C-C, 4 BD(C-H),

#### Natural bond orbital extensions (p234)

Densities (`nbo_density`): the SCF density, the relaxed PT2 density of MP2
and double hybrids (`src/properties/pt2_density.rs`: unrelaxed occupied and
virtual blocks, orbital gradient of the PT2 Lagrangian, `z = -A^-1 g`
through the response solver, relaxation `1/2 dP[z]`), and the CASSCF state
density with its spin densities (`CiSpace::rdm1_spin`); MC-PDFT uses the
CASSCF density of its state. The Fock matrix of a correlated density is
`h + J[D] - K[D_s]`. Periodic cells (`periodic-natural-bond`): the
Born-von Karman supercell density and Fock matrix
`X[(L mu),(L' nu)] = 1/N_k sum_k X(k) exp(-i k.(R_L' - R_L))`, labels with
the cell translation (`C2[1,0,0]`), imaginary unfolding residue and the
translation defect reported. Natural resonance theory (`nbo_resonance`):
structures enumerated on the sigma skeleton (pairs bonded in the reference
or with Wiberg index at least 0.1; valence capacity 4, hydrogen 1; bond
order at most 3), each structure's density built from its prescribed
orbitals (cores, bonds without mutual depletion, lone pairs with depletion,
forced vectors orthogonalized against accepted ones), weights from the
simplex-constrained least-squares fit of the reference density built from
the actual NBOs (active set; optimality residual and degenerate directions
reported). Natural chemical shielding (`natural-shielding`): canonical
occupied rotation `T = C_o^T S L` to the NLMOs and first-order orbitals
`C_v U - 1/2 C_o S^(1)_oo`, per-NLMO paramagnetic and diamagnetic terms.
Natural J coupling (`natural-coupling`): rotated triplet and singlet
amplitudes per NLMO, diamagnetic term from NLMO densities on the grid.
Natural energy decomposition (`natural-energy-decomposition`): inter-fragment
NBO Fock blocks deleted and each fragment occupying its Lewis count gives the
localized state; charge transfer `E[P] - E[P_loc]`, electrostatics of the
deformed fragment densities, exchange-correlation remainder, deformation
against ghost-basis isolated fragments; the identity is reported.

#### Reference selection and natural density orbitals

For an SCF density, `natural-bond` selects the shared RKS, UKS or ROKS
solver using `reference`. The GKS connection uses its full converged
spinor density and Fock matrix. It extracts a common spin axis from their
Pauli components and requires both matrices to reduce to real spatial
blocks in that frame. `nbo_spin_axis` records the axis. The largest
transverse or spatial imaginary components are reported separately for
density and Fock. A general noncollinear or complex spatial Lewis search
remains open.

`nbo_spin_density=true` diagonalizes the signed alpha-minus-beta density
in the orthonormal NAO frame. The report contains all ascending signed
eigenvalues, AO coefficients, and the raw trace and density reconstruction
defects. A list of Bohr triples in `nbo_spin_density_points` additionally
returns the signed spin density in electrons/bohr^3 at those points. ASE
physical units use Angstrom and electrons/Angstrom^3.
[Natural spin-density orbitals](https://doi.org/10.1080/00268976.2022.2091049)

`nbo_natural_orbitals=true` diagonalizes the spin-summed density in
the same frame. In addition to natural spatial occupations and AO
coefficients, it returns the occupation bound defect and the nonlinear
effectively unpaired weights `[n_i(2-n_i)]^2` and their sum. Occupations
are used directly, so the bound defect is available when interpreting an
approximate correlated density. Both flags use the requested SCF,
relaxed PT2 or CASSCF density on the supported path. Integrated numerical
acceptance for the new spectra is tracked separately.
[Nonlinear effectively unpaired index](https://iopenshell.usc.edu/pubs/pdf/jcp-146-224103.pdf)

In the H₂O⁺ STO-3G checks with grid level one and zero weight cutoff,
ωB97X-D/UKS gives signed spin-density weights
`[-0.03279991916,-0.03040355233,0,0,0.03040355233,0.03279991916,1]`
to the shown precision. At points `[0.34,-0.19,0.32]` and
`[-0.81,0.16,-0.17]` bohr the spin densities are
`[0.3637597511268,0.2017220180799]` electrons/bohr^3.
The effectively unpaired index is `1.00000402378`. With the VV10
term disabled for that initial API parity test, the ωB97X-V
ROKS spin densities are `[0.3583882242876,0.1966271022378]`
electrons/bohr^3, with a single nonzero spin weight of one and
unpaired index one. Both cases pass canonical CLI, native Python,
generic Python and ASE comparisons in atomic and physical units.
With the native VV10 term enabled and its grid level set to zero,
ωB97X-V/ROKS gives `-74.94715186285751 Hartree` and a nonlocal
contribution of `+0.03918733419770 Hartree`. The corresponding
point densities are `[0.3583898197715,0.1966274084011]`
electrons/bohr^3, with an effectively unpaired index of one.

The CASSCF H₂ singlet in CAS(2,2)/STO-3G gives occupations
`[0.02540959049,1.97459040951]` at 1.4 bohr and an effectively
unpaired count of `0.00503476697`. At 5.5 bohr the count is
`1.96843418780`, with signed spin weights at most `1.111e-16`.
The initial 7 bohr case gives `1.99879417901` but fails the
`1e-12` singlet spin-weight criterion with raw weights
`[-4.5626281e-12,4.5627946e-12]`. Tightening `ci_tol` from
`1e-12` to `1e-14` leaves those weights unchanged. They reconstruct
the supplied spin density with zero trace defect. The 5.5 bohr
repeat retains the original spin threshold.

`nbo_corresponding_orbitals=true` uses the occupied collinear determinant
on the SCF route. It decomposes `C_alpha^T S C_beta` and returns the paired
alpha and beta coefficient matrices and the orthonormal complements
of both occupied spaces. The report includes the maximum cross-overlap
defect and `S_z^2 + (N_alpha+N_beta)/2 - sum(sigma_i^2)` in hbar^2.
Selected integer occupations determine the occupied frames.
Four public cases pass, including the ωB97X-D/UKS and ωB97X-V/ROKS
water cation. The UKS corresponding overlaps are
`[1,1,0.9995377051444458,0.9994619378961782]` with cross-overlap
defect `5.551e-16`. The separate GKS/SVWN5/STO-3G H₂⁺ test
gives `-0.5228558178990663 Hartree`, natural atomic charges
`[0.5,0.5]` and spin weights `[0,1]` up to roundoff. CLI, native
Python and ASE agree on that report.
[Corresponding orbitals](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1961.0175)

#### Natural transition orbitals

`td_nto=true` adds a singular-value representation to each molecular
TDA state in `excitations` and to collinear `xanes` states. The input is
the directed one-particle transition with particle rows and hole columns
in orthonormal MO frames. Restricted singlets use the charge transition,
restricted triplets the spin-difference transition, unrestricted states
the independent alpha and beta transitions, ROKS the charge transition
of the common-orbital flag, and GKS the full complex spinor transition.
The report gives squared singular values, the original transition norm
squared, real and imaginary AO coefficients for each paired orbital, and
the raw Frobenius reconstruction defect in the orthonormal MO frame.
Within degenerate singular subspaces the orbital pairs admit unitary
rotations. The RPA solve currently supplies the combined amplitudes
`X+Y`. A directed RPA transition requires both blocks. Numerical and
public acceptance uses independent singular-value calculations. Five
public cases cover the canonical CLI, native Python and ASE. For
H₂O with ωB97X-D/RKS/STO-3G, grid level one and zero weight cutoff, the
first singlet NTO weights are `[1.999999999738482,2.6152245023e-10]`
and the orthonormal-frame reconstruction defect is `4.465e-16`.
For the H₂O⁺ ωB97X-D/UKS first state, the leading alpha and beta
weights are `3.17970017742e-5` and `0.9999682019817484`.
The ROKS doublet/quartet and full complex GKS cases use asymmetric
H₄⁺ with STO-3G and an independent reconstruction of their flag or
spinor transition. Maximum public pole difference is `1.887e-15 Hartree`.
A complex rectangular analytic case with singular values
`[0.5,0.2,4e-9]` retains all three pairs with AO reconstruction RMS
`3.255e-17`.
[Natural transition orbitals](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1558471)

`td_difference_density=true` reports natural difference orbitals of
the unrelaxed CIS-like TDA state density. The occupied block is
`-X^H X` and the virtual block is `X X^H`. Its negative detachment
and positive attachment weights share the orbital pairs obtained from
the same SVD. A normalized state conserves charge and transfers one
electron summed over channels. The restricted spin-adapted charge
transition has a separate `sqrt(2)` factor for the NTO report.
Collinear RKS/UKS and full-spin GKS use this construction. The ROKS
common-orbital flag requires a state-density definition to obtain
the difference. Orbital-relaxed excited densities remain a separate path.
Three public cases pass. In ωB97X-D/RKS water and ωB97X-D/UKS H₂O⁺,
the attachment and detachment occupations agree with independent
eigenvalues of the amplitude products. The asymmetric HF GKS H₄⁺
test covers all 15 full-spin TDA roots. Each tested root transfers
one electron within `1e-10`.
[Attachment and detachment density](https://doi.org/10.1021/j100039a012)

Assumptions of the relaxed PT2 density: integer aufbau occupations, all
electrons correlated (no frozen core), no singles. The spin-orbital
equations cover open shells; the acceptance above uses closed-shell water.

## Part 5: Functionals, correlated and multiconfigurational methods

### Skala learned functional

`xc = skala` with `skala_model = <file>` evaluates a Skala model (Microsoft
Research, MIT licence) on the molecular grid: seven logarithmic meta-GGA
features per point, a spin-symmetrized input perceptron, non-local layers
that gather the features of the grid points of an atom on the atom (radial
functions, real spherical harmonics, unpartitioned atomic quadrature
weights), contract them up to the correlation order and scatter them back,
and an output perceptron with a scaled sigmoid that multiplies the LDA
exchange energy density. The implementation (`skala`) is pure Rust with a
hand-written reverse pass for `dE/drho`, `dE/dgrad rho` and `dE/dtau` of both
spins, from which `skala::skala_fock` builds the Kohn-Sham matrices of every
SCF iteration.

No trained parameters are part of the package. Every size (feature width,
number and width of the non-local layers, maximum angular momentum,
correlation order, depth of the perceptrons) and every constant
(`feature_epsilon`, `sigmoid_scale`, `lda_prefactor`, radial temperatures,
harmonic polynomials, coupling tensors) is read from the model file, whose
layout is documented in the module. `tools/convert_skala_model.py` writes it
from an official checkpoint and needs the official Python packages;
`skala::random_tensors` builds a model of any sizes with pseudo-random
weights for tests.

Scope and status: energy, charges, dipole, orbitals, Molden and orbital
files and multipoles of molecules. Nuclear gradients, Hessians, response
properties and periodic cells are refused, the dispersion parameters
published with the functional are not provided, and the second-order SCF
step is disabled. The grid is the dft-rs molecular grid; points with a
vanishing partition weight are dropped, which also removes them from the
atomic sums. The converter and the comparison with the official
implementation on its own grid have not been run in the environment in which
dft-rs is developed: energies of a converted checkpoint are unvalidated
until that comparison is made.

Acceptance (models with pseudo-random weights; `skala::tests`,
`tests/p100_skala.rs`):

- Directional derivative of the energy with respect to all densities against
  central differences, steps 0.04 to 0.005: `p = 2.000366` (10 features, 3
  channels, lmax 1, correlation order 2, one non-local layer) and
  `p = 2.000828` (12 features, 4 channels, lmax 2, correlation order 3, two
  layers), `R2 >= 0.99999995`, Richardson differences -3.1e-10 and -4.2e-10.
- Kohn-Sham matrices of water (9390 grid points): `tr(V dP)` against central
  differences `p = 2.000073`, `R2 = 1.00000000`, Richardson difference
  -1.2e-12; the matrices are symmetric.
- Exchange of the spin channels leaves the energy unchanged and swaps the
  derivatives; a density change at one point changes the enhancement factor
  at the other points of the same atom (2.6e-8) and at no point of another
  atom; zero density gives zero energy and finite derivatives; the
  enhancement factor stays inside the scaled sigmoid.
- Self-consistent water energies -73.6007380047 and -70.4902583547 Hartree
  for two architectures (8 and 9 iterations). Hellmann-Feynman relation
  `dE/dF = -mu` of the self-consistent energy: field steps 0.008 to 0.001
  a.u. give errors 2.308e-5, 5.770e-6, 1.442e-6, 3.605e-7, `p = 2.000144`,
  `R2 = 1.00000000`, Richardson difference 6.9e-11 (Hartree-Fock on the same
  route: -0.6790029436 against the dipole 0.6790052154).
- Gradient and Hessian requests, a model file without `xc = skala` and a
  file that is not a model are refused by name.

### Double-hybrid components and PT2 Lagrangian

The molecular GKS energy entry accepts integer full-spin parent
references with a common PT2 coefficient. Its zeroth-order pair
contraction uses the same generalized complex amplitudes as the
one-body Taylor path. A distinct semilocal or hybrid target is
evaluated at the converged parent density. The report includes the
unscaled and scaled generalized PT2 energies, the optional target
correction, the absolute amplitude residual and imaginary-energy
coefficient in Hartree, and a dimensionless relative residual. The
audited Linux wheel agrees across the installed CLI, native Python
and ASE for both HF-parent H5 cases with a complex spinor source,
a uniform electric bias and common PT2 coefficient 0.27. The same-target
total energy is -1.569675193072060 Hartree. The SVWN5-target total
is -1.524043215033748 Hartree with a target correction of
+0.045631978038311 Hartree. Both give unscaled PT2
-0.015104211018929 Hartree and weighted PT2 -0.004078136975111 Hartree.
A separate normalized Gaussian Boys integral and stationary spinor
pair contraction gives -0.015104211018929 Hartree, with absolute
difference 2.082e-17 Hartree. The absolute amplitude residual is
9.814e-18 Hartree, relative residual 5.678e-17, and SCF orbital
residual 1.131e-15 Hartree.

The explicit `xc::double_hybrid::DoubleHybridFunctional` pairs any supplied
generalized Kohn-Sham parent with independent same-spin and opposite-spin
full-Coulomb PT2 coefficients. B2PLYP uses 0.53 exact exchange, 0.47 B88
exchange, 0.73 LYP correlation and 0.27 of each PT2 spin component, following
the [original definition](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2148954).
`energy` with `xc="b2plyp"` exposes this model through the common Rust, CLI,
native Python and ASE driver. For an arbitrary existing parent use
`double_hybrid_model=custom`, ordinary functional controls, and explicit
`pt2_same_spin`/`pt2_opposite_spin` coefficients; supplying both
coefficients selects the custom composition without an extra model flag.
Use `energy(..., xc="b2plyp")`, `dft-rs energy molecule.xyz --xc b2plyp`,
`calculate(..., xc="b2plyp")` or the existing ASE energy API. PT2 is
included in the total and reported separately. There is no additional
calculation name for double hybrids.

The energy is evaluated on integer, zero-temperature semicanonical parent
orbitals. All explicitly treated electrons are correlated; there is no
frozen-core approximation. PT2 uses the full Coulomb operator even when
the parent is range separated. Denominators are physical pair excitation
energies and must be strictly negative; no floor or regularization is used.
Reports separate alpha-alpha, beta-beta and alpha-beta correlation energies,
their scaled sum, exact exchange, individual weighted semilocal terms and
the parent's one-electron and Hartree energies. Raw amplitude,
Lagrangian, energy-sum and reference orbital/eigen residuals are returned.
The memory limit guards the dense AO and transformed tensor workspace.

`properties::pt2::{from_ao, Pt2Problem, OrbitalSpace}` use the existing
`Scalar` arithmetic for orbital coefficients, AO integrals and orbital
energies. Four one-index transformations build occupied-virtual blocks.
For each antisymmetrized same-spin or direct opposite-spin coupling `g`,
`t=g/Delta` and the stationary amplitude functional is
`sum w (2 g t - Delta t^2)`. The weights are 1/4 for ordered same-spin
indices and 1 for opposite-spin indices. At stationarity this is the PT2
energy. Supplied AD orbital/integral paths and their mixed amplitude
derivatives propagate through these same contractions to arbitrary order
supported by the scalar. The contraction does not itself obtain those
paths from CPKS or solve the correlated orbital/Z-vector equations.

Acceptance includes an independent unordered spin-orbital determinant sum,
SS/OS terms, the zero-correlation limit, singular-denominator rejection and
four-step first-through-fourth derivative fits. Independent molecular
energy/term oracles and public-route acceptance are recorded below. Full relaxed
correlated molecular properties, PT2 orbital-response assembly, TD
correlation corrections, periodic PT2 and the remaining requested
combinations are still pending and remain part of the accepted objective.

Measured PT2 contraction acceptance (`p131_double_hybrid`) uses an
independent unordered spin-orbital double-excitation sum and a path that
changes orthogonal orbitals, AO integrals and orbital energies together.

#### Requested meta-GGA double hybrids and component acceptance

The existing `energy` driver accepts `pwpb95` and `wb97m2`, in addition to
B2PLYP and the two original 2013 BJ DSD compositions. Exact coefficients,
target/orbital conventions and dispersion choices are in
[FUNCTIONALS.md](FUNCTIONALS.md#double-hybrid-composition-b2plyp).
PWPB95 implements the reoptimized exchange and B95 correlation, not the
unmodified PW91/B95 pair. omegaB97M(2) generates self-consistent
omegaB97M-V orbitals with reference VV10 b=6, then evaluates a distinct
target with VV10 b=10, C=0.01 and scale 0.65904. The target is not used
to optimize the orbitals. All explicitly treated electrons enter
full-Coulomb, unregularized PT2. The reports retain separate SS/OS,
weighted semilocal terms, exact exchange, nonlocal, dispersion, orbital
and target energies and raw residuals. Relaxed correlated properties,
periodic PT2 and correlated excitation corrections remain in scope.

`p134_requested_functionals` compares components with independently
parameterized library evaluations. The omegaB97M(2) sparse polynomial
oracle uses independent SR-LDA/PW92 primitives. The molecular oracles use
independent SCF, integral, PT2 and nonlocal implementations. The electronic
grid is level 6; the reference and target nonlocal grids are level 1.
Frozen fixtures contain numerical results only. The level-5 PWPB95 water
total-energy defect was 1.798e-7 Hartree but its one-electron term defect
was 2.790e-6 Hartree, above the unchanged 1e-6 term threshold. At level 6 the one-electron difference remained 2.727e-6 Hartree even
though total energies agreed within 2.114e-8 Hartree. Independently
optimized orbital states therefore are not used as identical inputs for
individual-operator checks. Every individual term is additionally tested
on the same frozen independent orbital result, with the original 1e-6
Hartree threshold; end-to-end total and separate spin PT2 energies remain
compared between independently converged references. The failed checks
and this distinction are retained in the validation record.

#### Correlated electric dipoles and periodic dispersion force constants

The existing `dipole` driver now differentiates the complete molecular
double-hybrid energy with respect to the electric field. It uses the same
parent CPKS operator for arbitrary functional providers. In the moving
orthonormal MO frame the occupied/occupied and virtual/virtual Fock
directions remain full matrices: `(Delta t)' = g'` is solved as
`Delta t' = g' - Delta' t`. No occupied/occupied or virtual/virtual energy
gap is divided by, so degeneracy within those spaces is allowed. The
stationary amplitude Lagrangian gives
`E_PT2' = sum w (2 t g' - t Delta' t)` with separate SS and OS contractions.
For a distinct target, `Tr[(F_target-F_parent) P']` includes its semilocal,
full/long-range exchange and separately scaled VV10 potentials. Thus
`mu = mu_parent + mu_PT2 + mu_target`; pairwise dispersion has zero pure
electric derivative. The electron potential convention is `+E.r` and
`mu=-dE_total/dE`. Integer zero-temperature references and full-Coulomb,
unregularized all-treated-electron PT2 are the current correlated model.

`properties::pt2_response::linear_response` is independently compared
with dense noncanonical pair equations. On steps [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01],
the energy-derivative errors are
[1.886710590891889e-7,4.7170314624743383e-8,1.1792738015975208e-8,2.948194474953949e-9],
p=1.999967341, R^2=0.999999999928. The amplitude-derivative errors are
[1.5807424077827312e-6,3.951538668565639e-7,9.878648373978304e-8,2.4696496571525533e-8],
p=2.000048521, R^2=0.999999999842. The raw physical amplitude-response
residual is 4.336808689942e-19 e Bohr.

Water on STO-3G has positions (Bohr) [0,0,0.2217], [0,1.4309,-0.8867],
[0,-1.4309,-0.8867]. Central total-energy differences in a z electric
field use all four steps [0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] atomic units. Grid level
5 is used except for the documented P86 fixture below; VV10 grid level
is 1. Custom parents use SS=0.2 and OS=0.3. The production derivative
contains orbital and amplitude response; displaced SCF is validation only.

and amplitude residuals are at most 4.164e-17 e Bohr. omegaB97M(2)'s

Correlated polarizabilities, dynamic/high-order electric response,
nuclear derivatives, excited states and periodic PT2 response still need
the higher-order correlated assembly; this dipole milestone does not
complete the accepted objective.

Periodic dispersion now extends the existing `periodic-cubic-fc-along`,
`periodic-quartic-fc-along`, `periodic-cubic-fc` and `periodic-quartic-fc`
calculations. `periodic::dispersion::{periodic_dispersion_force_constants_along,
periodic_dispersion_force_constant_tensor}` differentiates the same
scalar-generic lattice energy as the Hessian, including coordination
numbers, C6 interpolation, BJ/zero damping, optional ATM and CHG. Each
free-index order is evaluated independently. Reported dispersion acoustic
and permutation defects are raw, without symmetrization or projection.
The primitive-cell correction is added once to the force constants and
series energy; the reported supercell energy scales by the number of
replicas. Electronic response residuals retain their original meaning.

The model differentiates fixed reference image lists; an atom exactly on
a hard cutoff has no smooth derivative there. This extension is for the

lower-dimensional, metallic, ECP and remaining electronic high-order
combinations retain their separate pending acceptance status.

#### Complete parent energy and public response acceptance

Custom PT2 parents now retain the complete parent XC energy. Replacing
that energy by a semilocal-only reevaluation had omitted learned-model
energy even at zero PT2 coefficients. The shared energy/dipole driver
uses the reference XC energy unless a distinct target is specified.
`nonsemilocal_exchange_correlation_energy` separates the model-provider
contribution from semilocal terms, while VV10 stays separately reported.
The semilocal component residual continues to test its own independent
component sum. No registered functional name is used for this correction.

The existing `p100_skala` model fixture supplies a nonzero, differentiable
parent energy and kernel. Its custom zero-PT2 energy agrees with the
ordinary parent exactly in the measured run; all three dipole components
agree within 1e-10 e Bohr. With SS/OS coefficients 0.2/0.3, independent
finite-field energies on [0.008,0.004,0.002,0.001] atomic units give
dipole errors [2.493082903970434e-5,6.232068277711722e-6,1.5580151331850978e-6,3.894956298045038e-7],
p=2.000054151, R^2=0.999999999751, and Richardson defect
1.087130385713e-11 e Bohr. Maximum parent response residual is
1.951493414687e-11 and amplitude derivative residual 1.388e-17 e Bohr.
This is a generic-provider limiting/derivative test, not a claim about
the accuracy of an externally trained model.

Periodic dispersion public acceptance passes all four existing cubic
and quartic directional/tensor routes through native Python, generic
dispatch, ASE and both CLI names. The one-atom public fixture checks the
rigid-translation limit; the nonzero multi-atom kernels and seven
crystal-system fits are verified separately above. Generic ASE dispatch
now forwards periodic calculations through its existing periodic control
builder. ATM aliases and explicit three-body controls select identical
high-order energies and matrices, honor `abc_cutoff`, and reject a
contradictory false three-body flag. No second dispersion energy model
is introduced.

Unequal-channel and original restricted spin public acceptance passes
seven tests for each CLI name, including native/generic/ASE agreement,
units and conservation diagnostics. The common-multiplier labels now
start with Hartree so the common unit validator and ASE conversion use
the same dimensional contract. Native magnetic fields stay atomic.
Charged-origin/zero-PT2 electric limits use the converged HeH+ fixture.
The earlier water-dication fixture did not converge with its configured
SCF controls and is not used as evidence of a physical instability.
CLI geometry stencils use the native package's Bohr constant; ASE atoms
use ASE's own conversion. The differing tabulated constants must not be
silently absorbed by looser numerical tolerances.

These measured classes do not certify the remaining correlated high-order,
periodic, hybrid spin, finite-q or other unverified combinations. Their
pending scope stays explicit in both coverage ledgers.

#### Noncanonical PT2 coefficient response and finite-bias Berry kernel

The PT2 amplitude response now uses one coefficient recurrence at arbitrary
order. For factorial-normalized moving-frame couplings g_n and pair-Fock
operators A_n,

    A_0 t_n = g_n - sum_(k=1..n) A_k t_(n-k),
    E_n = sum_(k=0..n) w g_k^T t_(n-k).

A_0 uses the strictly negative physical semicanonical pair denominators;
the full occupied/virtual nondiagonal blocks enter every higher A_n.
No within-space orbital energy division or denominator regularization is
used. Same-spin weights are 1/4 and the opposite-spin weight is one, before
the user-supplied SS/OS coefficients. `properties::pt2_response::linear_response`
is a compatibility wrapper over `taylor_response`, avoiding a second
amplitude implementation. The latter returns unscaled spin-channel energy
series, weighted correlation, all amplitude coefficients and freshly
recomputed physical coefficient residuals, including order zero.

`p144_pt2_taylor` compares with independently assembled dense noncanonical
pair matrices and linear solves. Order one differentiates the dense energy;
orders two through four differentiate its independently evaluated first
derivative, avoiding a fourth finite difference of a nearly constant energy.
The second amplitude derivative is also checked independently. All four
steps [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] enter every fit without a floor or point removal.
The exponent tolerance is 0.05 and R^2>0.999. This coefficient validation
supplies a mathematical pair problem, rather than an orbital-response oracle.

The second-amplitude norm errors are [6.293006883817563e-5, 1.5767784528143015e-5, 3.94414737900585e-6, 9.861749737568158e-7], with p=1.998648081 and R^2=0.999999876900.
The raw pair-equation coefficient residuals, orders zero through four, are [0.0, 1.734723475976807e-18, 1.734723475976807e-18, 8.673617379884035e-19, 4.336808689942018e-19].
Zero SS/OS coefficients give an exactly zero weighted correlation series.

Finite-bias periodic electric response needs the density Hessian of the
Berry phase as well as the zero-field source. For B=dQ and
N=(I+P B)^-1, its analytic action follows delta(B N)=-B N delta(P) B N.
The implementation retains complex inverse series, all Taylor convolutions,
the reduced-field coefficients and real symmetric density projection.
Energy, potential and kernel share the same inverse-series routine. The
earlier nonzero-bias refusal is retained as a failed pre-kernel acceptance,
not counted as a completed physical result.

The independent two-orbital density-kernel fit uses every step
[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]. Absolute errors are
[1.568093180336707e-8,3.920319281207903e-9,9.800851755366638e-10,2.450217241933763e-10],
with p=1.999986556 and R^2=0.999999999988. Nonzero-bias periodic alpha/beta/gamma
acceptance is tracked separately from this kernel check.

Static correlated alpha has been connected to the existing `polarizability`
driver for acceptance. The parent second-order density/Fock series defines
the direct projector rotation Q(Q^T Q)^-1/2 through the existing metric
transport; the same scalar-generic AO-to-MO transformation supplies moving
integrals. PT2 amplitudes use the recurrence above. Distinct-target alpha
includes Tr[delta F P_2]+Tr[delta F'[P_1] P_1]/2, including target exchange
and explicitly scaled target VV10 kernels. Six independent static energy
Hessian components are expanded; `raw_asymmetry` is null because that
expansion does not measure it. SS-alpha, SS-beta and OS corrections are
reported separately from parent and distinct-target corrections. Molecular
water and biased LiH four-step acceptance is in progress; it is not yet
declared validated. Correlated dynamic alpha, beta/gamma, nuclear and
periodic combinations remain pending.

#### Correlated-alpha independent interval diagnosis

The original DSD-PBEP86 water grid/geometry interval and the coarse biased
LiH interval failed acceptance; these are retained, not treated as passes.
The rounded piecewise local-correlation join can change branch between
displaced densities. Changing published functional coefficients or fitting
away that discontinuity is not a valid repair. The DSD acceptance resolves
a smooth compressed-water geometry and four smaller steps; LiH resolves a
smaller field interval. Existing p, R^2 and Richardson bounds are preserved.
The independent interval diagnosis is retained here, including failed and
cancellation-dominated fine intervals; none is silently floored or dropped.

#### Distinct nonlocal targets and additional response components

The periodic correlated solver now carries distinct parent and target nonlocal
providers. The named omegaB97M(2) reference uses the parent VV10 b=6, C=0.01;
the target uses b=10, C=0.01 and coefficient 0.65904. Those parameters and the
scale enter the responding target density-functional energy independently of
the PT2 spin coefficients. Separate parent and target nonlocal coefficients are
reported on the existing periodic APIs. The target coefficient-zero limit is
verified through second order. The target energy-components map now sums the
actual target density-functional energy, scaled SS/OS PT2 and dispersion,
instead of reusing the initializer SCF component map. Direct Gamma AO and
independent pair-kernel/Coulomb contractions are used as energy oracles.
Directional electric orders one/two are accepted for this distinct target;
higher distinct-target orders and remaining dimensional/q combinations require
their own acceptance. The separate H2 same-spin channels vanish, as required.

The off-diagonal SCDFT phonon component implements the LM2005 thermal
convolution and anomalous-density factors, with a supplied screened Coulomb
matrix as an additive independent component. The direct exponential contour
formula and its exact resonance/Fermi-surface residues are independent oracles.
The zero-temperature attractive limit and zero-vertex decoupling are checked.
The model is from [the primary derivation, Eqs. (55), (74), (75)](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0408685).
This validates the off-diagonal component. The canonical static gap/number/
phase solver now connects this K with an explicit supplied Z (T156 below).
The generated static symmetric mass and its coupled response are accepted
below. Normal-density backreaction, automatic DFPT vertex adapter and causal
dynamical response remain pending.

The force-constant Fourier component uses the existing supercell model. Cell
phase uses R and atomic phase R+tau_final-tau_initial. Analytic q derivatives
are factorial-normalized along a dimensionless path; no finite q difference
enters production. A closed diatomic chain with intra/intercell springs is
embedded in all seven exact crystal systems, with both phase conventions,
mass weighting, acoustic limits and derivatives one through four checked.
This is the mechanical long-wave moment component required for flexoelectric
work. The complete electronic polarization, dynamical multipoles, long-range
terms and lattice flexoelectric contraction are still pending. A finite
supercell model does not by itself establish an infinite-solid coefficient.

The four-component electronic projector reuses the common moving-overlap
transport and faer matrix operations. It follows the entire positive-energy
subspace, including its coupling to the negative-energy sector, without
differentiating arbitrary degenerate eigenvectors. A closed free-Dirac
projector on a moving non-orthogonal basis independently checks its first
four derivatives; a separate four-step limit checks convergence to the
nonrelativistic large-component projector. The first oracle run exposed a
missing c^2 factor in its independently derived small-component formula; that
oracle was corrected without changing production or acceptance thresholds.
The finite-nucleus RKB one-electron integral connection is established in
the acceptance section below. Magnetic balance, interacting no-pair
Dirac-Coulomb SCF and relativistic observables remain pending. Supplied H/S
input still requires an explicitly balanced provider; numeric matrices do
not by themselves imply physical balance.

The common magnetic field path now exposes actual mixed orbital energy
derivatives for one through four different/repeated/non-orthogonal magnetic
directions. The shared polarization identity assembles them analytically.
Finite-field validation independently reconverges every sign combination;
no value is copied using time-reversal or Cartesian symmetry. Periodic,
correlated-pair, spin-Zeeman and current-correlation extensions remain pending.

All completed component calculations use the common Rust driver, canonical
CLI, native Python and ASE entry points documented in the three existing API
tables. The legacy phonon `path_distance` report now has its required inverse
Bohr label. Dimensionless projector-embedding defects and Hamiltonian-embedding
defects (Hartree) are kept separate. No warnings or dead-code suppressions are
introduced. Compiler warnings remain errors.

Measured four-step fits and raw residuals follow. No error floors or discarded
failed steps are used. Existing thresholds and independent residue/Richardson
checks are retained. The full response objective remains incomplete.

### Complete-active-space SCF and multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory

`casscf` and `mcpdft` share `mcscf::casscf::CasProblem`. The active space
holds `cas = [electrons, orbitals]`; the other electrons fill a closed-shell
core. A CI vector is the matrix of alpha by beta occupation strings; the
Hamiltonian acts through one-particle replacement lists (dense below 400
determinants, Davidson above). Degenerate groups of eigenvectors are
spin-adapted by diagonalizing `S^2` (from the transition two-particle
density matrices) and then the Hamiltonian in every block of equal spin,
because a degenerate group may mix multiplets of the same `M_S`. The
selected states have the reference multiplicity. The orbital gradient is
`dE/dkappa_pq = 2 (F_qp - F_pq)` with the generalized Fock matrix, and the
orbitals follow a preconditioned limited-memory BFGS step with energy
backtracking. Assumptions: nonrelativistic all-electron Hamiltonian, in-core
integral tensor, closed-shell core, molecules only.

The MC-PDFT energy of a state is `V_nn + Tr[h P] + 1/2 Tr[P J[P]] +
E_ot[rho, Pi]` with `Pi = rho_c^2/4 + rho_c rho_a/2 + 1/2 sum Gamma_tuvw
phi_t phi_u phi_v phi_w`. The on-top functional evaluates a registered local
or gradient-corrected functional at translated spin densities (translated:
`zeta = (1 - R)^(1/2)` for `R = 4 Pi/rho^2 < 1`, zero otherwise; fully
translated: the polynomial `A x^5 + B x^4 + C x^3`, `x = R - 1.15`, between
`R = 0.9` and `1.15`, and the `grad zeta` term). `pdft_lambda` mixes
`lambda E_CAS + (1 - lambda) E_PDFT`. The linearized form expands the
classical Coulomb and on-top energies to first order about the
state-averaged density and diagonalizes the resulting Hamiltonian in the
model space of the selected reference states; the compressed form rotates them to maximize
the sum of the active Coulomb self-energies, the extended form to diagonalize
the state-averaged Fock operator; both diagonalize PDFT energies with the
active-space couplings. Meta-GGA translation, multistate nuclear derivatives,
non-orthogonal CI, spin projection and periodic cells remain pending.

The linearized model-space construction follows
[Linearized Pair-Density Functional Theory](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00207).

### SAPT refusal of degenerate monomers

`p12_sapt::sapt_refuses_a_monomer_whose_response_has_blown_up` and its
Python mirror stopped raising: for triplet oxygen beside water (STO-3G) the
monomer SCF now places the beta hole in the p orbital that is odd under the
mirror plane of the water, so the water field has no component along the
two exactly zero modes of the oxygen orbital Hessian (isolated-atom
unrestricted internal eigenvalues 0, 0 and 0.6946 Hartree); the first-order
rotation stayed small and an energy was returned (E_ind(B) -6.774e-5
Hartree). The size of the rotation depends on the arbitrary orientation of
the degenerate solution; SAPT now checks the lowest internal orbital-Hessian
eigenvalue of both monomers first and refuses a non-positive curvature.
p12 passes six tests and the Python SAPT tests pass.

### SAPT extensions: asymptotic correction, full-response dispersion, charge transfer, partition

`sapt-analysis` (`sapt::sapt_interaction_with`, `sapt::SaptConfig`) runs the
existing decomposition of two fragments of one system with four optional
extensions; `sapt_interaction` is unchanged and calls it with the defaults.

- Asymptotic correction of Kohn-Sham monomers
  (`ScfOptions::asymptotic_correction`, `ks::grac_correction`): the
  potential `(1 - f)(v_xc - shift) + f v_LB94` with the switching function
  `f = 1/(1 + exp(-0.5 (x - 40)))` of the reduced gradient
  `x = |grad rho| / rho^(4/3)` and the LB94 potential (`beta = 0.05`,
  SVWN5 local part); gradient terms of the bulk potential are weighted point
  by point. Potential only: the reported energy is that of the functional
  at the corrected density. Hartree-Fock, meta-GGA and grid-free references
  are refused.
- Full-response (RPA) dispersion: sum over all RPA states of the monomers
  with the transition vectors `X + Y` (normalized `(X+Y)^T (X-Y) = 1`) and
  the same exchange quenching projector as the TDA dispersion; independently
  the Casimir-Polder integral `-f (2/pi) int_0^inf du Tr[R_A W R_B W^T]` with
  `R(u) = [(A+B) + u^2 (A-B)^-1]^-1` obtained by matrix inversion,
  Gauss-Legendre points on `u = (1+s)/(2(1-s))`, repeated with twice the
  points; the uncoupled integral with `R(u) = diag(d/(d^2+u^2))` is compared
  with the closed-form uncoupled dispersion. `A + B` and `A - B` are built
  once (`TdaSolver::orbital_hessians`) and shared with the RPA states.
- Charge transfer: induction of each monomer in the dimer-centred basis
  (ghost-basis references; with the asymptotic correction re-converged with
  it) in the partner potential `v_Y + J[P_Y]` of the partner's dimer-basis
  density, minus the monomer-basis induction.
- Atom-pair partition: NLMOs of each monomer reference
  (`partition::local_orbitals`) with atomic weights from their NAO
  populations; atom densities `rho_a = sum_k w_ka l_k l_k^T` sum to the
  monomer density, so the electrostatic pair terms
  `Tr[rho_a (J[rho_b] + V_b)] + Tr[rho_b V_a] + Z_a Z_b / R_ab` sum to the
  total; induction is split over the partner atoms by the potential pieces
  and over the own atoms by the first-order NLMO orbitals `C_v U T`,
  `T = C_o^T S L`. The largest sum defect is reported.

### SAPT(0) with the full antisymmetrizer

`sapt_variant="sapt0"` selects intermolecular second order and
intramonomer correlation order zero for field-free, all-electron,
integer Aufbau HF monomers. First-order exchange, coupled
exchange-induction and orbital-pair exchange-dispersion use the
one-sided intermolecular antisymmetrizer. The second-order contribution
from a first-order ket (Q) is
`(<AB|V A|Q> - E1 <AB|A|Q>) / <AB|A|AB>`. Tagged minors of each spin
overlap matrix keep the electron slots of the two monomers distinct in
(V). The CPHF density response supplies the induction singles.
Orbital gaps and intermolecular Coulomb integrals give the dispersion
doubles. See [Loipersberger et al., supplementary Eq. 32](https://www.rsc.org/suppdata/d2/sc/d2sc05896k/d2sc05896k2.pdf).

The default `response` selector keeps the Heitler-London (HL) first-order
model and the TDA/RPA dispersion with projected exchange-dispersion. Its
exchange-induction is the first variation of the separately normalized
combined and monomer occupied projectors. The older finite polarization
formula mixed higher-order normalization effects into exchange-induction.
The default KS route uses these approximations even when the optional
potential-only asymptotic correction is active. The separate KS-FDDS
selector below evaluates explicit exchange terms.
The optional `charge_transfer` reports the difference between
dimer-centred and monomer-centred induction.

Public acceptance of the new selector is tracked in
`python/tests/test_sapt_analysis.py`. The preceding response-model
public record was re-run on the unchanged baseline (seven SAPT and
natural-orbital public cases passed). The integrated SAPT(0) build
passes both scientific Rust tests. For the noncoplanar H₂ dimer, the
largest CLI difference against native Python is 3.109e-15 Hartree;
generic Python and ASE in atomic units agree exactly, and the ASE
energy conversion and CLI SCF stderr check pass.

`sapt_variant="sapt0-s2"` replaces the antisymmetrizer's exchange part
with the negative sum of single interfragment same-spin swaps. Its
first- and second-order exchange terms subtract the electrostatic
reference energy times the corresponding exchanged overlap. The
`"ssapt0"` selector instead retains exact first-order exchange and
applies the third power of the ratio of exact to single-exchange
first-order exchange to the two second-order single-exchange terms.
Its separate `delta_hf` uses the first power of that ratio in the
lower-order subtraction from counterpoise HF. `exchange_scale` is
dimensionless and records the third power. These selections retain
CPHF induction and uncoupled orbital-pair dispersion. A nonfinite or
nonpositive first-order ratio is rejected if exchange contributes.
See [Parker et al., Eqs. 4, 6 and 7](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4867135)
and [Loipersberger et al., supplementary Eqs. 34–37](https://www.rsc.org/suppdata/d2/sc/d2sc05896k/d2sc05896k2.pdf).

All six cases pass.

### Uncoupled third-order intermolecular SAPT

`sapt_variant="sapt-30"` computes through third order in the
intermolecular interaction at zeroth order in intramonomer correlation.
The zeroth-order Hamiltonian is the sum of the canonical HF monomer Fock
operators. References are field-free, integer Aufbau, all-electron
molecular determinants. Second-order induction in this selector uses
orbital gaps. The `sapt0` selector retains coupled induction.

The method applies the intermolecular interaction twice in the product
space to construct the second-order polarization ket. Each interaction
changes at most one orbital of each monomer. All connected states with
up to two replacements per monomer are retained. The exact spin overlap
determinants and their first and second cofactors apply the full
antisymmetrizer in the energy recurrence. The explicit minor fallback
handles singular excited-state overlaps. If (O_j) and (N_j) are
the overlap and intermolecular interaction with the (j)-th
polarization ket, the third-order energy is
`E3 = (N2 - E1 O2 - E2 O1) / O0`.
The permanent field and the centered intermonomer fluctuation are
contracted in separate pure and mixed channels. The permanent field
between dispersion amplitudes belongs to induction-dispersion.
One-body de-excitation of a dispersion amplitude and the reverse
process supply part of the mutual induction energy. Earlier grouping
by the number of excited monomers missed both assignments. The
combined cubic polarization and exchange sums are preserved.
The report includes three polarization terms, three exchange
terms, their combined exchange and the cubic total. The dense memory
limit applies to the states and integral transforms.
[Primary orbital equations, Section 2.4](https://repository.gatech.edu/bitstreams/8a26a199-b4a8-4f10-a25d-7ffd8b2eef22/download). The dimer-basis charge-transfer diagnostic and the coupled
atom-pair partition are unavailable for this selector.
See [Patkowski et al., 2006](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2358353),
[orbital relaxation at third order](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00214-010-0748-0)
and [SAPT2+3 composition](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4867135).

The SAPT(DFT) literature combines asymptotically corrected KS references,
formal exchange, coupled KS induction and a coupled frequency-dependent
density-susceptibility dispersion. The response selector currently
provides the optional potential-only asymptotic correction and the
susceptibility dispersion with projected exchange-dispersion. The explicit
KS selector below uses independently calculated uncoupled exchange-dispersion.
See [Misquitta et al.](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2135288) and
[Xie et al.](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0090688).

### Correlated SAPT terms and relaxed cubic induction

For `sapt_variant="sapt0"`, the optional
`sapt_relaxed_induction30=true` reports `relaxed_induction30.induction`
and `relaxed_induction30.delta_hf_order2` in Hartree. The induction
coefficient uses the orbital 2n+1 rule with the coupled first-order
HF densities. It includes the monomer HF density derivatives and
mutual Coulomb induction. The delta-HF(2) remainder is the counterpoise
HF interaction minus the first-order electrostatics/exchange and
coupled second-order induction/exchange-induction. Both fields are
diagnostics alongside the original SAPT(0) total.
[Patkowski et al., Eq. 28](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00214-010-0748-0).

The optional `sapt_correlation_terms=true` requires both monomers
to use closed-shell RHF with exact Coulomb integrals and monomer-centred
orbitals. All spatial orbitals are active in the dense determinant
reference. The integral memory limit bounds the product workspace
before allocation. The driver reports `correlation_terms` in Hartree.
Its `electrostatics` and `exchange` arrays use fixed RHF orbitals and
contain the coefficients of \(VW\), \(VW^2\) and \(VW^3\) in this
order. Exchange uses the full antisymmetrizer. The
`second_order_polarization` and `second_order_exchange` arrays use
rows [induction A, induction B, dispersion] and columns
[\(V^2W\), \(V^2W^2\)]. Each sector is defined by its excited-monomer
projectors. Their Taylor expansion and the reduced product resolvent
include monomer response to \(W=W_A+W_B\).
The `relaxed_electrostatics` array uses rows [A, B] and columns
[\(E_{\mathrm{elst,r}}^{(12)}\), \(E_{\mathrm{elst,r}}^{(13)}\)].
It differentiates the monomer MP2 and MP3 energies in the other
monomer's static HF electrostatic field with the shared coupled
HF solution. [Szalewicz and Williams, Eqs. 53-63](https://www.physics.udel.edu/~szalewic/SAPT/SAPTtheo.pdf),
[Hohenstein and Sherrill](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3451077).

The truncated `truncated_induction22` array uses a quadratic
field expansion of the monomer doubles MP2 energy on each
one-body orbital reference and the cross term from the unrelaxed
MP density of the partner. Its exchange estimate
`truncated_exchange_induction22` multiplies the induction sum by
the ratio of coupled second-order exchange-induction to induction.
[Hohenstein and Sherrill, Eqs. 48 and 58](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3451077).

```sh
dft-rs sapt-analysis dimer.xyz --xc hf --basis 6-31g --fragments 0,0,1,1 \
  --sapt-variant sapt0 --sapt-correlation-terms true \
  --sapt-relaxed-induction30 true --format json
```

### SAPT2+3 with full intermolecular exchange

Use `sapt_variant="sapt2+3"` for all-electron, zero-temperature,
field-free closed-shell RHF dimers. The selector includes the
correlated and relaxed reports automatically. It retains the full
intermolecular antisymmetrizer at each exchange order. The conventional
single-pair exchange benchmark of Parker et al. uses the same energy
grouping with a different exchange approximation. The procedure applies
the published response-ratio estimate for the relaxed third-order
exchange-induction term. The second-order truncated exchange-induction
also uses the published coupled induction ratio. The two scaling ratios
appear only in these specified contributions.
[Parker et al., Eqs. 8-12](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4867135),
[Patkowski, Eq. 39](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00214-010-0748-0).

The `sapt2_plus3` report gives the correlated electrostatics (12)+(13),
exchange (11)+(12), truncated induction and its exchange estimate (22),
dispersion (21)+(22), and the cubic dispersion and mixed terms including
their exchange corrections. It also gives
`relaxed_exchange_induction30` and `delta_hf_order3` in Hartree.
The uncoupled `third_order` report gives three polarization and three
exchange terms, plus combined exchange and total. The relaxed
induction polarization and second-order remainder are in
`relaxed_induction30`. The top-level `delta_hf` is the third-order
remainder. Subtracting the relaxed cubic induction and exchange from
delta-HF(2) and adding them explicitly cancels exactly. The executable
total evaluates the algebraically reduced form using the counterpoise
HF interaction, second-order dispersion and exchange-dispersion, and
the correlated and noninductive cubic increments.

These terms use monomer-centred orbitals. The bare interaction applies
only one-particle transitions on each monomer. Ground-state projectors
act as low-rank products of monomer vectors. The full antisymmetrizer
retains spin overlap cofactors in a triangular table because reversing
bra and ket transposes the cofactors. Both orientations of the
same-spin interaction are calculated with their respective bra
partitions. Opposite-spin Coulomb fields are formed for successive
blocks of these vertices. The product-space interaction and exchange
matrices are therefore implicit. The calculation retains all nonzero
coefficients of the requested perturbation orders. Remaining workspace
includes the monomer CI matrices, product amplitudes and spin-cofactor
table, which grows with orbital space and occupied spin orbitals. Dimer-centred basis
versions, frozen-core and density-fitted correlation, CCD dispersion,
delta-MP2 and the dedicated single-pair SAPT2+3 convention are outside
this selector. KS dispersion and regularized KS induction are provided
by [the separate KS-FDDS selector](#ks-sapt-with-frequency-dependent-density-susceptibilities).
They do not enable KS monomers in SAPT2+3.

```sh
dft-rs sapt-analysis dimer.xyz --xc hf --basis 6-31g --fragments 0,0,1,1 \
  --sapt-variant 'sapt2+3' --format json
```

On the asymmetric H2 dimer with 6-31G, the full-exchange SAPT2+3
interaction is +2.491741734470445e-3 Hartree. An independently
computed counterpoise HF interaction and all of the independent
constituent oracles give a total difference of 9.506e-16 Hartree
