The radial-only and angular-only controls separate resolution effects.
The global level-6 grid reduces the rotational energy defect substantially,
whereas refining only the quantum host does not. Hessian values remain
more quadrature-sensitive than total energies. The dense orbital Hessian is
positive at all six references, with minimum eigenvalue about 0.0714 and
condition estimate about 215. This is an algebraic/stability diagnostic,
not an independent Cartesian derivative proof.

Three representative entries, H[3,3], H[0,3] and the previously passing
remote-H control H[9,9], are tested by both gradient and energy differences.
The one common primary interval is [0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] Bohr. Primary
counts are global_l4: 2/6; quantum_local_l6: 2/6. A smaller predefined interval is retained only as a
diagnostic and cannot rescue the primary verdict. These subsets do not
certify the fourteen unresolved independent entries or the full tensor.

Fixed-geometry field controls separate orbital response from moving-grid
geometry derivatives. With the common primary field steps
[0.008,0.004,0.002,0.001] atomic units, baseline alpha fits pass 3/9;
fine-grid counts are global_l4: 4/9; quantum_local_l6: 5/9. The new diagnostic requires
abs(p-2)<0.025, R2>0.9999 and the retained Richardson bound. It is distinct
from the historical 9/9 component-resolved field acceptance above, which
uses smaller individual intervals and its own original gates. Neither
measurement is silently relabelled as the other.

An independent analytic oracle differentiates EPC17 directly in signed
quantum-wave amplitude and assembles each seven-by-seven quantum orbital
block without calling the production density kernel. Both baseline and
global-level-4 blocks agree in all 49 entries, with maximum defect
8.493206e-15. This rules out an algebraic error in those tested quantum
blocks to that comparison accuracy; it does not independently prove the
mixed electronic block or nuclear source jets. A separate scalar implicit
minimization control has a positive orbital Hessian and an exact relaxed
Hessian but first-order central-gradient error at a wave node
(p=1.000215). It establishes a possible regularity mechanism, not complete
causal attribution of the molecular failures or a replacement fit gate.
An additional scalar control starts away from the node at wave amplitude
0.003. The original broad steps cross the node and give p=1.776268,
R2=0.968457, although the reference itself is locally analytic. Steps
predefined solely from the node distance (0.4,0.2,0.1,0.05 times that
amplitude) are node-free and give p=2.000004, R2>0.99999999999.
This is not error-based interval selection, and no corresponding node-free
neighbourhood has been established for the unresolved molecular entries.

A further single treatment prototype forms the union of two fixed
level-4 angular orientations with equal weights and 150,000 points. The
second orientation uses the rational rotation fixed before the original
grid study; neither angles nor weights are fitted. Both raw and partitioned
weights are halved, and point ownership is preserved. The rotation is
constant in laboratory coordinates, so point motion remains the owning
atom's translation and existing first/second weight response applies.
This is a new density-independent discrete variational calculation, not an
average of separately minimized energies or an untracked moving frame.
Its common-primary representative result is 2/6.
The complete predefined interval and all failed fits remain available;
this subset does not establish full-tensor acceptance. The prototype is
private and is not registered as a new public grid/API option.

A final fixed-physics diagnostic covers all fourteen unresolved
independent entries on the original grid. It reproduces 209 physical states;
the largest energy difference from the retained same-input cache is
0.000000e+00 Hartree. These repeated inputs are
needed because the former energy-only cache did not retain the orbitals
required for this diagnostic. The new trace retains electronic densities,
overlaps, quantum coefficients and fresh quantum Fock matrices for reuse.

For each moving quadrature point, n_e is the electronic density, psi the
phase-aligned quantum orbital amplitude, w the full quadrature weight, and
a,b,c the original EPC17 coefficients. Define u=sqrt(n_e)*psi and a fixed
sign s from the reference quantum wave. The exact nodal contribution
is

```text
delta = -w*b*u^2*(abs(u)-s*u)
        / [(a-b*abs(u)+c*u^2)*(a-b*s*u+c*u^2)].
```

It is the actual EPC contribution minus its reference-sign analytic branch.
It vanishes in a neighbourhood of a nonzero reference wave. On the crossed
side its numerator is -2*w*b*abs(u)^3 and its denominator is the strictly
positive even polynomial (a+c*u^2)^2-b^2*u^2. Direct one-sided derivatives
therefore match zero through order two at a node. A production-provider
scalar identity preflight passes, including four-step cubic scaling. This
is postprocessing only: no alternative provider or modified energy is used
by SCF, optimization or a public calculation. The original physical
Hamiltonian, residual gates and finite-difference intervals are unchanged.

Independent reconstruction checks every saved crossing-point contribution,
state number and cached quantum Fock residual. On the single predefined
primary interval, physical energy witnesses pass
0/14; subtracting this known zero-second-jet
term for a separate auxiliary verification passes
11/14. Both sets of raw
errors, orders, R2 values and Richardson defects are retained. An auxiliary
equal-second-jet witness is not a new physical energy curve and does not
silently turn a failed original physical interval into a pass. The split
quantifies the finite-grid nodal contribution; any production integration
treatment must integrate that term correctly, not remove it or fit an
energy counterterm.

A separate, predeclared common halving checks every one of these fourteen
entries on [0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025] Bohr. All 209 previous states are reused;
only 52 missing nodal-observable states are calculated, and the reference
is reconstructed from its cache without another SCF. No component-specific
window is selected and no further interval search is performed. Physical
energy witnesses pass 0/14, and the
auxiliary equal-second-jet witnesses pass
13/14 on this one common
interval. The coarse 11/14 auxiliary outcome remains separately recorded;
fine results are not substituted into that outcome. The physical finite-step
failures remain, even when an independent equal-second-jet reference agrees
with the analytic Hessian. This separates correctness of the reference jet
from a uniform quadratic error claim for physical energy differences that
cross finite-grid orbital nodes.

The remaining fine-interval auxiliary failure is H[4,5]. Its four existing
smallest-step inputs are checked from the exact cached initial state and
from the same fixed full-space orbital rotation used in the earlier branch
control. Eight additional coupled solves retain the same Hamiltonian,
grid and tolerances; no new geometry or step is introduced. The maximum
warm/rotated density difference is 7.738254e-14, while the maximum observed
energy spread is 1.207923e-13 Hartree.
All 81 combinations of the three retained energy evaluations per corner
are reported as a repeatability diagnostic, never selected as replacement
data. They span 9.663381e-09 Hartree/Bohr^2 in the last mixed curvature
and p=1.951439..2.042908;
32/81 would satisfy the fit gates.
This is an observed numerical-repeatability envelope, not a rigorous
absolute error bound. The original fine result stays 13/14, and no passing
combination is adopted. The last gate is therefore not robustly certifiable
from the current double-precision physical-energy differences.

Merely tightening SCF iteration thresholds or choosing a favourable seed
is not an established remedy. This precision limitation is separate from
unresolved continuum quadrature convergence and finite-grid nodal regularity.

An independent scalar-arithmetic control reuses the sixteen cached states
at exactly those four H[4,5] mixed-energy steps. A small canonical-library
export obtains the electronic/proton one-body matrices, electronic and
electron-proton Coulomb integrals, and grid AO values. An independent
80-digit contraction reconstructs kinetic, physical classical attraction,
Hartree, exact exchange, electron-proton attraction, classical-field and
EPC terms. No SCF is repeated. The Gaussian integrals, core-matrix assembly,
AO evaluation and grid remain binary64: this is not an arbitrary-precision
integral implementation or a different physical functional.

With the original cached density, the equal-second-jet auxiliary H[4,5]
fit now passes: p=2.00323040, R2=0.9999481707, Richardson defect
1.320947e-09 Hartree/Bohr^2. A separately declared
constrained-density shadow applies one fixed McWeeny purification per spin
and normalizes the proton coefficient in its overlap metric; it also passes
(p=2.01389420, R2=0.9999888030). Both outcomes are retained, with no
selection between seeds, intervals or normalization variants. The original

##### Node-resolving physical EPC integration prototype

The fixed-grid regularity problem has a concrete numerical treatment candidate:
resolve the wave node in the integration domain rather than remove its EPC
energy. For signed amplitude `u`, EPC17 has the local expansion
`g(u) = -u^2/a - b*abs(u)^3/a^2 + O(u^4)`. At an exactly sampled simple node
`u(t)=v*t`, central energy differentiation contains a leading
`-2*b*abs(v)^3*abs(h)/a^2` error and central gradient differentiation contains
`-3*b*abs(v)^3*abs(h)/a^2`. A universal quadratic finite-step error law is
therefore not valid for every discrete nodal reference, even when its
analytic second derivative exists. This does not establish an exact active
node at the molecular reference or certify its unresolved entries.

A complete-energy one-dimensional EPC17 integral control splits its domain
at the moving wave node. It retains the entire physical integrand and includes
point-motion and Jacobian derivatives through second order. With common steps
`[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]`, both energy-to-Hessian and gradient-to-Hessian fits
pass the unchanged order, R2 and Richardson gates at 32 and 64 Gauss points
per panel. The fixed unsplit 64-point control fails both fits. This is an
integration-treatment control, not a molecular response certificate.

The same idea is tested on actual cached molecular densities at all 32
mixed-energy stencil geometries for H[0,3] and H[4,5], with common steps
`[0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025]` Bohr. The proton-centred spherical integral uses
the exact s+p wave form `A(r)+B(r).n`. Polar panels split at its nodal angle;
radial panels split where `abs(A(r))=norm(B(r))`, so the angular node enters
or leaves a sphere. All EPC17 terms remain present. This is a different
quadrature condition, not an altered functional or an energy counterterm.
The initial two-resolution trial and independent radial/angular controls
remain recorded as failures or partial controls. Angular refinement from
48 to 96 points agrees to the tested resolution, whereas radial refinement
remains limiting until the radial topology panels are introduced.

With 48 polar points per panel and 48 azimuths, radial orders 64 versus 128
per topology panel give a maximum energy difference of
1.225506e-12 Hartree and maximum EPC mixed-curvature
difference of 1.477207e-08 Hartree/Bohr^2 over all
eight stencil comparisons. Orders 96 versus 128 give
3.251566e-14 Hartree and
6.150636e-10 Hartree/Bohr^2. Both comparisons pass
the predefined 1e-9 Hartree and 2e-7 Hartree/Bohr^2 resolution gates.
There are zero new SCF calculations and zero library rebuilds; these
integration trials take 230.42 measured numerical wall seconds,
with separately recorded small links. The first molecular trial's Vec3
fixture compiler failure is retained and repaired without changing physics.

This establishes convergence of the tested frozen-state EPC component
integrals, not new stationary states or a relaxed Hessian. The radius is
restricted to four Bohr; no rigorous continuum tail bound or general
multiple/tangent-node certification is claimed. A production calculation
must use one variational integral treatment for energy, potentials, coupled
response and nuclear derivatives, and solve stationary states again.
The current `moving_grid_taylor` in
`src/response/nuclear/geometry.rs` reconstructs atom-owned Becke weights.
It cannot silently treat this unpartitioned proton-centred volume grid as
the same motion law. A fixed-reference quadrature recipe would need an
explicit fixed-volume/co-moving rule and result/response grid identity;
an adaptively changing orbital-dependent mesh instead requires its full
point, frame, root and Jacobian derivatives. Its larger point set also needs
resource-budgeted or batched response evaluation. No such public capability
has been registered by these private prototypes. The original physical
tensor failures remain, and full NEO Hessian acceptance is still pending.

## Part 7: Periodic response

### Complex Bloch orbital coefficient export

`electronic-structure` accepts the optional Boolean `coefficients` (default
false) through the common Rust driver, `dft-rs` CLI, native Python and ASE.
With the flag, every channel includes `orbitals` and `spin_weight` (2 for
the single restricted channel, 1 for each unrestricted channel). Existing
energies, occupations and populations are unchanged by export.

The split `coefficients_real`/`coefficients_imaginary` arrays have shape
`[k][AO][band]`, spherical AO rows in basis order and ascending band columns.
The Bloch sum is `psi_nk(r)=sum_mu C_mu,n(k) sum_T exp(i k.T) chi_mu(r-T)`.
Phases and rotations inside degenerate subspaces are arbitrary; export does
not impose a time-reversal gauge. `overlap_real/imaginary`,
`fock_real/imaginary` and `density_real/imaginary` are `[k][AO][AO]` matrices.
C, S and the contravariant per-spin density P are dimensionless; F and band
energies are Hartree. Occupations are electrons per band and spin, with
`P=C diag(f) C^dagger` and total density `sum_channel spin_weight*P`.

The existing complex generalized eigensolver reconstructs orbitals of the
actual converged Fock with the SCF overlap cutoff. No additional SCF or
functional-name branch is introduced by export. Per-k `metric_defect` is
the maximum real/imaginary entry defect of `C^dagger S C-I`;
`eigen_residual` is the relative Frobenius norm of `FC-SC epsilon` (absolute
when `FC` is zero); `band_energy_residual` compares reconstructed and
reference energies in Hartree; `density_reconstruction_residual` is the
maximum real/imaginary AO entry defect of `C f C^dagger-P`. These are raw
residuals, without a numerical floor or symmetry copying.

The Rust acceptance `p239_periodic_orbital_export` checks all bands, AO pairs,
k points and reported spins on a triclinic two-hydrogen cell. Restricted HF,
SVWN5, PBE, TPSS and PBE0, plus restricted/unrestricted PBE at 0 and 50000 K,
pass (three tests). Maximum measured metric, eigen-equation and density
entry defects are 8.882e-16, 4.441e-16 and 5.551e-16; electron-count defect
is at most 8.882e-16. Enabling export leaves energy and orbital metadata
identical. No derivative is added, so derivative error fits are not applicable
to this output operation. The Python acceptance adds an independent NumPy
complex Hermitian eigensolve, all band-projector entries and native/ASE/CLI
comparisons. All three tests pass; the maximum reported independent band-projector entry defect is 1.555e-15.

This entry currently uses the 3D collinear finite-k reference. Periodic ROKS,
generalized spinor GKS, 1D/2D orbital export and the double-hybrid correlated
driver connection remain pending. A parent orbital export is not a correlated
density or a PT2 response; no such support is inferred from this test.


### Periodic response and remaining work

The finite-q spectral propagator retains independent rectangular `(k+q,k)`
spaces and does not Hermitianize a density at the same q. It handles finite
temperature degeneracy limits, small Fermi tails in occupied bands, temperature
sources, and a chemical potential correction over the complete mesh. GMRES
solves the screening equation `deltaP = chi0 (V_external + K deltaP)`.
The physical density driver now connects analytic Gaussian plane-wave Hartree
and spin-coupled LDA/GGA/meta-GGA kernels in three dimensions. For incommensurate
q, the Fock operator at k+q is reconstructed from the original density mesh,
including the same quadrature points and weights. Generalized complex orbitals
are obtained from the existing doubled real eigensolver using rank revelation
in the complex overlap metric; exact degeneracy does not require a particular
ordering of real eigenvectors.

Cartesian q, reciprocal waves, and the spherical reciprocal cutoff use inverse
Bohr. The external scalar potential amplitude and frequency use Hartree.
Fourier density response is per cell volume, in bohr^-3/Hartree. The selected
inverse dielectric matrix uses `epsilon^-1 = I + v chi`, with
`v_G=4*pi/|G+q|^2` on the row index and fully screened density response `chi`.
Selecting reported modes retains the entire configured Hartree screening set.
The constant-potential zero mode is omitted; nonzero long-wavelength q modes
remain. AO and reciprocal cutoffs are independent convergence parameters.
The physical response driver uses `Cell::hartree_real_space_cutoff()` for
the Coulomb AO products. The shorter overlap cutoff is retained for the
reference metric; using it for Hartree products loses diffuse intercell
terms. Shell-pair Fourier forms are evaluated directly, with no combined
basis matrices for unrelated shell pairs.

Thermal references use the SCF chemical potentials. Static uniform fixed-number
response conserves each spin population over the whole mesh; the grand-canonical
option keeps the spin chemical potentials fixed. At finite temperature the
reported projector defect includes physical fractional occupations. The separate
occupation consistency defect compares `C^H S P S C` with the reference `diag(f)`.

The uniform static thermal driver combines analytic temperature, per-spin
particle-number, or reservoir sources with the same self-consistent Hartree/XC
screening equation. Number constraints and chemical-potential corrections use
the complete mesh. It reports the final occupation equation defect, number
constraints, chemical-potential shifts, and entropy/internal/free-energy
variations. Its independent temperature-SCF/Richardson gate and route checks
are evaluated separately; the existence of the driver alone is not acceptance.
The current XC functionals have no explicit temperature argument. The model
report declares temperature-independent XC; temperature acts through Fermi
occupations and the entropy term, with density-induced XC relaxation included.

This physical driver currently covers collinear semilocal references. Finite-q
exact exchange, periodic nonlocal correlation, reduced-dimensional electrostatics,
and additional electronic spaces remain in scope. Density and dielectric response
do not establish completion of nuclear Sternheimer, phonon, or electron-phonon
response, which also require metric, basis, and explicit-source derivatives.

Remaining work is recorded in the [response coverage ledger](#response-coverage-ledger). The original scope
includes periodic operators and incommensurate q, basis/grid/Pulay derivatives,
higher excited-state derivatives, magnetic/spin/transport response, additional
electronic spaces and functional classes, all public routes and acceptance
tests, extended regression, and distribution audits.

### Periodic D2 empirical dispersion

The 3D lattice sum uses Grimme's published H–Kr coefficients, radii and
functional-specific `s6`. It reuses the molecular D2 logistic radial function
and the periodic image, strain and Gamma displacement machinery. `cn_cutoff`
is unused by D2 and `three_body=true` is rejected. Gamma displacement tensors
and the lattice energy series retain the reference image list. Converge
`disp_cutoff` (Bohr) separately before interpreting a material calculation.
[D2 definition](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.20495)

The Rust `periodic_d2` test uses an asymmetric 3D ammonia cell and independently
enumerates the 12.37 Bohr image sphere. Explicit Cartesian derivatives of the
published pair expression through third order serve as the lower-order oracles.
The suite covers the energy per cell, twelve forces, six independent strain
entries, 78 Hessian entries, 256 nonzero cubic components and 636 nonzero
quartic components. Every component is compared at four steps. For 108 cubic
and 729 quartic components involving at least three atoms, both the pair model
and the independently displaced oracle are checked for exact structural zeros.
This test isolates D2 without an electronic grid or SCF. The `p76_periodic_dispersion`
suite connects the D2 correction to the PBE/STO-3G H₂ lattice stress and phonons.
Native Python, ASE and the CLI route have a separate helium
PBE/STO-3G fixture. Full electronic reference combinations, partial periodicity,
finite-q D2 and an independent D2 run of the elastic tensors are pending.

With PBE `s6=0.75` and 156 ordered images, the Rust lattice energy and explicit
oracle agree at `-5.429355294316e-4` Hartree per cell. The reference image
margin exceeds 0.14 Bohr. All 988 nonzero components pass on the first
four-step interval. For Cartesian derivatives, the steps are
`[0.008, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001]` Bohr. For strain they are
`[0.002, 0.001, 0.0005, 0.00025]` dimensionless.

| D2 derivative | Fits | Exponent bounds | Minimum R² | Prefactor bounds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

stderr. This comparison uses the staged binary and extension built from the
same release invocation. Installation checks are separate.

The PBE/STO-3G H₂ lattice at a `2 × 1 × 1` electronic mesh gives a D2

and the separate pair lattice sum agree within `3.513e-17` Hartree for the

and `1.302e-17` Hartree for all nine raw affine strain entries. The stress
term sum residual is zero. D3(BJ), D3(zero) and CHG also pass this regression.
In the Gamma phonon calculation, the maximum D2 force constant is
`2.604293832055e-4` Hartree/Bohr² and the maximum residual in the 36-entry
increment is `5.367e-17` Hartree/Bohr². The highest frequency moves from
`5505.0099` to `5503.7697` cm⁻¹ when D2 is included.

### Fixed-density molecular rVV10

`nlc::rvv10_potential` evaluates Sabatini et al.'s direct real-space kernel
and its analytic AO potential on a supplied total AO density and quadrature.
The revised kernel uses independent `1+q R²` endpoints, with the prefactor
`(kappa kappa')^(-3/2)` supplying the damping dimensions. The local counterterm
is unchanged. The parameters for the original rVV10 fit are `b=6.3, C=0.0093`.
The Gaussian quadrature and AO projection are shared with VV10. This checkpoint
has a Rust density-functional primitive. Molecular and periodic SCF, nuclear
derivatives and the common-driver settings remain pending.
[Revised kernel](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.87.041108)

The `rvv10_density` test uses C1 ammonia, PBE/STO-3G and
`grid_weight_cutoff=0` to compare the energy against a separate implementation
of both quadrature terms. It also compares with the original kernel evaluated
at the same parameters and checks the zero-density limit. Four-step fits of
all 36 independent AO potential elements use a smaller molecular grid and
a positive-definite total density formed by a 0.07 diagonal shift. The two
symmetry-related AO density entries are each varied by half of the step for
an off-diagonal component. This is a density derivative in Hartree, distinct
from an atomic displacement derivative in Hartree/Bohr.

On the 43,326-point level-3 grid, the reference converges in nine iterations
to `-55.68016583089` Hartree. The local counterterm is `+0.04504847303057`
Hartree and the pair term `-0.005744997010724` Hartree. The resulting rVV10
contribution `+0.03930347601643` Hartree agrees with the independent oracle
within `1e-11` Hartree. The frozen-density total is `-55.64086235488` Hartree.
At the same `b` and `C`, the original kernel gives `+0.03940530041787`
Hartree. The zero-density energy and potential both vanish exactly.

Thirty-three AO components pass on `[0.016, 0.009, 0.005, 0.003]` with
exponents `1.984640–2.018148`, minimum R² `0.99997194` and prefactors
`3.512e-8–2.751e-5`. For the three remaining components the smaller
`[0.003, 0.002, 0.0013, 0.0008]` interval encounters cancellation. Their
larger-step interval `[0.04, 0.025, 0.016, 0.009]` resolves all three.

### Unequal-channel periodic thermal spin response

The existing static periodic longitudinal susceptibility now accepts
unequal collinear thermal channels through the same density solver.
It solves both the Zeeman and common-reservoir perturbations, then
determines the common chemical-potential derivative from the raw
cell-integrated number constraint. The baseline spin bias
`(mu_alpha-mu_beta)/2` stays fixed. This is a constrained spin-biased
ensemble; it need not be the zero-bias equilibrium response. The raw
spatial sum of spin densities is physically nonzero and is not projected
away. No compressibility floor or separate spin-number constraint is
introduced. [Controls, units and report fields](periodic.md#35-exchange-enhanced-static-spin-susceptibility)
are shared by all public routes.

`p138_periodic_spin_constraint` compares the production response against
an independent finite-field nonlinear SCF using the full Fock evaluator,
fixed total number and fixed baseline bias. The fixture is asymmetric H3
at [0,0,-0.9], [0,0,0.9], [1.7,0.3,0.2] Bohr, cubic side 9.5 Bohr,
multiplicity 2, unrestricted STO-3G, Gamma sampling and 150000 K.
The acceptance quadrature has ten radial points and angular degree 7.
All four fields [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] atomic units enter every log-error
fit; no error floors or removed steps are used. Density errors are the
maximum over all entries of both AO spin-density matrices. Independent
Richardson checks preserve the existing bounds.

An initial reciprocal Hartree cutoff of 8 inverse Bohr failed despite
an equation residual below 9.165e-11. The SVWN5 susceptibility errors
were [0.00030928189251411276,7.742087470308245e-5,1.942560470968857e-5,4.9249104948634326e-6],
p=1.991280626, R^2=0.999995419877 and Richardson defect 9.134575651437e-8.
Its common-multiplier errors were
[9.801918328940055e-7,7.848998563909915e-7,7.351421714720495e-7,7.22647274384574e-7],
p=0.141380278, R^2=0.812261173770 and Richardson defect
7.184823086889e-7. These failed steps are retained here. Increasing
the reciprocal representation to cutoff 16 resolves the discrepancy;
no solver or acceptance threshold is relaxed. On the same reference,
cutoff 12 to 16 changes susceptibility by at most 8.565e-11 and the
common-multiplier response by at most 6.169e-10 across the three models.
A small Krylov residual alone does not certify Fourier-tail convergence.

### Unequal rigid-band spin and thermal response

The bare `pauli-spin-susceptibility` route now accepts two unequal
collinear bands through `collinear_fermi_thermodynamics`, reusing the
existing Fermi-level solver and stable occupations. No second root
solver is added to production. Both channels are reoccupied at fixed
total number and zero reservoir spin bias, on the frozen orbital
reference bands. Each requested temperature changes the reoccupation,
without reconverging the SCF. Thus this bare ensemble differs from the
enhanced branch, which fixes the baseline reference spin bias and
reconverges a thermal reference. Reports distinguish them explicitly.

For z=g/4, the field sources are +z/-z. With D=D_alpha+D_beta,
`mu'_B=z(D_alpha-D_beta)/D`, `D_spin=4 D_alpha D_beta/D` and
`chi=z^2 D_spin`. The raw spin-number derivatives are
`D_alpha(mu'_B-z)` and `D_beta(mu'_B+z)`; their sum is reported without
projection. The inert D=0 limit returns chi=0 and a null common
multiplier. Empty-channel, equal-channel and g-scaling limits pass
closed-form checks without floors. The bare heat capacity and common
temperature derivative use the combined-band L_n moments. Wilson ratio
uses D_spin, while the Sommerfeld DOS estimate uses total D.

`p139_rigid_spin_thermodynamics` independently solves the finite-field
and finite-temperature occupations with scalar bisection and direct
Fermi functions, without production moment/response routines. All
four errors enter each log-log fit. The synthetic bands are
[-0.5,0.1,0.7] and [-0.3,0.35,0.9] Hartree, weight 0.5 per level,
N=1.3, kT=0.2 Hartree and g=2. Physical bands come from the asymmetric
H3 Gamma cell of the preceding spin acceptance, with grid level 1,
grid shell 1 and a 150000 K unrestricted orbital reference. The common
reservoir reoccupation is not constrained to its initial 2/1 spin
populations. Native/CLI/generic/ASE public acceptance covers SVWN5,
PBE, TPSS and PBE0, including unit conversion and g-scaling.

Field steps are in atomic magnetic field; thermal steps are in Hartree
of kT. Errors in chi are atomic moment per field, common mu/B errors
are Hartree per field, heat capacity errors are k_B/cell and common
mu/kT errors are dimensionless.

### Periodic clamped-ion electric gamma acceptance

`periodic-gamma` uses the same Berry-phase enthalpy, transported metric,
Hartree/exchange/semilocal kernels and second-order orbital response as the
existing periodic path implementation. It returns the actual static
four-index tensor Gamma_abcd=d^3 P_a/(dE_b dE_c dE_d)=-E_abcd/Omega, not a
factorial-normalized Taylor coefficient; `chi3=Gamma/6`. The Gaussian
susceptibility convention has units e^2 Bohr^2/Hartree^2. Static intrinsic
permutation symmetry permits 15 independent components; the default expands
those values into the full 81-entry row-major tensor. `use_symmetry=false`
evaluates all 81 index orders. Its raw permutation defect is measured from
those results; the default reports null/None for this unmeasured diagnostic,
using Rust Option<f64>, not a null pointer. Actual Krylov residuals and
series-reference residual/energy differences remain in both report modes.
No such static symmetry is imposed on dynamic response.

Fixed-geometry field paths reuse spatial integrals and Berry matrices.
Their absent nuclear/strain coefficients are exact zeros. The response
recursion and field coupling are shared with moving paths. This avoids a
separate electric kernel and repeated spatial differentiation. The number
of directional response paths is reported separately from independent
tensor components: the mixed-derivative polarization identity can require
several directional paths for one component.

`p140_periodic_electric_gamma` uses neutral tilted H2 at
+/-[0.1,0.05,0.7] Bohr in a cubic 9 Bohr cell, STO-3G, overlap cutoff 7 Bohr,
10 radial points, angular degree 7, no pruning and grid shell 1.
The independent oracle reconverges the finite-field Berry dipole, with
orbital tolerance 1e-13, for fields along u=[0.2,-0.3,0.7]. Its central
third derivative is
[P_u(2h)-2 P_u(h)+2 P_u(-h)-P_u(-2h)]/(2 h^3).
It is compared to the contraction Gamma_abcd u_a u_b u_c u_d. Each fit uses
all four steps [0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] in atomic electric field. The additional
Richardson bound is 1e-6; exponent tolerance 0.05 and R^2>0.999 are unchanged.
The 81-component unprojected result is independently compared to the
15-component static expansion at a 1e-12 bound.

The native dedicated/generic, ASE dedicated/generic and both CLI names pass
the same shape, units, normalization and tensor checks. The inert He limit
is exactly zero for HF and TPSS; unit conversion uses the common label
converter. These are finite-model derivative checks, not basis/grid/k-mesh
converged material benchmarks. This acceptance covers compatible insulating
3D Gamma-supercell static clamped-ion parents in the six tested classes.
Relaxed-ion gamma needs the second-order internal-coordinate response;
dynamic, lower-dimensional, ECP, nonlocal/learned and correlated PT2 gamma
combinations remain tracked and are not declared complete.

### Biased periodic response and full periodic pair paths

The nonzero-bias H2 cell acceptance `p143_biased_periodic_electric` passes
HF, PBE, TPSS and PBE0. Its field is [0.004,-0.006,0.014] atomic units,
and its contraction direction is [0.2,-0.3,0.7]. All beta/gamma components
are evaluated without permutation expansion for this acceptance. Independent
finite-field SCF dipoles use all four steps [0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025].
The Berry density Hessian is included in the biased response operator.
No threshold, physical denominator or operator is changed to pass a fit.

`LatticeCorrelatedSolver` now uses the full periodic Ewald Coulomb tensor
and the same moving-geometry density recursion as the parent lattice
functional. Principal metric transport and direct projector rotation are
shared with molecular PT2. The full noncanonical occupied/virtual Fock
coefficient matrices enter the pair equations. Orders zero through four
are implemented; every required parent orbital order is solved. The
parent-only 2n+1 rule cannot replace these higher correlated density
coefficients. Reported SS-alpha, OS and SS-beta energies are unscaled;
the weighted PT2 energy is reported separately.

The existing `periodic-energy`, `periodic-efield`, `periodic-beta`,
`periodic-gamma`, `dielectric-tensor`, `born-charges` and `phonons` drivers
are connected to the correlated lattice path. A custom parent uses
`pt2_same_spin` and `pt2_opposite_spin`; named recipes use the same typed
functional components as molecular calculations. `periodic-efield` accepts
`response_order=0..4` and `field_direction` (field increment per
dimensionless Taylor parameter). Factorial-normalized energy coefficients
are Hartree per primitive cell along that dimensionless path. The direction
control has a field unit so ASE converts both bias and increment consistently.
Ordinary susceptibility and higher tensor fields retain their physical units.

This path is a 3D insulating finite Born-von Karman supercell model sampled
at Gamma. A primitive k mesh is represented by that supercell and must be
converged for an infinite crystal. The Coulomb zero reciprocal component is
removed with the same Ewald background convention as the parent Hartree
energy. Periodic scalar-probe and displacement patterns are accepted by the
Rust path; finite-q driver, noncommensurate-q, lower-dimensional, thermal,
nonlocal-correlation and dynamic correlated combinations remain tracked work.
Required nonlocal terms are never silently omitted. In particular a recipe
requiring periodic VV10 is not described as supported until that term is
connected and validated. Current physical acceptance is recorded below
only when the corresponding test has actually finished successfully.

### Periodic two-endpoint nonlocal correlation

`periodic::nonlocal::vv10_fields` sums the actual periodic subspace and
includes the variational derivative of both density endpoints. Generic
scalars carry density, gradient, point positions, quadrature weights and
lattice vectors. The finite physical pair cutoff is an explicit convergence
parameter; image and vacuum-screening topology is held at the reference.
No minimum-image replacement, finite-difference production derivative or
error floor is used. Indexed Rayon point rows preserve deterministic reduction.

The same operator supplies the Bloch SCF energy/potential and the moving
Gamma path energy/Fock/induced-potential. Nested dual numbers differentiate
the potential with respect to an independent density change, including its
mixed variation along a moving-coordinate/strain path. The common energy
coefficient has a separate `nonlocal_correlation` term. Arbitrary-q and
frequency-dependent nonlocal kernels and complete public/functional
acceptance remain pending. Existing finite-k derivative backends explicitly
reject an attached nonlocal reference until their missing terms are connected.

Independent closed-form lattice energy tests cover seven crystal-system
geometries and 1D/2D/3D sums. The mixed density/position/lattice/weight energy
fit uses steps [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]: first derivative p=1.999879460,
R2=0.999999999017, Richardson error=8.885e-17 Hartree; second derivative
p=2.001889287, R2=0.999997999905, Richardson error=1.465e-14 Hartree.
The exact hexagonal/rhombohedral fixture refinements require their fresh
acceptance run; previous numerical rows are not silently relabelled.

The independently differenced variational potential/kernel tests use the
same four-step interval and compare with the production analytic operator:

| Observable | p | R2 | Richardson absolute error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Energy derivative against Tr[V delta-P] | 2.000031911 | 0.999999999909 | 2.710505431214e-18 |
| Induced AO potential at fixed path origin | 2.000082026 | 0.999999999557 | 2.575742489306e-17 |
| Mixed moving-path induced AO potential | 2.000115155 | 0.999999999134 | 2.031396765753e-17 |

Raw errors, in descending step order, are respectively

[7.403826642252391e-11,1.8506064389647743e-11,4.626295202363069e-12,1.156558565141494e-12].
No failed steps were omitted. The reconverged moving-SCF acceptance is

### Explicit generalized reference on static periodic field SCF

`periodic-field-scf` with `reference=gks` or `reference=ghf` uses the
complex Bloch spinor backend shared with `periodic-spinor-scf`.
`ghf` requires the HF provider. The generic static field entry defaults
the one-electron nuclear spin-orbit scale to zero. Set
`nuclear_soc_scale` explicitly to include that operator. The complex
density and Fock matrices, spin magnetization,
field energy derivative and orbital residual retain the backend units.
The geometry response still requires the matching moving gauge and
operator derivatives for a nonzero field.

For the closed-shell helium chain fixture, keep the grid-number and
SCF gates fixed. At spatial grid level 2, the 4.3-Bohr overlap
radius gave a grid-number defect of 1.885e-5 electrons.
Level 3 with radii of 7.5 Bohr for overlap and 8 Bohr for XC AO
evaluation reduces the defect to 5.020e-10 electrons
in the canonical spinor reference for BLYP and M06-L. An earlier
fully spin polarized one-electron M06-L trial failed the projected
density check in the exact collinear path. The separately accumulated
Pauli contractions left roundoff in the empty spin channel. The
collinear path now uses the exact zero-density limit when the kinetic
density and all current components also vanish to the relative
arithmetic bound. A genuinely nonzero minority density remains active.

The 30-Bohr hydrogen chain M06-L/STO-3G with the same grid settings
as the helium fixture passes its one-spatial-orbital Zeeman check.
At amplitude 0.4 its energy is -0.496900942720647 Hartree per cell and
its raw orbital residual is 6.939e-17 Hartree. The difference between
amplitudes 0.3 and 0.4 matches the closed-form Pauli energy shift
within 1e-11 Hartree, and the magnetization is antiparallel to the
field with unit magnitude. The pre-fix projected-density failure is
reproduced by this same fixture.

The canonical Rust CLI, native Python and ASE atomic report agree with
the canonical spinor reference in both helium-chain cases. The 1D cell
has a period of 14 Bohr and helium at `(0.18,-0.11,0.23)` Bohr.
The basis is STO-3G, the k mesh is `[1,1,1]`, the XC weight cutoff
is zero and the Fourier Zeeman source is `0.4*(0.03,0.04,0.05)`
at zero wave index. The energy tolerance is 1e-12 Hartree and
the orbital and density tolerances are 1e-10.

| Functional | Energy (Hartree per cell) | Raw orbital residual (Hartree) | Im Fock[0,1] (Hartree) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BLYP | -2.841251474128594 | 3.469447e-18 | -0.016 |
| M06-L | -2.851040474492518 | 0.0 | -0.016 |

The filled spinor pair has zero magnetization and a zero first
derivative in the field amplitude. The imaginary Fock matrix element
checks the Pauli-y source independently. Energy, field derivative,
magnetization, density, Fock and raw orbital residual agree between
routes within the 1e-10 absolute gate with their reported units.

### Current static periodic and magnetic acceptance

The production periodic nonlocal functional now uses a C-infinity taper in
squared pair distance between 0.8 Rcut and Rcut, and a C-infinity vacuum
switch between 1e-8 and 2e-8 electrons/Bohr^3. Density denominators are not
clipped. Endpoint partial derivatives include the vacuum-switch derivative;
coordinate/strain derivatives include the distance-switch derivative. The
finite pair cutoff must be converged. Screening is a quadrature/model
convention, not a floor in derivative-error fits.

The magnetic tests independently reconverge finite-field London SCFs for
HF/PBE/TPSS/PBE0 and validate the second/fourth derivative along a declared
field direction. They do not validate arbitrary tensor components, spin
Zeeman, current-dependent correlation, correlated magnetism or periodic
high-order magnetic response. Public tests compare Rust's shared-driver
results through native Python, ASE and both CLI names, including units and
SCF progress on stderr. Cross-surface fixtures convert atomic geometries
using the declared CODATA convention; acceptance tolerances are unchanged.

The latest release and Python-feature all-target compilation retain denied
warnings and no unused-code suppressions. Kernel or partial-route acceptance
does not complete flexoelectricity, four-component no-pair Dirac-Coulomb,
SCDFT or the full accepted response objective.

<!-- current-physical-acceptance:end -->

<!-- additional-components-acceptance:begin -->

### Nuclear response of a finite-bias periodic electric enthalpy

`phonons`, `periodic-cubic-fc`, `periodic-quartic-fc`,
`periodic-cubic-fc-along` and `periodic-quartic-fc-along` accept the existing
`field` control (Hartree/e/Bohr in Rust/native/CLI; eV/Angstrom in the
default ASE convention). All routes use the shared nuclear path engine.
The field is fixed in Cartesian coordinates while the atomic positions,
Gaussian basis, overlap metric and Berry coupling are differentiated.
`series_reference_energy` and `field_energy`, when present, describe the
stationary biased electric enthalpy per primitive cell. The legacy
`energy` field still describes the zero-field starting supercell.

Rust supplies `lattice_path_energy_at_field`,
`lattice_force_constants_along_at_field` and
`lattice_force_constant_tensor_at_field`. The tensor entry accepts nuclear
orders two through four; the existing zero-field tensor retains its
three/four-order API. The wrappers share one implementation and do not
duplicate a physical kernel. Integer-occupation insulating three-dimensional
Gamma/Born-von Karman boundary assumptions and existing functional-provider
restrictions apply. No functional registered-name branch is introduced.

The finite-field harmonic driver reports freshly recomputed response
residuals, reference residual, force constants (Hartree/Bohr^2 per primitive
cell), modes and frequencies (cm^-1). Intrinsic tensor permutation is used
for production. Independent ordered asymmetry has not been evaluated on
this path and is not fabricated as a zero residual. Cubic and quartic
force constants have Hartree/Bohr^3 and Hartree/Bohr^4 per primitive cell.
The full tensor driver also reports every raw response residual.

Independent acceptance uses four displaced-cell enthalpy/force steps
against production analytic coefficients through nuclear order four.
Native/ASE atomic and physical units and both CLI variants are checked
separately. Measured acceptance is recorded only after those tests pass.
This connection does not establish finite magnetic/joint-field nuclear
response, arbitrary-q biased nuclear DFPT or correlated PT2 nuclear
response; those remain required by the full objective.
<!-- biased-nuclear-api:end -->

<!-- incremental-response-evidence:begin -->

### Repaired metallic electron-phonon vertex regression

`p75_electron_phonon`: four tests passed, including twelve independent
order-1--4 scalar fits of the Pulay-complete mode vertex and its squared
amplitude, and nine independent physical band-energy derivative fits for
metallic LDA/PBE0 and insulating HF/PBE0. Both coarse LDA intervals are
reported explicitly with the resolved intervals; only the first coarse
component failed. No failed step is discarded and |p-2|<0.05 and R2>0.9999
are retained. For the first metallic
component p improved from 1.850760095 on [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] to 1.991618865
on [0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025]; the Richardson error was 9.610985621071e-9.

Gamma static thermal response now uses independent Hermitian matrix
coordinates. Fermi occupations and holes are evaluated together without
losing the small hole to subtraction. Nonzero energy differences use an
expm1 divided difference, and exactly degenerate energies use the analytic
Fermi slope; no physical band gap or number-response denominator is floored.
Finite-q (k+q,k) response retains its separate non-Hermitian space.
The long-running metallic force-constant and gapped thermal-limit regression
is separate and is not accepted on the strength of these vertex tests.

### Resolved existing metallic force-constant regression

Both independently displaced columns of the 3000 K LDA hydrogen-chain
Mermin-force regression now pass unchanged p=2 +/-0.05, R2>0.9999 and
Richardson<2e-5 gates. All seven steps [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025,
0.00125] are retained. The longitudinal coarse interval failed at
p=1.745484422, R2=0.957736278004 and Richardson=1.9615773234771261e-4;
its resolved interval [0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.00125] passes. The transverse
column also passes the same finer interval. The analytic raw asymmetry is
1.0450867601874414e-12 and acoustic defect 1.9484414082171497e-14.
Fresh response residuals are at most 5.345834421844914e-12 at the default
1e-10 tolerance. No ASR repair, physical gap floor, source clipping or
threshold relaxation is used. The independent gapped finite-temperature
limit previously passed with maximum force-constant difference
1.9892421043721242e-12. These cases do not establish every metallic q,
frequency, functional or nuclear-order combination.

### Shared complex Berry electric enthalpy component

The finite-cell Berry electric energy, Fock, density kernel and moving
polar-operator Taylor convolution are now shared by real collinear and
complex spinor references. The general density has complex Hermitian
coherence; it is not projected to a real or collinear matrix. The Fock
is HermitianImag[K] and its kernel -HermitianImag[K deltaP K], with
K=(Q-S)[I+P(Q-S)]^-1. The electric enthalpy uses the matching determinant
and moving ionic phase. The existing real Berry kernel regression also
passes (p=1.999986556, R2=0.999999999988).

Two independently phased 2x2 cases pass eight nuclear/field-path order-1..4
fits against a closed determinant polynomial and analytic scalar force,
plus two density-kernel fits against a closed adjugate. Production uses
the matrix inverse/log-determinant recurrences, while the oracle uses
explicit 2x2 determinants and adjugates. All four steps
[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] and existing p=2 +/-0.05, R2>0.9999 and
Richardson<2e-6 gates are retained. No finite differences enter production.
This component acceptance does not by itself certify the independently
running relaxed-SCF nuclear and public joint-field reports.

### Relaxed nuclear response in simultaneous periodic electric/magnetic fields

The 3D finite-Gamma point-source provider passes all four additional
physical cases: neutral HF with joint fields, custom full/range exchange
with generated nuclear SOC and joint fields, charged coherent-spinor HF
with three-face flux and joint fields, and the electric-only zero-magnetic
limit. Each case passes independent nuclear order-1..4 SCF-energy and
variational-force fits on seven retained steps
[0.12,0.09,0.06,0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075]. The force interval for order
four is [0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075], with the other orders using the first
four steps. All 16 fits retain p=2 +/-0.05, R2>0.9999 and Richardson<2e-6
gates. Exponents are 1.998893795..2.024968677, minimum R2=0.999930991556,
maximum Richardson=2.3653388546429621e-8 and maximum fresh response
residual=3.298481918729003e-14 at requested tolerance 1e-12.

The charged one-electron case independently contracts the occupied
orbital with exp(i b.r), rather than using the production full-space
inverse/determinant. Its energy and the separate Hartree/exchange
self-interaction cancellation pass at every displaced point. The electric
work is also checked against the Berry dipole. Every source/image,
complex overlap, kinetic/full/range Coulomb term, Zeeman and nuclear SOC
keeps the same geometry; no finite difference enters production.

The charged joint-field scalar path passes native Python, ASE atomic and
physical units, canonical CLI and compatibility CLI comparisons, including
all energy orders zero through four, dipole, field and electric work.
Neutral full gradient/Hessian/contracted cubic/quartic public comparisons and the remaining six crystal metrics passed, as recorded below. The real-path regressions are repeated after the separate overlap repair. These measurements do not establish magnetic-BZ,
1D/2D, semilocal/nonlocal, finite-width, correlated PT2 or arbitrary-q
field-biased nuclear response.

### Joint-field nuclear acceptance on all seven crystal metrics

The existing cubic case and six additional metrics now pass independently
relaxed SCF-energy/variational-force nuclear order-1..4 fits: cubic,
tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, rhombohedral (trigonal), monoclinic
and triclinic. All fields carry exactly one quantum through the a1/a2
face, B=2pi*a3/volume, including the nonorthogonal tilted fields. Cartesian
electric bias stays (0.0007,0.0005,-0.001) Hartree/(e Bohr). The unchanged
crystal arrays are shared by the operator, gauge-boundary and physical
nuclear acceptances. All original 420 closed operator fits passed again.

The six noncubic cases add 24 accepted force fits, with
p=1.999258075..2.019379249, minimum R2=0.999994062038 and maximum
Richardson=2.631939118036275e-8. All seven h values and the same four-point
intervals/gates as the cubic case are retained. Coarse fourth energy
differences remain separate cancellation/nonasymptotic diagnostics;
their failed p/R2 values are preserved, while independent variational
force differences establish the resolved quartic order without loosening
the 2e-6 energy-Richardson gate. The four earlier model/limit cases plus
these six metrics give 40 newly accepted physical force fits.

The canonical dft-rs CLI, native Python, ASE atomic and ASE physical routes
also pass the neutral joint-field scalar path, full gradient, Hessian and
contracted cubic/quartic matrices. Largest measured fresh response is
6.105269315465323e-14 at tolerance 1e-12; stationarity maximum is
3.0526796368501863e-15 Hartree and reference energy defect
5.88418203051333e-15 Hartree. Gradient response order zero has empty
residual/stationarity arrays, not measured zeros. Both CLI names also
pass a dedicated default-stderr SCF energy/residual test. Its first fixture

### Berry branch-cut translation failure before repair

A separate neutral rigid translation parallel to B exposed a phase-label
discontinuity in the principal-determinant convention. At z shifts 1.26
Bohr and above the electric enthalpy changed by 0.005 Hartree and dipole by
5 e Bohr, while the zero-field terms stayed invariant to 3.34e-16 Hartree.
All SCF references converged. This does not invalidate the earlier local
fits away from the cut, but it prevents broad translation acceptance.

The common real/complex Berry functional now continues the total electronic
determinant phase near an electron-number-weighted effective nuclear charge
centroid. Only an integer 2pi branch offset is added. Fock and density
kernels are unchanged; explicit field-direction coefficients retain the
corresponding branch work. The fixed compensating-charge dipole is still
separate. The independent branch-quantum, near-cut nuclear and neutral/charged translation acceptance results are recorded below; this original failure is preserved.

### Accepted Berry phase and overlap corrections

The preceding translation failure is retained as the pre-repair measurement.
The phase-continuation repair now passes 24 energy and two density-kernel
four-step fits against independent closed determinant/adjugate expressions,
with two complex AO gauges and branch offsets -1, 0, +1. All four nuclear
orders also pass an independently relaxed energy/force path whose common
translation crosses the old principal phase cut. Its quartic force fit has
p=2.029857868, R2=0.999956455210 on [0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075] Bohr and
Richardson error 1.9024637420983481e-9 Hartree/Bohr^4. The coarse energy-only
quartic fit p=2.304991678, R2=0.997920787987 fails the power-law gate; it
remains recorded, and the unchanged energy Richardson gate still passes.
Maximum freshly reevaluated response residual is 3.651935294251671e-14.

Seven neutral magnetic translations preserve enthalpy within 3.34e-16
Hartree. Six charged translations, including a full-cell displacement,
obey delta-E=-Q E.dot(delta-R) and delta-dipole=Q delta-R: maximum work
error 1.48e-16 Hartree, dipole error 1.34e-15 e Bohr. Native Python, ASE
atomic/physical units and both CLI names pass neutral translated nuclear
orders 0..4 at three origins. This local branch convention does not imply
a global conducting polarization or a different magnetic boundary model.

An additional real-collinear regression exposed a distinct overlap defect:
the polar operator subtracted a Coulomb-pair G=0 transform instead of the
SCF overlap. At image cutoff 4, translation changed the enthalpy by up to
2.482e-6 Hartree even after phase continuation. The common lattice builder
now subtracts the actual SCF metric in Q-S at every nuclear Taylor order.
No overlap renormalization, image-cutoff increase or tolerance change was
used. Seven translations now differ by at most 1.7763568394002505e-15 Hartree.
The permanent native/ASE atomic/ASE physical/CLI regression at origins
0, 1.26 and 2.6 Bohr passes with both executable names, including default
SCF iteration energy/residual stderr diagnostics. Maximum reference
residual is 2.3159223691958793e-15. Fresh nonzero electric and nuclear derivative regressions passed and are recorded in the alpha.2 verification section below.

## Part 8: Superconductivity and phonon-coupled response

### Canonical complex superconducting gap and parameter response

The common `superconducting-state` driver now solves the static complex
band-decoupled singlet gap, chemical potential, particle number and global
phase together. `GapFunctional` retains scalar-generic mu/gap dependence;
the LM2005 off-diagonal provider recomputes its phonon/Coulomb kernel at
the responding chemical potential. The diagonal mass renormalization Z is
an explicit required input. Newton and coefficient equations use the same
AD Jacobian actions and matrix-free GMRES; no physical denominator is
floored. Original gap, number, phase, phase multiplier and U(1) Goldstone
residuals are measured. Non-finite AD actions and nonreciprocal kernel
coefficients fail; no symmetrization conceals them. The zero seed selects
the normal stationary branch without claiming thermodynamic stability.

Five Rust acceptance cases pass. Closed analytic one- and two-band
Bogoliubov solutions check complex phase covariance, particle-hole
reflection, normal-state/Fermi-level limits and every coefficient through
order four. Independent contour phonon expressions test the mu-dependent
kernel and the coupled gap solution. The 52 four-step fits use
h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] with no floors or omitted steps:
p in [1.999924726,2.000731059], minimum R2=0.999999964118. Richardson checks and
the 16/32-order coupled quadrature comparison retain their separate gates.
Native Python, generic driver, ASE atomic/eV and both CLI routes agree;
independent NumPy BdG diagonalization checks occupations and anomalous
density. Raw measured Rust coefficients and defects follow below.

This completes the supplied-normal-band static solver component, not the
full superconducting objective. Generated static symmetric LM2005 mass is
accepted below; normal-density/orbital backreaction, the automatic
DFPT-vertex/screened-Coulomb adapter,
general interband pairing, finite-q/causal dynamic kernels, zero-temperature
superconducting equations and thermodynamic branch selection remain pending.
No functional/reference class is promoted by this band-model acceptance.

### Mermin Hessian and equilibrium Gibbs from the electronic entry

`mermin-free-energy --gibbs` / `mermin_free_energy(..., gibbs=True)` reuse
one converged reference, the common analytic Hessian, Eckart projection and
RRHO thermochemistry. The default Mermin request has no Hessian cost.
Finite-temperature Hessians now include complete orbital/occupation/mu
response and both density and energy-weighted-density metric terms, with
the existing functional kernels and skeleton terms. Fixed-number response
also has the integer-occupation limit without an artificial Fermi-surface
weight. `gibbs-free-energy` and the frequencies driver reuse the same paths.
Positive electronic/nuclear temperatures must agree for equilibrium Gibbs;
the zero-electronic-temperature approximation retains the usual RRHO model.
Electronic entropy is counted once. An imaginary mode refuses the Gibbs
request. Gradient requests on the Mermin entry still differentiate A_e;
RRHO Gibbs geometry derivatives and higher finite-temperature responses
are not inferred from the Hessian implementation.
The existing electronic functional has no explicit temperature dependence;
thermal electronic entropy is the independent-particle Fermi entropy. No
additional finite-temperature XC free-energy model is implied.

An independent Bose partition-function identity exposed and corrected the
old vibrational entropy `ln(1+exp(-x))` sign: the oscillator requires
`ln(1-exp(-x))`. The independent occupation entropy oracle and dG/dT=-S
fit retain this as a physical regression. HF, LDA, GGA, meta-GGA and hybrid
H2 tests compare the production analytic Hessian, full density derivative
and energy-weighted-density derivative against separate converged SCF
gradients/densities on all four h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] Bohr. The thermal
partition test uses h=[40,20,10,5] K. All 16 fits pass with no discarded
steps: p in [1.997554988,2.019189671], minimum R2=0.999978462386. Integer-limit,
full residual and pressure/pV checks remain independent gates. Water is
included in the public Gibbs-route regression. Functional classes reuse
their providers; no registered-name calculation branch is introduced.

The final Python-feature build of all Rust targets passes with warnings
denied. All 18 common-driver tests pass, including every declared control
unit, report unit grammar and the three aligned API tables. With
`DFT_RS_STRICT_UNITS=1` and Python warnings treated as errors, each CLI
variant passes 26 public acceptance cases covering the canonical Mermin
and Gibbs names, optional Gibbs from one Mermin SCF, all nonlinear optical
presets, both explicit/preset ASE frequency representations and the static
superconducting component. The combined Gibbs CLI test measures exactly
one SCF convergence message. Native, generic, ASE atomic/eV and CLI results
agree, including finite-temperature energy/entropy and ideal-gas pV identities.
The new coupled report's frequency and raw Hessian asymmetry labels are
explicit; their initially missing labels failed the strict acceptance and
are corrected rather than suppressing that check.

The unchanged dynamic-response implementation also passes all five long
Rust regressions: independent spectral/Floquet oracles, static limits,
covariance and four-step electro-optic fits for LDA, GGA, hybrid, range-
separated hybrid, meta-GGA and an unregistered weighted local hybrid. The
existing six molecular vibrational/gradient/density/Raman acceptance cases
pass with their original four-step thresholds. One duplicate dynamic test
process was stopped; it is not counted as a pass. The original complete
dynamic regression supplies the accepted result. The Hessian's five-class
15 physical derivative fits are retained from the numerical acceptance;
the subsequently changed water partition oracle is rechecked separately,
without repeating unchanged physical calculations.

The final distributable-source audit covers 826 files, 157 unique API IDs
in three aligned tables, 156 physical targets and 68 coverage families.
It finds no restricted names, machine-specific paths, non-English code or
documentation, undeclared dependencies, missing packaged sources/tests or
build/reference/validation entries. The original dependency declarations
and lock dependencies are unchanged. All 576 packaged code files have the
library notice. Exact/structural/partial source-body inspection finds no new
duplicate candidate in the added or extended superconducting, ensemble,
thermochemistry or molecular/vibrational driver code. Existing candidates
in other physical models are not automatically classified as duplicates.

This is acceptance of the stated components and combinations. Generated
static symmetric SCDFT mass is accepted below; reference backreaction and
dynamic kernels, correlated finite-
temperature Mermin/Gibbs, higher thermal derivatives and the other pending
coverage combinations remain part of the active full implementation program.

<!-- phonon-mass-acceptance:begin -->

### Generated static phonon mass and coupled superconducting response

The shared scalar-generic LM2005 provider now generates the diagonal phonon
mass Z from the same normal spectrum, chemical potential, kT, band weights
and squared vertices as the phonon pairing kernel K. The band component
and canonical gap driver share this implementation. Z includes the final-band
quadrature weight once; K excludes it. Screened Coulomb remains a separate
additive K term and has no implicit diagonal mass. No registered electronic
functional name selects the response equation.

The particle-hole-symmetric mass uses the overall minus-J convention in
[PRB 88, 014514 Eq. (10)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0390), with the confluent
Fermi derivative product consistent with its Eq. (44). The production
second divided difference is an integral of the analytic Fermi second
derivative. The odd numerator at the Fermi surface is divided by tanh
analytically using a nested dual derivative. No physical denominator floor
or finite difference is used in production. The stable algebra retains
temperature, phonon, vertex, chemical-potential and band-weight derivatives.

Three new kernel acceptance cases and all six coupled gap cases pass,
along with the existing off-diagonal kernel suite. Independent exponential
mass expressions test generic, exact resonance, fixed Fermi-surface,
Fermi-crossing and joint Fermi/resonance paths. Each has independent
1..4 derivative fits on h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] in a dimensionless parameter.
Their raw coefficient and 16/32 quadrature differences are below. Independent
term sums verify mode/weight factors, zero vertex and Coulomb independence.
Both signs of each physical input are evaluated independently.

A flat, symmetric, finite-band DOS with Omega=0.025 Hartree, half-bandwidth
B=0.25 Hartree and squared vertex 0.0001 Hartree squared approaches the
independent mass-enhancement limit 2*g^2*N(0)*(1/Omega-1/(Omega+B)), N(0)=1.
The zero-temperature limit is checked without changing the finite band.
The symmetric kernel has an explicit linear-kT contribution from the
derivative of the divided difference. Independently integrating
-4*kT/(Omega+abs(y))^3 gives the slope
4*g^2*N(0)*(1/Omega^2-1/(Omega+B)^2). The resolved thermal fit uses
kT=[0.000125,0.0000625,0.00003125,0.000015625] Hartree after subtracting
that analytically known linear term, while retaining the raw zero-T errors.
The cutoff correction is retained rather than comparing a finite band
against an infinite-band lambda. The generated K/Z provider also solves a
complex gap with an independently specified exact gap, number, anomalous
density, mu and quasiparticle-energy-squared path: twenty more fits check
all four orders of the five observables using one shared AD Jacobian.

All 41 new fits retain every raw step and use no error floors:
p in [1.987500674,2.010034914], minimum R2=0.999993367037.
Kernel derivative fits require abs(p-2)<0.03 and R2>0.9999 with a separate
Richardson gate; the thermal limit requires abs(p-2)<0.05. Existing
gap/number/phase/multiplier/Goldstone and GMRES residual gates remain intact.
Native Python, the generic driver, ASE atomic/eV and both CLI variants each
pass the same 29 public cases with strict units and Python warnings as errors.
The cases include generated K/Z, independent BdG diagonalization, all
optical presets, water Gibbs thermochemistry and Gibbs from one Mermin SCF.
Generated-mass public maxima are gap/Goldstone
1.290634266127e-15 Hartree, number
1.887379141863e-15, and original GMRES relative
residual 2.611231061513e-13. The weighted
two-band mass path has maximum 16/32 relative quadrature difference
7.302824390115e-14, separately labelled dimensionless from K errors.

This accepts the static symmetric mass and coupled band-model response.
Normal-density/orbital/phonon backreaction, an automatic DFPT-to-pairing
vertex and screened-Coulomb adapter, general interband anomalous pairing,
finite-q causal dynamics, a zero-temperature gap solver and thermodynamic
branch selection remain pending. Functional/reference matrix cells are not
promoted by a supplied-normal-band component test.

The initial thermal test incorrectly assumed a purely quadratic low-T
error: its four raw errors were [0.000602126635136928,
0.00030804402062867796,0.00015620042235121433,0.00007870039246858206]
at kT=[0.001,0.0005,0.00025,0.000125], giving p=0.978661078 and
R2=0.999974541282. This failure is retained and resolved by the independent
linear term above, not an error floor or a looser quadratic-fit gate.
The initial derivative fixture with phonon path Omega=0.025/(1-0.12*t)
had a small leading quadratic-error coefficient in its third derivative:
errors=[1.305120899353085e-6,2.4515570551386645e-7,
5.621575294156855e-8,1.3740973692222269e-8] on the four stated h,
p=2.183331819, R2=0.998408292848. The accepted mixed path uses
Omega=0.025/(1-0.25*t); it retains the same four h, independent formula,
Richardson comparison and original fit gates. All accepted steps follow.
For the Fermi-crossing case, directly differentiating the exponential
numerator/tanh quotient at displaced points lost precision: order-three
errors=[0.0013346170199612928,0.0003314569291434921,
0.00007869217388378758,0.0004827991595446335], p=0.647532156,
R2=0.244366515620; order-four errors=[0.0012051021685702823,
0.00025672651003205704,0.0012025156779041923,0.02625568561865166],
p=-1.556395902, R2=0.515053806024, on the same four h. The production
coefficients still agreed with the closed zero-point coefficients to
7.9581e-13 or better. The resolved oracle instead divides its independent
exponential power series at the exact removable zero, evaluates it at every
original step, and checks 24/32-order truncation agreement below 1e-10.
No failed fine step is discarded or replaced by a numerical floor.

### Phonon mass public contracts and portability acceptance

The Python-enabled optimized library and both CLI executables build with
warnings denied. All-target checking also passes with warnings denied, and
all 18 common-driver contracts pass, including control/report unit grammar
and the three aligned API tables. The public suite passes 29 cases with
each CLI variant, strict units and Python warnings as errors. The generated
mass component is exercised without an Atoms object on native, generic,
ASE atomic/eV and CLI routes; supplied-Z compatibility remains accepted.
The Gibbs-from-Mermin route still reuses exactly one electronic SCF and
passes the entropy, enthalpy and pressure identities, including water in
the separate molecular Gibbs acceptance.

The ten Rust pairing/gap/mass acceptance cases contain 101 measured
four-step fits: 72 gap/number/phase-related fits, 20 independent mass
derivative fits, one resolved thermal-limit fit and eight existing
off-diagonal kernel fits. Forty derivative fits and the thermal-limit fit
are new to this mass milestone. Failed initial mass-oracle steps and their
resolved intervals remain documented above. No derivative gate is relaxed.

The final source audit covers 828 packaged files, 157 API IDs in three
aligned tables, 156 physical targets and 68 coverage families. It finds
no restricted content, machine-specific absolute paths, non-English text,
reference/build/scratch entries or missing source/tests. The original
dependency declarations and lock dependencies are unchanged. All 578 code
files have the library header. The optimized artifact audit finds no
private build roots in its four audited artifacts. Source-body inspection
finds no new exact, structural or partial duplicate candidate in the
pairing, superconducting response and their drivers; one kernel and common
parsing helpers are reused. Existing candidates in unrelated models are
not automatically classified as duplicate implementations.

This is component acceptance. The normal-state/DFPT/causal combinations
listed above, double-hybrid finite-temperature Mermin/Gibbs correlation,
the remaining relativistic and magnetic theories and all other pending CSV
combinations remain within the full implementation objective.
<!-- phonon-mass-verification:end -->

### General complex Nambu density component

The supplied-operator `pairing_model="nambu"` route of
`superconducting-state` accepts complex normal Hamiltonians, overlap and
antisymmetric pairing matrices, including interband pairing. Its analytic
matrix Fermi function uses scaling and bounded logistic doubling, with
moving overlap, chemical-potential and temperature coefficients through
order four. `chi=-R_eh` is the anomalous density and the particle number is
`Tr(S rho)`. The ensemble is grand canonical with supplied operators.

The Rust acceptance has 48 independent four-step fits at kT=0.2 and
0.00002 Hartree, over [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01], comparing orders 1--4 against
closed spectral projectors transported by a complex nonunitary frame.
The exponent interval is [1.999730627,2.000540713] and minimum
R2=0.999999980393. All raw steps and Richardson differences follow.
Exact Fermi-surface degeneracy, the normal-state polynomial limit and
global pair-phase covariance are also checked. An initially chosen
purely imaginary frame shear made one real observable identically zero;
that unusable log-fit fixture was replaced by a general complex shear.
The failed initial oracle log remains outside the source package.

Native Python, generic driver, ASE atomic and physical units, and both
CLI variants pass the same component under strict units and warnings as
errors. A separate full 8 by 8 dense complex BdG oracle supplies four
additional order-1--4 fits on [0.24,0.18,0.12,0.06], without copying
symmetry-related matrix elements. Maximum particle-hole defect is
2.526e-15, metric defect 9.992e-16, relative commutator 4.321e-16 and
inverse residual 4.053e-17.

This component does not imply a self-consistent normal/pairing functional,
canonical general-pairing gap equations, normal-density backreaction or a
causal dynamic kernel. A periodic provider must supply a complete paired
momentum space; a single arbitrary k sector is not assumed to pair with
itself. A relativistic provider must supply its intended no-pair electronic
space. Full SCDFT and electronic functional/reference combinations remain
tracked work.

## Part 9: Magnetic fields, spinors and relativistic response

### Public ROKS and GKS calculation coverage

This table follows the explicit `reference` dispatch and the named acceptance
fixtures. Each measured subset has its own functional, basis, perturbation
and convergence limits. The individual family records distinguish these
subsets in `property_targets.csv`.

| Domain | Calculation | ROKS / ROHF | GKS / GHF |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Molecule | Stationary energy and analytic nuclear derivatives | `energy`, `gradient`, `hessian` and `force-constants` have common-orbital paths. `p115`, `p247` and the screened catalogue checks give subset evidence. `p320` covers semicanonical PT2 energy; its common-orbital gradient and response Lagrangian are open. | `energy`, `gradient`, `hessian` and `force-constants` have full-spin paths. `p241`, `p243`, `p246` and `p265` cover selected operators and orders. Scalar ECP and fixed external electric sources have separate scopes. The complex spinor PT2 nuclear Lagrangian is open. |
| Molecule | Electric moments and response | `dipole`, `molecular-multipole`, static/dynamic dipole and higher electric response use constrained orbitals. `p118` and `p297` give selected static, causal and general one-body evidence. | Static moments and general one-body operators use the complex Pauli density. `p114` and `p286` give selected static, causal and mixed-operator evidence. Correlated static electric subsets require a supported spin-covariant PT2 pair weighting. An unequal-weight model or nonzero-frequency spinor PT2 response needs additional terms. |
| Molecule | Vibrations and excitations | `frequencies` and `gibbs-free-energy` postprocess the common-orbital Hessian. The MRSF excitation route has separate applicability. Full VPT2 and frequency-resolved vibrational intensities still require reference-specific connected derivative combinations. | `frequencies` and `gibbs-free-energy` postprocess the spinor Hessian. Spinor TDA excitation and state derivatives have separate tests. Full VPT2 and frequency-resolved vibrational intensities still require reference-specific connected derivative combinations. |
| Molecule | NMR, EPR and magnetic moments | Orbital NMR shielding has common-origin and London paths. Static EPR and zero-field magnetic quadrupole have explicit selectors. `spin-susceptibility` and the total, diamagnetic and paramagnetic orbital magnetizability are still missing on this manifold. | Orbital shielding and Ramsey couplings have common-origin paths. Static EPR and magnetic quadrupole have explicit selectors. Static common-origin orbital magnetizability is connected. London shielding/magnetizability, spin Zeeman magnetizability, bulk spin susceptibilities and higher magnetic tensors remain open. |
| Molecule | Higher magnetic, optical and core excitation response | `bfield`, `bfield-gradient`, `hypermagnetizability`, `cotton-mouton`, `magnetoelectric` and `magneto-optical` reject this reference. NEXAFS requires a common-orbital core-hole/CVS provider. | The same higher magnetic selectors reject this reference. NEXAFS requires a complex spinor core-hole/CVS provider. Optical calculations from supplied tensors retain the applicability of their input tensors. |
| Periodic | Energy, first geometry derivatives and electronic DOS | `periodic-energy`, forces, `stress` and `dos` use the integer common-orbital Gamma/mesh or dimensional reference. The 3D `opt-fixed-cell` path has a separate test. Force/stress support depends on the overlap rank and functional provider. Periodic common-orbital PT2 and the 1D/2D optimizer are open. | The public reference selector reaches `periodic-energy`, `stress` and `dos`. First derivatives are gated by the dimensional spinor provider. Selected field-free affine stress fits are in `periodic_gks_stress` and `periodic_gks_coulomb_strain`. `periodic-spinor-scf` has its own field and reference contract. |

These routes need a constrained first-order projector with shared-orbital occupation blocks through the requested k/q and strain paths. | The selector rejects these calculations. They need full complex Pauli finite-k/q orbital and metric response, including the corresponding long-range operators. Acceptance of stationary GKS affine stress covers the first strain derivative. |

The periodic electric entries require the model's insulating polarization
branch. A metallic stationary reference can still supply a DOS, while a
metallic Berry-polarization derivative is outside that insulating model.
Directional LO–TO also requires a long-wavelength polar dynamical matrix
for the cell's dimensional Coulomb kernel.

### Static spinor orbital magnetizability at a common gauge origin

`magnetizability` with `reference=gks` or `reference=ghf` requires
`gauge=common-origin`. It evaluates the all-electron, fixed-nuclei, orbital
curvature at zero magnetic field using the complex spinor stationary
Hessian. The linear source is `L(O)/2` on each diagonal spin block.
The explicit quadratic term is `|B × (r − O)|²/8`. The negative
energy curvature gives the total magnetizability and the report exposes
its separate fixed-density diamagnetic and relaxed paramagnetic tensors in
`e² Bohr²/m_e`. The gauge origin is in Bohr and defaults to the centre of
nuclear charge. The tensors depend on the common origin in a finite basis.
The report carries raw imaginary, symmetry, response and reference Fock
defects. [Gauge-dependent and London magnetizability formulations](https://trygvehelgaker.no/Publications/JChemPhys_099_03847_1993.pdf)

Exactly real, spin-diagonal LDA/GGA references for this static orbital
source use the antisymmetric same-spin density sector. Density and
squared-gradient perturbations vanish in this sector. The shared pair
kernel preserves all signed full- and range-exchange coefficients. An
initial timed diagnostic finished SCF in 0.241 s and fixed-geometry pair
setup in 0.231 s before the full Pauli descriptor cache exceeded
75 s. The reduced path avoids building that cache in its exact domain.
The general response retains the Pauli descriptor Hessian, including
the intrinsic kinetic-density/current terms for meta-GGA.

`p323_gks_orbital_magnetizability` independently reconverges GKS with
each of the linear, quadratic and summed field Hamiltonians on a C1
ammonia cation. The test fits six independent components per tensor,
including mixed fields for off-diagonal components. London derivatives, spin Zeeman response,
magnetic derivatives of nonlocal ECP projectors, frequency dependence,
additional AO spin operators and magnetic PT2 response are outside this
connection.

A separate static-sector diagnostic on the same system originally omitted

then showed a nonconvergent total error. At `h=0.012` the absolute errors
