### Complex reference and spinor acceptance

The new complex periodic-field fixture preserves the imaginary density and
exchange in all three dimensional masks. At amplitude 0.4 its raw orbital
conjugation defect is about 0.5131, while canonical orbital residuals are
below 3.43e-16 and energy-component defects below 5.55e-17 Hartree.
Four independent SCF central differences at 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 give
p=1.99965417..1.99965418 and R2=0.9999999920. Raw errors are approximately
2.9032474e-4, 7.2622757e-5, 1.8158286e-5, 4.5397337e-6 Hartree.
No physical orbital conjugation is imposed, and reversing A reverses the
imaginary density. The first oracle incorrectly equated a periodic Green
Hartree energy to localized free-space exchange. Its raw J+K discrepancies
(-0.1023368, -0.0487508, -0.0354278 Hartree) are retained in the initial log.
The corrected independent dense free-space ERI oracle compares like kernels:
free J+K is below 1e-16 and the production localized exchange defect is zero.
Fresh Fock and total-energy checks keep the actual periodic Hartree separately.

#### Uniform open-boundary field acceptance

The analytic uniform-field extension uses the physical periodic subspace,
with the existing open-direction Coulomb Green operator. It adds the full
continuum `(p+A)^2/2`, spin `sigma.B/2`, and nuclear
`sigma.[grad(V) cross (p+A)]/(4 c^2)` in the two-component route.
Nuclear contact integrals differentiate both Gaussian factors and the
explicit linear coordinate after integration by parts. The energy and
Fock use the same contact; the analytic amplitude derivative includes it.
Neither a discrete hopping model nor a finite-difference production field
derivative is used.

For a wire with unit tangent t, define Bp=t(t.B):
`A=t[(t cross B).r]+(Bp cross r)/2`. For a slab with unit normal n
and B.n=0, `A=(B cross n)(n.r)`. Both gauges have div A=0,
curl A=B, and M times every periodic translation equals zero.
An origin change uses `A=lambda M(r-O)` and the common AO phase
`exp(i lambda (M O).r)`. Matrix elements are evaluated in the origin-zero
gauge frame, preserving exact origin covariance for this gauge family.
The phase must also accompany any future real-space orbital sampling.

Acceptance covers the seven crystal metrics, every wire axis and slab plane,
the closed Gaussian diamagnetic contact, independent four-step nuclear
source-derivative fits, independently relaxed SCF amplitude fits, field
reversal and origin changes. The aligned public tables expose the controls
on Rust, CLI, native Python and ASE. Rust acceptance measurements and public-route checks are recorded below.
Normal slab flux requires magnetic Bloch translations and its open-direction
Coulomb integrals; it remains part of the full accepted objective, together
with nonlocal core/current-XC and the remaining response combinations.

#### Normal-flux magnetic slab acceptance

The magnetic slab retains discrete in-plane waves and continuous open-normal
Fourier integration. Its zero in-plane mode is the physical
`-2 pi abs(z-z')/area` Green function, restored by analytic Gaussian
subtraction. The long-range zero mode is referenced to equal open coordinates:
`-2 pi/area * (z erf(omega z) + (exp(-omega^2 z^2)-1)/(omega sqrt(pi)))`.
The omega=0 limit is exactly zero. A charged slab uses explicit finite
transverse Gaussian compensation. It never acquires an artificial open-axis
period or a three-dimensional uniform background.

The existing eight spinor/SOC and eight uniform-flux current/derivative
regressions also pass unchanged, as do the two aligned API registry tests.
The source audit covers 633 distributable files, 84 API IDs, 147 targets and
68 families: restricted names, non-English content, machine paths, PowerShell
scripts and packaged build/reference/validation entries are all zero.
The original dependencies and author metadata remain intact, and the docs
Markdown file count remains ten. Relocated artifacts run with Python site
packages disabled, with embedded-basis H2 energy -1.1167143251757703 Hartree
and zero differences on native Python and both CLI names.
This accepts the measured HF/local-density/generic exchange subsets; the
remaining functional classes and full response combinations remain tracked.

#### Generic semilocal spin projection under acceptance

`periodic::spinor_xc::spinor_semilocal_point` projects all Pauli density,
gradient, kinetic-density and current descriptors onto global spin directions.
The effective integrand is `f + D_spin f`. Nested duals differentiate both
the input variables and the spin-scaling direction; the native provider's
analytic first/second derivatives give the variational descriptor potential.
No division by the spin magnitude or functional-name dispatch is used.
The construction follows the [global projection derivation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09897).

For meta-GGA the projected kinetic density is `tau-j^2/(2 rho)`, using tau
and j in the same gauge frame. Exact nodal projected densities currently
require an angular rule avoiding that node; that boundary remains tracked.
Angular convergence is independent of the spatial grid and SCF residuals.
The acceptance suite compares native collinear energies and each weighted
term on four angular rules, applies a common phase-gradient transformation,
and fits four independent energy-difference steps against the analytic
32-descriptor derivative for LDA, GGA and meta-GGA providers.
The local core passes both acceptance tests; its measurements are recorded below. Magnetic/dimensional SCF grid
connections, raw angular/grid diagnostics and all public routes must be
completed before this core is classified as a completed physical calculation.
The vorticity-dependent provider and double-hybrid PT2 amplitude/orbital
responses remain required parts of the same accepted full objective.

### Finite-nucleus kinetically balanced Dirac integrals

`integrals::dirac::restricted_kinetic_balance` generates the actual
finite-Gaussian-nucleus RKB one-electron operator, metric and complete
one-electron spin-orbit block, including analytic moving-nucleus, radius,
basis-parameter and speed-of-light dependence. The common `no-pair-projector`
calculation accepts `dirac_integrals="rkb"` and connects these generated jets
to the previously validated sector/metric response. Distinct finite nuclear
charge distributions contribute their Gaussian Coulomb interaction; individual
nuclear self-energies are excluded explicitly. Every shell pair is evaluated
independently. Shared Scalar integrals, nested duals, rayon, moving-metric
transport and faer are reused; no finite difference enters production.

Acceptance: `tests/p163_balanced_dirac.rs`, four passed cases. Independent
closed normalized Gaussian radial integrals check S, T, V, the small-component
potential and the positive electronic eigenvalue term by term. A separate
closed p-shell spin-orbit splitting fixes multiplicities and the absolute
matrix sign. Displaced-center radial/Laplacian formulas check relative nuclear
motion and Gaussian nuclear interactions. Translation invariance, raw
Hermiticity, the point-nucleus limit and the nonrelativistic limit are checked.

There are 28 derivative fits (orders one through four for seven nonzero
components) plus two independent four-step physical-limit fits. All derivative
fits use h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]; p ranges from 1.991416646 to
2.002020080, with R2 at least 0.999994972436. No failed steps, error floors or
symmetry-copied finite-difference values are removed. Original Richardson and
component thresholds are retained. Full raw measurements follow below.

The native Python/common-driver/ASE/canonical-and-compatibility-CLI suite
passes on a moving finite-nucleus water system with nonzero complex SOC,
including response order four, an independent generalized dense projector,
Gaussian nuclear energy and dimensional unit conversion. Supplied-matrix
behavior remains accepted. All explicit Python/ASE public declarations are
also checked against their descriptions/signatures in existing
`docs/python-api.md`; the aligned calculation tables are in the existing Rust, CLI and Python/ASE manuals.

This closes the finite-nucleus and zero-field restricted-kinetic-balance
one-electron integral connection. It does not close restricted magnetic
balance/London spinor integrals, interacting no-pair Dirac-Coulomb SCF/XC,
periodic Dirac references or their complete physical response. Those remain
in R049 and are not inferred from this component's acceptance.

For order n, the fit compares n*c_n with a central difference of the independent lower factorial-normalized coefficient c_(n-1); the actual derivative is n!*c_n. This constant normalization does not alter the fitted power.

### Continuum magnetic-translation nuclear operator acceptance

All 420 four-step fits passed for Fourier, bilinear kinetic and three
kinetic-momentum operators: seven crystal metrics, physical 1D/2D/3D
boundaries and nuclear orders one through four. The oracle uses closed
complex Gaussian means/covariances and explicit translation enumeration,
independent of the production Hermite, normalization/contraction and jet
recurrences. Every ordered matrix element is measured independently;
nonzero-wave vertices are not Hermitianized. The accepted primitive-shell
oracle is an s-pair subset. The existing s/p magnetic boundary/gauge and
spatial derivative gates also pass after sharing the production operator.
The full eight-test magnetic SCF regression passed, including interacting
relaxed amplitude response and physical time-reversal checks.

These coefficients supply only moving one-electron operators. They do not
alone establish relaxed periodic nuclear force constants, electric Berry
bias, general functional components or finite-q DFPT. The interacting
finite-torus nuclear provider is being accepted separately.

### Initial periodic magnetic fourth-energy difference failure

The first finite-Gamma point-nuclear HF and custom range-exchange/SOC
acceptance run passed the order-1..3 energy fits but failed the quartic
energy-only fit. Fine fourth differences amplify the independently
recomputed SCF energy roundoff. At h=0.0075 the error is about 1.5e-5,
whereas the h=0.03 error is 2.3e-6 (HF) or 1.4e-5 (range exchange).
No error floor is applied and none of these steps is deleted. An independent
fixed-density Hellmann-Feynman/Pulay slope, without any density-response
solve, is added to check higher orders on an interval with resolved errors.
The original 2e-6 Richardson gate and 0.05 exponent/0.9999 fit gates remain.
This physical nuclear provider is not accepted until the additional
independent slope fits and public-route checks pass.

### Relaxed 3D finite-flux nuclear response: complete-density oracle

The full complex-density response through nuclear order four passes eight
independent point-source finite-Gamma SCF energy/variational-force fits:
HF and custom full/range exchange with generated nuclear SOC. The static
field carries one flux quantum through the cubic magnetic face. Geometry,
source Ewald, complex overlap, kinetic/contact, Coulomb/full/range exchange,
Zeeman and nuclear SOC all follow the same displacement. Independent
Hellmann-Feynman/Pulay slopes use no density-response solve. The initial
quartic energy-only cancellation failures remain recorded separately.
All coarse energy Richardson checks retain their 2e-6 gate; no failed fine
energy points are discarded. The resolved quartic force interval is
[0.03,0.0225,0.015,0.0075]. Exponents are 1.999297739..2.025293208,
minimum R2=0.999937253242 and maximum Richardson=2.3651973372895707e-8.

This full-density result is also the oracle for the separately tested
2n+1 energy-only implementation. The current public driver/units,
low-order stationary energy and complete-density agreement are accepted
only when their own tests pass. This is not magnetic-BZ integration,
1D/2D source response, electric Berry bias, arbitrary-q DFPT, semilocal/
nonlocal or correlated PT2 acceptance.

## Part 10: Implemented, not yet validated

### Implemented, not yet validated

The calculations of this section compile and are connected to Rust, the
CLI, native Python and ASE. Initially their acceptance files had not been
run. Subsequent measured subsets are recorded in the acceptance sections
below and in the two coverage ledgers; the existence of an acceptance
file alone does not establish numerical acceptance. Unmeasured combinations
remain pending. Finite differences in these files are validation only.

#### Periodic path response

A k mesh is sampled at the Gamma point of its supercell, where the Bloch
sums are real. `periodic::path_series::lattice_series` gives the Taylor
coefficients, along a path of displacements, Lagrangian strain
`F(t) = (1 + 2 t eta)^(1/2)`, reduced electric field and scalar probes, of
the lattice sums of the overlap and kinetic integrals, of the Ewald sums of
the Coulomb terms with the compact/diffuse split of the production code, of
the minimum-image exchange tensor and of the Becke weights and orbital
values on the periodic grid. The reference is converged again on the
functional of these series, and the difference to the production energy is
reported (`series_reference_energy_difference`). The transported-frame
recursion of the molecular nuclear Taylor driver then gives the energy
through order `2k + 1` from the response through order `k`. A uniform
field couples through the single-point Berry phase
`-Omega E.P = sum_a (E.a_a)/(2 pi) [sum_s Im ln det(1 + D_s dQ_a) - ionic]`.
Assumptions: insulating, neutral, all-electron cells; the dense Coulomb
tensor of the supercell is held in memory for every order; electric-field
responses are clamped-ion. Acceptance files: `p105_lattice_force_constants`,
`p106_lattice_strain_paths`, `p107_lattice_electric_field`.

Measured `p105_lattice_force_constants` acceptance for the Gamma-point
directional cubic derivative uses [0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01] Bohr and errors
[2.163853060298815e-3, 5.421457052582068e-4,
1.356136680865372e-4, 3.39083066525081e-5] in the reported atomic units.
The fitted exponent is 1.998664, R^2 is 0.99999988 and the Richardson
defect is 9.360e-9. The acoustic residual is 1.776e-14, reference-energy
difference is 1.344e-11 Hartree and response residual is 2.415e-11.
Existing acceptance thresholds are unchanged. This measures one cubic
direction, not a full quartic tensor or arbitrary-q acceptance.

#### Commensurate wave vectors

Scalar probes `cos(q.r)` and `sin(q.r)` of the supercell give the density
response and `1/eps(q) = 1 + 4 pi chi/q^2`. The transverse cosine and sine
current operators at the same wave vector give the orbital response. The
uniform-vector-potential sum rule supplies the finite-basis diamagnetic
term. The nuclear shielding of a cell is `(1/q) d2E/(da dm)` for a
wave centred on the nucleus and the Ewald lattice of its magnetic dipole
images; the `G = 0` term is left out, so the value excludes the
shape-dependent bulk magnetization. The scalar density and NMR shielding
checks in `p109_commensurate_response` and `p111_periodic_nmr_shielding`
test physical limits. Independent four-step fits for those observables
remain open.

Both RKS orbital regressions in `p109_commensurate_response` pass. The
SVWN5/STO-3G chain with a `4 x 1 x 1` mesh reports
`[-1.220993768620e-4, -2.660957876482e-6]` at reduced `q=(0.25,0,0)` and
`[-5.231275487288e-5, -2.817253595340e-6]` at `q=(0.5,0,0)` in atomic
units. The independent spectral check uses the separate compact H2
fixture below.

At this real spin-restricted LDA reference, the first-order density
from an orbital-current perturbation is imaginary, so the Hartree and

units and records the central-difference exponent, fit quality, error

##### Meta-GGA current response at finite q

For a real collinear Gamma reference, the imaginary first-order density
changes the paramagnetic current and leaves the real density, gradient and
conventional kinetic density stationary at first order. The gauge-invariant
kinetic density `tau_A - |j_A|^2/(2 rho)` cancels the explicit vector
potential pointwise. Its current-current derivative contributes
`-v_tau |delta j|^2/(2 rho)` to the quadratic energy. The implementation
evaluates the weighted coefficient on the stationary lattice grid and
shares the blocked AO current contraction with the molecular magnetic
response. Full and range-separated exchange use the same ordered pair
contraction as the zero-field reference.

The skew H2 setup above was repeated with TPSS on the same `2 x 1 x 1`
Gamma supercell. The restricted reference energy is
`-1.7000335067296153` Hartree per supercell. CLI, native Python and ASE
agree on the units and all six response values. Explicit UKS on this
closed-shell fixture agrees within `5.5e-19` in either susceptibility
component. The maximum reported relative response residual across these
routes is `4.214e-16`. The independent finite-field spinor SCF turns
off SOC and cancels the spin Zeeman Fourier source with the spin-field
control. At zero bias its energy is `-1.7000335021074486` Hartree per
supercell. All 48 displaced references converge, with maximum fresh
orbital residual `5.751e-15` Hartree and maximum spin-density
defect `1.333e-15`.

##### Fixed-mesh periodic spinor density kernel

The dimensional spinor backend applies the analytic SCF Fock differential
to Hermitian density changes. Hartree reuses the fine SCF quadrature and
its pair cache. Full-range and long-range exchange act on all four Pauli
densities. The local spin-density kernel includes the rotation of the
magnetization axis and its isotropic zero-magnetization limit.

`periodic_spinor_density_kernel` perturbs the density of LiH in a skew
3D Gamma cell with rows `(7.1, 0.3, -0.2)`, `(-0.4, 8.3, 0.7)` and
`(0.2, -0.6, 8.9)` Bohr. The Cartesian Li and H positions are
`(0.17, -0.29, 0.33)` and `(2.89, 0.24, -0.18)` Bohr. There is one s
primitive per atom, with exponents `0.61` and `0.83` Bohr^-2. The grid
uses level 1, AO cutoff 12 Bohr and `grid_weight_cutoff=0`. The test
combines SVWN5 with exact-exchange coefficients `0.18` (full range) and
`0.29` (long range with omega `0.31` Bohr^-1) to exercise both contractions
at a prescribed noncollinear density.

All 136 independent entries of the 16-coordinate Hermitian density
Hessian pass the central-difference fit over `[0.048, 0.032, 0.024, 0.016]`.
The exponent range is `1.945218–2.002445`, minimum R^2 is `0.99991124`,
and C ranges from `1.014e-5` to `2.147e-2`. The largest raw error at
`0.016` is `5.477e-6` Hartree and the largest Richardson defect is
`1.242e-8` Hartree. Maximum reciprocity defect is `4.302e-16` Hartree.
In the test's orthonormal density coordinates, entries `[0,0]` and `[0,7]`
are `0.01591767115982066` and `0.1618451826137481` Hartree. These fits
exercise a fixed-mesh Fock differential. Coupled orbital susceptibility
with spinor sources at finite q remains a separate calculation.
All eight `p83_spinor_reference` regressions pass, including collinear
limits and spin rotation of the noncollinear Fock.

##### Coupled periodic spinor orbital current

For a 3D insulating Gamma supercell, the spinor solve retains the full
complex occupied/empty space. The orbital vertices are the cosine and
sine transverse Fourier components of `(p.A+A.p)/2` and the uniform
comparator. They share the field-SCF AO current integrals. The static
operator response supplies energy second derivatives; one half converts
them to the quadratic coefficients. Each coefficient is divided by the
number of primitive cells. For the two field axes, the phase-averaged
susceptibility is `-4*(P2-U2/2)/(volume*|q|^2)`, with `P2` the mean of
cosine and sine coefficients and `U2` the uniform comparator. The maxima
of the unscaled imaginary response and reciprocity defects are reported
before taking the symmetric transverse matrices.

The HeH+ fixture uses primitive lattice rows `(4.4, 0.17, -0.31)`,
`(0.31, 6.0, 0.26)`, and `(-0.19, 0.38, 6.5)` Bohr. He and H sit at
`(0.17, -0.21, 0.34)` and `(1.63, 0.08, 0.16)` Bohr. Each atom has one
Gaussian s primitive with exponent `0.9` for He and `0.72` for H in
Bohr^-2. SVWN5 uses two repeats of the first lattice vector with reduced
`q=(0.5, 0, 0)` and uniform background charge compensation. A fixed
noncollinear local spin field has real Fourier coefficient
`(0.05, -0.01, 0.04)` and imaginary coefficient `(0.02, 0.045, -0.03)`
at that wave vector. The orbital perturbations leave this reference
operator fixed. The overlap, partition and XC AO cutoffs are `6`, `8`
and `10` Bohr, respectively. All fits use zero grid-weight cutoff.

With angular pruning, grid level 2 gives a charge quadrature defect of
`2.01744e-4` electrons although the orbital residual is `3.970e-16`
Hartree. Pruned level 9 still gives `1.60358e-4` electrons. Switching
only angular pruning off gives `3.53134e-6` electrons at level 2 and
`2.83855e-6` at level 9. The unpruned test keeps the `1e-5` electron
criterion and uses the same level-2 radial rule.

`periodic_spinor_orbital_current` uses 72 individually relaxed SCFs at
signed amplitudes of magnitude `0.08`, `0.04`, `0.02` and `0.01`.
The finite-field energy derivative includes the quadratic contact
operator. The expectation of that contact at zero field is removed
before comparing with the coupled paramagnetic coefficients. A field
along the normalized sum of the two polarizations supplies the mixed
entry. All nine independent entries pass in the first interval. The
minimum R^2 is `0.999999995731`, maximum Richardson defect across the

Hartree per supercell. The largest cross product of two AO-diagonal
Pauli spin density vectors is `2.316e-4`.

##### Projected GGA and meta-GGA current kernel

The orbital response reuses the SCF's complex AO collocation and its
adjoint. The projected density Hessian maps the first variation of each
Pauli density, gradient, kinetic density and current to the variation
of the XC Fock. At finite magnetization the analytic angular kernel is
refined against the operator tolerance using the grid-weighted sum of
the AO bounds. The point Taylor evaluator covers the derivative
boundaries shared with other spinor response calculations.

At zero spin descriptors the spin blocks have identical curvature and
the mixed charge/spin blocks vanish by angular averaging. The single
projected evaluation agrees with the independent full spin-angle rule
for all 256 PBE and all 1,024 TPSS and M06-L matrix entries. Their
maximum absolute differences are `2.221e-16`, `1.666e-16` and
`1.277e-14`. The point has density `0.7`, Cartesian gradient
`(0.12, -0.21, 0.29)`, kinetic density `0.42` and current
`(0.032, -0.018, 0.026)` in atomic units. [Point timing](performance.md#spinor-xc-kernel-at-zero-spin)

For each projected spin density, the changes of the momentum
descriptors under an explicit vector potential are `j_A = j + rho A`
and `tau_A = tau + j.A + rho |A|^2/2`. The corrections cancel in the
gauge-invariant kinetic descriptor. Thus the external amplitude enters
the spinor orbital perturbation through the one-electron current and
diamagnetic vertices, while the response of the zero-field XC current
to the density perturbation enters the coupled Fock.

The same HeH+ geometry and unpruned grid used above also give insulating
closed-shell GKS references with PBE and TPSS at zero spin bias. For each
functional, `periodic_spinor_orbital_current` independently relaxes 72
signed external fields. It fits all nine entries at amplitudes
`[0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01]`, including the mixed transverse direction.
The minimum R^2 is `0.99999999652` for PBE and `0.99999999729` for TPSS.
The largest Richardson defects are `6.181e-12` and `5.167e-12`,
respectively. Maximum orbital residuals over the displaced calculations
are `1.038e-15` and `1.454e-15` Hartree. The TPSS check independently
collocates the explicit covariant momentum at amplitude `0.04` for
each of the nine sources. The largest field-energy derivative
difference is `1.388e-16` in atomic units.

omegaB97X-D GKS, noncollinear semilocal end-to-end acceptance, and the
density-dependent nonlocal XC response remain open.

#### Finite magnetic field

The London integrals are entire functions of the field. Their series are
summed at the requested field in the frame of the centroid, the field part
of the Coulomb and exchange matrices comes from one contracted series, and
the semilocal functional is evaluated on the complex London orbitals with
the gauge-invariant kinetic energy density. The gradient differentiates the
centres of the London orbitals, the nuclear terms and the grid with dual
numbers. Acceptance file: `p108_finite_magnetic_field`.

Measured finite-field regression: the molecular translation energy defect
is 1.421e-14 Hartree. The gradient fit over [0.04, 0.03, 0.02, 0.015] Bohr
has errors [2.334193742433155e-4, 1.313085400256181e-4,
5.8362432323211255e-5, 3.282938002852065e-5] Hartree/Bohr,
exponent 1.999854 and R^2 1.00000000. The translation gradient residual is
7.637e-15 Hartree/Bohr. The independent energy fit to the zero-field
magnetizability (-2.41040841 atomic units) over magnetic fields
[0.08, 0.06, 0.04, 0.03] has errors [3.0940950916589216e-3,
1.7357178286410146e-3, 7.699343477982623e-4, 4.3279358508341303e-4],
exponent 2.005341 and R^2 0.99999953. The separate open-shell OH Zeeman
regression failed because its preparatory zero-field PBE SCF did not
converge in 150 iterations. The final finite-field SCF was not reached;
the failure is retained as a regression record. The direct London-metric
core initializer now removes that prerequisite. A subsequent run exposed
another root cause: an axial molecule has zero London phases, so its
physical diamagnetic polynomial terminates at B^2. Testing that retained
coefficient as a truncation error rejected an exact polynomial. The code
now checks both of the first two omitted orders at the unchanged bound.
The original OH Zeeman test subsequently passes with shift
5.0057982609e-3 Hartree, equal to its analytic spin value at reported
precision. The one-electron terminating-polynomial test gives exactly zero
omitted tail and a Zeeman defect of 1.302e-17 Hartree.

`bfield_initial_guess=core` starts directly in the actual London metric;
`zero-field` requires the converged zero-field seed, and the default `auto`
may use the core seed only after a zero-field convergence failure. Requested
stability following is never skipped. With no converged zero-field
reference, `energy` is null; `field_energy` and `converged` describe the
computed field state. Core and warm seeds on the H2 acceptance fixture
give energy difference 2.221e-16 Hartree. Its independent gradient fit over
[0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005] Bohr gives errors
[4.0836971354674123e-4, 1.0202947859550004e-4,
2.5503437452667477e-5, 6.3756135056936e-6] Hartree/Bohr,
p=2.000372609, R^2=0.999999990678 and Richardson defect 3.279e-10.

#### Two-component states

`response::spinor` converges a molecular two-component state with the
one-electron spin-orbit operator in its Fock matrix on the generic spinor
SCF, and solves the coupled response of its spinors with complex
amplitudes. Coulomb and exact exchange act on the whole spinor density;
every density-functional term is the collinear functional of the two
spin-diagonal blocks, in the reference and in the kernel. Periodic spin
spirals are seeded by the Zeeman field of the spiral in the supercell that
holds it and converged again without the seed; the chirality-odd
spin-orbit energy is the half difference of the nuclear spin-orbit energy
of the two chiralities, the second obtained from the first by a rotation
of every spin. Acceptance files: `p112_magnetoelectric_and_berry_dipole`
(physical limits only, fits owed), `p113_spin_spiral_and_dmi`,
`p114_spinor_polarizability`.

#### Restricted open-shell and spin-flip surfaces

In the transported frame a restricted open-shell state is a pair of
orthogonal projectors on the closed and on the open orbitals. Idempotency
and orthogonality fix every block of a Taylor coefficient except the
closed-open, closed-virtual and open-virtual rotations, which solve
`sum_s [F_s, D_s] = 0` on the orbital Hessian of the reference. The
Hessian follows from second-order energy coefficients of the Cartesian
directions and of their pair sums. For a mixed-reference spin-flip state
the rotations are solved at every order, the moving projectors give
orthonormal orbitals of each class, the spin-flip matrices are assembled
per Taylor order from the Kohn-Sham blocks and the projected kernel
responses (exact exchange and the non-collinear kernel as series on the
moving grid), and the eigenvalue of the channel matrix follows from
non-degenerate perturbation theory. Assumptions: gas phase, all-electron,
integer occupations, the Coulomb integral series in memory; a root within
1e-6 Hartree of another root of its channel is refused. Acceptance files:
`p115_roks_hessian`, `p116_mrsf_derivatives`.

The measured `p115_roks_hessian` regression passes the one-electron
restricted/unrestricted Hessian limit (maximum difference 1.027e-15
Hartree/Bohr^2). Both OH tests fail at the restricted open-shell reference
SCF after 150 iterations, before a derivative fit can be measured. The
four-step OH fit and path-gradient acceptance remain pending; their
existing thresholds have not been changed.

### ROKS common-orbital fallback: implementation awaiting acceptance

Phase B adds an optional constrained Newton fallback to
`scf::roks::run_roks_with_orbitals` for near-converged or stagnant DIIS.
The common spatial frame preserves closed/open/virtual occupations.
For spin occupations n_s and antisymmetric generator K, d_s=[K,n_s].
The exact symmetric exponential-coordinate energy curvature uses
`1/2 [n_s,[F_s,K]] + 1/2 [[K,n_s],F_s] + [n_s,G_s(d)]`, including the
nonstationary connection terms and the complete common density kernel.
Pair coefficients are twice the corresponding upper-triangle entries.
The existing truncated Newton iteration and orthogonal exponential are
shared with ordinary SCF; denominator floors affect only preconditioning.
Actual trial energies satisfy Armijo descent, and a non-descent direction
is not accepted. The existing SCF energy/orbital criteria are retained.
An unavailable optional kernel retains the previous DIIS route.

The implementation and Rust unit acceptance were written, but their
fmt/clippy/compile and molecular p115/p118 runs have NOT executed:
automatic approval review repeatedly failed because its selected model was at
capacity. This is an execution blocker, not a numerical pass or an unsafe
action determination. The user chose to resume these commands after the
review service recovers. The earlier all-feature clippy pass predates this
new ROKS change and must not be quoted as validation of the current edit.
T024 and the other ROKS combinations therefore remain unvalidated.

The following six fits check an independent small-matrix derivation only,
not the production Rust implementation. A three-orbital model has common
occupations [2,1], two distinct one-body matrices and energy
`sum_s Tr(h_s P_s) + 0.2 [Tr(B(P_alpha+P_beta))]^2`.
An independent closed SO(3) Rodrigues formula supplies the finite rotations.
Each first/second derivative uses four dimensionless angles [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01].
No sample or failed measurement is floored or discarded. Rust's added test
uses the production Hessian against the same independent energy formula,
checks raw bilinear symmetry, and still needs to run.

## Part 11: Acceptance run records (chronological)

Kernel-only validation and preliminary performance measurements for the
arithmetic-preserving Hermite tensor storage sweep are recorded in
[Numerical kernel performance and validation](performance.md). The 163,800
bitwise comparisons pass both in the isolated source harness and against the
newly rebuilt Python-feature library. Affected integral/HF/periodic-Hartree
and native Python/ASE/CLI regressions pass; the existing faer/Rayon matrix
contracts pass scalar-oracle checks in sequential/shared-pool settings.
Full-suite certification and end-to-end timing remain unrun. The record
preserves an exploratory high-order reverse-axis recurrence failure and a
bounded independent high-precision diagnosis without claiming general
conditioning is resolved.

### Acceptance runs of 2026-10-19 (first group)

Release build without link-time optimization, `DFT_RS_STRICT_UNITS=1`, one
test thread. Numbers are the printed raw values; no threshold was changed.

- `p121_exafs_double_scattering`: closed-form collinear double scattering
  9.975e-18, right-angle double scattering 0, the signal without angle
  tables equals the single-scattering one. No derivative is involved.
- `p122_xanes_core_hole`: the first run failed: explicit `core_orbitals`
  were passed to the beta channel of a one-electron molecule, which has no
  beta electron ("core orbital 0 is not an occupied orbital"). The `xanes`
  driver now keeps for the beta channel only the indices that beta
  occupies. Rerun: one-electron relaxation shift 2.220e-16 Hartree
  (ionization 1.0826953691 Hartree); water oxygen 1s relaxed ionization
  19.906435 Hartree, shift -0.335436 Hartree, smallest core-hole overlap
  0.934376. No derivative is involved.
- `p123_hyperfine_dipolar`: trace 5.684e-14, rotation defect 1.248e-10,
  hydrogen atom 1.137e-31 (repeats the record above).
- `p117_london_rotatory_strengths`: origin independence 1.529e-11,
  translation 6.052e-12, common-origin Tamm-Dancoff limit 1.605e-17
  (velocity 3.816e-17), mirror plane 3.276e-16; under the same translation
  the common-origin strengths change by 2.643e-3. The independent four-step
  fit against the frequency-dependent London optical rotation near a pole
  is still owed: no London optical rotation exists yet, so T031 stays
  partially validated.
- `p120_g_tensor_london`: origin independence 2.059e-14 and the one-centre
  limit (exact) pass; the translation test failed with 3.046e-3 on the
  hydroxyl radical. Its 2Pi ground state has a degenerate pi pair and the
  translated SCF converged to a rotated hole: energies 7.4e-9 Hartree
  apart, g changed by 7.6e2 ppm, and by 613 ppm with a common origin moved
  along with the molecule. London shieldings of water, closed shell and
  unrestricted, were translation invariant to 1e-7 ppm in the same check,
  and the unrestricted Hartree-Fock magnetic response of that OH diverged
  (relative residual 0.47). The test now uses the water cation (2B1).
- `p126_dynamic_response_save`: the first run failed under strict units:
  the `dynamic.*` report entries had no unit labels. Labels were added.
- `p104_reduced_order`: the cubic contraction against the full reduced
  tensor agrees to 7.661e-15 over 109 paths, but this part alone took
  about 16 minutes for H3+ in STO-3G. The run was stopped to optimize the
  code. One direction of `reduced_order_taylor` (H3+, STO-3G, 25822 grid
  points) took 0.015 s with Hartree-Fock and 2.125 s (one solve) or
  2.527 s (two solves) with PBE, so the moving grid dominated. The runtime
  Taylor arithmetic (`response::series`) now keeps every coefficient array
  in one flat arena and writes each result in place, without an allocation
  per operation: 1.107 s and 1.294 s, energy coefficients bitwise
  unchanged. The moving-grid AO series contract the radial factor and its
  slope once per shell instead of per primitive and spherical component:
  0.566 s and 0.819 s, coefficients unchanged to 1e-17. The response solve
  and the reduced-order energy now share one moving-geometry series built
  through order `2 solved + 1`.

### Alpha.2 verification after the Berry overlap repair

The corrected actual-overlap metric passed the unchanged HF/PBE/TPSS/PBE0
finite-bias alpha/beta/gamma acceptance: twelve independent four-step fits
on [0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025], p=1.997631500..1.999599989,
minimum R2=0.999999445284 and maximum Richardson error
7.901348290928e-10. The independent finite-bias HF nuclear order-1..4
energy/force regressions also passed on seven steps. Every original coarse
and finer diagnostic interval remains below; only the explicitly labelled
acceptance interval is certified. No error floor or relaxed gate is used.

The release candidate passes warning-as-error release checks for every
Cargo target with default features and with Python features. The selected
Rust term-oracle/component regressions pass 11 tests across six files,
and the common Berry unit subset passes five tests. Python/ASE/public-driver
regressions pass 35 tests with each CLI executable name, with Python
warnings treated as errors. These include all five named double-hybrid
energy recipes, explicit thermodynamic potentials, supplied-space Nambu,
pairing and no-pair components, and the phase/metric translation checks.

The PEP 517 pip wheel builds using the existing dependencies. Installed
into an otherwise empty environment outside the source tree, the console
prints `dft-rs 0.2.0-alpha.2` and metadata reports `0.2.0a2`. Native and CLI
HF/STO-3G H2 at exactly 1.4 Bohr both give -1.1167143251757703 Hartree,
matching the existing independent frozen energy oracle. Author name and
email remain unchanged. The installed package requires neither NumPy nor
ASE for this core calculation.

The longer all-route finite-bias nuclear tensor repeat has now passed
with both executable names (3973.58 s and 5182.88 s). Native Python, ASE
atomic/physical and CLI Hessian/contracted cubic/quartic reports agree;
maximum fresh response residual is 5.180339330624797e-16. This post-release
repeat is separate from the frozen archive and its native seven-step checks. The entire Rust/Python regression
catalogue was not rerun to completion for this milestone. No Windows or
other-platform runtime validation is inferred from these Linux tests.
Source and packaged-content portability audits remain separate checks.
The complete accepted program and all unaccepted CSV combinations remain
open; no functional/reference matrix cells are promoted by these repeats.

### Reduced-order baseline repeat: two measured route-comparison tests

The pre-ROKS-fallback release binary passes its two original p104 tests in 2626.60 s. The full run remains expensive; the earlier moving-grid microbenchmark does not establish this full-suite speedup. No accuracy threshold changed. The largest cubic tensor versus complete mixed response errors are 4.863e-14 (HF), 8.882e-15 (PBE) and 8.882e-16 (PBE0) Hartree/Bohr^3. The PBE cubic/full-tensor contraction defect is 9.215e-15; the quartic/complete-mixed-response contraction defect is 3.886e-16 Hartree/Bohr^4.

These are response-route comparisons, not independent finite-difference order fits or independently evaluated tensor-permutation asymmetry. A third test was added afterwards: HF/PBE/PBE0 reduced cubic derivatives versus independently converged displaced SCF energies at four path steps [0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01], with all errors, p, R2, C, log RMSE, Richardson and response residuals. Those fits have NOT compiled or run. T138 records the measured route equivalence and the outstanding independent derivative fit separately; it is not fully accepted.

The binary predates the new ROKS edit and cannot certify the current source build. The already authorized batch then proceeds to p103, p102 and p226; inspect their individual summaries before claiming success.

### ROKS rational energy-series oracle and metric covariance

An independent stdlib rational-arithmetic energy-series calculation uses the explicit nonstationary three-orbital model of the ROKS section. Multiplication of the orbital energy series, without the production commutator formula, gives

```text
gradient = [-53/250, -11/250, 233/1250]
Hessian = [[247/125, 329/2500, 357/2500],
           [329/2500, 924/125, -501/2500],
           [357/2500, -501/2500, 7107/3125]]
```

Nine directions retain exactly equal energy coefficients through order two after an invertible nonorthogonal AO transformation, with `C^T S C = I`, `h_AO=C^-T h_MO C^-1` and `P_AO=C P_MO C^T`. The added Rust unit compares every Hessian column independently against these coefficients and checks the retraction metric. It still awaits compilation and execution. The six four-angle fits above validate only the independent mathematical derivation until their production Rust counterparts run. p115/p118 now also print the fit prefactor and log RMSE; p115 prints raw response, projector, stationarity and reference defects without changing any gate.

### Phase B spin coupling baseline and the corrected pair-axis gate

The pre-edit p103 baseline passes three tests (649.61 s). H2 HF/PBE Fermi-contact couplings agree with an independent one-amplitude triplet-Hessian expression to relative errors 2.156e-16/8.006e-16. Water contact-only/full-route and isotropic frame checks pass, but the original pair-order comparison took the smaller per-element direct/transposed error. The corrected check determines the transpose from the pair labels and has not compiled/run. The backend preserves the supplied nucleus order, rejects duplicate nuclei and reports the pair-axis convention through the common driver. New native/Python generic/ASE/CLI component-wise and independently reversed-pair checks are written but unrun. Independent four-step coupling derivative fits, open-shell and relativistic combinations remain pending.

The pre-edit p103 H2/STO-3G SVWN5 vertical-gradient and vertical-Hessian sum-rule cases pass: retained-state sum 0.99870339 at 2000 K for both models; vertical-Hessian zero-temperature sum 1.00000000. This validates normalization in these three cases, not general vibronic band shapes, additional molecules or all functional classes.

The production physical kernel is unchanged by the pair-contract correction. The source comment previously claimed `M < N` while the implementation actually followed the requested nucleus order. The new report makes that convention explicit and rejects repeated indices. The new Rust comparison selects one transpose for each labelled pair, with the original 1e-7 relative threshold retained. The additional public test checks each FC/SD/PSO/DSO component, the same units, independently reversed order and default CLI SCF stderr. None of these post-build edits has compiled or run. ### Merged-source acceptance: resolved local Hessian interval and magnetic kernel

Molecular CASSCF and translated/fully translated LDA/GGA MC-PDFT, hybrid fraction and state-specific/L/CMS/XMS energies are implemented. Current p230/p231/p232 pass 8/5/1 tests: nine frozen total-energy cases (maximum PDFT defect 1.475e-5 Hartree) and twenty independent term comparisons (maximum 4.418e-7 Hartree). Analytic state-specific nuclear gradients/Hessians include complete orbital/CI response, including state-averaged references. The local off-diagonal Hessian fit fails on grid 3 even with tighter orbital convergence; grid 6 resolves the original wide interval with p=1.924921914, R2=0.999178980426; all failed and additional fine steps are retained. Smooth LDA and closed-active GGA gradient/Hessian four-step subsets pass. Native/generic Python, atomic/ASE energy-length units and canonical CLI comparisons including gradients/Hessians pass; maximum public path stationarity 3.641000695387e-12 Hartree, solve residual 3.379567348010e-13. Open-active GGA has small-step/Richardson checks only and still owes a resolved four-step fit. Multistate derivatives, nonorthogonal CI, spin projection, meta-GGA translation and periodic cells remain pending. MC-PDFT gradient/Hessian state axes follow state_total (reference-state order), not the sorted pdft_energies; CASSCF follows cas_energies.

The latest release/Python build passes 24 selected integration tests,
16 affected library unit tests, the independent reduced-cubic fit, and
eight Python tests (six public-route cases and two metadata checks)
with warnings treated as errors.
All-feature library/binary/test clippy passes with `-D warnings`.
These are selected gates, not a full-suite or full-program completion.

The magnetic regression was caused by trial-density-dependent direct
screening: rescaling a Krylov vector changed the operator. Reusing
`JkEngine::with_reference_screening` fixes that nonlinearity. The
magnitude-only symmetry-zero shortcut is removed. Both exactly axial
and 1e-13-Bohr tilted HF retain their nonzero sources, require a real
MINRES iteration, satisfy the fresh relative residual and agree with
in-core density responses within 1e-11. No physical denominator,
acceptance threshold or right-hand side is regularized.

The failed local on-top fits above are not erased. Tightening the
orbitals left them unchanged. A separate level-3 scan of all steps

## Correlated TDA transition API and kernel acceptance

`response::correlated_tda::correlated_tda_states(parent, basis, scf, eri,
problem, pt2, coefficients, nstates, memory_mb)` returns
`CorrelatedTdaResult`. The parent is the existing generic `TdaSolver`;
`problem` and `pt2` are the same stationary spin-resolved full-Coulomb PT2
objects used for energy. Reference occupations/energies must agree.
The combined parent-resolvent and tensor workspace is checked before
allocation. Semicanonical occupied-virtual gaps remain physical; no
within-space or response denominator is floored. Real collinear RKS and
UKS references are supported by this model; exactly degenerate parent
blocks use symmetric metric transport, including off-diagonal overlap
terms, rather than independent scalar normalization. The entire block is
returned if a requested root count cuts through it. Individual residue
vectors within a degenerate block use that normalization gauge; subspace
observables are the invariant quantities of this truncation.

The result contains `states` (including all three electric, momentum and
angular-momentum components), `parent_energies`, `energy_corrections`,
`singles_correction_norms`, signed `doubles_norms`, `pole_residuals`,
`normalization_defects`, `smallest_double_denominators`, `parent_residual`
and `model`. Pole residuals are freshly evaluated second-order coefficient
equations, not residuals of a fully resummed frequency-dependent response.
Normalization defects are also through second order. Strengths use the
reported corrected energies and moments in the existing line-strength
formulas, without re-expanding their products. Large correction norms
remain visible; numerical convergence does not establish perturbative or
chemical accuracy. The model retains the adiabatic parent kernel and a
normal-ordered residual interaction, and is separate from the stationary
correlated static-response and London-origin models.

The same `ecd-spectrum` / `ecd_spectrum` / `get_ecd_spectrum` entry accepts
existing `double_hybrid_model`, `pt2_same_spin`, `pt2_opposite_spin` and
`pt2_memory_mb` controls. `nstates`, `td_spin`, `td_tolerance`, broadening
and energy-window conventions are unchanged. The report adds the
`pt2_transition_*` diagnostics and correlated ground-energy decomposition.
Native transition dipoles are e*bohr, momentum coefficients 1/bohr and
angular-momentum coefficients dimensionless (the real coefficient of
the anti-Hermitian r-cross-gradient operator). ASE converts the first
two to e*Angstrom and 1/Angstrom. Existing rotatory atomic/cgs and spectral
line conventions are unchanged. Coupled double poles are named errors;
no causal resummation or distinct-target excitation kernel is inferred.

The independent complete-determinant oracle in
`tools/oracle/pt2_propagator.py` freezes all 452 nonstructural A/B/metric,
singles-doubles coupling and electric/time-odd property-gradient
derivatives. Production contractions agree with the direct commutators
within 2e-14. Every derivative fits four signed interaction strengths
[0.16,0.12,0.08,0.06], p=1.991859..2.012248,
minimum R2=0.99999757; no failed interval is removed or floored.
The weighted coupling is adjoint under the SS/OS pair metric, and signed
coefficient linearity passes. The molecular `p258_correlated_ecd` run
passes every HF/SVWN5/PBE/TPSS/PBE0/synthetic-learned RKS H4 and UKS H5
case, with zero-correlation transition-vector defects at most 3.609e-16
and coefficient-linearity defects at most 4.441e-16. Both electric and
magnetic moments change when PT2 is enabled. B2PLYP water/water-cation
checks also pass. The full dense pole fits and public native/ASE/CLI acceptance pass; these measurements do not upgrade unmeasured combinations.

Additional common-origin PT2 NMR acceptance covers all LDA/GGA RKS H4 and
UKS H5 entries, including every unscaled spin channel and mixed magnetic
contact term. These 810 independent mixed-energy fits bring the accepted
HF/SVWN5/PBE/TPSS/PBE0 total to 2,025. The leading interval is
[0.04,0.03,0.02,0.015] in the dimensionless mixed path parameter; all
printed finer/coarser intervals and failed attempts remain available.

| Additional parent | Complete fits | Accepted p range | Minimum R2 | Failed intervals retained |

| SVWN5 | 405 | 1.800247..2.134919 | 0.99937729 | 243 |

All 80 independent pole-energy/electric/momentum/magnetic transition

The shared complex field provider evaluates the entire global learned graph
and both spin densities on every grid endpoint, with the full density,
gradient and tau-|j|^2/(2 rho) pullback. Owned network scalars cover orders
0..7. Independent forward AD of the energy graph and finite trigonometric
AO phases validates all 18 Hermitian Fock coordinates plus energy through
two coefficient orders. The U(1) coefficient defect is 2.775557561563e-17.

`p255_correlated_nmr` passes 2025 independent London mixed B/nuclear-moment
fits on HF/SVWN5/PBE/TPSS/PBE0 RKS/UKS, in addition to the 2025 earlier
common-origin fits. A synthetic global learned model adds 810 fits across
RKS/UKS and both gauges on the full molecular quadrature. This is provider
extensibility evidence, not trained-model chemical accuracy. Its artificial
five-point SCF failed (residual 0.08771158076942426); that run is retained.

requires an additional asymptotic interval [0.0008,0.0006,0.0004,0.0003],
with a further [0.0003,0.000225,0.00015,0.0001125] interval available.

Exact (x,y) finite-SCF caching keeps both signs as independent evaluations.

## Explicit nonlocal field-model connection, 2026-10-24

VV10 energy and unweighted endpoint potentials now share one scalar-generic
endpoint row in nlc.rs. The real SCF, owned coefficient scalars through
width eight and arbitrary-width runtime fallback evaluate that same body.
The complex field provider reuses its rho/gradient coefficients and the
common complex AO pullback. Finite London SCF uses exact trigonometric AO
phases. Both density endpoints remain variational. The earlier real p29
energy/potential/kernel/high-order regression passes, as do the 38 independent
complex energy/full-Fock fits and complete U(1) coefficient check
(6.606856988584e-20) on the first unified-body build. The final version adds
separate parent/target nonlocal coefficients and is being rechecked with
the coupled molecular suite. Point-kernel acceptance alone does not certify
the public molecular nonlocal magnetic combinations.

The fixed-grid coefficient body reduces exact sparse support before its
scalar evaluation: if every active endpoint contains only powers of t^s,
it evaluates in u=t^s and restores every output coefficient to the original
order. Constant input uses the scalar body; generic paths retain all their
coefficients. The stride uses exact nonzero coefficients of rho and sigma,
never a magnitude threshold or a point-group inference. Requested nonlinear
orders remain intact even when the input density is only linear. Minimal
owned widths two and three avoid padding every low-order operation to four.
The earlier dense mixed-moment timing runs were interrupted before a pass
claim; all measurements and failed intervals are retained. Sparse/dense
two-endpoint coefficients, a nonzero 1e-20 odd coefficient, and independent
even self-pair derivatives through order twelve have added acceptance.
Their measured results and the resumed coupled/public results are tracked
separately; this arithmetic change does not permit copying tensor entries
in the independent acceptance calculations.

`FieldEnergyModel` explicitly composes a target functional, an optional
weighted VV10 term and an optional entire learned graph. The parent and
target may have different nonlocal parameters and coefficients. No parent
auxiliary term is inherited by an explicitly different target. Existing
Rust signatures remain compatibility wrappers; advanced model variants
share the same implementation. The existing common NMR/J drivers construct
the explicit composition from the requested recipe. Custom registered
VV10 target functionals now resolve their declared parameters at driver
configuration, rather than branching a response calculation on its name.
The custom-parent nonlocal metadata also records the actual parent term.

`ScfOptions::nonlocal_grid` defines the same dedicated quadrature for SCF,
gradients/Hessians, spinor/ROKS response, scalar/complex response and target
energies. `vv10_grid_weight_cutoff` defaults to 1e-14 for low-level callers;
the common molecular driver's `grid_weight_cutoff` also applies to this
auxiliary grid. In derivative tests it is zero. The grid level stays
`vv10_grid_level`. Invalid finite/nonnegative weight cutoffs are rejected.
No physical denominator or density is floored by this grid policy; the
pre-existing VV10 vacuum convention is kept separate.

`p260_nonlocal_complex_response` is the new full molecular magnetic
energy-Hessian acceptance for HF/PBE0 RKS/UKS, independently varied
parent/target nonlocal terms and all SS/OS plus explicit nonlocal channels.
It uses independent reconverged finite London SCF, direct occupied-orbital
nonlocal pair energies and direct semicanonical PT2 sums. All 408 independent component/channel fits pass on the measured
RKS/UKS subset. This validates the magnetic energy Hessian, not unmeasured
B/nuclear-moment or nuclear-pair derivatives. Owned/runtime density self-pair derivatives through order
twelve have an additional independent closed-form/24-fit acceptance test.
These density-path limits do not certify molecular rank-twelve tensors.

## Nuclear and electric high-order coverage boundary, 2026-10-25

The next implementation emphasis is complete third/fourth nuclear-coordinate
derivatives and electric response, including RKS/UKS, generic functional
providers, biased references and the orbital/PT2 amplitude terms. Existing
ordinary analytic tensor/pattern providers remain the starting point; a
second implementation of their assembly or response equations is avoided.

The common static beta/gamma and contracted cubic/quartic connections now
reuse the complete orbital/PT2 energy providers. Their measured subsets,
raw diagnostics and remaining full Cartesian, nonlocal nuclear and
reference-space combinations are described in the following section.

## Correlated nuclear/electric high-order connections, 2026-10-25

`amplitude_response_residuals` retains the fresh maximum absolute PT2
equation residual in Hartree. `amplitude_relative_residuals` additionally
reports, per order, the maximum over spin channels of
`||A0 t_n - rhs_n||_2 / ||rhs_n||_2`, where
`rhs_n = g_n - sum_(k=1..n) A_k t_(n-k)`. The full physical equation
is recomputed after the solve. No norm floor or modified denominator is
used: a zero source requires zero residual. High-order convergence applies
the requested dimensionless tolerance to this relative residual while
retaining the unscaled absolute measurement. Large Taylor coefficients
therefore do not fail solely because of the units or source magnitude.

The existing static `beta`/`gamma` entries accept named double hybrids
or a generic parent, optional distinct target and SS/OS coefficients on
integer RKS/UKS references, including `reference_field` electric bias.
They return all 27/81 Cartesian elements from full parent-orbital and
noncanonical amplitude energy coefficients through orders three/four.
The same polarization and tensor-summary helpers are reused. No new
calculation identifier is introduced. `assembly=energy-polarization` names
the actual calculation; `tensor_assembly=projector` remains an accepted
compatibility request. Parent-only variational 2n+1 assembly is not used
for a nonstationary post-SCF target.

Additional tensors are `parent_tensor`, `target_tensor`, `pt2_tensor`,
`pt2_same_spin_alpha_tensor`, `pt2_opposite_spin_tensor`,
`pt2_same_spin_beta_tensor`, `parent_nonlocal_tensor` and
`target_nonlocal_tensor`, in e^3*bohr^3/hartree^2 for beta and
e^4*bohr^4/hartree^3 for gamma. SS/OS tensors are unscaled;
total=target+weighted PT2. Nonlocal tensors are weighted parts already in
their corresponding totals. Target auxiliaries remain explicitly composed.
`energy_permutation_defect`/`intrinsic_permutation_defect` are null and
their comparison counts zero: scalar-energy permutation reuse is not an
independent observed-dipole-leg Maxwell measurement. Native legacy electric
wrappers retain a summary `units` string and authoritative `unit_labels`;
the common driver/CLI returns the labels in `units`.

The existing `cubic-fc-along`/`quartic-fc-along` entries also accept these
correlated collinear references. Every remaining Cartesian matrix element
is returned, with `probe` and optional `second_probe` as leading contraction
patterns. Parent, target, PT2, unscaled SS-alpha/OS/SS-beta and dispersion
matrices use the corresponding prefixes on `contracted_force_constants`.
Units are hartree/bohr^3 or hartree/bohr^4 per dimensionless patterns;
total=target+weighted PT2+dispersion. Parent/target matrices exclude the
separately returned empirical dispersion. The static electric bias is
`reference_field`; the finite-London `field`/`bfield` correlated nuclear
combinations remain separate. This contracted export does not complete the
uncontracted correlated Cartesian rank-three/four API.

All routes retain response, amplitude, projector, stationarity, metric,
particle-number, frame and reference diagnostics. Amplitude/stationarity
and reference defects use Hartree, number defects electrons, frame/metric
defects dimensionless; coefficients use the reported normalized atomic-unit
path coordinates. `pt2_memory_mb` also bounds the high-order integral and
amplitude workspaces. ROKS/ROHF and spinor GKS/GHF correlated constraints,
moving molecular nonlocal nuclear providers for both parent and target, ECP/solvent/RI paths and
finite-frequency correlated kernels retain their own open coverage.

The finite electric reference enters every one-electron dipole coefficient
and the constant nuclear field energy in the shared complex field provider.
`FieldWavefunctionPath::particle_number_coefficients` is raw Tr[S P_s]
minus the constant spin population, shape [path order+1][alpha,beta].
`orbital_metric_defects` independently recomputes the max coefficient
defect of C_s^dagger S C_s=I for every order; both enter the new driver
convergence decision. No finite difference is used in production.

The ASE adapter, native layer and XYZ reader now use the same package

independently validated derivative are different states of implementation.
The presence of one does not certify the others or every Hamiltonian term.

## Common-orbital/spinor tensors and SCF globalization, 2026-10-26

The existing `force-constants` common driver now connects common-orbital
ROKS/ROHF and full complex GKS/GHF energy coefficients to complete cubic
and quartic Cartesian, coordinate-block and pattern exports. They share
the exact multi-channel polarization/cache and empirical-dispersion AD
with the correlated/ordinary providers. The `parent_tensor` and
`dispersion_tensor` channels sum to `tensor`; raw reference, stationarity,
projector, response and unprojected acoustic diagnostics are retained.
The fixed Hermitian AO spinor source is a prescribed operator; this does
not imply its nuclear SOC derivatives or correlated constrained PT2.

`p264_reference_force_tensors` contains 364 cubic and 1365 quartic
unisolvent directions for the C1 H4 cation, three nonzero physical
channels, finite electric bias, zero quadrature cutoff and fresh displaced
SCF analytic-gradient oracles. This is 5187 required component/channel
fits per reference, not one-direction acceptance. The new public suite is
`python/tests/test_reference_force_tensors.py`; public acceptance is still
in progress. HF/semilocal/hybrid provider connections are implemented;
this does not certify every functional or additional Hamiltonian term.

The first closed-limit run refused an empty open-shell class. ROKS now
returns the genuine restricted SCF solution in that limit; the corrected
cubic/quartic coordinate-block comparison passes. The first open tests
failed displaced SCF: ROKS exhausted 500 iterations and GKS retained an
orbital residual 1.066971204e-3. Common-orbital Newton line searches now
use stable finite-density quadratic work for quadratic energy providers.
The same nested-commutator density change is shared with ordinary SOSCF.
The first corrected SCF regression passes eight retained displaced cases
at +/-0.08 and +/-0.16 Bohr, with the original 1e-14 reference gates.
It does not complete the full tensor acceptance.

The full corrected run found a further GKS failure at t=-0.03 Bohr,
generic cubic direction 0 (residual 2.526e-4 after 500 iterations).
Intermittent canonical descent followed by unrestricted CDIIS repeatedly
restored a higher-energy stationary region. Globalization now remains
active after stagnation and also guards CDIIS proposals. A rejected
proposal uses backtracked convex canonical mixing, preserving matrix
occupation bounds and total particle number. Quadratic providers declare
that property through `SpinorEnergyBackend::quadratic_density_energy`;
their exact endpoint Fock work uses compensated complex/k-point products.
Other providers use their actual energy difference. No physical Fock,
occupation law, denominator or final convergence gate is modified.
Fresh physical Fock, number, canonical-consistency and density/energy
tests still decide convergence. The new +/-0.03 cases are retained.

The corrected ROKS cubic run resolved 1091 of 1092 channel fits
(p=1.830361..2.199997, minimum R2=0.99904683); the remaining total
channel, generic 205, showed h^4-dominated cancellation and is not yet
validated. All failed intervals are retained. Quartic tensor generation
then failed raw diagnostics: maximum flag defect 8.185452316e-12 and
acoustic residual 3.698687578e-9 Hartree/Bohr^4. Centered exact homogeneous
polarization and compensated matrix-series convolution now reduce
cancellation; their independent algebra and physical reruns are pending.
Centering is a Taylor-coefficient identity, not production finite differences
or acoustic projection. These failures remain open until measured reruns
pass the unchanged gates.

The final retained displaced-SCF regression passes all 12 cases at
+/-0.08, +/-0.16 and +/-0.03 Bohr, without changing the 500-iteration or
1e-14 reference gates. ROKS needs 8..10 common-orbital iterations (maximum
final residual 1.549e-15); GKS needs 47..280 (maximum final orbital residual
1.342e-15, density change 9.756e-15 and canonical occupation defect
2.220e-15). The previously failing GKS t=-0.03 case converges in 280
iterations, residual 7.857e-16. A persistent energy guard alone had stalled
near floating precision, so globalization now returns to local CDIIS only
after the physical residual falls by a factor 100 from its entry value.
The unchanged final gates still determine convergence; this transition is
not acceptance at a looser residual.

The independent common-orbital rational oracle has maximum gradient,
Hessian and metric defects 5.551115123e-17, 4.440892099e-16 and
2.220446049e-16. The six independent Rodrigues gradient/curvature fits on
h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01] give p=1.999112697..1.999905477,
minimum R2=0.999999947062. Compensated complex multi-k quadratic work
matches the closed polynomial down to h=1e-14 (defect 3.944304526e-31).
The focused quadratic suite passes seven tests and common-orbital suite
two. The final native/ASE/common-driver/canonical-CLI gradient, API,
ledger and Ruff suite passes nine cases in 30.49 s, with strict units and
Python warnings as errors. Both public references reproduce the retained
displaced case; CLI stderr contains iteration energies and residuals.
All-feature library/binary/test Clippy passes with warnings denied;
formatting passes after formatting-only corrections in two existing
files. Complete cubic/quartic acceptance remains a distinct open gate.

Molecular RKS/UKS nuclear paths also connect the shared moving VV10 pair

The production quadratic complex-spinor gradient reuses the real integral

Multicomponent correlation is a sum of independent electron/partner-density
channels. QuantumParticle::correlation_channel selects a channel; particles
in one channel contribute their summed density and every electron potential
and kernel contribution is added. EPC17 and the dilute-positron relaxation
model share this interface. Structured particles describe quantum nuclei,
positrons, positive/negative muons or explicit mass/charge particles. They
remain distinguishable Hartree orbitals, with laboratory COM kinetic energy.
This does not establish identical-particle exchange, intrinsic mass
polarization, photon, periodic or correlated-PT2 multicomponent response.

The positron local model follows [PRL 107, 207402 (2011), Eq. (2)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.207402),
E_ep=int n_+ Delta(r_s(n_-)). Its positive-density low-density limit is
Delta=-0.262005 Hartree; the fit is not the exact RPA high-density limit
below r_s=0.1. Scaled density derivatives and binary exponent bookkeeping
retain finite kernel contractions in dilute AO tails without a density
floor. Exactly absent AO density retains the existing absent-endpoint
convention; a finite-density impurity model is not inferred from this fit.

p281 includes independent Decimal(500) energy, both potentials and all
nonzero two-density Hessian entries at seven density pairs down to n_-=1e-300.
The partner diagonal is identically zero and checked exactly. Sixteen
four-step fits of both kernel rows along two independent density directions
pass on h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01], with no discarded steps or error floor.
All 42 point/term comparisons pass with maximum relative defect
1.273258272116e-15. The first extreme-tail oracle used only 100 digits and lost 2.254e-7 relative
accuracy by cancellation; the 500-digit independent quotient calculation
resolves it without changing a threshold or a production value.

The two-photon annihilation integral evaluates n_-*gamma directly, rather
than an overflowing enhancement multiplied by a vanishing density. The
independent-particle, QMC contact and three polynomial enhancement models
match closed Gaussian-product integrals: maximum contact defect
8.604228440845e-16 and enhanced-contact defect 3.119726699197e-14 Bohr^-3.
The alpha=0 gradient correction is exactly the local model, including dilute
tails; positive alpha uses the same contact model with gradient damping.
The final full-crate p281 acceptance passes all four tests (0.61 s),
including the 16 fits, 42 point/term comparisons, five Gaussian models and

#### Molecular positron orbital stability in a minimal rotation space

The original Davidson subspace limit panics when the coupled rotation space
contains fewer than eight amplitudes. The M06/RKS H2 plus positron case with
one off-centre s Gaussian reproduces this in the common driver. The restart
limit is now bounded by the actual positive dimension. A request for three
roots in the one-dimensional space returns its single curvature
`1.1225583611056680` Hartree. The dense 1x1 Hessian action from a separately
converged reference agrees to the reported precision and the raw eigenvalue
residual is zero. The fixed Rust test passes in 2.99 s.

The frozen-source existing p222 multicomponent regression passes all five
tests. The p223 regression passes five of six tests, but unrestricted TPSS
fails in an electronic frozen-potential SCF (500 iterations, residual
1.883662093344e-4). Its trace alternates residuals near 1.884e-4 and 8.034e-4
while density changes are about 7.85e-17. This invalidates the older aggregate
TPSS geometry claim; it remains implemented but unvalidated until the
physical Fock inconsistency is resolved. No tolerance is relaxed.

The shared energy/Fock orbital globalizer resolves the retained electronic
SCF failures in six RKS/UKS quantum-potential cases (p282): grid level 2,
an independently displaced lmax=1 basis, and grid level 4. Maximum final
electronic orbital/density-map residuals are 8.857688887920e-13 Hartree
and 5.559346725674e-14. All requested inner e/gradient/density tolerances
remain 1e-13/1e-12/1e-12, maximum 500 iterations. Existing p222 (five tests),
p281 (four tests), all 32 retained ROHF/GHF displaced SCFs and all eight
p5 gradient regressions also pass on the shared-SCF build. The native,
ASE and canonical CLI TPSS parent-energy comparison now passes, alongside
the existing HF/LDA/GGA/hybrid/RSH cases. The shared-SCF public aggregate
passes all 50 cases with Python warnings as errors (1087.15 s): native,
ASE, canonical CLI, five independent molecular energy/term oracles,
structured units, reference tensors, API documentation, ledger and lint.
The five-molecule HF set includes H2, LiH, water, phosphine and ferrocene;
maximum energy and individual term defects are 4.547473508865e-12 and
4.047251422890e-11 Hartree. This does not validate the later endpoint
correction or restore the still-open TPSS coupled-Hessian claim.

This exposes a separate TPSS coupled-Hessian discrepancy. With the former
point-weight selection, the retained directional energy-difference fit gives
p=1.850451025521, R2=0.998556991180 and Richardson defect
7.266109415427e-6 Hartree/Bohr^2. At zero weight cutoff the analytic value
changes from 0.193354709418838 to 0.193337328203690 Hartree/Bohr^2 while
the gradient is unchanged to 4e-16 Hartree/Bohr. Independent fresh analytic
gradient differences also approach a different Hessian, so this is not
accepted as energy-difference cancellation. The physical iso-orbital endpoint
of the total-density tau_W/tau cap can choose opposite derivative branches
under AO-contraction roundoff. An inward-endpoint roundoff enclosure keeps
the capped value and differentiates the physical interior; genuinely
super-bound inputs retain the constant cap. Private closed-form endpoint
checks and p283 all-component RKS/UKS nuclear/electric fits were then run
together with the retained p223 failure; their measured results follow.

The endpoint rerun resolves the retained TPSS coupled failure: gradient
p=1.999112560929, R2=0.999999948574 and Hessian
H=0.193361970012764 Hartree/Bohr^2, p=1.997884081962,
R2=0.999999698518, C=0.7509145142503 and Richardson defect
5.532513308593e-9. Both fits use h=[0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] Bohr. The
raw response residual is 2.033352129667e-14 and the reference energy
defect -2.242650509743e-14 Hartree. All six p223 cases pass (81.04 s).
This is directional coupled-response evidence, not complete Cartesian
multicomponent derivative acceptance.

Independent p283 acceptance passes all 266 fits (4937.22 s): fourteen TPSS/
revTPSS point potentials, eighteen molecular gradient entries, 162 Hessian
entries, eighteen alpha entries and 54 beta entries across RKS/UKS. All
accepted fits are second order, p=1.955170..2.013108, minimum R2=0.99989964.
The initial nuclear interval is [0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025] Bohr; mixed Hessian

The retained semilocal elastic column [2][1] exposes eight accepted rows

The endpoint core also passes the retained six-case real SCF suite and the

and thermal-stationarity (one test) regressions. The all-feature/library/bin/
test Clippy gate passes with warnings denied; Ruff, API-table, ledger,

The endpoint-specific public tensor comparison initially used the wrong

Periodic exchange uses the shared four-pair-distance quartet enumeration
introduced by the exchange translation-invariance correction. The previous

The continuation runner is Python and builds immutable source snapshots,

recorded above; complete fresh tensor acceptance remains incomplete. The

The rSCAN test-only branch recorder/replayer passes all 126 independent
molecular component fits: gradient 9, Hessian 81, alpha 9 and beta 27,
p=1.918816..2.051137, minimum R2=0.99964605, with no failed interval.
Nuclear h=[0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025] Bohr and electric
h=[0.016,0.008,0.004,0.002] atomic units retain the reference branch at

changing production SCF. It does not validate unfrozen finite-step crossings
of the polynomial junction. The earlier claim that the smooth-interpolation
fixture passed every component was wrong: 38 components failed (34 Hessian
and four alpha/beta entries); those failures remain recorded. Pointwise

The original p5 gradient regression exposed two angular-quadrature failures
at the pruned level-9 grid: SVWN5 torque 2.445e-8 and B3LYP atomic gradient
covariance 1.511e-8, against unchanged 1e-8 gates. Tightening SCF alone did
not resolve them; neither did radial refinement at angular degree 83.
The tests now use 200 radial points, unpruned degree-131 Lebedev quadrature,
zero weight cutoff and explicit e/gradient/density SCF gates
1e-13/1e-12/1e-12. Torques for SVWN5/B3LYP/CAM-B3LYP are
2.221691609986e-11/2.254609893453e-10/2.210387518632e-10; all three B3LYP
atomic covariance defects are at most 1.404372988373e-10. Doubling radial
points changes these defects by about 1e-12. All eight p5 regressions pass
with the refined grid (477.53 s). This establishes quadrature convergence
for the fixture, not a universal error bound for the default grid.

### Bounded meta-GGA response kernels

The common molecular ResponseSolver retains local first/second XC derivatives
for one immutable basis, grid and pair of spin-density matrices. Its cache
budget is one eighth of ScfOptions::incore_mb; checked size arithmetic includes
all 36 order-two arrays, a full last batch and the output headers. If the
estimate exceeds that budget, the same on-demand kernel is used. Cache reuse
does not change an energy, a physical denominator, a response tolerance, the
moving-grid terms or the functional-provider interface. Functional families
and declared hybrid parameters determine the route; registered names do not.

The complete fixed-density kernel acceptance covers TPSS, revTPSS, M06-L and
M06-2X on a C1 four-centre STO-3G fixture, a 2000-point level-0 grid and zero
weight cutoff. Each model uses all twenty independent symmetric spin-density
matrix directions and both complete 4x4 output matrices: 640 entry fits per
model, 2560 in total (including symmetry-related output entries). Cached and
on-demand outputs are bitwise equal. Independent differences of the assembled
XC potentials pass all 2560 second-order fits, p=1.877946..2.154855 and minimum

This source archive captures the current bounded implementation and acceptance.
It is not certification of the complete molecular/periodic/high-order response
objective or of an unrun full Rust/Python release regression. The full fresh
405-entry periodic elastic suite is incomplete, with no final suite result;
retained individual
failed intervals do not by themselves establish a failed or passing complete
suite. Its corrected CLI-control repeat remains separate. Remaining functional,
reference, arbitrary-q, nonlocal/correlated and coupled combinations retain
