are excluded.

### Exact isotropic nuclear-spin spectra and basis expansion, 2026-10-29

The existing nmr-spectrum entry accepts nmr_spin_model="exact" with
nmr_couplings=true. A generic spin-Hamiltonian postprocessor takes the
shieldings and isotropic J constants supplied by the existing molecular
reference/functional provider; it does not branch on registered functional
names. In frequency units,

H/h = -sum_i nu_i Iz_i + sum_(i<j) J_ij (Ix_i Ix_j + Iy_i Iy_j + Iz_i Iz_j).

The signed shielded frequencies use the actual computed sigma_i:
nu_i = (nmr_spectrometer_mhz * 1e6 * g_i / g_proton) * (1-sigma_i*1e-6).
Reference-compound shieldings enter only the reported ppm axis; they do not
change the Hamiltonian, its eigenvectors or line strengths. Unobserved active
partners remain in the spin space and need no display reference. Nuclear
spins are specified as twice I; arbitrary positive integer twice-I values
are supported. Distinct nuclear labels are not identified by chemical-shift
rounding. Equivalent isotope groups use a coherent sum of transverse spin
operators, retaining the roofing effect and dark-state cancellation.

Conserved total-Iz blocks are diagonalized with the common faer-backed
symmetric eigensolver. A signed rotating frame avoids cancellation of large
common Larmor frequencies. nmr_spin_max_dimension (default 1024) limits the
complete product-space dimension; exceeding it is a resource error, never
a truncation. Every adjacent-Iz candidate transition, including exact dark zero weights,
is retained without a weak-line threshold. The display window is determined
from chemical shifts and rigorous scalar-coupling spin-operator bounds,
independently of tiny rounded transition weights. Raw transitions remain
available outside the display window and all Lorentzian tails contribute. Lorentzian widths remain full widths at half
maximum in ppm. Intensities are normalized transverse strengths with unit
integrated area per observed nucleus, with the common high-temperature
population factor removed. Absolute thermal populations, quadrupolar or
anisotropic terms, pulse sequences and relaxation are outside this model.
The unchanged first-order mode remains the default.

New report keys are spectrum_spin_model, spectrum_line_positions
([element][transition], ppm), spectrum_line_weights (integrated dimensionless
areas), spin_hilbert_dimension, spin_hamiltonian_residual (Hz),
spin_hamiltonian_relative_residual (dimensionless), spin_hamiltonian_converged
and spin_transition_sum_rule_defects. Raw eigen and sum-rule defects enter
the existing requested response-tolerance gate; no denominator floor is used.
The remaining shielding/J provider restrictions, including unimplemented
ROKS/GKS electronic combinations, are not removed by this postprocessor.

Independent p284 acceptance covers all four AB transitions for both signs
of carrier and J, equivalent-spin and single-spin-I=1/2..9/2 limits, resource
guards and an independent full-space Kronecker Hamiltonian/detection oracle
for mixed spins 1/2,1,1/2. The first numerical-module run passes all four
cases: maximum AB position/weight defect 2.220446049250e-16, maximum AB raw
eigen residual 7.105427357601e-15 Hz, maximum AB area defect
4.440892098501e-16; dense spectral defects 2.389199948993e-13 and
1.256494908120e-13, raw eigen residual 5.684341886081e-13 Hz.
This postprocessing introduces no electronic derivative; its upstream
shielding/J derivatives retain their separately measured component fits.
Complete rebuilt/public acceptance, including reference invariance, is in
progress and is not inferred from these numerical-module checks.

Thirty additional BSE bases bring the embedded catalogue to 78: pcseg-0..4,
aug-pcseg-0..4, pcSseg-0..4, cc-pCV(D,T,Q)Z, cc-pwCV(D,T,Q)Z,
aug-cc-pCV(D,T,Q)Z, cc-pV(D,T,Q)Z-DK and pcJ-0..2. All 860 element records
and 49,901 nonzero exponent/coefficient pairs agree exactly with independent
version-pinned JSON exports. p285 checks every pair after runtime Gaussian94
parsing; all 78 basis sets parse in the first numerical-module regression.
Exact source URLs, versions, hashes and the upstream notice are retained in
third_party/bse. No data is invented for missing elements. DK-optimized
orbitals do not activate a relativistic Hamiltonian. These data checks do
not establish basis convergence or experimental accuracy of a calculation.

functional, reference, field or periodic combination. Listing a test or
returning a complete tensor is not itself independent validation. A
directional fit certifies only that directional quantity unless a complete
unisolvent set has the full number of independent tensor components.

`tests/support/c1_geometry.rs` gives a sufficient C1 certificate: distinct
element-labelled distance fingerprints fix every nucleus, and noncoplanar
centres exclude any residual proper/improper symmetry. p288 checks the
actual shared H4/H5 high-order fixtures and rejects planar water and a
distorted planar four-centre geometry as C1 evidence. It is a geometric
audit, not a replacement for derivative fits. Derivative tests keep zero
grid-weight cutoff and the shared independent component/stencil gates.

C1 describes the molecular geometry and Hamiltonian, not an AO label. The
high-order hydrogen fixtures use atom-centred s functions; the ammonia
electric/VCD subsets also exercise valence p functions. These bounded
STO-3G measurements do not certify every basis, angular momentum,
contraction pattern or near-linear-dependence regime.

The electronic J response has not been silently replaced with a nuclear

### Covariant finite-q exact-exchange density kernel, 2026-10-29

`dfpt::exchange::FiniteQExchange::new(cell, k_points, q, cutoff, kernel)`
and `apply(density)` now supply the complete complex AO exchange-density
derivative in independent (k+q,k) spaces. Inputs and outputs contain one
full square AO matrix per reference k point. Density coefficients are
dimensionless; the returned exchange potential is Hartree. k and q are
Cartesian inverse Bohr, cutoff is Bohr and range omega is inverse Bohr.
The returned map has no functional prefactor; the density solver contracts
it with -cx and -clr. Coulomb, erf and erfc kernels share the same path.

The image convention is D_q(U)=sum_k exp(-ik.U) P_q(k)/Nk and
P_q(lambda C,sigma D)=exp(iq.C) D_q(D-C). Four centre-pair distances select
the same quartets as reference SCF, and both source and target density
pairs carry its atom-resolved minimum-image weights. No same-q matrix
Hermitianization, density-amplitude threshold or denominator shift is used.
The density-image radius also includes the home-cell shell spread, which
prevents missing selected pairs in a cell with widely separated centres.
Converge the exchange cutoff and k mesh for the intended crystal.

p291 independently enumerates T, U=D-C and C on a C1-centre triclinic
model with two offset k points and an incommensurate q. All 12288 real
kernel entries (including both real and imaginary input/output components)
pass four-step fits on h=[0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]. The dimensionless density
chart P(t)=t E+(t^3+t^5)W has unit-entry tangent E. Its known curvature
makes even structural zero tangent entries measurable without an error
floor. This is a kernel contract test, not a finite-field SCF test.
All exponents are 2.002891 at printed precision, with minimum R2
0.99999944. The maximum independent dense defect over all three kernels is
3.217629826114e-17; the complex-superoperator adjoint defect is at most
5.551115123126e-17. The Gamma
derivative agrees with nonlinear reference Fock exchange to
1.665334536938e-16 Hartree. Tiny 1e-22 density scaling passes without a
physical amplitude floor. The initial test-only unused-stencil diagnostic
was corrected by a genuine fourth-order alternate stencil; no warning
suppression was introduced and the failed build record is retained.

`PeriodicDensitySolver` now contracts same-spin full and long-range exchange
alongside Hartree and the semilocal XC kernel, using functional coefficients
rather than registered names. Existing `periodic-response`, `dielectric`
and `thermal-response` bindings share this physical solver. p292 adds
full complex dense screened-density checks and independent nonlinear Gamma
field fits for HF/PBE0/CAM-B3LYP. Their bounded coupled and native/ASE/CLI
acceptance, including the post-SCF-repair repeat, is recorded below. Kernel
acceptance alone does not validate those physical combinations. Finite-q graph, nonlocal-correlation, correlated
pair, ROKS, spinor and Dirac density providers remain separate work.

### Fourth-order Gaussian integral checks from d through i

The one-electron check covers every nonzero spherical matrix entry of the
tested overlap, kinetic/core and dipole blocks on the curved path, with
four-step fits of derivative orders one to four for d, f, g, h and i. The
direct assembly checks the structurally zero coefficients too.

The separate `(s s | s l)` quartet check covers every spherical component
of each high-angular shell for Coulomb and long-range exchange. Removing
three common translations leaves nine relative centre coordinates. The
fourth-order tensor for each AO entry is checked along 495 full-rank
directions against an independent real shell-quartet implementation. The
suite specifies 44,550 component-direction fits with four steps each and
retains failed intervals for both central and Richardson stencils. It also
checks uniform translation against the real quartet.

Every direction uses the same staged intervals and fit gates set before
the run. A separate accuracy check evaluates the exact Cartesian
Gaussian derivative polynomial `L^4 - 12 Q L^2 + 12 Q^2` with real
quartets at the undeformed geometry. The check uses a comparison bound
of `2e-13 * (1 + abs(reference))` Hartree/Bohr^4 and uses no step sizes.
On the fixed-library preflight all 44,550 absolute comparisons passed.
The largest defect was `1.41553435639707459e-15` Hartree/Bohr^4 for the
i-shell Coulomb quartet. The raw log includes the maximum by angular
momentum and operator (SHA-256
`bc805a163e21408e0132a0e5dfcffa6890ca0681d1bef7f0647a0c4761621ea1`).

### Scope of the mathematical provider contract

A common response solver guarantees the solution of the operator it is
given, not that an incomplete provider supplied the correct physical
operator. The reference energy/action, Fock/gradient, Hessian action,
mixed/high-order jets, explicit observable derivatives, metric/Pulay terms
and stationary reference constraints must all describe the same model.

The semilocal provider composes weighted generic energy-density bodies;
the same bodies supply ordinary XC derivatives and Taylor energy/potential
coefficients. Where those full terms are connected, the response algebra
does not need functional-name branches. Exact exchange, nonlocal terms,
PT2 amplitudes, ECP/projector terms and reference constraints must satisfy
the same contract. Their missing providers cannot be inferred from the
semilocal interface or from a small Krylov residual. Nondifferentiable
branches, quadrature/integral accuracy and SCF/root continuity also require
their stated domain and numerical checks. This is why independent dense,
term-by-term and all-component fits remain necessary alongside common
mathematical construction. There is no current blanket certification of
all functional/reference/periodic combinations.

## Continuous chemical species and reduced substituents: theory and scope

### Two ways to make chemical identity a parameter

A useful chemical model should allow a substituent to change continuously while retaining a well-defined electronic energy and meaningful derivatives. There are two different operations in this implementation. The all-electron continuous-species model changes real nuclear charges while preserving the integer element labels used to select basis functions and integration grids. The reduced-fragment model instead replaces selected occupied electrons and their nuclei by a fixed effective operator, leaving fewer electrons to optimize. The first operation does not by itself establish the accuracy of the second.

In the all-electron model, let q be a vector of continuous coordinates, Z0 the reference physical nuclear charges, and A a fixed matrix of charge directions. Then Z(q) = Z0 + A q. The number of electrons, AO shell sequence and exponents, occupation sector, and grid recipe remain fixed within a chart. An integer nitrogen label can therefore retain the same nitrogen AO template while its physical charge varies. The fixed-template nitrogen-to-carbon/oxygen charge path is not a calculation with independently selected endpoint element bases.

The reduced model adds a separate approximation: electrons assigned to an internal occupied subspace no longer respond explicitly in the production SCF. Its construction uses an explicit reference molecule, but its production calculation evaluates the reduced basis and saved operators. A control calculation that retains the native frozen density is useful for isolating the freezing error; it is not the compressed potential and does not demonstrate its cost or transferability. These responsibilities are separated in [the continuous model](../src/driver/continuous_species.rs), [reference generation](../src/pseudo_sub/reduction.rs), [primitive production](../src/driver/continuous_species/few_center.rs), and [contracted production](../src/driver/continuous_species/contracted.rs).

The objective is a common fixed format for atoms and spectator fragments. Ordinary atoms retain their ordinary calculation, with zero additional fragment and shape terms. This boundary condition does not permit interpolation between arbitrary electron counts, basis sets, or fragment topologies. A continuous path belongs to a specified discrete chart.

### Functional and basis dependence: current limits

**Functional independence and basis independence have not been established.**
Continuous input and analytic differentiation are numerical capabilities; they
do not make DFT energies invariant to the functional or the finite AO space.
The implemented all-electron charge selector currently exposes LDA and PBE,
not the entire ordinary molecular functional catalog. Its nuclear charges can
vary at fixed integer electron/spin counts, AO template and grid, but changing
that template defines another chart and requires new SCF/response and
convergence checks. The fixed C/N union basis and ordinary element-selected
STO-3G endpoints are different finite approximations, not interchangeable
definitions of a physical endpoint. The measured 103.23 kcal/mol discrepancy
and its reduction to 7.44 kcal/mol illustrate this dependence; the latter is
not a basis-limit accuracy estimate.

The frozen few-center model has an additional dependence. Its electrostatic
distribution, short-range and nonlocal residual operators, and E0 are extracted
from a particular reference DFT calculation. The active Hartree/XC terms in
production must use the corresponding functional; moving fitted frozen-XC
effects to another functional can introduce a mismatch or double counting.
Changing the AO template also changes which operator action was compressed.
Neither operation is certified by preserving the coefficient-vector length.
The record generator/parser has LDA/PBE mechanisms, whereas the accepted public
saved-model evidence is the bounded PBE energy/force subset: RKS CoreSp,
CoreSpH and CoreSpHH, and UKS CoreSp. Callable or parseable LDA is not
cross-functional transfer evidence. The current four-candidate generation and
target experiment uses PBE/RKS, STO-3G reference/retained atoms, a fixed
five-AO CoreSp site, primitive eight-projector/local-three/Gaussian-three
operators, grid level 1 and zero weight cutoff. It does not test hybrid or
meta-GGA transfer, other basis families, arbitrary spin sectors or the
functional independence of its parameters.

Reproducible provenance therefore includes the generation functional and
projection rule, reference and retained-atom basis, effective-site template,
operator widths/order, exact basis-data/code identity, reference geometry,
integer full/frozen/active electron ledger, spin sector, attachment class and
tested application domain. The bundled `src/basis/data/sto-3g.g94` used in the
accepted core and current experiment has SHA-256
`e1d1a1aed4bf79bbfbf662cd1dcbc39ea73b05ded00d159a3c7b0a859cc40cf6`.
Generated records retain functional, template, fixed widths, source version,
geometry, ledger and construction fingerprint. Their construction fingerprint
alone is not a cryptographic identity of every bundled basis byte; the run
provenance also pins basis data and the compiled core. Old records must not be
silently relabeled as parameters for a different functional or basis.
Cross-method/basis reuse needs an explicit regeneration or transfer experiment,
followed by independent property, derivative and held-out checks. No such
general transfer claim is made here.

### Electron accounting before basis reduction

Let N_full be the electron count of the explicit reference molecule, N_frozen,X the integer number assigned to the internal occupied subspace of fragment X, and Z_A the nuclear charge of atom A. Define the active electron count and the effective ionic charge of each removed fragment by

$$
N_{active}=N_{full}-\sum_X N_{frozen,X},\qquad
Q_{ion,X}=\sum_{A\in X}Z_A-N_{frozen,X}.
$$

The molecular charge is consequently the sum of retained nuclear charges and effective ionic charges, less N_active. Basis removal never determines the electron count. With spin-summed density matrix P and AO overlap matrix S, the converged density must satisfy Tr(PS) = N_active. Fixed-spin calculations additionally check the separate alpha and beta populations.

For the present methyl convention, the removed nuclei have total charge 9. Freezing the carbon 1s pair and the three internal C-H bond pairs removes eight electrons: Q_ion = +1 and one methyl electron remains active. This is more than an inner-core approximation. Neutral ethane therefore changes from 18 to 10 explicitly optimized electrons when one methyl group is reduced. Neutral methylcyclopropane changes from 32 to 24. Neither electron reduction guarantees a particular AO reduction or a useful energy error.

For a frozen singlet, four electrons are removed from each spin channel. A declared active sector (N_alpha, N_beta) corresponds to the full sector (N_alpha + 4, N_beta + 4). Changing this spin sector requires a different chart; it is not a continuous coefficient update. The accounting and overlap-trace checks are implemented in [reduction_linear.rs](../src/driver/continuous_species/reduction_linear.rs).

A small Rust accounting example uses the existing types and performs no SCF:

```rust
use dft_rs::driver::continuous_species::reduction_linear::{
    ElectronLedger, FrozenFragmentSpec,
};
fn main() -> dft_rs::Result<()> {
    let ledger = ElectronLedger::new(
        &[6, 1, 1, 1, 6, 1, 1, 1], 18,
        &[FrozenFragmentSpec {
            explicit_atoms: vec![4, 5, 6, 7], frozen_electrons: 8,
        }],
    )?;
    assert_eq!(ledger.active_electron_count, 10);
    assert_eq!(ledger.fragments[0].effective_ionic_charge, 1);
    Ok(())
}
```

### A scalar energy defines the operator and its derivatives

For a static reduced model, P denotes the active spin-summed AO density, T the kinetic matrix, V_el the electron interaction with retained nuclei and effective charge distributions, V_sr a short-range local correction, and V_nl a nonlocal projector correction. E_H and E_xc are the usual active-electron Hartree and exchange-correlation functionals. E_core is the consistent classical interaction of retained nuclei and effective distributions. E0 is the reference energy of the removed internal degrees of freedom. A prospective shape residual contributes E_G. At zero external field the energy is

$$
E[P]=\operatorname{Tr}\{P(T+V_{el}+V_{sr}+V_{nl})\}
      +E_H[P]+E_{xc}[P]+E_{core}+E_0+E_G.
$$

Current measured static fragment candidates set the shape contribution to zero; a generated and chemically validated shape correction is not available. The local and nonlocal corrections are density independent. Their energy is Tr(PV), and the same V enters the Fock matrix. E0 and the classical correction enter both iteration energy reports and final totals through the scoped energy context. Adding E0 only to the final printed answer would give inconsistent convergence histories.

The eliminated nuclei and electrons define an effective signed charge distribution sigma. Its integral is Q_ion. Electronic attraction, interactions with retained nuclei, permanent dipoles, and external-field coupling must use the same distribution. In the current representation the main +1 ionic charge is supplemented by three Gaussian charge corrections whose sum is zero, and body-frame dipoles. Short-range Pauli and XC corrections are separate electronic operators; a nonlocal Pauli operator is not also applied to retained nuclei as if it were electrostatic charge.

An embedding Fock matrix already contains contributions from the active density. Adding the entire reference embedding Fock to an ordinary active SCF would therefore count active Hartree and XC terms twice. Generation instead projects a residual after subtracting terms already supplied by the active calculation. The resulting static correction approximates the influence of the frozen electrons, including short-range effects; it is not an exact density-dependent embedding functional for arbitrary environments.

If F is an external electric field, the electronic position operator and the permanent core coupling -F dot mu_core belong to this same energy. The origin convention must be shared by both contributions. For a charged system, translating the origin changes the reported dipole in the known charge-dependent way. A future internal polarization energy would require a scalar variational definition and its density derivatives in both Fock and response; it cannot be added only to the reported polarizability.

The production representation is not an exact frozen-density SCF: the frozen density is used to generate and diagnose the effective operator, but is not explicitly added to the production XC density. Finite fitted exclusion also does not impose exact orthogonality to the physical frozen occupied space. For the original C13 contracted/fitted example, the measured lifted-density diagnostic Tr(P_active S P_frozen S) at R0 is about 0.166, whereas the separate native frozen control enforces the complementary occupied-space constraint. This diagnostic is not a claim that the compressed density is an exact full-system Slater determinant. The active model has a variational scalar energy, but is not an established variational upper bound to full DFT. Neither electron removal nor rigid internal geometry means that all molecular nuclei are held fixed.

### What is fixed, and what can vary

The principal electronic record contains 51 amplitudes: three Gaussian charge amplitudes, nine Cartesian components of three body dipoles, three fixed-width local Gaussian amplitudes, and 36 independent entries of an 8 by 8 real symmetric projector matrix D. E0 is a separate energy-reference scalar. The saved internal geometry xi, attachment map, Gaussian exponents, radial contractions, functional and grid prescription also belong to the model definition. They are not extra coefficients silently fitted at each geometry.

With fixed total ionic charge, the three charge corrections obey one linear constraint. There are then 50 independent electronic tangent directions. This statement is conditional on the same dictionary, normalization, coordinate ordering and scales. The primitive and contracted implementations currently use different packing and tangent conventions in their test helpers. Equal vector length does not establish that index 7 represents the same physical perturbation in both. An explicit named conversion and operator/chain-rule invariant tests are required before calling them a common physical chart.

The short-range operator uses fixed Gaussian functions f_a, and the nonlocal operator uses fixed projectors beta_u:

$$
V_{sr}(r)=\sum_a c_a f_a(r),\qquad
\hat V_{nl}=\sum_{u,v}|\beta_u\rangle D_{uv}\langle\beta_v|,
\qquad D=D^{T}.
$$

The full D matrix need not be positive definite. A separately identified repulsive component can have its own physical constraints. The implementation uses eight projectors; eight projectors do not imply eight active electrons or eight AO functions. One-, two-, and three-center electronic templates are discrete alternatives with a common coefficient count. Center count must not change midway through a claimed continuous optimization.

The contracted methyl dictionary contains carbon 1s and 2s functions, three carbon p functions, and three hydrogen 1s functions. Only the p block rotates with the body frame; treating every contracted function as a scalar would change the operator under a rigid molecular rotation. This basis of projector functions is distinct from the reduced SCF AO basis. The current contracted production route retains the original full eight-site ethane grid and its moving partition. It therefore reduces the active electronic problem without claiming that all eight geometrical or grid sites have disappeared. The primitive role-site route uses its own saved role grid instead. Their force and cost evidence cannot be interchanged.

### Generation is a separate map from production

Reference generation selects an occupied internal subspace, forms its embedding residual, and projects that residual onto a fixed dictionary. In an AO metric convention, let v be a target operator, K_a the dictionary matrices, and W an explicitly chosen metric weight. A typical constrained projection minimizes

$$
\left\|W\left(v-\sum_a\theta_aK_a\right)W\right\|_F^2
+\lambda\|L(\theta-\theta_0)\|^2,
\qquad C\theta=d.
$$

Here theta contains the coefficients, C theta = d enforces constraints such as charge conservation, L fixes coefficient scales, and lambda specifies regularization. The Gram matrix of a nonorthogonal dictionary is part of this solve. Independent inner products with each dictionary function are generally not its least-squares coefficients. Rank, conditioning, regularization and residuals are reported rather than hidden by dropping inconvenient directions.

Three comparisons identify different failures: full explicit DFT versus the native frozen-density control measures freezing error; that control versus the compressed operator measures compression error at the chosen reference; fixed coefficients in unused environments measure transfer error. Numerical SCF and quadrature errors are checked separately. A good frozen control together with a poor compressed curve points toward the operator space, active-space capture or projection metric, rather than justifying an arbitrary geometric correction.

Smooth coefficients in production do not prove that generation is smooth. Reference orbital localization, fixed occupied-subspace dimension, projection rank, frame construction and branch selection must also remain continuous. Schur elimination is used as a fixed one-electron diagnostic, including nonzero interblock overlap and pole/solve diagnostics; it is not by itself the density-dependent production energy or its response theory.

### Geometry, forces and frames

Let y be the saved reduced coordinates and xi the fixed internal geometry. The rigid expansion R = L(y, xi) reconstructs the explicit geometry needed for model sites and reference comparison. Let J be the derivative of this map. Reference forces must be compared after pullback:

$$
\mathbf F_y=J^{T}\mathbf F_R.
$$

Deleting the forces on eliminated atoms is incorrect. A frame made from attachment anchors transfers its derivatives back to those anchors. Projector-center motion, p-function rotation, local-potential motion, electrostatic terms, AO Pulay terms, and moving grid weights must participate in the same gradient. The staged contracted implementation constructs a full-site gradient and applies one rigid pullback. Adding another frame torque or a second role pullback would count part of the force twice.

Low-symmetry geometries are essential tests because symmetry can make missing terms vanish. Collinear attachment anchors make the local frame undefined and must be rejected. Independently choosing a new principal-axis eigenvector at every structure can produce discontinuous signs near degeneracy. A global rigid rotation, an internal methyl torsion and a change of molecular orientation in a fixed external field are different operations with different expected results.

Analytic primitive-role forces have independent derivative evidence within their measured scope. Contracted force expressions and the true 50-coordinate coefficient adapter are staged in the next source candidate; they are not promoted to accepted derivatives by their presence in source. The public primitive saved-model report is deliberately restricted to energy, primary-coordinate forces and accounting/convergence metadata.

### Current derivative capabilities and required extensions

R denotes nuclear coordinates and q denotes the specified electronic parameter chart. E_RR is a nuclear Hessian; E_qq is a parameter Hessian. A dipole/parameter derivative is -E_Fq and must not be relabelled E_Rq. The following entries concern the continuous/reduced extension, not unrelated ordinary-molecule features.

| Domain | E_R | E_RR | E_q and E_qq | E_Rq |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Molecular all-electron LDA/PBE RKS/UKS | Analytic, tested components | Not implemented/exposed | Analytic coupled response for supported nuclear-charge/local-amplitude charts | Not implemented/exposed |
| Primitive reduced RKS/UKS, measured templates | Analytic internal force subsets | Unsupported | Genuine 51-coefficient response not accepted; dummy zero direction is not evidence | Unsupported |
| Best contracted Me candidates | Staged analytic force provider, uncompiled | Unsupported | Fixed three-amplitude response executed; complete component acceptance pending. General coefficient adapter remains uncompiled | Unsupported |
| Periodic neutral all-electron RKS/UKS prototype, now paused | Unsupported | Unsupported | First E_q only; eight executed profiles retained | Unsupported |
| ROKS/GKS continuous or reduced models | Unsupported | Unsupported | Unsupported | Unsupported |

The existing all-electron APIs are ContinuousSpeciesModel::nuclear_gradient and ContinuousSpeciesModel::sensitivity, exposed by the continuous-species common driver and native wrapper. The sensitivity result includes parameter_energy_gradient and parameter_energy_hessian; those names do not promise a coordinate Hessian. The primitive saved-record unit-label repair has now passed five actual compiled Rust common-driver tests, including saved-model energy/force parity. The first selected Python/ASE run on the same new wheel ended with 96 passes, one failed legacy resource-envelope test and two explicit template skips. Correcting only the mock's missing active-scope state, while retaining its exact three-envelope assertion, was followed by 102 passing affected tests on the unchanged wheel. Fourteen alias/logging tests and the routine Python release entry point also passed. The original failures remain recorded; these outcomes cover the tested public routes rather than unmeasured templates or chemical accuracy. Primitive force evidence does not validate the contracted model. Tests include continuous_species.rs real-charge RKS/UKS nuclear and parameter components, continuous_species_few_center.rs / continuous_species_few_center_open.rs primitive force components, and continuous_species_few_center_driver.rs saved-record envelope checks.

A complete reduced-coordinate Hessian must include the curvature of the lift. With g_R the full-site gradient and H_R its Hessian, the exact chain rule is

$$ H_y=J^{T}H_RJ+\sum_i (g_R)_i\,\partial_y^2 L_i. $$

The second term does not vanish merely because the reduced coordinates are stationary. Moving frames, projector centers and rotations, overlap/Pulay terms, moving quadrature and its partition, classical terms, and self-consistent response belong to the same E_RR and E_Rq contract. Freezing a supplied potential while calling an ordinary molecular Hessian is not the complete model Hessian. Implementing these missing routes is required before claiming relaxed reaction thermochemistry. Finite differences are independent validation only.

### Parameter derivatives and response

At fixed AO basis, grid and geometry, let h_a be the derivative of the one-electron matrix with respect to coefficient q_a, and P^(b) the self-consistent density response to q_b. Let E_class contain the density-independent classical and reference terms. Then

$$
E_a=\operatorname{Tr}(P h_a)+E_{class,a},\qquad
E_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}(P^{(b)}h_a)
      +\operatorname{Tr}(P h_{ab})+E_{class,ab}.
$$

For an affine density-independent coefficient dictionary, h_ab is zero, but the density-response term is not. Coupled response includes the existing Hartree and XC kernel; frozen-density matrix differentiation alone misses orbital relaxation. With the field sign convention above, mu_i = -E_Fi, alpha_ij = -E_FiFj, and mu_i,a = -E_Fi,a. Nuclear-coordinate derivatives need the additional moving-basis and grid terms and cannot reuse this fixed-geometry formula without them.

The all-electron molecular nuclear-charge acceptance includes 82 independent component error fits. These establish their own charge chart, not the 50 reduced-fragment coefficient directions. The new coefficient adapter has a proposed suite covering every first derivative, all 1,275 unique coefficient Hessian elements and all 150 dipole derivatives per context, plus independent field-dual comparisons. That suite is prepared, not executed acceptance. Mixed geometry/coefficient derivatives, generation-map continuity and unit-scaled property Jacobians remain separate gates. A property metric J_P^T W J_P, where J_P is a scaled observable Jacobian, would describe sensitivity to the chosen observables rather than a unique distance over chemistry.

Active-electron polarizability is not the whole fragment polarizability. Frozen internal electrons cannot relax in the static model. Adding the full explicit-fragment polarizability would double count the active response, and clipping negative eigenvalues of a response difference is not a derivation. For the compressed coefficient model, internal response modes, dynamic response and alpha_q remain unaccepted. A separate Rust-only all-electron affine charge/local alpha_q implementation and its tests do not establish the same capability for compressed coefficients. A finite orbital gap alone does not prove response stability; fresh SCF residuals, response residuals and occupied-subspace tracking are also needed. Continuation from a previous density and an independent second seed should agree on the same solution branch.

### Small examples and the public boundary

The following all-electron CLI input follows the validated fixed-nitrogen-template example. Run it from the repository source root with the matching built executable. Coordinates in the XYZ file are Angstrom; the charge controls, field and response output use the report's atomic-unit conventions.

```sh
dft-rs continuous-species tests/data/continuous_species_nitrogen.xyz \
  --format json --xc pbe --basis sto-3g --dispersion none \
  --fixed-electron-count 14 --physical-nuclear-charges '[7,7]' \
  --charge-directions '[[-1,1]]' --charge-coordinates '[0.25]' \
  --charge-bounds '[[-1.5,1.5]]' --charge-parameter-names '["lambda"]' \
  --charge-origin '[0.11,0.07,-0.09]' --field '[0.0013,-0.0009,0.0017]' \
  --charge-nuclear-gradient true --grid-level 1 --grid-weight-cutoff 0 \
  --guess core --conv-tol 1e-13 --conv-tol-grad 1e-11 --conv-tol-dp 1e-12
```

The corresponding native Python input uses Bohr positions. This demonstrates the existing all-electron entry point; it does not construct a reduced fragment.

```python
import dft_rs
report = dft_rs.continuous_species(
    [7, 7], [[0.0, 0.0, -1.05], [0.0, 0.0, 1.05]],
    fixed_electron_count=14, physical_nuclear_charges=[7.0, 7.0],
    charge_directions=[[-1.0, 1.0]], charge_coordinates=[0.25],
    charge_bounds=[[-1.5, 1.5]], charge_parameter_names=["lambda"],
    xc="pbe", basis="sto-3g", dispersion="none", cpu_threads=1,
)
```

Saved fragment evaluation is a different record route: `evaluate_reduced_fragment(..., model=record, fragment_mode="few-evaluate")` and its existing ASE getter forward an opaque, native-unit record through the common driver. The record fixes the operator dictionary, functional, geometry map and spin sector. Auxiliary electronic sites do not add public force coordinates; forces have shape N_primary by 3. Native inputs use Bohr, while ASE Atoms positions use Angstrom. Common CPU/memory controls remain at the driver boundary.

This new primitive route currently has an unresolved public acceptance failure on the last executed artifact: the common unit validator correctly rejects a missing dimensionless label for `overlap_condition_number`. Four Rust record-route cases and typed record export passed before the 16 native/ASE/CLI fixture setups stopped at that failure. The next candidate adds the owned label and a common-driver regression, but has not completed acceptance. Therefore no successful reduced public example is claimed here. The intended accepted surface is PBE RKS CoreSp/CoreSpH/CoreSpHH and fixed-spin UKS CoreSp, energy/forces only. Callable internal alternatives, including LDA, are not public chemical acceptance.

### What the current curves say

For a fixed saved candidate, compare relative energies E(R) - E(R0), keeping theta, E0, xi and the dictionary unchanged along the curve. Reprojecting or adjusting E0 at every geometry would change the question and could conceal a poor energy surface. Existing construction experiments compare projection weights, AO templates and fixed one-, two- and three-center alternatives without adding substituent-specific coefficient dimensions. A shape term must not absorb electronic compression error.

The best reported occupied-weighted 15-AO construction candidate has relative-energy MAE about 1.422 kcal/mol and P95 about 4.496 kcal/mol. It fails the joint 1 kcal/mol MAE and 2 kcal/mol P95 criteria. The earlier 13-AO methylcyclopropane transfer test had nine points, 36 converged SCF calculations, MAE about 5.841 kcal/mol, dipole-vector RMSE about 0.348 D, and predictive R-squared about -4.0386. Those results do not transfer to the newer construction candidate, whose independent transfer evidence is still missing.

Predictive R-squared is 1 - SSE/SST, with SST measured about the reference mean and no fitted adjustment to predictions. A negative value means that predicting the reference mean would give a smaller squared error. It is not evidence of a reliable chemical trend. This statistic differs fundamentally from the R-squared of a finite-difference error-versus-step fit. A derivative can have an excellent convergence-order fit while the approximate energy curve is chemically inaccurate.

The wider target includes Me, Et, CF3, Cl, Ph and tBu in untouched low-symmetry environments. Me has controlled construction and failed transfer evidence. The other five groups do not inherit Me acceptance; ordinary Cl provides an atom identity control, not proof of interpolation to a frozen fragment. Port classes and whole scaffolds must be held out separately. If a held-out environment is used to revise the projection or dictionary, it becomes construction data and needs a new independent holdout.

### Reactions, periodicity and practical use

A useful first reaction objective is a balanced electronic energy difference, Delta E = sum_s nu_s E_s, evaluated with the same saved theta and E0 for each occurrence of a reduced group on both sides. Here nu_s is the signed stoichiometric coefficient. The contribution sum_s nu_s n_X,s E0,X cancels only when the count of each identical reduced group balances. The same cancellation applies to barriers within a fixed reduced composition. Different reference constants or regenerated models on opposite sides invalidate this argument. Reactions that break the frozen internal bonds or strongly rearrange their electrons lie outside the present spectator approximation.

An electronic Delta E is not a zero-point-corrected energy or a finite-temperature enthalpy. Removed internal vibrational modes are absent from a reduced-coordinate vibrational calculation. The project does not currently provide a validated reaction optimizer that restores these contributions. Expansion to explicit structures and explicit validation remain necessary for final candidate ranking.

Molecular fixed-spin all-electron support and the restricted primitive UKS route are evaluated separately from frozen-fragment transfer. Current continuous-species development is restricted to molecular systems. The completed periodic experiment is preserved as prior evidence: eight profiles spanning RKS/UKS, LDA/PBE and Gamma/three-k-point sampling, plus the guard test, passed sixteen independent four-step first-charge-derivative fits. Their observed orders span 1.999645 to 2.002411, with minimum error-fit R-squared 0.999999613. These are derivative-convergence statistics, not predictive accuracy. The experiment keeps cell, k mesh, occupations and electron count fixed and conserves total nuclear charge. It establishes energy and first-q consistency for that all-electron periodic chart only. Periodic reduced fragments, nuclear forces, stress, second-q derivatives and response remain unsupported, and further continuous-species periodic implementation and calculations are paused. Conventional periodic calculations are unaffected.

Cost must be measured separately for model generation, SCF, forces and response. Electron count, AO count, total role/grid sites, projectors and SCF iterations all matter. Keeping the full labelled grid can limit savings even when active electrons are removed. Shared-resource validation timings are not benchmarks. No accepted speedup or amortization count is claimed. Practical acceptance requires accuracy, continuous fixed-size parameters, electron conservation, derivative consistency, transferability and measured cost together.

The current cost audit gives the following concrete sizes for the private
contracted-Me evaluation. These are distinct candidates, not a common accuracy
or speed comparison.

| System | Full to active electrons | Full to reduced AO functions | Retained grid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ethane, one/two/three electronic centers | 18 to 10 | 16 to 13/14/15 | All 8 labelled sites, 25,192 points |
| Methylcyclopropane, original one-center transfer | 32 to 24 | 28 to 25 | All 12 labelled sites, 40,496 points |

Both examples retain four projector sites and eight projector functions. The
production effective-potential path does not rebuild the original full-fragment
DFT Fock on each iteration. It still evaluates active density and XC on the
retained full labelled integration grid. Integral and unit-operator matrices
are reused within a fixed geometry; a persistent cache across arbitrary
geometries or parameter calls has not been demonstrated.

Existing shared-machine measurements include 108 SCFs in 155.14 seconds for
the weighted projection curves, and a different 108-SCF occupied-first batch
in 173.24 seconds. The original transfer batch took 468.68 seconds and contains
18 model and 18 ordinary SCFs plus electrostatic sampling. Its time was not
split into matched model and ordinary evaluations. The recorded direct-child
peak RSS values for the two curve batches were about 15 MiB, excluding the
compiler and other processes. These workload times establish that the trials
ran; they establish no acceleration factor. User/system CPU time, isolated
force and parameter-response cost, fresh reference-generation cost and a
matched end-to-end optimization benchmark remain to be measured.

The first reaction experiment varies three existing Gaussian amplitudes within
the fixed common coefficient format. It calibrates a fixed-geometry electronic
reaction energy against full-electron calculations. One reaction supplies at
most one independent observed combination of three parameters; regularization
selects a solution but does not establish chemical identifiability or transfer.
Only a frozen parameter vector tested on separate reactions can supply an
out-of-sample predictive score. This calibration is also distinct from a later
design search for a different real substituent with an improved reaction
enthalpy.


### Relation to primary work

Projection-based embedding provides a reference for separating active and frozen occupied spaces while enforcing Pauli exclusion; it does not make a static compressed potential exact in new environments. See Manby, Stella, Goodpaster and Miller, [A Simple, Exact Density-Functional-Theory Embedding Scheme](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3419460/), DOI [10.1021/ct300544e](https://doi.org/10.1021/ct300544e) (2012).

A one-active-electron methyl potential and the need to distinguish electrostatics from exchange repulsion have direct precedent in Slavíček and Martínez, [Multicentered valence electron effective potentials: A solution to the link atom problem for ground and excited electronic states](https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article-abstract/124/8/084107/349195/Multicentered-valence-electron-effective), DOI [10.1063/1.2173992](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2173992) (2006). The spectator-electron restriction remains relevant here.

Effective potentials for spectator groups also precede this implementation: Poteau and coauthors, [Effective Group Potentials. 1. Method](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jp002500k), DOI [10.1021/jp002500k](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp002500k) (2001). These papers motivate model structure; their reported accuracy is not an acceptance result for the present dictionary, parameters or software.



### Balanced-reaction calibration trial and current result

The first concrete reaction experiment has reached converged reference and
initial-model SCFs, but its response consistency check failed before parameter
optimization. This restricted closed-shell PBE trial uses the fixed-geometry reaction

```text
ethane + cyclopropane -> methylcyclopropane + methane.
```

Both sides contain C5H12 and 42 electrons. Replacing one methyl group on each
side with the same frozen-eight model gives 34 active electrons per side.
The identical model reference constant occurs once on each side and cancels.
The internal methyl geometry, all 51 stored amplitudes except the selected
three, projector convention, charge distribution, AO template and grid recipe
remain fixed during this trial. No shape correction is fitted.

The selected coordinates q are dimensionless changes in the three existing
local Gaussian amplitudes: c_i(q) = c_i(0) + 0.05 Eh q_i, with -1 <= q_i <= 1.
The initial recipe is the previously generated weighted C15 model. This is
an energy-calibration counterexample with known dipole limitations, not a
new practical model selected using this reaction target. Ethane and
methylcyclopropane are development data here; neither is a final holdout.

Let Delta E_ref be the consistent full-electron electronic reaction energy,
Delta E(q) the reduced-model value, and r(q) their difference. The prepared
regularized objective is

```text
L(q) = r(q)^2 / (2 s^2) + lambda q^T q / 2,
s = 0.01 Eh, lambda = 0.001.
```

If g and H are the analytic parameter gradient and Hessian of Delta E,
then its objective derivatives are

```text
L_q  = r g / s^2 + lambda q,
L_qq = (g g^T + r H) / s^2 + lambda I.
```

The three reaction gradients, nine reaction-Hessian entries and their twelve
objective counterparts must all pass independent four-step checks before
optimization. A bounded damped Newton step and recorded Armijo trials use
these derivatives; a stabilization shift belongs to the optimizer and is
never reported as a physical Hessian. Parameter continuation reuses the
previous density for one seed while a fresh independently rotated core seed
checks the same solution. Particle count, occupied projector, fresh Fock
residual, gap, seed agreement and response residual remain separate gates.

This reaction workflow is currently a validation harness using the library's
SCF and response machinery. A public reaction-parameter optimization driver
has not yet been accepted. The existing `optimizer::optimize` entry point
optimizes molecular Cartesian geometry with L-BFGS; its displacement units
and convergence rule are different from this bounded dimensionless chart.
Connecting a production parameter optimizer therefore requires an explicit
objective and chart adapter rather than passing q as nuclear coordinates.

Static total dipoles are diagnostics at each parameter point, without a
dipole refit or an offset correction. This detects whether improving the
reaction-energy calibration worsens the already imperfect density. Cold
context construction, each SCF seed and response time are recorded separately.
The three-center choice changes ethane from 16 to 15 AO functions and
methylcyclopropane from 28 to 27, while retaining their labelled grids. Such
small basis savings require measurement; they imply no speedup.

Even a converged fit of this one reaction would establish only calibration
and numerical consistency. Transfer requires separate balanced reactions
and untouched scaffolds evaluated with the frozen final parameters. A search
for an improved real substituent additionally requires expansion to an actual
candidate and full-electron reevaluation. Zero-point corrections, thermal
enthalpy and nuclear-Hessian acceptance are outside this pending trial; its
bare Delta E must not be described as a measured reaction heat.

The executed initial trial used two independent SCF seeds for each of the four
full-electron species and each of the two reduced species: twelve SCFs in total.
The full-electron reaction energy was -0.008247266650 Eh
(-5.175238 kcal/mol). The converged initial reduced-model energies give
-14.216631 kcal/mol, an initial error of -9.041393 kcal/mol. These are
development observations from the weighted C15 model, not the earlier C13
transfer test and not evidence of an improvement in transfer accuracy.

The run then failed the comparison between the public density response and
the independently reconstructed occupied/virtual response. That attempt did
not validate a reaction gradient or Hessian. A subsequent executed trial
tightened the public solver's absolute tolerance from 1e-8 to 1e-13 while
retaining the density comparison threshold of 1e-8, the particle-number
derivative threshold of 1e-9 and the independent relative response-residual
threshold of 1e-11. At both the initial and asymmetric derivative-reference
points, the largest density discrepancy was 2.341e-13 and the largest fresh
relative response residual was 9.029e-13. The original failed attempt remains
recorded; the correction did not change the physical model or initial error.

The subsequent trial completed 45 reaction evaluations and 182 new SCFs,
reusing eight previously validated ordinary-reference SCFs. In its first
four-step interval, all three reaction-gradient components, seven of nine
reaction-Hessian entries, all three objective-gradient components and six of
nine objective-Hessian entries passed the unchanged convergence-order and
fit-quality gates. The other five entries failed those gates. The original
900-second supervisor limit then interrupted the second predefined interval;
that interruption is distinct from a measured derivative failure. No complete
Hessian or optimization result was accepted.

Continuity was also checked from the saved physical SCF densities at the 45
completed fixed-geometry parameter points. With overlap S = L L^T and
spin-summed density P, the occupied projector in an orthonormal metric is
Q = L^T P L / 2. The diagnostic Tr(Q_a Q_b)/(N_active/2) between consecutive
points had minimum values 0.999913 for ethane and 0.999956 for the ring system;
the maximum Frobenius projector changes were 0.02957 and 0.03253. The smallest
orbital gaps were 0.50275 and 0.38830 Eh, respectively. These observations,
together with independent-seed agreement, support consistency of the sampled
branch. They do not prove orbital stability, global smoothness, continuity of
parameter generation, or moving-frame continuity under nuclear displacement.

The prepared continuation retains the failed interval and adds a finer
interval, h = [0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025], to test the asymptotic regime. It reuses
only strictly validated scalar results with identical input, artifact, physical
recipe, solver tolerances and exact floating-point parameter coordinates.
Selection uses the first chronological matching result, independent of its
fit error. This is validation memoization, not a fitted lookup replacement for
the continuous electronic model. A second finer interval,
h = [0.1, 0.05, 0.025, 0.0125], is predefined as a fallback; completed results
within the new run are also reused at identical coordinates. At most twelve
new parameter points, requiring 48 SCFs with both seeds, remain for these
checks, with early exit only after all 24 components pass. The prepared
supervisor has an explicit 3600-second numerical limit, coordinated for the
same serial experiment after checking the cost of up to 20 optimizer iterations.
Execution still requires the predecessor's final release and fresh resource
admission; scientific convergence thresholds are unchanged.

That continuation subsequently executed all four declared intervals. All 24
reaction/objective gradient and Hessian components passed a resolved interval,
with accepted orders 1.880694 to 2.049514 and minimum log-error-fit R-squared
0.999277365. All 24 additional absolute Richardson goals passed. Thirty failed
component/interval attempts remain recorded. This validates the three specified
parameter directions at fixed geometry, not the full 51-coefficient or nuclear
Hessian interfaces.

The actual calibration walk reduced L from 1.038006627 to 0.926134324 and the
signed reaction-energy error from -9.041393 to -8.537812 kcal/mol. It stopped
with `line_search_failed` at q = [-1, 0.183301328, 0.195682003], projected
gradient norm 0.03495204, rather than reaching its 1e-6 stationarity goal.
An independent audit found positive projected directional derivatives and
increased actual loss in all twelve final backtracks: descent was checked
before the step was clipped at the active bound. Repairing the bounded search
must preserve the physical Hessian and model. Program completion and passing
derivative tests are not optimizer convergence.

The measured reaction-energy gradient at that final point is approximately
[-0.000829, -0.000253, -0.0000316] Eh per dimensionless coordinate. Maximizing
its local linear model over the remaining box predicts only another 0.212
kcal/mol shift toward the reference. This is a local leverage diagnostic,
not a global nonlinear error bound or evidence that the full common
51-coefficient template is inadequate. It separates repairing convergence
from selecting physically useful electronic parameter directions.

Dipole vector errors worsened from 0.53690 to 0.67517 D for ethane and from

traces of 0.9999982/0.9999991, supporting the sampled SCF branch without
establishing global stability. This is one seen calibration reaction, so
predictive R-squared is undefined. Neither chemical accuracy nor inverse-design
success is established. End-to-end design still requires a target-property
optimization, mapping to actual molecules and independent full-electron checks
on untouched validation data.

A separate proposed control makes that distinction explicit. For a molecule
`M` and its protonated counterpart `MH+`, define the clamped electronic target
`A(q) = E(MH+; q) - E(M; q) - E(H+)`, with the bare proton electronic energy
set to zero. The same charge-conserving parameter direction must be used on
both sides. A paired C/N charge interpolation can keep the AO template,
electron number and spin fixed while testing whether minimizing `A(q)` selects
a useful real endpoint. This is an all-electron control of the search machinery;
it does not validate compression of a substituent's frozen electrons.

After optimization, each selected integer-charge endpoint must be recomputed
with its ordinary element-specific basis and an independent initial density.
Agreement within a fixed interpolated AO template is insufficient because the
ordinary endpoint basis can differ. Predictions on an untouched scaffold must
be compared with those independent ordinary calculations, including a reversed
ranking or a failed improvement. Several distorted geometries of one scaffold
remain one scaffold, not several independent transfer examples. This proposed
control subsequently executed as described below. Relaxed geometries, zero-point energies
and thermal corrections are separate stages; its electronic target must not be
reported as an experimental proton affinity or finite-temperature enthalpy.

The completed all-electron control converged from both q=0 and q=1 to the
q=1 methyl-isocyanide endpoint. Independent ordinary element-basis calculations
confirmed a 19.8892 kcal/mol improvement in the clamped electronic protonation
target, and improvements of 21.0752, 22.0775 and 21.0483 kcal/mol on the three
predeclared ethyl configurations. Those configurations represent one additional
scaffold. The fixed-AO predictions overstated the improvements by approximately
103.23 to 103.41 kcal/mol. All six neutral/cation/reaction parameter gradient
and Hessian components passed the independent four-step fits, with orders
1.999395 to 2.001159 and minimum fit R2 0.999999910. This establishes the tested
fixed-geometry one-parameter derivatives, not nuclear or full-fragment Hessians.

Across these four target changes, the descriptive prediction-versus-reference
regression with an intercept has R2=0.996648052, slope 1.068166064 and intercept
-101.921878870 kcal/mol; all six pairwise orderings agree. This is a promising
local affine trend. It does not remove the raw predictive R2=-17796.856489 or
raw RMSE=103.354929 kcal/mol. Removing the mean bias estimated on the same four
points gives RMSE=0.071359 kcal/mol; that is a same-data diagnostic. Estimating

points gives MAE=0.162262 and RMSE=0.162899 kcal/mol. These are retrospective
calibration diagnostics, not new held-out acceptance, and no correction was
applied to the production energies or continuous optimization. Fresh scaffolds
and reactions are required for a predictive calibration test.

Existing-data accounting checks confirm identical endpoint nuclear charges,
electron counts, formal charges and fixed geometries between the two routes.
There is no frozen core or fragment E0 in this all-electron control. At the
methyl endpoint, the fixed-template neutral energy exceeds the ordinary
element-basis/grid energy by 1307.8771 kcal/mol, and the cation by 1204.6439;
their difference is the -103.2332 kcal/mol target-change discrepancy. The
saved energy-formula defect is at most 6.3e-13 Eh. Both calculations use PBE,
so this comparison does not measure functional-form error against nature.
That original endpoint comparison coupled basis and grid changes. The
completed matched calculation below isolates their effects; the original
evidence is retained. A fitted constant is not a substitute for that test. Evidence:
`.work/validation/real-molecule-target-actual-05/endpoint-accounting-diagnosis.json`
and `independent-affine-trend-assessment.json` in the same validation directory.

There is also a useful cancellation test for any proposed reference-energy
correction. Let the same fragment at the same parameter q contribute an
internal constant E0(q) to both the neutral and protonated molecule. Write
their energies as E_s(q)=E_tilde_s(q)+E0(q), where s identifies the charge
state. The electronic protonation target is then
A(q)=E_cation(q)-E_neutral(q)=E_tilde_cation(q)-E_tilde_neutral(q).
E0(q), its parameter gradient and its parameter Hessian cancel. Consequently,
a species-only energy constant cannot repair the observed error in
A(1)-A(0). A regression correction to that target is a separately tested
property predictor; it is not a corrected variational energy, force or Hessian.
Charge-state-dependent polarization would require an explicit energy model
and consistent density and response derivatives. It cannot be supplied as a
hidden fitted reference constant. The all-electron control above has E0=0.

#### Executed nuclear-geometry example at fixed fractional charges

A separate all-electron molecular example now optimizes nuclear coordinates,
rather than q. Two explicitly virtual centers have physical nuclear charges

state. Their integer nitrogen labels select the fixed ten-AO STO-3G basis and
grid recipe; the physical centers are not represented as ordinary nitrogen
atoms. PBE, grid level 1 and zero cutoff are used. Basis centers and the grid
are rebuilt at each geometry, and the public continuous-model nuclear gradient
includes their motion and the physical-charge correction. The midpoint and
orientation are rigid-body gauges; the bond length is the sole internal degree
of freedom and is relaxed.

#### Ethane: unconstrained all-atom reference and two reduced methyl groups

The ordinary ethane reference is now optimized with all 24 Cartesian
coordinates variable. No C-C or C-H length, bond angle, torsion, atom, point
group, or rigid methyl group is constrained. The calculation uses neutral
singlet PBE RKS, ordinary STO-3G (16 AOs, 18 electrons), grid level 1 and zero
weight cutoff. It starts from the previously computed rigid-methyl minimum;
that structure is only the starting point, with no inherited constraints.
The analytic Cartesian gradient rebuilds and differentiates the molecular
basis and grid. All 24 initial components pass independent central-energy
differences at 0.08, 0.04, 0.02 and 0.01 bohr: fitted orders range from
1.978821702 to 2.000885337, with minimum R2=0.999968648336. No component,
interval, or error floor is omitted.

The unconstrained optimizer converges after 69 updates. Its final energy is
-78.7583956010832 Hartree, C-C length 2.9300998573 bohr, and six C-H lengths
2.0900840814 through 2.0901289653 bohr.
The six C-C-H angles move from 109.4712 degrees to 110.7774--110.7917
degrees. The signed axial twist between the designated hydrogen pair changes
from -23 degrees to -59.9963 degrees; torsional relaxation is therefore
included rather than inferred from bond-length convergence. The maximum atomic force is
8.7937974e-6 Hartree/bohr; the RMS Cartesian force component is
4.3496980e-6 Hartree/bohr. Both are below the declared 1e-5 thresholds.
The entire gradient audit and optimization use 262 SCFs in 505.07 numerical
wall seconds, with the 35.31-second small harness link recorded separately.
These are measured costs under shared machine load, not a speed benchmark.
Coordinates, every accepted and rejected trial, gradients, electron traces
and SCF residuals are retained in
`.work/validation/ethane-cartesian-comparison-01/`.

The earlier C-C-only calculation remains a separate rigid-methyl diagnostic.
It converges to 2.9659338804 bohr for full ethane and 4.5224478030 bohr for two
identical reduced methyl records. The 1.5565139227-bohr disagreement is a
failed model-accuracy result, despite numerical convergence. That comparison
uses 16 full AOs versus 10 reduced AOs and 18 full electrons versus 16 frozen
plus 2 active electrons. Each saved internal-energy constant is added once.
Absolute energy comparability and frozen-fragment pair corrections are not
established; relative curves subtract each model's own computed minimum.
The reduced representation omits active internal C-H stretch and bend
coordinates. A subsequent calculation relaxes the distance and both fragment
orientations, removing only overall rigid-body gauges. All seven numerical
pose-coordinate derivative checks pass four-step fits; the production reduced
pose gradients are numerical, not analytic. After 20 accepted updates the
retained-coordinate optimizer converges to R=4.5219923116 bohr
(2.3929352792 Angstrom), radial force 2.8874e-6 Hartree/bohr and maximum
rotation-coordinate torque 4.8514e-6 Hartree/radian, each below 1e-5.
This run uses 800 SCFs in 135.76 numerical wall seconds, including independent
seed checks and the initial derivative audit. Its earlier compile failure is
retained and performed zero SCFs. The relaxed reduced C-C distance exceeds
the unconstrained full reference by 1.5918924544 bohr (0.8423932091 Angstrom):
chemical geometry accuracy fails. Orientation relaxation does not repair the
bond-length error. This is a local optimization from the declared starting
pose, not a global-search proof or full nuclear-Hessian acceptance.
Raw results are in `.work/validation/ethane-orientation-comparison-02/`.
The distance error is about 54.3 percent. Improving this reduced ethane model
is future work, not an accepted capability or the current optimization
benchmark. Saved-data decomposition already finds a large short-range
effective-core electrostatic contribution; an independent Gaussian formula
reproduces the two inspected core-pair energies within 2.3e-13 Hartree.
This does not establish the correctness of the transferred charge distribution
or the missing frozen-frozen short-range/XC terms. Future work must separate
these from projector, basis, frame and electronic-branch effects while
preserving the common parameter dimension and electron ledger. No fitted
constant, geometry-specific correction or shape term has been used to repair
this failure. Parameter optimization and real named-candidate validation
remain the active priority.
Neither this
ordinary all-atom success nor the fractional-charge example above establishes
reduced-fragment nuclear-gradient or chemical-accuracy acceptance.

The electron ledger deliberately distinguishes real-candidate provenance
from the continuous production chart. For a neutral monovalent fragment,
the chosen frozen count is N_f=sum(Z_fragment)-1: 8 for Me/NH2/OH/F,
16 for Et/Cl/OMe, 32 for CF3/tert-butyl, and 40 for phenyl. The methyl-capped
references therefore contain 18/26/42/50 total electrons respectively, but
all retain ten active electrons and use twelve reduced AOs. Every fragment
has effective ionic charge +1. In the primary target host the active count
is fixed at 26 with thirteen electrons per spin; the separately declared
N-methyl host retains 34. Differences in full-electron counts belong to
the explicit ordinary molecules, not to an interpolated frozen population.

Continuous simplex weights interpolate the fixed 51 operator coefficients
and the separately accounted reference energy E0. The model assigns no
N_f(q) or fractional nuclear identity to an interior mixture. Thus unequal
integer frozen counts do not silently change occupied rank or total active
charge along q. Fractional active occupations at fixed electron number
would be a separate ensemble extension requiring occupation constraints,
entropy/free-energy conventions and their response derivatives; it is not
used to conceal a non-Aufbau or unconverged SCF solution. Different active
electron, spin, basis, port or dictionary charts require explicit separate
searches and balanced ordinary reaction comparisons.

Electron counting and frozen-space exclusion are different conditions. In
the full frozen-reference construction, occupied coefficient matrices A
(active) and B (frozen) satisfy B^T S A=0, with densities P_A=2 A A^T and
P_B=2 B B^T in the AO overlap metric S. Their traces fix electron numbers,
while the orthogonality condition excludes reoccupation of the frozen
space. `pseudo_sub::reduction_reference::FrozenReferenceModel` constructs
and checks this constrained reference. A compressed production potential
approximates its action without retaining the full B matrix. Therefore
Tr(P_active S)=N_active alone cannot establish that the active state avoids
the original frozen space. The added-basis experiments below test this
distinction; an occupation count on one added orthogonal AO is not itself
a measurement of overlap with B. Neither a fractional frozen count nor a
fitted scalar energy constant repairs missing exclusion automatically.

The v3 reference partition diagonalizes the fragment-region population
operator in the orthonormal occupied space and freezes a prescribed integer
rank. Occupied orbital rotations leave this subspace invariant. A fixed
rank-cut spectral-gap guard rejects degeneracy rather than switching ranks;
the ten accepted references have minimum gap 0.3994, above the fixed 1e-6
guard. This guards the generation map locally, not global smoothness across
state crossings. Nuclear and pose derivatives still require their separate
complete model response. The subsequent ten-candidate calculation uses nine
independent simplex coordinates and must independently validate all nine
gradients and 81 ordered parameter-Hessian entries before optimization.
Its clamped ordinary-molecule ranking and optimization are not inferred from
the completed reference-generation checks.

Actual primary-host calculations on that ten-candidate four-AO chart accept

The best saved near-stationary determinant has fresh residual 6.943e-7,
trace 26.00000000000005, occupied/virtual block gap -0.0132887 Hartree,
and distance 0.6896 from the canonical Aufbau density. The overlap condition
number is only 12.41. Thus residual relaxation would accept the wrong
occupation branch; it is not a justified cure. A fixed-total-electron
occupation-mixing diagnostic lowers the energy for small fractional
redistribution, without changing the trace, but loses idempotency. It is
explicitly a diagnostic, not an accepted ensemble implementation or a
fractional frozen-electron model. These failures and the zero-SCF saved-state
audit remain in `named-ten-search-01`, `named-ten-search-02` and
`named-ten-state-inspection-01` under the private validation directory.

The earlier input-only four-candidate protocol contains 20 explicit structures: four capped
references, eight primary neutral/cation structures and eight untouched-host
structures. Its formulas, valences, charges, electron counts, finite
coordinates and minimum pair distances have been checked without DFT.
It is retained in `.work/validation/real-substituent-realization-plan-01`.
Even nominal size reduction is modest: the primary ordinary STO-3G AO counts
are 29, 28, 27 and 26, respectively. A common CoreSp template would use 26,
and CoreSpHH 28, before adding the proton AO. Thus some reduced routes would
have no AO saving or more AOs; actual timing and memory must determine any

frozen common-basis experiment.

The distinction is mathematical as well as numerical. Let B be the fixed AO
space, and let E_B(q) be the minimum of the same DFT energy over densities
representable in B, at the prescribed electron number. Continuous charge
derivatives describe E_B(q). An ordinary endpoint calculation instead uses its
element-specific space B_q. Even at an integer nuclear charge, minimizing in
B and in B_q need not give the same density or energy. A correct analytic
derivative of E_B does not establish that E_B approximates E_(B_q) accurately.
Here the two routes agree when their spaces and grids are matched, isolating
this finite-space effect from the tested implementation identity.

For each charge state s, define delta_s(q)=E_B,s(q)-E_(B_q),s(q). The error in
the predicted target change is
delta_cation(1)-delta_neutral(1)-delta_cation(0)+delta_neutral(0).
Large individual endpoint errors therefore cancel only when their charge-state
dependence cancels too. In the original control, B is the ordinary q=0 basis,
so the two q=0 deltas vanish; their q=1 difference produces the observed bias.
This explains why neither a common species energy constant nor a successful
finite-difference derivative fit removes the target error.

A common fixed span can enlarge the allowed densities at both endpoints while
keeping one smooth chart: its shell exponents, coefficients and order are
independent of q. It also increases evaluation cost and can worsen overlap
conditioning, which must be measured. In contrast, varying the basis with q
would require differentiating overlap, integrals and all affected response
terms. Simply selecting an element's basis at an integer or threshold value
would introduce an algorithmic discontinuity. Neither operation is silently
substituted for the fixed-chart derivatives in this work.

Nitro retains its formal N+/O- bookkeeping. These cover different donor,
acceptor, hydrogen-bonding, size, flexibility, polarity and shape hypotheses;
those descriptors are selection motives, not measured model properties.

`presets::get` constructs idealized, unrelaxed explicit atom coordinates,
integer atom labels, bonds and transported attachment-pose metadata. It does
not construct reduced electronic coefficients. `methyl_capped_reference`
creates an actual neutral, even-electron reference molecule instead of treating
an open-valence fragment as a closed-shell molecule. Formula, valence,
connectivity, collision, charge and rigid-pose tests are prepared; only Rust
syntax checking has run so far. No entry is advertised as a generated,
SCF-validated or transferable reduced model, and no heavy-element basis or
response coverage is implied. The legacy fitted-site parser still rejects
unsupported models. A generated record must separately establish the frozen
electron ledger, fixed operator dimension, chart compatibility, conditioning,
continuous derivatives and independent molecular validation. Adding a catalog
entry introduces no substituent-specific electronic parameter dimension.

Electron reduction also does not directly specify response cost. For the
