## Continuous chemical-species model

The `continuous-species` driver separates integer element/basis-template labels
from real physical nuclear charges `Z(q)=Z_ref+B q` and an independently supplied
fixed integer electron count. Physical total charge is `sum(Z)-N_e`; formal
input charge remains distinct. The first model is isolated all-electron
closed-shell RKS with LDA or PBE. AO shells/order/exponents/coefficients,
quadrature arrays, electron number, occupations and geometry remain fixed for
parameter derivatives. ECP, periodic, spin-changing, thermal, empirical
dispersion, solvent, modified functional and additional electronic models are
explicitly refused by this extension without removing ordinary capabilities.

`ContinuousSpeciesModel` owns these immutable arrays and caches the negative
unit-charge attraction matrices `V_A=-<chi|1/|r-R_A||chi>`.
`h_a=sum_A B_Aa V_A` enters every self-consistent Fock through the existing
scoped potential provider. The optional complete classical energy is supplied
before SCF, so iteration logs and final totals use the same physical charges.
The ordinary and multicomponent provider paths retain their previous classical
energy handling by passing no override. No geometry-dependent operator is put
in the ordinary `extra_hcore` option.

With spin-summed `P`, fixed AO/grid/electron number and converged variational
orbitals, `E_a=Tr[P h_a]+E_class,a` and
`E_ab=Tr[P^(b) h_a]+E_class,ab`. The classical Hessian includes
`sum_(A<B)(B_Aa B_Bb+B_Ab B_Ba)/R_AB` even though `h_ab=0`.
The existing Hartree/XC CPKS kernel supplies both spin density responses;
their sum is used without another occupation factor.

For recorded fixed origin `O`, the model uses
`mu=sum_A Z_A(R_A-O)-Tr[P(r-O)]`,
`mu_ia=sum_A B_Aa(R_A-O)_i-Tr[P^(a)(r-O)_i]`, and
`alpha_ij=-Tr[P^(F_j)(r-O)_i]`, consistent with
`E(F)=E(0)-mu.F-(1/2)F.alpha.F+...`.
The electronic origin shift is `-F.O S`; its explicit metric derivative is
included in the separate nuclear gradient. Nuclear gradients differentiate
moving AO/grid templates at fixed q and correct the attraction, repulsion and
nuclear field terms to use the physical real charges. This is distinct from
the clamped-geometry q derivative. Relaxed-geometry response and analytic
`alpha_q` are unsupported; they are never filled with zeros.

Native energy/dipole/alpha units are Hartree, e*Bohr and Bohr^3. The initial
driver coordinates are dimensionless, with explicit bounds and scale metadata;
their derivative axes follow parameter order. Reports include real total
charge, electron count, origin, functional, raw SCF/CPKS residuals, gap, AO
condition number and content fingerprints. Fingerprints include the complete
geometry, basis, quadrature and chart arrays. Cross-model state reuse is
refused. Continuation is an initial guess only; density/subspace comparisons,
independent guesses and reverse scans diagnose branch changes. Gap is not a
stability proof; the current report explicitly says stability was not evaluated.

The reproducible fixed N-template example uses labels `[7,7]`, coordinates
`[[0,0,-1.05],[0,0,1.05]]` Bohr, `fixed_electron_count=14`, reference charges
`[7,7]`, direction `[[-1,1]]`, midpoint origin and lambda in `[0,1]`.
The endpoint charges `[6,8]` retain N templates and are distinct from an
ordinary element-specific C/O basis calculation.

The authorized extension roadmap, after closing M1 acceptance, includes
molecular UKS with fixed integer alpha/beta counts and fixed spin occupations,
then fixed-cell/fixed-template periodic charge-conserving paths and their
open-shell combination. These are implementation stages, not current support
claims. Net-charge-varying periodic backgrounds, spin transitions, noncollinear
spin, SOC and ECP combinations remain separately scoped. The local Gaussian/
steric model and analytic alpha-parameter/Jacobian stages remain on the roadmap;
no neural-network training is included.

The isolated neutral Ewald chart now preserves integer template identifiers
separately from real charges and caches the complete real/reciprocal/self/
background charge matrix. Two source-local tests pass, covering both parameter
gradients and all four Hessian entries at four steps, translation/permutation
and invalid charts. The direct Ewald energy defect is 1.86e-15 Eh; maximum
gradient and Hessian finite-difference defects are 1.05e-13 and 3.93e-15 in
their native parameter units. This energy is exactly quadratic in charge,
so its structural Taylor identities are checked without claiming a nonzero
truncation-error exponent. Periodic electronic SCF/response integration remains
pending. Ordinary integer-charge forces, stress and shifted-k reconstruction
cannot be reused as real-charge derivatives without their own integration.

The fixed-spin molecular implementation now has an explicit
`fixed_spin_electron_counts=[N_alpha,N_beta]` control, with non-negative
integer counts, alpha >= beta and sum equal to `fixed_electron_count`.
It fixes the collinear UKS sector and includes both occupied/virtual response
blocks in the coupled Hartree/XC solve. Reference type and spin sector enter
the state fingerprint. Separate LDA/PBE UKS all-component, nuclear-gradient,
ordinary-reduction and public-surface acceptance is prepared; this new sector
is not yet included in the closed-shell acceptance measurements below.

The initial fixed-spin body passed all five new Rust cases and twelve
closed-shell regressions, but retained three public failures from a missing
spin-squared unit label. The rebuilt local-model body fixes that label and
passes all 33 continuous-species/local-model native/ASE/CLI cases, together
with 150 unit/driver-forwarding cases. A repeated-state regression also checks
occupied-subspace diagnostics against the actual separate spin occupations.

The local model code adds fixed-exponent spherical Gaussian electronic
potentials, affine electronic and nonnegative steric amplitudes in the same
dimensionless chart, explicit complete pair masks, and atom-centered or
three-anchor attached frames. Center/AO/frame derivatives enter nuclear
gradients; the classical steric overlap has no density kernel. Zero charge
columns can describe local amplitudes or an explicitly null direction.
Gaussian exponents, frame offsets, topology, basis and quadrature stay fixed
for parameter derivatives. A fitted constant fragment internal energy enters
the complete classical energy before SCF, including iteration logs.
Independent polynomial-moment integrals, all active center/AO derivatives,
all 27 frame Jacobian entries and steric gradients pass five isolated tests:
237 independent component fits, p=1.9960752282--2.0013886875,
minimum R2=0.9999989589, no failed intervals. Full SCF/local-model integration
now passes all four LDA/PBE by RKS/UKS cases: 116 independent component fits,
p=1.987782--2.017259, minimum R2=0.9999668, no failed intervals. Analytic q
gradient/Hessian, dipole Jacobian, static alpha, moving-template nuclear
gradients and static paired-response reduction are covered. Warning-strict
library/CLI/harness builds, Python lint, API/ledger checks and portable
source/artifact audits pass on the same immutable body.

Explicit Cartesian probes report positive electron-number density and the
physical electrostatic potential with zero at infinity. The non-Coulomb local
potential is not silently relabeled as a physical charge source. Optional
frequency response uses the existing coupled paired operator on the same
Hamiltonian; static and dynamic properties are separate fitting targets.

`tools/all_electron_center_baseline.py` and its matching test fixture retain
all nine methyl electrons on a charge-nine carbon template. This unexecuted
diagnostic is distinct from frozen-electron fragment compression. Its shape
coefficient is fixed to zero; electronic errors are not fitted into shape.

The candidate generator `pseudo_sub::reduction::generate_methyl` instead
extracts four internal occupied spatial orbitals from a closed-shell ethane
reference: carbon core and three C-H bonds. Its electron ledger is 18 full,
8 frozen and 10 active electrons, with a +1 effective ionic center. The chosen
H-like STO-3G center reduces the reference AO count from 16 to 9. The saved
rigid expansion restores the original integer atom labels and internal
geometry. Ordinary atom paths remain unchanged.

The generator uses a common constrained operator projection in the full
reference AO metric. Three fixed Gaussian charge widths carry a neutral
correction to the +1 point ion and its permanent dipole. Three local Gaussian
amplitudes and a symmetric eight-projector operator approximate the remaining
frozen electrostatic, Pauli and nonadditive XC residual. Active Hartree and XC
are subtracted before projection. The internal reference energy is fixed once
at the reference active density, rather than fitted to a reduced SCF energy
or a bond curve. The generated coefficients remain fixed during geometry scans.

Two generation tests pass, including deterministic generation, strict model
roundtrip, charge/dipole constraints and invalid-model rejection. For PBE the
same-AO frozen reference differs from the full reference by 2.84e-14 Eh. The
sigma projection has rank 8/8 and weighted squared residual 14.023267; the
remaining electronic projection has rank 39/39 and residual 0.496386. These
operator residuals do not establish chemical accuracy. Independent kernel
tests pass 1008 derivative component fits (p=1.994395--2.018343, minimum
R2=0.9999782); the assembled static-core operator and classical energy pass
492 fits (p=1.987767--2.073252, minimum R2=0.9996866).

The production consumer `continuous_species::reduced::evaluate_candidate`
assembles the active variational SCF with those fixed operators and reference
constant. Electron/core/field interactions use the same effective charge
distribution; frame and moving-AO derivatives enter its nuclear gradient.
The first compiled candidate converges with 10 active electrons in 9 AOs,
orbital residual 2.99e-13, and trace defect below 2e-15 electrons. All 15 nuclear
gradient and three dipole component fits pass (p=1.999704--2.019818, minimum
R2=0.99996265, no failed intervals). The nine-point rigid ethane attachment
curve nevertheless fails chemical accuracy: relative-energy MAE 0.456471 Eh,
maximum 0.947421 Eh and stretch-force RMSE 4.212620 Eh/Bohr. Its reference
energy offset is not reset. Thus variational/derivative consistency passes,
while this one-center projection is not an accepted chemical model. The
electrostatic and electronic projection defects require separate diagnosis;
shape coefficients are not fitted to absorb them.

Records explicitly say candidate, shape not generated, and active-only
response with no internal polarization. Shape projection and transferable
chemical accuracy have not been established. Frozen-model UKS
and periodic combinations remain subsequent independent stages.

Independent diagnosis found the original charge projection was dominated by
removed frozen AO support: exact-sigma full-metric norm 25.43 versus 24.23 in
the frozen block. Fitted neutral Gaussian monopoles were approximately
[14.391, -43.781, 29.390]; the retained-core electrostatic energy defect was
-2.2394 Eh. A single separately recorded physical-ESP construction experiment
uses 47 fixed reference probes with weight 1e6, unchanged dictionary dimensions
and no shape/energy fit. It reduces that defect to -0.1678 Eh and curve MAE to
0.084790 Eh, but stretch-force RMSE remains 0.809146 Eh/Bohr. This is still an
unaccepted candidate. The nine-AO span also misses 0.4356 electrons of reference
occupied-space metric weight; minimum occupied capture is 0.7926. A common
one-center valence s/p template is compared below.

The controlled construction comparison fixes the same 47 reference ESP
probes and their weight 1e6, then crosses H1s versus valence s/p AO templates
with the full-AO versus physical-support/Pauli-normalized projection metric.
Both retain 12 electrostatic and 39 electronic coefficients, the same frozen
eight electrons and an E0 determined only at the reference active density.
All failed candidates are retained. Selection uses only the nine-point rigid
ethane construction curve. The proposed chemical gates remain relative-energy
MAE below 1 kcal/mol, 95th percentile below 2 kcal/mol and generalized-force
RMSE below 1e-3 Eh/Bohr; derivative and convergence gates remain independent.
Propane and isobutane are separate C(sp3)-port transfer evaluations
with the selected coefficients and exact same internal template. They are not
used to retune that candidate. Any later use for tuning changes their split
status and requires a new held-out scaffold. Other port classes remain separate.

The exact shared practical-03 artifact passes all seven Rust acceptance suites.
The four construction alternatives all fail the predefined chemical gates:

| Fixed AO template | Projection metric | Relative-energy MAE (Eh) | P95 (Eh) | Cartesian force RMSE (Eh/Bohr) | Dipole-vector RMSE (e Bohr) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H1s, 9 total AOs | full AO | 0.084789599 | 0.190431633 | 0.315018826 | 1.768482174 |
| H1s, 9 total AOs | normalized support | 0.083531189 | 0.195610541 | 0.320086716 | 1.787095805 |
| valence s/p, 12 total AOs | full AO | 0.069657351 | 0.161686490 | 0.249535411 | 0.287435541 |
| valence s/p, 12 total AOs | normalized support | 0.055804209 | 0.138377925 | 0.214507274 | 0.380415726 |

These are nine-point rigid C-C stretch curves, with relative energies measured
against each model's own central point, a fixed reference E0, G=0 and no
eliminated internal polarization. Cartesian force RMSE averages the generalized
Cartesian components and is distinct from the earlier stretch-force RMSE.
The construction-only energy winner still has MAE 35.02 kcal/mol. Its unchanged
parameters and internal geometry give propane MAE 0.066127308 Eh, P95
0.163643252 Eh and force RMSE 0.199069795 Eh/Bohr; isobutane gives 0.067706394,
0.168749404 and 0.174669260 in the same units. Both transfer evaluations fail.
They may inform later design, but must then cease to be called unseen holdouts.
The full-metric s/p candidate has the smallest dipole error; selecting on
energy alone does not select the best electronic property model.

The selected candidate passes 27 independent nuclear-force, dipole and active
static-alpha component fits (p=1.997149--2.006407, minimum R2=0.99999718).
Same-AO constrained frozen and unprojected static controls reproduce the full
reference energy to about 1e-13 Eh from two independent seeds. Separately,
transporting the reference frozen occupied coefficients with metric
normalization over nine distances gives maximum freezing error 0.000387501 Eh
(0.243 kcal/mol), with seed energies agreeing within 8.53e-14 Eh. This transport
differs from a rigid charge-field transport; the remaining large error combines
operator compression and transport approximations, rather than measuring AO
compression alone. No transported-reference force claim follows.

A rejected test-only four-charge-site/one-electronic-center sigma dictionary
improves the retained-core energy defect from -0.167789 to +0.013689 Eh but
worsens excluded-probe ESP RMSE from 0.077616 to 4.82599 atomic units, with
large cancelling coefficients. It is retained as a failed candidate, without
production integration or fitting its error into G.

Three interleaved energy-plus-analytic-force timings give full-model median
3.59483 s versus reduced 1.54199 s, excluding 2.37183 s generation. This small
fixture reduces 18 to 10 active electrons, 16 to 12 AOs and 25192 to 15068 grid
points; the measured median ratio is 2.33 and the estimated generation
amortization is 1.16 calls (two whole evaluations), excluding candidate
selection and validation scans. Three repetitions are not a general performance
claim, and speed does not establish chemical accuracy. Response was not timed.

The isolated analytic `alpha_q` extension now passes numerical LDA/PBE by
RKS/UKS acceptance on the same artifact: all 120 independent mixed-response
components pass four-step fits, with three failed initial intervals retained
and resolved on predefined alternate intervals. Independently refitting the
printed raw errors gives p=1.961699436--2.078499976, minimum R2=0.999059775.
Public integration remains
pending; the driver rejects that response rather than returning zeros.

A subsequent test-only projection maps all twelve frozen-complement reference
eigenstates through the square polar factor of their reduced-basis overlaps.
It constructs a ten-electron idempotent reference and a commuting effective
operator, subtracts the active-system Fock at that same density, and projects
the residual with the unchanged 39 electronic coefficients. This is an
isometric proxy, not the physical least-squares projection of the reference
density: discarded overlap singular values remain reported. The same fixed
sigma and a once-only E0 give curve MAE 0.035311358 Eh for the original eight
primitive projectors, or 0.034360913 Eh for eight fixed contracted original
fragment AOs used solely as projectors. The latter has four projector sites
and one electronic AO center, not four explicit electronic atoms. Both
candidates still fail chemical accuracy; neither has analytic-force or
transfer acceptance. Their central energy slopes remain positive
(+0.27147/+0.26412 Eh/Bohr), whereas the explicit curve has -0.04449 Eh/Bohr.
Thus the lower MAE has not recovered the local bonding trend. These slopes
are finite-interval curve diagnostics, not analytic forces. Their operator
Gram-matrix data condition numbers are about 1.54e8
and 3.89e7, respectively, with regularization recorded separately.

Both initial densities agree at every point under strict fresh Fock, trace and
idempotency gates. An independent nine-point full-reference oracle checks all
converged flags and fresh physical residuals (maximum 4.07e-13), reproducing
the cached curve energies within 2.85e-14 Eh. The diagnostic evaluator first
reproduces the unchanged production candidate within 8.53e-14 Eh in energy
and 7.85e-13 e Bohr in dipole. No test-only rule is mislabeled as an accepted
serialized model or integrated into production.

A separate fixed one/two/three-center AO-span comparison adds zero-ion-charge
H1s auxiliary contractions along predefined fragment directions. Reference
occupied-space metric losses are 0.0515270, 0.0491218 and 0.0399146 electrons
for 12, 13 and 14 AOs; overlap condition numbers increase from 11.29 to about
142--144. These are capture diagnostics only: no electron count is inferred
from AO count, and no multi-center SCF, force, chemical or speed acceptance is
claimed. The small capture gain alone does not justify those extra centers.

An exact-density diagnostic further restricts active orbitals to the physical
SP12 AO span intersected with the frozen-occupied orthogonal complement.
This has eight available spatial directions: all nine points have rank-four
frozen constraints, with a clear positive eigenvalue gap rather than a
numerical rank ambiguity. Eighteen two-seed SCFs pass strict fresh physical
gates. The reference energy rises by 0.998499460 Eh relative to the full-AO
frozen model; its relative curve MAE is 0.067341163 Eh against explicit DFT
and 0.067323212 Eh against the full frozen curve. Thus exact exclusion within
the plain reduced AO span is highly restrictive. Orthogonalizing that span
in the full AO space adds implicit frozen-space tails and defines a different
space; the square-polar trial transfers the one-electron operator but does
not restore the exact density functional. This comparison establishes neither
a production compression scheme nor a force result. Its compile-only unused
diagnostic failure is retained separately from the repaired numerical run.

Keeping the carbon core-s basis contraction while still freezing the same
eight electrons changes that conclusion substantially. A bundled five-AO
carbon contraction on the +1 ionic role gives thirteen total AOs and nine
active intersection directions. The reference exclusion penalty falls from
0.998499 to 0.021336 Eh; the relative-curve MAE falls to 0.00519423 Eh
(3.26 kcal/mol), maximum 0.0119305 Eh. All eighteen strict two-seed solves
pass. Adding a basis function is distinct from unfreezing its occupation:
the ledger remains eight frozen and ten active electrons. This promising
basis diagnosis still exceeds the energy criterion and uses the exact
full-density frozen reference, not a generated thirteen-AO static potential.
It cannot replace the measured 0.03436 Eh best static-candidate result.

Nested two- and three-center exact-density controls retain the same C5 basis
and add the first, then second, ordered internal H1s contractions at their
original positions. These auxiliary sites have zero ionic charge. With
fourteen/fifteen total AOs and ten/eleven available active directions, relative
curve MAEs are 0.00357830/0.00170172 Eh (2.245/1.068 kcal/mol), maxima
0.00830092/0.00412451 Eh (5.209/2.588 kcal/mol). Both miss the unchanged
1 kcal/mol MAE and 2 kcal/mol P95 criteria. All thirty-six strict SCFs pass
and the nested variational bounds hold. These reference controls neither fit
new coefficients nor establish production multi-center forces or speed.

The common experimental `CarbonCoreValenceSp` AO template is implemented with
the distinct ID `one-center-core-valence-sp-local3-projector8-charge3-v1`.
Four isolated contraction/ledger/metric/capture tests pass. It captures
9.97757434 of ten reference occupied-space electron weights versus 9.94847299
for the valence-only alternative, with overlap condition 11.36. A consumer
preflight changes only this basis, preserving the selected old sigma, all
39 electronic coefficients and E0: its curve MAE is 0.06007147 Eh, worse than
the twelve-AO candidate. The exact-density reference improvement therefore
does not carry over automatically to an unchanged static operator. New
whole-library and strict Clippy gates pass on the isolated practical-05
artifact, and all 52 native/ASE/CLI cases pass, including this template.
The same saved-template native/ASE comparison also passes through the second
compiled CLI entry, `dft_rs_cli`; the two CLI artifacts have identical hashes.
Analytic-force/active-response acceptance is tracked separately: the initial
new test stopped before finite differences because it expected three residual
entries rather than the actual null-parameter plus three-field entries.
The corrected test retains every residual tolerance and derivative gate; the
first failed run remains preserved. The corrected test passes all 27 component
fits on steps [0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025], with independently refitted
p=1.993043067--2.002307818, minimum R2=0.9999970516 and no failed intervals.
Finest/Richardson maximum errors are 4.36213e-6/1.27462e-10 Eh/Bohr for the
15 nuclear gradients, 7.94387e-6/3.17735e-10 e Bohr for three dipoles, and
1.88691e-5/1.74307e-9 Bohr^3 for nine active-only alpha entries. These are
model derivative checks, not agreement with explicit chemical forces.
An additional independent energy difference at h=0.001 Bohr checks all
fifteen nuclear-gradient components against the 1e-6 Eh/Bohr absolute target:
maximum error 6.97931e-7 Eh/Bohr, all pass without requiring the predeclared
finer fallback. The original twenty-seven four-step fits remain unchanged.
The 150 unit/forwarding checks, API/ledger checks, Python lint and final
portable audit also pass. These measurements remain separate from
the accepted practical-03 artifact and the failed chemical criteria.

Further fixed-dimension electrostatic ablations retain twelve coefficients,
eight free directions and exact charge/dipole constraints. Fitting normalized
full-AO and 78 geometric ESP samples with equal group weights worsens exterior
potential/electric-field RMSE to 0.18282/0.32097 for centered Gaussians and
0.37475/0.51817 for three C-H midpoint sites, versus the old candidate's
0.03131/0.07640 on the same 190 exterior validation points. Both are rejected.
They have positive Coulomb self-Gram regularization without eigenvalue floors;
improving an inner-AO operator fit does not ensure an accurate external field.

Removing only the AO fitting rows, with the same widths, 78 training samples,
constraints and Coulomb regularizer, improves RMS errors on a freshly rotated
192-point exterior set: centered potential/field RMSE is 0.01672/0.04550,
midpoint 0.02049/0.05127, versus unchanged old coefficients 0.02135/0.05259.
Maximum errors worsen slightly in both new fits. Retained-core force defects
remain -0.15978 and -0.42189 Eh/Bohr versus old -0.15759. These are field-fit
candidates, not evidence of bond-force or transfer accuracy. The centered
ESP-only data Gram condition is 2.63e7 (regularized 284), explicitly exposing
radial nonidentifiability; no unstable direction is silently clipped.
Previously inspected probe sets become seen validation/stress sets and are
not reused under an unseen-holdout label.

Consistently regenerating the 39 electronic coefficients for each ESP-only
sigma at the same mapped reference, with each E0 fixed before SCF, also fails
to improve the nine-point static-model curve. MAEs are 0.03620577 Eh for the
centered correction and 0.06884307 Eh for the midpoint correction, compared
with 0.03531136 Eh for the prior primitive-projector trial. Eighteen points
from two seeds pass strict physical gates, so this is a chemical limitation
rather than SCF failure. Both correction proposals are rejected. Independent
four-step scalar-potential differences validate all nine components of the
analytic frozen-reference field oracle; no curve fit or G compensation is
used to rescue the failed candidates.

A density-consistent core model is a subsequent hypothesis for testing, not
an implemented accuracy claim. The [projection embedding energy derivation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3419460/)
uses the combined active/frozen density and orbital exclusion; its original
full-AO construction does not certify a truncated AO model. Here the static
consumer instead evaluates active-density Hartree/XC with a fitted fixed
operator for the missing effects. The failed ablations motivate comparing
that approximation with a consistent frozen-core-density treatment. Such a
new model version must derive its scalar energy, Fock, response kernel and
moving-core forces together, using the same charge distribution for electron,
core and field interactions and removing any duplicated fitted XC term.
Increasing a penalty or fitting G to the remaining electronic error is not
an established remedy.

To isolate a consistent rigid frozen-core reference, the four selected frozen
orbitals are S-metric projected onto the original eight Me AOs and normalized
once. Their coefficients then remain fixed on the rigid fragment; host rows
are zero and no geometry-dependent renormalization or E0 offset is applied.
All eighteen full-sixteen-AO reference solves pass strict physical checks.
The unshifted localization/freeze penalty at the central geometry is
0.012482153 Eh; the relative curve MAE is 0.000654653 Eh (0.411 kcal/mol),
maximum 0.001643208 Eh (1.031 kcal/mol). Frozen charge eight, ionic charge
one, internal kinetic/self-Hartree energies and body-frame permanent moments
remain invariant. This meets the proposed relative-energy criteria at the
uncompressed reference level only; it establishes neither compressed-model
accuracy nor nuclear forces. Later operator extraction must use this new
localized-frozen SCF minimum, since the old active reference belongs to a
different constraint subspace. The compile-only first attempt is retained.

Same-reference decomposition: PBE/STO-3G ethane, nine rigid C-C distances R0 +/-0.20 bohr in 0.05-bohr steps, one fixed strictly Me8-localized frozen density (8 electrons), 10 active electrons, and the same original eight-nucleus grid. The 72 two-seed constrained SCFs passed their fresh physical gates. The signed energy differences are full DFT -> localized frozen full16 -> physical C13/C14/C15 intersection; relative errors subtract each channel at R0 before taking absolute values. All fitted-electrostatics candidates fail the 1 kcal/mol mean-error target;
the smallest mean error is approximately 7.005 kcal/mol. Exact frozen-density
electrostatics is an uncompressed diagnostic and does not establish a
production-model success. Contracted Me8 projectors require four sites even
when the electronic basis has fewer centers. Dense static oracles remain
R0 checks only: a physical geometry transport for their XC/Pauli matrices
has not been declared. No new force, response, speed or heldout acceptance
follows from these energy curves. All failed candidates and raw iterations
are retained in `.work/validation/localized-fixed-curves-01/`.

The separate Rust-only few-center consumer now distinguishes positive ionic
sites from exactly zero-ion auxiliary basis roles and enforces operator,
functional and fixed-dictionary identities before SCF. Its isolated second
candidate passes seven metadata gates, including whole-library unit
typechecking and strict Clippy. Actual quantum-force and fixed-spin response
acceptance on its native artifact is still pending; this is not a public
few-center API or a chemical-accuracy promotion.

The rectangular mapped chart is a new approximation, not recovery of the same physical frozen-density intersection. C13/C14/C15 now map all12 physical complement states into 13/14/15 model AOs and exclude an abstract rank1/2/3 complement; the previous physical intersections allowed9/10/11 states and excluded four physical frozen directions. The new projection uses plain W=Smodel^(-1/2), whereas the previous objective normalized active/Pauli support. Both chart and objective change; the comparison is not a pure basis ablation. The common format remains39 electronic plus12 sigma coefficients (51 raw coefficients), with identical sigma coefficients in each matched old/new template. Coefficients across different templates are close but not identical (maximum difference from C13 is 5.53e-6).

These allowed/excluded dimensions describe the reference or chart construction. Both static consumer SCFs solve the full n-AO problem with finite exclusion potentials.

The active trace is10 and frozen trace8, but the mapped active density overlaps PB. The resulting off-shell total-density functional value is a raw diagnostic, not a physical frozen-embedding minimum. E0 assigns the localized full16 reference energy at Pmap once. Dense static SCF recovery checks that assigned anchor; it does not demonstrate physical density or energy recovery. Fixed39 models subsequently relax away from the anchor without resetting E0. Both static consumer SCFs use the full n-AO model space with finite exclusion potentials; stated dimensions describe the reference/chart, not a hard SCF projection.

The descriptive lowest fitted-sigma MAE is C13 contractedMe8-4projectorsites fittedsigma-plus-shortrefit: 1.918576 kcal/mol, prespecified nearest-rank P95/max 6.464791. The original descriptive report instead labels interpolated P95 5.562649; both conventions are preserved explicitly, and the nearest-rank rule remains the gate. Its R0 total dipole vector error is 0.069745 D, an isolated seen static result rather than response/transfer acceptance.
For mapped C13 contractedMe8, fitted sigma improves the full-DFT curve although its operator residual is larger than the exact-sigma variant. The same sigma coefficients also yield different curves after39 coefficients are refitted. This supports combined-error cancellation as a diagnostic and cannot establish pure electrostatic improvement. Native-versus-mapped residual norms use different metrics and must not be ranked as a common error norm. All data are already seen ethane/reference data. No force, alpha, independent scaffold holdout, speed or completed chemical-model claim follows.

The current experimental native few-center consumer implements the primitive projector recipe and continues to reject contracted-projector records. The descriptive best contracted candidate therefore has no native force or public API acceptance. Body-frame conversion and its analytic geometric derivatives require a separately validated provider.

Methylcyclopropane first-scaffold transfer: all 36 SCFs passed numerical gates (32 full electrons/28 AO; 8 frozen, 24 active electrons/25 AO; one fragment electronic center, four projector sites). With fixed parameters and E0, all nine zero-field points including R0 give relative-energy MAE 5.841226 kcal/mol and nearest-rank P95=max 13.322393 kcal/mol, failing the predeclared 1/2 kcal/mol gates. Total dipole-vector RMSE/max are 0.347803/0.529278 D. All 216 predeclared far-field ESP errors give RMSE/max 0.000788922723/0.00289817721 Eh per positive elementary charge; no independent ESP accuracy threshold was predeclared. Applied field was zero; the nonzero fixture field was unused metadata. Input hashes and protocol verified. Construction accuracy remains failed; no force, alpha, frozen internal response or speed acceptance. This independent query must become seen validation if it informs further model choices. Raw data and independent assessment: .work/validation/methylcyclopropane-transfer-01/.

A controlled occupied-space metric ablation keeps the mapped chart, contracted eight-projector dictionary, electrostatic coefficients and common 51-coefficient schema fixed. Increasing occupied amplitude from 1 to 2 reduces occupied-transition squared residuals to 0.6000–0.8578 of baseline in all six R0 cases across the three fixed center templates and paired exact/fitted electrostatic controls. Unweighted residuals increase by factors 1.1456–1.3417 and virtual-block residuals by 1.61–4.90. All 12 independently seeded SCFs pass, with less downward R0 relaxation and less abstract excluded population in every case. These observations justify the predefined six-case bond-curve falsification test; they do not establish chemical improvement or repair the unchanged physical mapping defects. The exact electrostatic controls remain uncompressed diagnostics. Baseline coefficient/E0 replay zero errors are harness assertions because replay arrays were not exported; new preflight/final coefficients and block-norm identities were independently verified. No held-out environment entered the fit. Evidence: `.work/validation/occupied-metric-ablation-01/independent-assessment.json`.

The fixed occupied-amplitude2 metric ablation completed all six matched construction curves (54 points, 108 SCFs) without refitting the 39 electronic coefficients, 12 Gaussian electrostatic coefficients or E0 along a curve. Independent recomputation retained all nine points including R0 and the nearest-rank P95 protocol. All numerical branch, SCF, number and projector gates passed, but every chemical energy gate failed.

| C13 | fitted | 1.918576 / 6.464791 | 5.767250 / 13.144339 |

Only the three-center fitted-electrostatics curve improves; its MAE of 1.421571 and P95 of 4.495999 kcal/mol remain above the 1 and 2 kcal/mol targets. All exact-electrostatics curves and the one- and two-center fitted curves worsen. This supports a changed residual balance, not a universally better projection metric or a pure electrostatic improvement. No new C15 heldout test was performed; the earlier C13 methylcyclopropane errors do not characterize this model. C15 uses 15 AO versus 16 full AO and retains the full 8-site grid and 4 projector sites; no speedup is claimed. Gap values, relaxed physical-PB overlaps, full-DFT dipole accuracy, contracted forces and response are not established by these outputs. Raw curves, matched inputs and independent assessment are in `.work/validation/occupied-metric-fixed-curves-01/`.

Chemical precision is a joint target with fixed common parameter dimensions, physical electron/charge accounting, continuity, transferability and useful cost reduction. The 51-coefficient static representation has one charge-neutrality constraint, hence 50 independent coefficient directions; E0 is held separately. Existing nuclear-charge sensitivities do not validate these coefficient sensitivities. The fixed saved-model consumer currently evaluates a zero nuclear-charge direction, so coefficient Eq, Eqq, mixed dipole sensitivities, branch continuation and generation-map continuity remain separate pending gates. Explicit center/AO/electron/spin/topology/model-version changes define different charts. Each production curve holds its generated coefficients and reference-energy offset fixed; no pointwise regeneration or accuracy-dependent thresholds are used. A candidate that loses these common-model conditions is ineligible for practical acceptance even if its mean energy error becomes small.

The occupied-first fixed-chart experiment completed all six contracted one-, two- and three-center construction curves (nine geometries per model, 54 model points and 108 SCFs) with plain amplitude1 projection. All fixed theta/E0/sigma bits, source hashes, 54 raw summaries and numerical gates were independently checked. The reused ELF retains its generic amplitude2 header; generation provenance and the raw-output fingerprint identify the occupied-first input. The raw output is unchanged, and normalized metadata preserves identical numeric curves.

All values above are kcal/mol over all nine points including R0, with nearest-rank P95 equal to the maximum. All six new curves fail the unchanged MAE 1 and P95 2 kcal/mol criteria. All three exact-electrostatics curves improve relative to symmetric/plain1, while the fitted curve improves only for C13 and worsens for C14/C15. Improved occupied capture and physical mapping diagnostics at R0 therefore do not establish a practically accurate compressed model. Exact/fitted differences include electronic reprojection and residual cancellation; they are not a pure electrostatic ablation. The previous symmetric-map amplitude2 C15 fitted candidate retains the lowest fitted-model MAE among these experiments; the new C13 fitted candidate has a lower P95 but a higher MAE. Both fail the criteria. The C15 exact-electrostatics diagnostic is uncompressed and is not a production-model accuracy result. No old C13 heldout error is transferred to the new candidates. Full-DFT dipole truth, gap, contracted forces, parameter-response derivatives and internal response remain unestablished here. All fitted models retain 51 stored coefficients and a common 50-dimensional charge-preserving tangent; fixed chart and continuity conditions still apply. The full 8-site quadrature and four projector sites remain, so no speedup is inferred. Evidence: `.work/validation/occupied-first-fixed-curves-01/independent-assessment.json`.

The common static amplitude vector contains 51 principal operator coefficients (39 electronic and 12 electrostatic), with E0 stored as a separate scalar: this is not a claim that the entire serialized model has only 51 numbers. The charge-preserving tangent has 50 amplitude directions only after fixing E0, the template, dictionary, electron/spin sector and geometry conventions. The contracted Me8 provider additionally stores three ordered internal hydrogen offsets (nine geometry values); they are rigid internal coordinates that affect the electronic projector and grid, not purely steric G coefficients. Its radial exponents and contractions come from fixed bundled C/H basis data and are not independently fitted per reference. The dictionary fingerprint binds the offsets, source labels and template, so equal amplitude-vector lengths do not establish a compatible chart across references or scaffolds. This implementation explicitly supports a C/H3 fragment; a general substituent or ligand workflow is not yet established. Expanding every fragment AO into an unrestricted projector would make the symmetric projector matrix dimension fragment-dependent and is not an accepted generalization of the fixed common representation. Evidence: `.work/validation/common-parameter-storage-audit-01/audit.json`.

Independent reconstruction of all 18 cached curves reproduces every signed error and odd/even pair exactly; RMS values differ by at most 4.44e-16 kcal/mol, and the parity sum-of-squares identity holds within 2.72e-20 Eh^2. With exact-sigma diagnostic operators, the occupied-first mapping reduces odd/even RMS for all three AO templates: C13 from 8.458/0.523 to 6.043/0.419, C14 from 5.049/0.319 to 3.416/0.273, and C15 from 2.253/0.171 to 1.728/0.150 kcal/mol. Conversely, amplitude2 on the symmetric mapping worsens both oracle residual components for every template. The fitted-sigma models show a different interaction. For C13, occupied-first reduces odd RMS from 1.597 to 0.211, while even RMS remains large at 2.327; its P95 still fails at 4.122 kcal/mol. For C15, amplitude2 reduces odd/even RMS from 4.690/2.901 to 0.869/1.955, whereas occupied-first with amplitude1 worsens odd RMS to 5.006. C14 fitted-sigma likewise gains slightly in even error but worsens in odd error under the new mapping. There is no universally superior mapping or metric in the completed data.

The next controlled experiment should complete the missing occupied-first mapping x preexisting amplitude2 quadrant for all three templates and both sigma modes, retaining the common 51 coefficients, fixed widths/ridge, integer electron ledger, and one R0 energy constant per candidate. This tests the mapping-metric interaction without tuning another weight or adding substituent-specific channels. Odd/even components are parity diagnostics, not analytic force or Hessian measurements. Exact/fitted sigma pairs also reproject 39 electronic coefficients and relax their densities, so their differences are not a pure electrostatic decomposition. All completed models still fail the declared chemical gates; the successful standard-library analysis does not establish an angular floor for the current localized reference or validate the uncompiled force/q providers.

Predictive trend metrics are now reported separately from the absolute accuracy goals. The cached assessment scores 24 seen ethane construction models and only the original frozen C13 methylcyclopropane query. Predictive R2 is 1-SSE/SST on unadjusted relative-energy predictions. Each full/model curve uses its own fixed R0 reference once, without fitted offsets, pointwise correction or pooling between molecules. Pearson correlation squared, descriptive slope/intercept, Spearman rank and pairwise order counts are separate quantities; the descriptive regression is never applied to the predictions. Finite-difference error-fit R2 measures another property entirely.

| Candidate and evaluation | Predictive R2 | MAE (kcal/mol) | Spearman | Concordant pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Symmetric/amplitude2 C15 fitted, seen construction | 0.796524 | 1.421571 | 0.783333 | 30/36 |
| Occupied-first/amplitude1 C13 fitted, seen construction | 0.757224 | 1.646844 | 0.850000 | 31/36 |
| Occupied-first/amplitude1 C14 fitted, seen construction | 0.343784 | 2.304085 | 1.000000 | 36/36 |
| Original symmetric/plain1 C13, original new-scaffold query | -4.038597 | 5.841226 | -0.533333 | 13/36 |

The perfectly ordered C14 construction curve has a descriptive energy slope of 1.695867, so its ordering success does not establish calibrated energy differences. The original new-scaffold query also fails trend prediction: energy RMSE is 6.953454 kcal/mol, maximum error is 13.322393 kcal/mol, and slope is -0.558356. Its dipole-vector RMSE/max remain 0.347803/0.529278 D; absolute component predictive R2 values are strongly negative despite large squared correlation for some components. Undefined zero-variance scores are reported as unavailable, never zero-filled. Full-DFT construction dipole truth remains pending.

A useful trend model and an absolute chemical-accuracy model are distinct possible outcomes. No retrospective trend-qualified threshold or accepted model is declared here. The existing 1 kcal/mol MAE and 2 kcal/mol P95 goals remain visible separately. These Me-only attachment curves do not validate ranking different substituents or transfer to Et, CF3, Cl, Ph, tBu or untouched low-symmetry environments. The original methylcyclopropane query becomes seen validation if used for later choices, and its scores are not assigned to new candidates. Evidence: `.work/validation/few-model-trend-assessment-01/metrics.json`.

The final public candidate suite passes 51 native/ASE/CLI cases after repairing
an omitted optional resource-key lookup in the ASE getter. The first 50/51
failure remains recorded; the corrected Python-only overlay uses the exact
same compiled library. The frozen body also passes 150 unit/forwarding cases,
API/ledger checks, lint and portable artifact audit. These implementation
results remain separate from the failed chemical criteria.

For the eight-atom ethane ordering and Bohr coordinates in
`python/tests/test_reduced_fragment.py`, the actual saved-model entry is:

```python
import dft_rs

spec = dict(explicit_atoms=[4, 5, 6, 7], retained_atoms=[0, 1, 2, 3],
            port=[4, 0, 1], electronic_centers=1,
            single_bonds=[[0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [0, 4],
                          [4, 5], [4, 6], [4, 7]])
generated = dft_rs.generate_methyl_fragment(numbers, positions_bohr,
                                           fragment_spec=spec, cpu_threads=1)
result = dft_rs.evaluate_reduced_fragment(
    [6, 1, 1, 1, 1], [positions_bohr[i] for i in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]],
    model=generated["model_json"], cpu_threads=1)
```

The last H label selects an ionic/basis role, while the saved source retains
the original carbon and hydrogens. It does not change the frozen-electron
ledger into an ordinary five-atom all-electron model. The generator's default
is the original H1s candidate; alternative fixed template and projection-rule
controls must be supplied explicitly. Reading a saved candidate never
regenerates parameters at the evaluated geometry.

The bounded M1 acceptance passes: 12 Rust cases, 19 native/ASE/CLI cases,
9 unit-regression cases, all registered driver forwarding checks and an
additional native/ASE/CLI analytic-force comparison. Warning-strict builds,
Clippy metadata, Python lint, API/ledger consistency and portable artifact
audits pass. A stale generated API reference was repaired and rechecked; its
original failing check remains in the validation record.

The 82 independently refitted derivative components cover LDA/PBE asymmetric
charge gradients/Hessians, dipole Jacobians, static alpha, mixed field/charge
derivatives, nuclear gradients and tilted N-template path derivatives. Every
fit uses four distinct steps without floors: accepted p spans
1.9560576090--2.0504100845 and minimum R2 is 0.9991301119. Sixteen failed
intervals are retained; their predeclared resolved intervals pass the unchanged
|p-2|<0.2 and R2>0.999 gates. At h=0.00025, maximum absolute errors are
3.477855e-10 (E_q), 1.165048e-9 (E_qq), 8.295353e-9 (mu_q),
1.007055e-7 (alpha), and 4.951588e-9 (mixed field/charge), in native units.
Ordinary H2/water/N2 reductions pass for both functionals. Independent/reverse
charge scans, parity, charged translation, rotation and refusals pass.
The rotation energy/dipole/alpha maximum errors are respectively
9.084118e-9, 3.687609e-8 and 1.750433e-7.

The reproducible input is `tests/data/continuous_species_nitrogen.xyz`.
At lambda=0.25, PBE/STO-3G, field [0.0013,-0.0009,0.0017] and origin
[0.11,0.07,-0.09] in atomic units, the common CLI gives
E=-108.02302363075418 Eh, SCF orbital residual 1.681071e-13,
maximum response residual 6.808671e-11, and iteration/final energy difference
1.847411e-13 Eh. The exact commands, raw fits, failed intervals, logs and
independent fit summary are retained outside the package in the M1 validation
record. Subsequent local-model and mixed-response acceptance is described above;
periodic electronic integration and reduced-fragment open-shell combinations
remain incomplete.


## Response coverage ledger

See the [implementation status](development-status.md) for the current
overview, representative results and the checks interrupted at the
documentation checkpoint.

Status labels follow the [authoritative vocabulary](conventions.md#status-vocabulary).
The CSV separates implementation `availability` from `validation_state`;
historical scoped passes do not certify every current reference/order.

This section replaces the former `response_coverage.csv`. One entry per
observable and perturbation records the scope it must eventually cover
(space, derivative orders, wave vector, frequency, temperature, internal
space and functional classes), the current status, the implementing entry
points, the acceptance tests and, per functional class and reference type,
how far the combination is implemented and validated. Target rows of
`property_targets.csv` refer to these entries by their `R` number.
`tools/ledger_check.py` (run by `python/tests/test_ledger.py`) reads the
**Status** and **Tests** lines of every entry, so keep their form.

The `mixed_*` columns in `property_targets.csv` track the four references
for explicit weighted compositions. They distinguish the connected
molecular energy and gradient subset across the four reference sectors
from the remaining combinations.

Matrix cells: *validated (subset)*, a validated subset of the scope;
*implemented (subset)*, implemented for a subset, validation as stated in
the status; *implemented, not validated*; *backend validated* / *backend
only*, the numerical backend exists without the public route;
*pending*, not implemented; *not audited*, not yet examined; *n/a*, the
combination does not exist (for example Skala with exact exchange).

`p249_common_orbital_dynamic` passes all four tests. All nine Cartesian
components of the constrained static alpha, real-frequency zero limit and
imaginary-frequency zero limit are independently fitted for HF, SVWN5,
PBE, TPSS, PBE0 and a synthetic learned model on C1 ammonia cation, plus
the retained soft hydrogen-cation regression: 189 accepted component fits,
p=1.912146..2.077098, minimum R2=0.99959542. Energy mixed fields independently
check off-diagonal alpha. The usual frequency interval is
[0.04,0.03,0.02,0.015] Hartree and the energy interval is
[0.016,0.008,0.004,0.002] atomic field units. All 54 failed interval fits
remain printed. The soft reference needs frequencies below its nearby
pole (resolved intervals down to [0.001,0.00075,0.0005,0.000375]); nonlinear
finite-field contamination and cancellation/SCF noise are resolved with
the explicitly printed intermediate/finer energy intervals. The learned
alpha(xx) cancellation is resolved on [0.008,0.006,0.004,0.003]. No error
floor or changed fit gate is used. The HF/PBE0 one-electron limit agrees
with independent UKS dynamics within 1.155e-14 in every complex component.
The synthetic learned model tests provider derivatives, not chemical accuracy.

`p251_collinear_correlated_alpha` passes 252 complete-component fits for
restricted C1 H4 and unrestricted C1 H5: HF/PBE0 parents with a distinct
PBE target, total/parent/target-correction/weighted-PT2/unscaled-SS-alpha/
OS/SS-beta tensors. Independent mixed-field energy differences use
[0.008,0.006,0.004,0.003]; p=1.974560..2.067147 and minimum R2=0.99993414.
The complete-tensor zero-PT2 parent limit is within 2.265e-14. Raw orbital,
amplitude, particle-number, projector, stationarity and transported-frame
residuals are checked individually against the existing 1e-9 gate.
This validates static correlated alpha, not a finite-frequency PT2 kernel.

The common native/ASE/CLI reference, unit and regression suite passes
27 tests with strict units and warnings as errors. `p25_dynamic_response`
and `p114_spinor_polarizability` each pass three regression tests; the
independent dense resolvent defect is 4.441e-16. The legacy CLI text unit
compatibility is repaired without changing the structured ASE dimensions.

reference and Taylor quadratures now refine consistently through order 128.

[0.01,0.0075,0.005,0.00375]. Static, positive/negative retarded and imaginary
frequencies satisfy the raw operator gates, maximum 6.67768838734e-12.
This deliberately fixed five-point nonsymmetric spatial quadrature isolates
the covariant spin kernel; it does not establish chemical grid convergence
or production-grid performance. The expanded native/ASE/canonical-CLI suite
passes 43 tests with strict units and warnings as errors.

#### Molecular VV10 density kernel

The real AO Hessian action `vv10_fxc_contraction` is used by the
collinear response solver and the common-orbital trust-region SCF
solver. It differentiates the same molecular VV10 density fields as
the variational potential. A directional dual perturbs both endpoints
of each pair and the final contraction differentiates the factor
`2 v_sigma grad(rho)`. Frequency and damping factors are evaluated
once per grid point. The retained reference-density cutoff is the same
as in the potential.

The matched `p29_nonlocal_taylor` replay on C1 ammonia uses four
spherical s functions and the level-0 molecular grid with zero weight
cutoff. It spans all ten symmetric AO-density directions with an
orthogonal rotation. The 55 independent Hessian entries each for
omegaB97X-V and original VV10 pass four-step potential differences at
`[0.09, 0.06, 0.04, 0.027]` in the density perturbation, on both
source snapshots. The maximum Richardson errors are 1.255558e-11 and
1.290550e-11 Hartree. The 110 exponents span 1.922341 to 2.059208 with
minimum R² of 0.99946712. The maximum optimized reciprocity defect is
3.931e-19 Hartree. The older Taylor agreement and the existing
finite-difference potential check using a converged water density also
pass.

On the level-0 STO-3G ammonia cation catalogue fixture, the optimized
omegaB97X-V/ROKS gradient passes all 12 Cartesian fits on
`[0.020, 0.014, 0.009, 0.006]` Bohr. Its maximum absolute component is
0.182924471288 Hartree/Bohr. The fit exponents range from 1.997250 to
2.000322 with minimum R² of 0.99996232, maximum Richardson difference
2.283780e-8 Hartree/Bohr and maximum displaced orbital residual
4.839964e-13 Hartree. The static response passes all nine ordered field fits
with p from 1.998208 to 2.012717 and maximum Richardson error
7.577628e-8 e² Bohr²/Hartree. The maximum displaced orbital residual is
5.502235e-13 Hartree. The reference energy is -55.37883066785078
Hartree and the diagonal polarizabilities are
`[3.045951302044403, 3.989428081516938, 2.888088084089042]`
e² Bohr²/Hartree. The three reported response residuals are
`[5.082897e-11, 3.644374e-11, 7.618782e-11]` dimensionless.

An initial CLI comparison used XYZ coordinates rounded to eight
decimal places. That changed the largest tensor entry difference to
2.887486e-8 e² Bohr²/Hartree and exceeded the 2e-8 absolute tolerance.
A separate native run on the rounded geometry reproduces this shift.
With 17 significant digits in the XYZ and the original geometry in
native Python and ASE, the maximum CLI and ASE differences relative
to native are 7.106e-15 and 1.022e-14 e² Bohr²/Hartree. Units agree
and the CLI reports SCF iterations and residuals on stderr.
[Matched SCF benchmark](performance.md#molecular-vv10-response-in-roks-scf).

Scope of the matrix: A scalar-generic kernel or derived-data calculation; a determinant/functional-class matrix does not describe this entry.

Explicit weighted molecular XC is connected to the existing RKS, UKS,
ROKS and GKS Cartesian Hessian drivers. The same resolved functional
enters the SCF, moving basis and response kernels. Collinear and ROKS
reports expose the atomic polar tensor, and the ROKS Hessian reports its
constrained static polarizability. The GKS Hessian reports its complex
nuclear response diagnostics. `p313_weighted_xc` compares all ordered
Hessian entries against displaced analytic gradients, all reported
atomic polar tensor entries against finite-field gradients, and the six
independent ROKS polarizability entries against separate total energies
with mixed electric fields. The remaining reference and public-route
checks continue separately.

For the 0.65 HF + 0.35 SVWN5 fixtures, all 144 ordered RKS Hessian
entries and all 36 atomic polar tensor entries pass. Hessian exponents
are 1.992355 to 2.008734 with minimum R2 0.99999876. Atomic polar
tensor exponents are 1.999663 to 2.001985 with minimum R2 0.99999993.
The RKS acoustic defect is 5.308e-16 Hartree/Bohr² and the SCF residual
is 4.598e-15 Hartree. The UKS Hessian also passes all 144 ordered fits
with minimum R2 0.99919839, using the retained staged intervals.
Thirty-five UKS atomic polar entries pass the initial staged checks.
The remaining entry `d mu_z / d R[4]` fails the first two second-order
intervals, a coarser interval and a fourth-order interval. Independent
installed-native sampling resolves it at (0.002, 0.0015, 0.001, 0.00075)
Hartree/(e Bohr) with p=1.904218611, R2=0.999812046606 and C=107.9977327.
The finer interval (0.001, 0.00075, 0.0005, 0.000375) gives p=1.977239763,
R2=0.999991118653 and C=180.5824037. The analytic entry is
-1.925277589204271 e. The first resolved interval is included in the
Rust suite with the existing fit gates.

Dynamic Raman subset (T017): restricted HF/STO-3G distorted water and genuinely C1 ammonia pass all 81 mode/tensor four-step fits at photon energy 0.1 Hartree, p=1.978644..2.063736, minimum R2=0.99979176, zero grid-weight cutoff. The 0.001-Hartree static limit and native Python/ASE/canonical CLI checks pass. Tensor derivatives are Angstrom^2/sqrt(amu); activities are Angstrom^4/amu. Exact source/artifact scope, residuals, normal-mode phase convention and remaining combinations are recorded in [bounded validation acceptance](validation-matrix.md#t017-dynamic-raman-mode-derivatives). This is not acceptance of other classes or periodic Raman.


A supplemental installed-wheel water HF/STO-3G audit passed native Python,
canonical CLI and ASE parity for all three harmonic frequencies, IR intensities,
Raman activities and depolarization ratios, with zero reported route differences.
The frequencies are 2078.400665252904, 4357.547177413179 and
4652.514284972435 cm^-1. IR intensities are 10.15237109377333,
38.63570520056858 and 21.98347725697168 km/mol; Raman activities are
8.497108695069434, 45.82490105432439 and 18.54360860765081 angstrom^4/amu.
Six rigid modes are projected. The unprojected Cartesian Hessian translation
defect is 3.39797634474337e-14 Hartree/Bohr^2. Analytic Raman permutation
defect is 8.881784197001252e-16; response convergence and CLI SCF logging pass.
These are fixed ASE water coordinates, not a comparison with experimental
fundamentals or a new all-component derivative acceptance.
The installed wheel SHA-256 is
`996ef1646291fe42ae867d4a201955b9fd2d8847888268282346c3a1e9cfc743`.
The earlier audit-only unsupported Hessian control error is retained.

`properties::pt2_axial::{PairAxialState, PairStateTangent, PairAxialOverlap}`
provide the reusable normalized first-order pair-wavefunction model. The complete double-substitution tensors avoid a fixed-word orbital limit. Nuclear and magnetic
connections are complete anti-Hermitian MO connections. The zero-field
nuclear tangent is real and the magnetic tangent purely imaginary. The
model uses `M=1+sum_c w_c <T_c|T_c>` and
`Im<d_R Psi|d_B Psi> = (I_parent+sum_c w_c I_c)/M
- M_R Im<Psi|d_B Psi>/(2 M^2)`. SS/OS weights multiply channel bilinears
and their norm; negative custom weights are an explicit signed continuation
and a nonpositive resulting norm is refused. Linear imaginary cancellation is explicitly evaluated; the cross-channel
terms are reduced by the one-body commutator selection rule described below. This is the
normalized MP1 AAT model of the
[analytic pair-wavefunction formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06632),
with generic orbital-generating DFT references and explicit spin scaling.

The independent oracle converges real displaced SCF determinants and

amplitude by direct four-AO sums, and evaluates determinants of cross-AO
orbital overlaps. Nuclear steps are [0.02,0.015,0.01,0.0075] Bohr and

The expanded all-parent force-field/APT measurements are recorded below.

The production pair contraction now uses the exact fermionic identity
`Im<G_R T|G_B T> = -Im<T|G([K_R,K_B])T>/2` for anti-Hermitian orbital
connections. `G(K)T = Tr_occ(K)T - pair_action(K,T)` reuses the same
occupied-minus-virtual tensor operation as the complex PT2 amplitude
equations. Nuclear/magnetic amplitude cross terms and both contributions
to the magnetic Berry connection, `G(K_B)T + T_B`, are retained. Thus no
triple-substitution state expansion is allocated: each contraction scales
as O(N^5) with O(N^4) coefficient storage. `cancellation_defect` measures
the explicit single-space linear cancellation and the commutator's
anti-Hermitian defect; the cross-channel reduction is an exact one-body
spin-sector selection rule tested by the full Slater-overlap oracle.

`PairAxialState::with_memory_limit(dimensions, occupied, amplitudes,
memory_mb)` checks the estimated coefficient/matrix workspace before
allocation. `new` uses the existing default memory budget. The molecular
driver forwards `pt2_memory_mb`; no fixed orbital-count mask is introduced.
The exact contraction passes the full-crate/all-parent regression,
including SVWN5 and PBE parents. A preflight caught an omitted amplitude
Berry term during this optimization; it was restored without changing any
fit threshold, and a normalized two-state closed-form/four-step regression
plus a field-dependent global-phase limit were added. The failed run is
retained outside the source package.

unit system. The numerical AAT convention is unchanged. Public acceptance
includes this reconstruction and the physical conversion of every tensor.

The existing `ecd-spectrum` entry is now code-connected to
`response::correlated_tda::correlated_tda_states`. Its explicit model is a
second-order normal-ordered full-Coulomb TDA propagator on an adiabatic
parent, with second-order singles Hessian/metric, first-order doubles
coupling, second-order ground singles and electric/momentum/magnetic
property gradients. Spin coefficients weight channel bilinears, including
signed custom continuations. The parent target energy is reported through
the existing double-hybrid energy merge; a distinct target does not replace
the parent excitation kernel. The complete parent spectral resolvent is
dense and memory-checked; correlation actions use O(N^5) work and O(N^4)
storage. Exactly degenerate parent roots are treated as a subspace;
coupled double poles are diagnosed without denominator shifts. This is a
perturbative residue model, not a claim of a fully resummed causal kernel.

The conventional field-free 3D `elastic` and `phonons` routes accept
explicit non-PT2 `xc_terms` on the existing collinear reference path.
In oblique HeH⁺, the recipe 0.25 HF + 1.0 PBE - 0.25 PBE exchange
recreates PBE0. The cell rows are [8.4, 0.7, 0.3], [0.4, 8.9, 0.6]
and [0.2, -0.5, 9.2] Bohr. The He-H distance is 1.35 Bohr, with
one s primitive of exponent 1.1 on He and 0.85 on H. The mesh is
2 × 1 × 1, grid level zero, shell one, grid weight cutoff zero and
response tolerance 1e-11. The energy is -2.505610553661516 Hartree
per cell. Clamped and relaxed C11 are 34.57786868728740 and
-1.014762093673525 GPa. All 81 affine, 54 mixed and 36 nuclear
entries are included in the named-reference and CLI/native/ASE
comparison, with a maximum defect of 2.172e-12 in atomic units.
The Voigt tensors agree to 2.177e-10 GPa across these runs. The
initial 1e-10 comparison had treated GPa as atomic units. The
regression compares the reported elastic constants in Hartree/Bohr³
and retains the raw GPa discrepancy. The largest reported SCF orbital
residual is 7.847e-13 Hartree and the largest relative coupled response
residual is 8.327e-12 at the 1e-11 threshold. These results validate that the weighted
public routes use the existing analytic response with equivalent XC.

#### Finite electric bias with empirical dispersion

The three-dimensional insulating Gamma-supercell routes `periodic-efield`
and `phonons` include the geometry-only D2, D3 zero and BJ, D3 ATM and
CHG terms. The primitive-cell lattice correction contributes the energy,
forces and Hessian to the stationary Berry electric enthalpy at fixed
Cartesian bias. The polarization and orbital stationarity equations are
independent of this correction. `field_energy` and
`dispersion_energy_per_primitive_cell` are in Hartree per primitive cell;
`energy` and `dispersion_energy` refer to the electronic supercell. The
nonzero-field path uses the neutral-cell Berry convention.

The biased omegaB97X-D LiH test compares six analytic force components
with displaced enthalpies and all 36 ordered Hessian entries with displaced
analytic forces, at zero grid weight cutoff with four step sizes per fit.
It tests the implicit CHG correction. Numerical and public-route
acceptance of this extension is pending.

#### Charged Gamma force constants and higher elastic constants

The fixed-lattice uniform background and monopole correction permit
analytic Gamma FC3 and FC4 of a charged cell. The monopole correction is
constant under nuclear displacement. Under affine deformation the full
shape-dependent unit-charge Ewald sum follows the direct and reciprocal
lattice and the volume. Its self term stays constant for the fixed Ewald
split. This connects the correction through fourth order for the clamped
and internally relaxed Lagrangian elasticity paths. Charged Berry electric
response remains unavailable. The scalar ECP geometry series uses the
same centre recurrence as the molecular derivatives. A polynomial in the
relative AO and projector positions yields higher coefficients by the
analytic chain rule, including products of strain and nuclear displacement.
The cubic and quartic operator acceptance is pending.

The shared driver reports the TOEC and FOEC tensors per undeformed
primitive-cell volume in Hartree/Bohr^3 and GPa, the Voigt order
`xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy`, and the fresh relative orbital response
residuals. The FC3 and FC4 tensors retain Hartree/Bohr^3 and
Hartree/Bohr^4 per primitive cell, with Cartesian indices `3*atom + axis`.
The full and contracted cubic and quartic drivers pass the configured
geometry-only dispersion model to the electronic path setup. This allows
the implicit CHG term in omegaB97X-D while requiring the driver to assemble
the corresponding periodic dispersion derivative separately. The prior
CLI build converged the HeH+ electronic reference at a residual of
`1.400e-14` Hartree and then rejected the FC3 calculation at the
displacement setup (exit 1, log SHA-256
`d08abbe1d83d87a5f6536118cde9c2db7c150c2666a0ac92c9dbfcd468e08f32`).
The acceptance tests compare the combined charged-cell FC3 and FC4 with displaced analytic
Gamma Hessians along 56 and 126 full-rank directions. Numerical acceptance
of this named-functional route is pending.

The TOEC and FOEC drivers accept the geometry-only D2, D3(zero), D3(BJ),
the D3 ATM variants and CHG. They reuse the periodic dispersion energy on
fixed reference image lists throughout each Lagrangian strain path. The
electronic SCF is stationary at the same density. The dispersion energy
enters the strain, nuclear and mixed Taylor coefficients before computing
the first- and second-order internal relaxations. Reports include its
reference contribution per primitive cell and per electronic supercell.
The D3(BJ) total-energy and force acceptance test uses 56 cubic and 126
quartic independent strain directions for each of the clamped and
relaxed tensors. Numerical acceptance of this extension is pending.

`toec` and `foec` also accept a fixed Cartesian electric field in Hartree/(e
Bohr). The energy is the stationary Berry electric enthalpy on the Gamma
supercell, including the lattice dependence of the reduced field and any
geometry-only dispersion. `field_energy` is per primitive cell and `energy`
is the zero-field SCF energy per electronic supercell. The finite-field
path uses a neutral insulating reference. The relaxed path holds the
reference material-coordinate internal force fixed. At ionic equilibrium
this force is zero. The reports retain the raw series and orbital response
residuals.

The staged finite-field test spans 21, 56 and 126 independent strain
directions for orders two, three and four, respectively, for both clamped
and relaxed tensors. It compares against fresh Berry enthalpies and forces
in an oblique LiH cell with omegaB97X-D, a field of
`[0.001, -0.0015, 0.002]` Hartree/(e Bohr) and zero grid weight cutoff.
The independent forces are transformed to material coordinates with `F^T`
before checking the relaxation. Full component fits and CLI, native Python
and ASE comparisons are pending.

The unit-charge shape-derivative operator passes all 209 independent
full-rank directions at orders one through four, with central steps
[0.04, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01] in the dimensionless strain parameter. The
fourth-order stencil resolves two cubic directions at the same steps
after both second-order intervals fail. The second interval is
[0.08, 0.06, 0.04, 0.03]. All four failed fits remain in the raw log.

The conventional `elastic` driver also includes the charged monopole in

ordered affine components with derivatives of the composed analytic stress
using the existing fit and Richardson gates. All 81 components remain
unresolved after three tested intervals. The reference energy is
-7.037464813255174 Hartree/cell and the raw xx/xx affine curvature is
-0.01339130440175234 Hartree/cell. The maximum relative strain solve
residual is 3.144455566772336e-12.

The old 12 Bohr overlap cutoff changes the AO image list at
`epsilon_xx = -0.02935715567907782`. The two `(1,0,-1)` and `(-1,0,1)`
images enter under compression. Their lengths at `epsilon_xx` of `-0.04`,
`-0.02` and zero are 11.9422939170, 12.0510288357 and 12.1610032481 Bohr.
The real Gamma integral diagnosis finds 11 vs. 9 image blocks and limiting
jumps of `5.15694248e-2` in overlap and `4.13774425e-3` Hartree in kinetic
energy across `epsilon_xx` separations of `2e-8`. The diagnostic log
SHA-256 is `9a81de247888ab087c5cebd49a5830e59340ad55d5d955649193cf9290e00856`.
The reference test now uses 13.8 Bohr, between the last retained and first
omitted overlap images over all nine affine components and
`abs(epsilon_ab) <= 0.08`. This removes the identified overlap and kinetic
image switch from the stencil. The real overlap assembly returns the same
19 lattice images at the centre and at all 144 signed affine samples
(log SHA-256 `bc15abd50f6bc0c32158a152ae8bc2e120bd4d925ec43113fb09c8b24a695c8a`).
The previous finest xx/xx error of
`1.15655e-5` Hartree at the 0.005 step lies within the unchanged-list
interval of the old cutoff. With the 13.8 Bohr cutoff the xx column still
fails all nine component fits. On [0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025], the xx/xx
errors are [1.64541e-5, 1.17750e-5, 1.07931e-5, 8.82981e-6] Hartree,
giving p=0.281961 and R²=0.94553629. The reference energy is
-7.037238013447765 Hartree and the largest of the nine coupled solve
residuals is 2.07254e-12. The narrowed run log has SHA-256
`5d3561b5b439bce472de4d8124b06469106a6f898c79262261a23e85d04303b2`.
The remaining discrepancy needs term-by-term isolation before the full
81-entry rerun.

A fixed-density diagnostic on the same Li geometry isolates another
cutoff effect. A 16 Bohr Bloch-AO grid truncates 2,871 nonzero-weight
point/image pairs within 0.08 Bohr of its boundary. Two nearest pairs
cross at 15.9999459983 Bohr. With identical atomic-orbital data and a
fixed diagonal test matrix per spin (0.72 on the first s basis function
and 0.32 on the second), the XC energy changes by 1.76405e-9 Hartree
across that boundary. Its two values remain constant on both sides
when the distance to the boundary is halved from 2e-6 to 1e-6 Bohr.
On affine steps [0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025], the fixed-matrix energy
curvature at 24 and 28 Bohr agrees within 7.11e-10 Hartree. The 16 Bohr
result differs from the 24 Bohr result by 2.504e-3 Hartree at the
finest step. This isolates a numerical problem in the candidate
finite-difference oracle. It does not establish that the remaining
stationary-SCF Hessian discrepancy originates solely in the XC grid.

An independent comparison of reconverged total energies at the same
four signed xx strains also diagnoses the first derivative. At 16 Bohr,
the analytic zero-strain derivative is 0.0023836781976526167 Hartree
per cell. The absolute central-difference errors are
[6.46119e-6, 2.27476e-6, 1.27462e-6, 8.27887e-7] Hartree.
Their log-log fit gives p=0.97285, R²=0.95836 and C=2.45349e-4
Hartree. At 24 Bohr, the corresponding independent energy difference
estimates are [0.0023905876930685, 0.0023864306646360,
0.0023853923236670, 0.0023851328039720] Hartree. Successive
step-to-step differences decrease by factors 4.0035 and 4.0010.
The three successive Richardson estimates span 1.309e-9 Hartree at
24 Bohr and 2.623e-7 Hartree at 16 Bohr.

With the 24 Bohr radius the unstrained SVWN5/RKS calculation gives
-7.037238120349491 Hartree per cell and an analytic xx strain
derivative of 0.0023850463026610647 Hartree. It converges in seven SCF
iterations with orbital residual 7.30381e-14 Hartree. The independent
energy-difference errors at [0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025] are
[5.54139e-6, 1.38436e-6, 3.46021e-7, 8.65013e-8] Hartree, giving
p=2.00044363, R²=0.999999988 and C=0.01387498 Hartree. The finest
Richardson error is 5.25406e-12 Hartree. Changing from 16 to 24 Bohr
changes the total analytic xx derivative by 1.36811e-6 Hartree and its
XC term by 1.46519e-6 Hartree.

The same off-centre energies give a second independent check on the
xx/xx curvature. Form `S(h) = E(h) + E(-h)` and, for each pair of
successive steps, evaluate `[S(h) - S(h/2)] / [h^2 - (h/2)^2]`.
The 24 Bohr results are [-0.0154492136802, -0.0154387513143,
-0.0154361344571] Hartree. The two Richardson extrapolations are
-0.0154352638590 and -0.0154352621713 Hartree, separated by
1.688e-9 Hartree. At 16 Bohr the same extrapolations differ by
7.360e-5 Hartree. Both checks use the same affine displacements.
The direct energy curvature is compared with the raw Hessian. The
stress differences differentiate each displaced cell's local strain
derivative, so their analytic comparator includes the product-rule
term from composing the local and reference-cell distortions.

The 24 Bohr analytic clamped Hessian xx column was checked against

`[0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025]`. The coupled response residual was
2.094371e-12. Eight rows meet the existing p, R² and Richardson
cutoffs, and zy/xx fails the p and R² cutoffs. Curvatures and errors
below are Hartree per cell before division by the undeformed volume.
