The other eight perturbation columns remain to be measured at this
radius before full 81-component acceptance.

For zy/xx, the signed central errors at 24 Bohr are
`[-6.343958236e-9, -1.235846603e-9, -1.472082218e-10, -4.937502189e-11]`
Hartree. Repeating every signed stress at 28 Bohr changes the four
slopes by `[-2.682316175e-14, -7.866970964e-14, -4.069661275e-13,
-8.253814299e-13]` Hartree. The observed error trend persists under
AO radius refinement. The SCF orbital residual stays below 3e-13
Hartree across both sets.

The successive estimates of the leading central-difference coefficient
are obtained by subtracting two slopes and dividing by
`h^2 - (h/2)^2`. The nuclear attraction, nuclear repulsion and Hartree
coefficients are of order 1e-2 Hartree with opposing signs. The summed
coefficient is of order 1e-5 Hartree and varies strongly across the
intervals. The Hartree estimate changes from 0.0170166467 to
0.0169936812 and 0.0170024384 Hartree. This identifies cancellation
among the stress terms as the source of sensitivity and makes Hartree
integration the next independent diagnostic. The original fit remains
failed and the thresholds are retained.

An additional pre-change stress replay uses the same 24 Bohr XC AO
radius, charged Li model, and eight signed xx strains at magnitudes
`[0.032, 0.024, 0.016, 0.012]`. All SCF references converge with
maximum orbital residual 2.849e-13 Hartree. Six of the nine stress
rows meet the strict rate gate on this coarser interval. The xx, zx,
and zy rows fail the rate or fit-quality gate. For zy/xx the signed
errors are -3.545370e-8, -1.207901e-8, -3.136613e-9, and -1.604869e-9
Hartree. The fit gives p = 3.180450 and R² = 0.99244584, with a
Richardson difference of 3.645175e-10 Hartree. The Hartree term's
successive estimates of the h² coefficient range from 0.0170133
to 0.0170557 Hartree, while the six-term sums are -5.21757e-5,
-2.79450e-5, and -1.36763e-5 Hartree. The broad strain interval
therefore retains competing orders after term cancellation and does
not resolve the original failed row.

The screened Hartree reciprocal contractions now form the compact-diffuse,
diffuse-compact and diffuse-diffuse products explicitly. The shared
calculation is used in the strain stress, the nuclear Hessian and the
strained reciprocal energy jets. On a scale-separated two-channel
algebraic check, the previous difference of products rounds to zero.
The explicit contraction gives 2.168404344971009e-18 and its directional
derivative is 0.5, as in the closed form. This checks the rounding
mechanism. The full ordered fixed-density Hartree strain check also
passes on a triclinic H/He cell with compact and diffuse primitives.
All 81 entries use independent stress slopes at [0.024, 0.016, 0.011,
0.008] with zero failed fits. The fitted exponents are 1.965148 to
2.002149, the minimum R² is 0.99997043, and the maximum Richardson
error is 6.263442e-9 Hartree. This test uses a prescribed density in
the H/He cell throughout the strain path.

The charged fixture now uses the measured 24 Bohr XC AO radius, and
the elastic fit uses each interval's actual step ratio for Richardson
extrapolation. The primary rate and absolute-error thresholds are
retained. The fixture checks the reference, all nine coupled strain
residuals and every displaced SCF orbital residual against 1e-11.
The failed 16 Bohr and 24 Bohr intervals above remain part of the record.

A separate Hartree split replay at the same 24 Bohr radius changes
only the split exponent from 1.0 to 1.2 Bohr^-2. At the two signed
magnitudes 0.012 and 0.016, all four independently reconverged energies
change by at most 1.635e-13 Hartree. The zy/xx slope changes by
3.334e-10 and 1.844e-10 Hartree, respectively. The Hartree term alone
accounts for 3.332e-10 and 1.844e-10 Hartree. Thus the finite Hartree
sums affect the slope below the dominant truncation error of the
coarse interval and at a scale comparable to the unresolved finer
errors. The split replay is a sensitivity diagnostic with two
magnitudes.

Holding the converged Li density at h=+0.012 fixed reproduces the
Hartree zy stress shift at the default screening threshold. The two
split values give -0.002612879569432900 and -0.002612879565817674
Hartree, a difference of 3.615226e-12 Hartree. The fixed-density result
isolates the change in the Hartree evaluation from the SCF iteration.

The same fixture's occupied s space reproduces that change to within
1.3e-17 Hartree. With the local Hartree screening threshold reduced from
1e-13 to 1e-16, the two split values give -0.002612879553059261 and
-0.002612879553059570 Hartree. The split difference in zy drops to
3.092145e-16 Hartree, and the largest difference over the nine stress
entries drops from 3.615238e-12 to 3.580469e-15 Hartree. The bulk Hartree
energy, Fock matrix and analytical derivatives now use the tighter
default together. With the full STO-3G density, the corresponding
zy difference is 3.395721e-16 Hartree and the nine-entry maximum is
3.580469e-15 Hartree. The rebuilt fixed-density Rust regression passes
all nine stress entries. Its maximum difference against a second
refinement to 1e-17 at split exponent 1.2 is 8.110179e-14 Hartree, within
the 2e-13 Hartree gate. The fully reconverged charged Li curvature check
retains the original rate and Richardson limits.

The fully reconverged charged Li elasticity replay is deferred. Its
zero-strain baseline reached -7.037238120346 Hartree, with a final
orbital residual of 1.222e-14 Hartree and RMS density change of
1.177e-15. The Hartree stress stage took 277.809 seconds in that run.
The full ordered strain Hessian and displaced stresses were not
completed. The earlier fixed-density checks and failed 24 Bohr
reconverged intervals remain the current numerical record.

The pure-strain reciprocal Hartree path uses the strain invariance of
`G · P` when both the pair centre and reciprocal lattice transform
affinely. The general moving-centre path still differentiates the phase.
An extracted Li/STO-3G kernel comparison used 27 translated shell pairs,
5,957 reciprocal vectors and one thread. Five alternating measurements
per version gave median times of 24.845 and 18.143 seconds and identical
value, gradient and Hessian lanes. This measures the reciprocal kernel.
The full elasticity timing and its 81 reconverged fits remain deferred.

For 3D collinear SOEC with scalar ECP, the derivative of each retained
one-electron image uses its AO positions relative to the translated
projector. The mixed term includes the derivative of the affine lever
arm with respect to internal displacement in the chart `F(R+T+u)`.
The existing ECP displacement sources and nuclear Hessian contribute to
the internal relaxation. The finite-k fixed-density suite covers all
81 ordered affine entries, 81 internal-strain entries and 81 independent
real and imaginary strain Fock entries on a triclinic fixture. A
NaH/PBE/LANL2DZ trial cell exercises the relaxed SCF route against
displaced analytic stress for all 135 entries. Numerical acceptance for
these tests and installed API parity are pending.

The dedicated `stress` route and the `periodic-energy` stress option share
the existing field-free 3D Gamma GKS/GHF affine derivative. For every
new stress sector, fit all independent ordered strain entries on an
asymmetric cell before projecting to a symmetric or Voigt view. Apply
the bulk volume, periodic area or periodic length normalization for
3D, 2D or 1D respectively. ECP, finite field and missing reference or
functional sectors remain separate acceptance entries.

The dimensional strain path differentiates the 1D and 2D
Coulomb model. An ordered Cartesian affine deformation changes the
periodic measure, the embedded reciprocal vectors and the open-space
projector. The nonzero Green terms use the existing mixed Cartesian
Hermite recurrence with an analytic derivative of its exponent and
normalization. The zero modes retain the isolated slab convention and
the logarithmic wire convention. Point sources and Gaussian AO
integrals use the same reciprocal derivative. Physical nuclear and AO
centres move affinely. A specified Cartesian Gaussian countercharge
centre remains fixed.

The common driver uses the converged dimensional collinear reference for
RKS and UKS energy, forces and stress. The collinear XC derivative uses
the stationary energy grid, including the moving quadrature points,
partition weights and AO support. The affine and nuclear operators share
the kinetic, overlap, Coulomb and exchange derivatives with the spinor
implementation. The Pulay term uses the occupied energy-weighted density
from the rebuilt Fock. The report includes the fresh orbital, occupation,
number, energy, Fock, XC and Coulomb defects. The collinear geometry
provider requires zero temperature and field-free all-electron inputs.
Nonlocal correlation and learned functional derivatives have separate
gates. The independent finite-k cases in `tests/periodic_weighted_xc.rs`
fit all nine Cartesian and nine affine derivatives for each RKS/UKS wire
and slab fixture. Installed CLI, native Python and ASE comparisons are
separate from those derivative fits.

Dimensional Gamma ROKS uses the same common-orbital stationary solver as
bulk ROKS and evaluates both physical Focks with the dimensional SCF
operators. Each spin density is formed from the common orbitals. The
occupied subspace multipliers sum to the total Pulay density, so both
geometry derivatives use the shared dimensional contractions. The report
includes the constrained orbital residual, metric defect, spin counts,
idempotency and closed-subspace defects, and separate geometry diagnostics.
This first-order path requires a field-free, all-electron, integer-occupation
Gamma reference with full retained AO rank. The wire/HF and slab/PBE
fixtures fit all 36 Cartesian and ordered affine components across the
two cases. The implementation, independent fit results and installed
route parity have separate acceptance gates.

The finite-k ROKS connection solves a common set of complex spatial
orbitals at each k with fixed integer alpha and beta ranks. The
time-reversal mesh uses conjugate partners. The common-orbital
stationarity residual contains both parts of the complex rotation
gradient before mesh weighting. The report retains both parts of the
orbitals, spin densities, Focks and gradient, and the raw conjugation,
metric, idempotency and particle-number defects. The forces and stress
use the constrained occupied multipliers with the existing 3D or
open-boundary energy derivatives. The fixed-occupation model leaves
thermal occupations, fields, nonlocal correlation, PT2 and moving
discarded overlap spaces to separate providers. The mesh tests cover
nine independent conjugate orbital rotations and 54 Cartesian and
ordered affine derivatives on the wire, slab and bulk fixtures.

The collinear finite Fourier field shares the stationary dimensional
geometry assembly. Its additional operator derivative includes the
scalar potential, the current anticommutator and all zero and second
harmonics of A squared. Each Bloch phase k dot T stays fixed. The
physical wave vector follows the strained periodic subspace at fixed
reduced wave indices, including rotation of a wire or slab into an
open direction. The Cartesian Fourier amplitudes stay fixed. The
external scalar term follows the reference electron potential energy.
The stress report retains all nine ordered affine components before
normalization by length, area or volume. The external field term and
the defect against the SCF field energy are reported separately for
both strain and atomic coordinates. Uniform magnetic flux and
spin-dependent operator derivatives have separate gates.

The fixed-density field-operator suite covers tilted 1D and 2D cells
and an asymmetric 3D cell with s/p functions and a complex k density.
The independent finite-field Hamiltonian at each moved geometry gives
54 passing fits on (0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025). The steps are in Bohr
for atomic displacements and dimensionless for strain. Exponents span
1.977250 to 2.001241, minimum R2 is 0.99996373, and prefactors span
2.661e-4 to 2.728e-1. The maximum field-energy reconstruction defect
is 9.714e-17 Hartree. A 3.25-Bohr image cutoff crossed a pair at
3.251307 Bohr and invalidated ten wire fits. The retained-image
interval with a 3.45-Bohr cutoff resolves the full suite.

Independent relaxed HF energy differences cover finite-k UKS wire and
Gamma RKS slab and bulk references in simultaneous scalar and orbital
vector Fourier fields. All 54 Cartesian and ordered affine components
pass the first four steps (0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025). Exponents span
1.998620 to 2.001073, minimum R2 is 0.99999989 and prefactors span
6.063e-3 to 5.347. The xx stress is -0.0483386606721901 Hartree/Bohr,
-0.00929845922079446 Hartree/Bohr^2 and -0.0000338926210248047
Hartree/Bohr^3 respectively. The maximum orbital residual across the
three reference calculations is 1.385e-14 Hartree. The largest
external field energy reconstruction defect is 8.327e-17 Hartree.

The audited Linux wheel with SHA-256
33ef59e9f7878e9e46e41226a30e47a533fe711034f21216c4f7472ccc06749d
passes the finite-k UKS wire parity check after clean pip installation.
The installed canonical CLI, native Python and ASE agree on the
energy, complete force and stress tensors, field contributions and
raw diagnostics. The installed wire gives energy -2.425319457913290
Hartree, xx stress -0.03488483283215991 Hartree/Bohr, xx field affine
contribution 0.01595752723600282 Hartree, orbital residual 6.667e-16
Hartree and field energy reconstruction defect 1.041e-17 Hartree.
The same public test passes with the standalone Rust CLI. At zero
wave vector a constant scalar potential changes the energy by its
amplitude times the electron count. The total forces, ordered strain
and stress agree with zero potential within 1e-10 in their respective
atomic units. The field overlap term and the Pulay term cancel in
this limit.

The scalar semilocal ECP stress uses the retained energy-operator
images. The bra and ket derivatives use the molecular ECP integral
derivative, and the centre derivative is their negative sum. Each
contribution enters the affine virial at its translated coordinate.
The contraction uses the occupied Bloch density at fixed reduced k.
The 3D report exposes an `ECP` strain term. Dimensional reports expose
`strain_components.ecp` in Hartree and `gradient_components.ecp` in
Hartree/Bohr. The Coulomb terms use the same effective valence charges
as the reference SCF. The field-free scalar-ECP first derivatives are
connected for the collinear, common-orbital and spinor references.
The relaxed-energy fixtures check 72 Cartesian and affine components.
Separate fixed-density checks cover 72 components of the ECP term
alone on the same four boundary variants. Installed parity is tested
independently. Spin-dependent ECP, field and higher-order ECP
derivatives retain separate operator requirements.

The H–Na–H scalar ECP wire passes all nine Cartesian and nine ordered
affine fits on the finite (3,1,1) HF/UKS mesh. The four steps are
(0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025) in Bohr for the Cartesian derivatives and
dimensionless for affine strain. All fits pass the first interval.
The exponents span 1.981712 to 2.000485, minimum R2 is 0.99997584, and
prefactors span 4.759e-4 to 2.971e-1 in the respective fit units.
The reference energy is -0.616936345196983 Hartree per cell with
orbital residual 4.798e-14 Hartree. The xx stress is 0.00880859455395
Hartree/Bohr and the ECP xx affine term is -0.412935291134 Hartree.
This run measures the Windows development candidate wire. Its
SHA-256 is
`be0f070ee201083220c3903ec2d2ddcf957f5e00fcf7d1238c6cd5e2a68386e2`.
The Gamma HF/GKS wire passes the same 18 four-step fits with exponents
from 1.999751 to 2.001267, minimum R2 of 0.99999988 and prefactors from
1.567e-3 to 1.652. The energy is -0.8099510159403436 Hartree per cell,
the orbital residual is 1.926e-16 Hartree, the xx stress is
0.0937533381178696 Hartree/Bohr, and the ECP xx affine term is
-0.4931858713808252 Hartree. The two wire calculations use different
occupied references and k meshes. The bulk RKS and slab ROKS tests
encountered exchange image lookup failures in strained cells.
The exchange quartet iterator now subtracts integer lattice labels
before resolving translated shell and density indices. The strict
Linux rerun passes all 54 Cartesian and affine components for the
RKS bulk, ROKS slab and GKS wire with the same four-step interval.
The RKS bulk exponents span 1.997969 to 2.002757 with minimum R2
0.99999917 and prefactors 7.585e-5 to 0.2032. Its energy is
-2.528805849403457 Hartree/cell with orbital residual 1.782e-16
Hartree and xx stress 0.00154597272476348 Hartree/Bohr³.
The ROKS slab exponents span 1.999466 to 2.000197 with minimum R2
0.99999999 and prefactors 0.003662 to 1.545. Its energy is
-0.810014182823871 Hartree/cell with orbital residual 9.298e-16
Hartree and xx stress 0.0187331422805454 Hartree/Bohr².
The GKS wire reproduces its earlier result with exponents 1.999751
to 2.001272, minimum R2 0.99999988 and prefactors 0.001567 to 1.652.
The independent fixed-density ECP suite also passes all 72 components.
Three component-17 fits fail at the coarsest 0.02 step. They resolve
on (0.01, 0.005, 0.0025, 0.00125) with the original second-order
stencil. Across the accepted intervals, exponents span 1.999582
to 2.000234, minimum R2 is 0.99999999 and prefactors span 3.413e-4
to 0.2207. The raw log retains the three failed intervals. The installed
Windows wheel passes the HF/UKS wire and HF/GKS slab route tests across
CLI, native Python and ASE. Atomic reports agree, and the ASE physical
stress and forces use the package's CODATA 2018 factors. The initial
force comparison used ASE's default constants and differed by 3.461e-8
eV/Angstrom. The corrected oracle passes at 1e-9 eV/Angstrom.
The installed fixtures have xx stresses of -0.00403896574452183
Hartree/Bohr and -0.000763072817834802 Hartree/Bohr², respectively.

All nine ordered components are returned in Hartree per cell before
division by the periodic length, area or volume. The lower-dimensional
stress and pressure use Hartree/Bohr and Hartree/Bohr². Pressure is the
negative stress trace in the active subspace divided by its dimension.
The GPa fields apply to 3D. Standard ASE volume stress is available
for fully periodic cells. The `get_periodic_stress_report` route
converts the dimensional units independently.

The standalone long-range kernel passes 180 fits, covering all nine
affine components and ten Cartesian derivative indices of degree zero
through two for each tilted geometry. The independent estimates rebuild
the primal reciprocal kernels at (0.02, 0.015, 0.01, 0.0075). The wire
exponents span 1.999070 to 2.006600, minimum R2 is 0.99999929 and C spans
1.138e-6 to 0.1312. The slab exponents span 1.987508 to 2.030572,
minimum R2 is 0.99998541 and C spans 2.031e-5 to 0.1688. All fits
pass the first interval. The complete point/Gaussian kernel and
self-consistent finite-k affine fits and installed API parity have
separate acceptance gates.

The 3D Gamma HF spinor fixture passes all nine ordered affine derivative
fits at strain steps 0.04, 0.02, 0.01 and 0.005 with zero grid weight
cutoff. Exponents span 1.999034 to 2.000036, minimum R2 is 0.99999994
and prefactors span 5.795e-4 to 4.204e-1 Hartree. At the base reference,
the orbital residual is 2.456e-16 Hartree, the occupation defect is
2.220e-16, the number error is zero and the Coulomb energy defect is
8.882e-16 Hartree. This run measures the shared analytic operator.
The dedicated driver and installed public route have separate gates.

The Linux 0.3.0 development checkpoint passes independent clean pip
installations from the wheel and the source distribution. The installed
`dft-rs` command reports the matching distribution version and registry.
Molecular HF energy, 3D periodic HF energy and the ordinary periodic HF
stress smoke case agree with native Python within 1e-10 Hartree in energy
and 1e-12 Hartree/Bohr³ in stress, with matching units and SCF iteration
counts. Each calculation emits the SCF iteration energy and residual on

Field-free three-dimensional RKS and UKS double hybrids use the moving
Born-von Karman orbital and noncanonical PT2 amplitude equations at
fixed reduced k mesh. The homogeneous path maps each position and
lattice vector by the same Cartesian deformation. The reported ordered
derivative is in Hartree per primitive cell, and the stress is its
symmetric part divided by the primitive volume in Hartree/Bohr^3.

alpha-beta and beta-beta PT2 terms are reported separately. Dispersion
adds its own ordered derivative when selected. Charged cells keep
constant net charge with the 3D uniform Ewald background. The affine
derivative includes the volume dependence of that background and the
shape dependence of the monopole correction shared with ordinary SCF.

results are recorded below. Open-boundary and higher charged strain
orders still require additional operators or conventions.

#### Scalar ECP on the first-order correlated lattice path

The Gamma Born-von Karman path takes its constant scalar ECP matrix from
the retained SCF image blocks. The linear coefficient uses the same two
AO-centre derivatives and image selection as ordinary periodic forces and
stress. For each retained integral, translation covariance supplies the
core-centre derivative from the two AO-centre derivatives. Their relative
velocities include the affine motion of the translated bra, ket and core
centres. The coefficient enters the parent Fock response and the target
energy before the PT2 derivative is contracted. ECP core charge enters the
same valence-electron ledger and Ewald background as the reference.

The connected scope is scalar ECP with the existing field-free 3D
collinear double-hybrid energy, forces and stress. Second-order scalar ECP wiring and its acceptance are recorded below.
Moving coefficients of order three and higher and spin-orbit ECP remain separate. The tests
exercise the full matrix of first ECP coefficients and the relaxed total
forces and ordered strain derivative on an asymmetric charged cell.
Numerical and installed-route acceptance is tracked separately.

#### Scalar ECP second-order lattice path

The second coefficient uses the molecular Gaussian-centre recurrence for
each retained translated AO/projector triple. Image selection is shared
with the ordinary analytic force and stress contractions. For
`F(t)(R+T+u(t))`, the coefficient is `D(v1)^2/2 + D(v2)`, where
`v1 = u1 + F1(R+T)` and `v2 = u2 + F2(R+T) + F1 u1`.
This includes the nuclear/affine cross term and preserves rigid translation
exactly. The coefficient is added to the same parent orbital and PT2 pair
path as the first coefficient. No finite displacement is used in production.

The common correlated Gamma Hessian and its supercell spectrum can now
consume this scalar ECP coefficient through Rust, CLI, native Python and
ASE. The 3D charged fixed-cell branch keeps the uniform Ewald background.
The ordinary scalar ECP CPKS connection is described separately below. Third and higher
moving ECP coefficients, SOC projectors, finite-q electronic response and
lower-dimensional correlated Hessians remain separate work.

density. The report gives force constants per primitive cell, acoustic
residual and the stationary-reference and response residuals. The tensor
has intrinsic permutation symmetry. The asymmetric NaH omegaB97X-V

residual is 3.546398951088156e-16. The energy is
-0.2687593278978422 Hartree/cell and the optical modes are
818.521652, 1435.174205 and 1547.295113 inverse cm.

#### Scalar ECP in the conventional periodic CPKS Hessian

The ordinary collinear Gamma force-constant driver now includes the
fixed-density translated scalar ECP Hessian. Its first-order core Fock
matrices already contained the translated ECP derivatives. The missing
second term reuses `hessian::pair_second_blocks`, including Cartesian to
spherical density transformation and the same retained image selection as
the scalar ECP energy and forces. Local bra/ket derivatives scatter with
opposite signs onto the projector owner. Translation covariance is local
to each integral, without acoustic or symmetry projection of the result.
Finite-k densities enter through the existing real Fourier image weights.

The response capability object enables scalar ECP for nuclear force
constants only. ECP strain, electric and electron-phonon source gates
remain explicit. No functional-name branch is added to response code.
This connects the existing Rust `gamma_force_constants` and common
`phonons`, `phonon-bands` and `phonon-thermo` routes; native Python and ASE
already use those drivers. Raw force constants and acoustic/asymmetry
diagnostics retain Hartree/Bohr^2 units. Perturbed occupations and all
functional/provider/reference combinations require their own acceptance.

(PBE) and `6ab5e2cce08343ba15949b46eb1135018e0ffa2933567d73277ad6740cb6a44c`

The independent refit of the fixed-density finite-k ECP skeleton covers
all 81 ordered Cartesian entries. All fit the interval
`[0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025]` Bohr with a second-order stencil, exponents

references failed at the earlier guard in that wheel.

#### Correlated stress at fixed Cartesian electric bias

For neutral 3D collinear double hybrids, the ordered deformation is
evaluated on the existing local Berry electric enthalpy. For a fixed
Cartesian field E and deformation F(t), the reduced field follows
E · F(t) a_i. The lattice path receives the first coefficient of
F(t)^T E in the reference-lattice frame. The parent orbital and PT2
pair equations then respond to this same path. The report labels the
field convention and retains the ordered terms, symmetric stress and
raw residuals. A fixed laboratory field can exert a torque under rigid
cell rotation. The antisymmetric ordered derivative can therefore
contain a physical term as well as finite-quadrature error. This branch
is subject to the local insulating reference
and Berry branch assumptions of the existing field solver. Charged
nonzero-field cells retain the named charged Berry field refusal.
The neutral RKS B2PLYP test compares all nine ordered components of the
total, target and opposite-spin energies with four-step independently
relaxed energies at a common Cartesian bias. The preliminary skew-cell H2 run at
(0.0013, -0.0021, 0.0017) Hartree/e/Bohr gives -1.1447666320584962
Hartree per cell and symmetric xx and xz stresses of 8.21077943826342e-6
and 2.48555933977366e-5 Hartree/Bohr^3. The series orbital residual is
1.047339e-15 Hartree. Increasing the XC AO range from 16 to 20 Bohr
changes the energy by zero at reported precision and the ordered strain
derivative by at most 1.388e-17 Hartree. The two identical atoms leave
inversion symmetry in this fixture. Final derivative acceptance uses
a C1 LiH cell with unequal nuclear charges at generic positions and the
compact all-electron basis shared with the correlated phonon test.
At the same bias LiH gives -6.5521976220757496 Hartree per cell,
xx stress 3.57691210302952e-5 Hartree/Bohr^3, xz stress
1.13206733235061e-4 Hartree/Bohr^3 and series residual 1.307982e-15
Hartree. The 16 and 20 Bohr XC AO ranges agree in energy and all
ordered strain entries at reported precision.
The first C1 run resolves 26 of 27 fits. The weighted opposite-spin zz
component has p = 1.887626 and R2 = 0.99728896 on the first central
interval. The finer central interval gives p = 2.146250 and
R2 = 0.99677905. Its fourth-order errors are nonmonotone, so all
three failed intervals remain in the log. The best Richardson defect
for this entry is 3.434e-10 Hartree. Independent CLI energies on four
consecutive finer steps (0.003, 0.002, 0.0015, 0.001) give signed errors
1.045783e-9, 4.797236e-10, 2.944885e-10 and 1.379410e-10 Hartree,
p = 1.834391890 and R2 = 0.999560806. The intervening four-step fits
and the coarse failures are retained. Changing the Coulomb split
exponent from 1.0 to 1.5 Bohr^-2 leaves the first failed fit unchanged
at the reported precision. The full suite repeat passes all 27 fits with
exponents 1.834403842578 to 2.073414320986 and minimum R2 0.999558424893.
It preserves three failed intervals for the weighted opposite-spin zz
entry, whose fourth interval gives p = 1.834403843 and R2 = 0.99956079.
The passing fit log SHA-256 is
`e8288c607fcc55e8ccd16e0e06d3aed7594947dba3f3b3e0a25415cb3abacf5b`.
The installed-route gates remain separate. The Rust CLI returns exit
code 1 and the named charged Berry field error when charge is added at
nonzero bias.

Fixed-geometry and moving correlated paths share the reduced-field
projection. An experimental zero-order path borrowed the stationary
geometry buffers to avoid copying Gamma integrals and grid data. Five
alternating trials per binary agree on the neutral H2 B2PLYP energy and
separate PT2 terms. Baseline and experimental median times are 40.726 s
and 42.520 s, median peak RSS 38,522,880 and 38,625,280 bytes, and managed
peaks 4,136,008 bytes for both. The copy change did not pass the performance
gate and was removed from the working source.

#### Geometry-only dispersion in conventional elasticity and polar modes

The conventional 3D elastic driver adds the periodic dispersion virial
and all three geometry curvature blocks before the ionic Schur
complement. The affine and internal-strain blocks differentiate the
existing CHG/D3 pair and optional ATM lattice energy on its retained
images under `r = (I + eps)(r0 + u)`. The mixed block includes the
first-order derivative from the moving strain lever arm. The nuclear
block uses the existing periodic dispersion Hessian. The electronic
response operator is the converged reference's CPKS operator.

At fixed nuclear geometry the pair energy has no field derivative.
The dielectric and Born routes include its reference energy, and the
clamped piezoelectric derivative retains the electronic strain response.
Relaxed piezoelectricity uses the dispersion-corrected internal
relaxation. Crystal IR, static dielectric and directional LO-TO use the
dispersion-corrected Gamma Hessian. Raw acoustic, Hessian and Fock-image
defects and the field/displacement solve residuals remain available.
Periodic VV10 response requires separate density and geometry terms.

#### First geometry derivatives of variational periodic VV10

The field-free GKS common driver now attaches the defining VV10 term for
omegaB97X-V and omegaB97M-V. The lattice kernel contracts the scalar
Pauli density. Its Fock contribution acts identically on both diagonal
spin blocks, and the semilocal operator still uses all four channels.
The analytic nuclear and affine derivatives reuse the lattice kernel's
moving AO, grid-weight, quadrature-point and image terms. Reports give
the nonlocal energy in Hartree per cell, the gradient contribution in
Hartree/Bohr and the ordered strain contribution in Hartree per cell.
The energy and force/stress routes retain separate SCF and XC energy
reconstruction diagnostics. The frozen 1D, 2D and 3D GKS public-route
tests agree across CLI, native Python and ASE on the force and ordered
stress tensors and their units. At a fixed reduced [2, 1, 1] mesh, the
omegaB97X-V wire, omegaB97M-V slab and omegaB97X-V bulk give total energies
of -4.685203182986292, -4.624969049725900 and -4.696690974145660
Hartree per cell, respectively. Their VV10 terms are 0.022407137455906,
0.022200790412963 and 0.021905099650841 Hartree per cell. Raw orbital
residuals are 3.581e-16, 4.818e-16 and 2.627e-16 Hartree. The finite-k
GKS relaxed-energy component fits, finite fields, finite-q response and
higher spinor VV10 geometry orders require separate coverage.

The conventional 3D collinear force and stress drivers now use the
same two-endpoint, smooth-cutoff VV10 pair sum as the SCF. The analytic
pair derivative includes the two weight endpoints, the rigid
owner-atom motion of each quadrature point and the explicit affine
motion of the partner lattice translation. The density and its
gradient use the existing moving Bloch AO contractions. The energy,
gradient and ordered strain derivatives use the same converged SCF
plan, including k mesh, grid, and VV10 parameters.

The fixed-descriptor suite checks three weight derivatives, nine
point-coordinate derivatives and nine ordered image-strain entries
against the independent integer-image energy oracle. The NaH
omegaB97X-V test checks six nuclear and nine ordered strain derivatives
against independently reconverged SCF energies on a 3 by 1 by 1 mesh
in a triclinic scalar-ECP cell. These gates distinguish the pair
contraction from the full stationary geometry derivative.

With a compact 10-radial, 7-angular grid, the finite-k NaH reference
gives -0.2653740203549878 Hartree per cell, of which
0.009165414681155651 Hartree is VV10. The orbital residual is
5.121251173615568e-15 Hartree. The Na force in Hartree/Bohr is
`[0.200980264823,-0.095289266277,0.133258407382]`.
The stress diagonal in Hartree/Bohr^3 is
`[3.682533893015e-4,8.982282805298e-5,1.807990472285e-4]`.
The raw ordered strain rotation residual is 0.03245293824030304
Hartree per cell at this compact grid. All 15 force and ordered
strain derivative fits pass with steps `[0.018,0.012,0.008,0.005]`,
exponents `1.995310..1.999916`, minimum `R2=0.99999500` and
prefactors `2.313e-2..1.409e0` in the corresponding atomic units.
These fits compare derivatives of the discretized energy at fixed grid
policy. They leave the continuum quadrature rotation limit open.

The initial fixed-descriptor test passes 20 of 21 entries. The xz
image-strain entry shows competing powers from the distance taper
on the original intervals. The centered fits have
`p=0.024215` and `1.799608`; the fourth-order interval gives

`p=1.989574` and `R2=0.99999750`. The original failures remain recorded.

Field-free 1D and 2D RKS/UKS use the same VV10 geometry assembly with
image translations restricted to active axes. The active length or area
normalizes the ordered Cartesian strain derivative. The common driver
reports the nonlocal energy separately from semilocal XC.

| 0 | -7.052821105264184 | -3.419072878641445 | -3.633748226622739 | -1.867667928892671 | 0.021711901430042 | 1.507e-15 |
| +0.01 | -7.055245989655848 | -3.418138796696959 | -3.637107192958890 | -1.867078435676298 | 0.021716561714952 | 3.820e-15 |

The positive shift changes the XC term by `+5.895e-4` Hartree; the
negative shift changes it by `+1.595e-6` Hartree. The corresponding VV10
changes are `+4.660e-6` and `-3.293e-6` Hartree. The energy-component log includes both spin densities
(SHA-256 `93716b233da3eb6bdc1a314929a5b9540173ae3e9d8e2e9fc374ae4a58971cc6`).

The common orbitals at the centre were transported in AO column order
using the new overlap metric. This preserves the nested closed/open
subspaces before any SCF optimization. The energy anomaly was present
in this evaluation. Between Li x shifts `+0.005` and `+0.01` Bohr, the
transported Hartree plus exchange energy changes from `1.5466471933832313`
to `1.5446147689813596` Hartree; extrapolation from the centre and `+0.005`
would give `1.5448864842974521` Hartree at `+0.01`. The semilocal XC and
VV10 changes along the transported path are smooth at this scale. The grid
contains 1,840 points at both displacements. The unoptimized orbital
residuals are `0.002644818937142926` and `0.03132256651740424` Hartree.
The frozen and relaxed data for all five geometries are retained (SHA-256
`9ef029beedb93d030f596834cfdd588c41f531088366a4672cd892b23db4c0a9`).

The short-range shell-pair cutoff and the Born-von Karman exchange image
projection are distinct. Solving the equality of squared image distances
for the Li--H pair gives a minimum-image change from `[0,0,0]` to
`[1,0,0]` at Li x displacement `+0.007916666666667` Bohr. The opposite H x
displacement changes images at `-0.007916666666667` Bohr. For the failing
affine `[0,1]`, `[0,2]`, `[1,0]` and `[2,0]` channels, the first changes
are at `-0.0077665261`, `-0.0039448040`, `-0.0077525993` and
`-0.0039430848`. The `[2,2]` channel stays in the same image chart for the
initial interval. These cutoffs explain why carrying over the short-range
shell-pair check did not find the bulk issue. A separate local-chart test
holds the cell, grid, basis, functional, k sampling and fit gates fixed.
It verifies that each signed sample retains the reference image labels at
steps `[0.0035, 0.0025, 0.00175, 0.00125]`. All 18 Cartesian force and
ordered strain fits pass on the local interval. Exponents are 1.999530 to
2.015384 with minimum R2 of 0.99999308 and prefactors from 8.598e-4 to
2.047. The original run retains six unresolved components across the
tested broad intervals: Li x and H x forces, and ordered strain entries
[0,1], [0,2], [1,0], and [2,0]. The new fits describe the derivative on
one smooth image chart. A path that crosses the image boundary still
samples two different exchange image assignments.

The bulk reference uses ten SCF iterations at -7.052821105264186 Hartree
per cell. Its VV10 term is 0.02171190143004188 Hartree per cell and its
orbital residual is 7.702e-16 Hartree. The xx stress is
-0.003562655253684393 Hartree/Bohr^3 and pressure is
0.001103416344326805 Hartree/Bohr^3.

Evaluating the same transported orbitals 0.00001 Bohr on either side of
the predicted crossing separates the Hartree and exact-exchange terms.
The exchange energy changes from `-1.1577349580945753` to
`-1.1580446739059294` Hartree per cell, a `-3.0971581e-4` Hartree change.
The Hartree energy changes by `-7.0182375e-6` Hartree, semilocal XC by
`+1.9371104e-7` Hartree and VV10 by `+7.9998068e-9` Hartree. The change
in exchange across the minimum-image boundary occurs before
self-consistent relaxation. These two samples and both stationary
reference comparisons are retained separately (seam log SHA-256
`3833a08b0a084be6e529fa7ffe4e9ad3d3781126adc15ebc463fb87c79c10100`).

For the same cell with a `2x1x1` k mesh, the former crossing and its
two displaced geometries give energies `-7.081943171714359`,
`-7.081941386823085`, and `-7.081944956593253` Hartree per cell
(centre, minus, plus). Their central energy second difference is
`+1.2380319e-11` Hartree at `h=1e-5` Bohr. Each SCF uses 11 iterations
and the largest orbital residual is `5.7797501e-15` Hartree. The sampled
energy is smooth through the former Gamma crossing at this resolution
(SHA-256 `8508db73bc1dda0085557049f9392d3923a24372507fbd0d5361afacd2fc6114`).
This three-point diagnosis leaves the full finite-k tensor gate open.

#### Dispersion curvature acceptance

The first D3(BJ) operator fit rebuilt the hard cutoff lists at every
sample and left all 81 affine entries unresolved. Its Richardson defect
was 5.846992e-4 Hartree. The fixed-list oracle uses the same reference
cutoff as the production analytic derivative and independently rebuilds
the first-order stress on each displaced geometry. The corrected oracle
passes all 81 affine and 81 mixed entries per model on [0.008, 0.006,
0.004, 0.002]. The steps are dimensionless for strain and Bohr for
displacements. No intervals fail with the fixed list. The Richardson
defect is the maximum numerical defect over both blocks, with Hartree
for affine entries and Hartree/Bohr for mixed entries.

##### Static four-component uniform magnetic response

The molecular Dirac-Coulomb route connects the magnetic dipole and
magnetizability through the common magnetizability entry. The
NMR shielding entry uses a mixed Cartesian nuclear dipole and uniform
magnetic field derivative of the same electronic energy. Both use
`relativistic_method="dirac"` and London orbitals with restricted magnetic
balance. The source series differentiates the four-component core,
overlap, Coulomb and full/range-separated exchange, semilocal grid
descriptors, VV10, and the nuclear-core positive-energy chart; CPKS
relaxes the occupied space within that chart. A fixed angular quadrature
is selected by the converged reference. The second energy coefficient
contains the explicit mixed nuclear operator at nonzero uniform
field. The derivative of the stationary reference is checked against
its Fock and total energy, and operator, projector, reciprocity and
coupled residuals are retained.

The outputs are `magnetic_dipole[i] = -dE/dB_i` in atomic units,
`magnetizability[i][j] = -d2E/(dB_i dB_j)` in `e^2*bohr^2/m_e`,
and `shielding_tensors[nucleus][i][j] = d2E/(dmu_i dB_j)` in ppm.
Explicit-sector and orbital-relaxation parts are reported in the same
units as their respective totals. NMR takes one positive Gaussian
magnetization RMS radius per input atom in Bohr and can restrict the
output with `nuclei`. The optional finite reference field uses the
reported magnetic phase expansion. At zero field the second-order
London phase is exact for these derivatives. The accepted Hamiltonian
uses an all-electron, even-electron generalized reference, finite
charge radii and a static perturbation. Applied electric operators
and nonzero reference nuclear dipoles require additional differentiated
operators. Magnetic quadrupole response needs balanced operators for
the vector potential of a source-free field gradient. State-resolved
many-electron four-component hyperfine and ESR need a spin manifold
and effective-spin projection beyond the even-electron reference.

##### Uniform magnetic Gaunt and Breit interactions

The London-RMB basis changes the large-small alpha-current pair
polynomials. Their Hermite contraction retains both the instantaneous
Gaunt kernel and the frequency-independent Breit longitudinal tensor.
Gaussian pair coefficients share the full and range-separated
interaction's orientation machinery. The optional current interaction
enters the stationary energy, Fock, density kernel and two explicit
field coefficients. The zero-field full complex J/K matrix comparison
with RKB gives Gaunt defects 6.776264e-20 and 5.421011e-20 Hartree.
The Breit defects are 8.131516e-20 and 8.809143e-20 Hartree.

[10027.971221924843,9963.834878613816,9816.184278710632] ppm.
The raw coupled residual is 8.073793e-12 and stationary Fock defect
6.883607e-15 Hartree. All 18 independently reconverged entries pass
the absolute gate of 2e-9 with the fourth-order stencil at h=0.004.
The largest absolute difference is 1.18192944e-9. Sixteen components
pass the h=[0.044,0.032,0.023,0.016] central interval. Shielding [0,1]
fails on that interval with p=1.629328, R^2=0.99334085 and
C=3.266e-6. It passes at [0.032,0.023,0.016,0.011] with
p=1.841373, R^2=0.99906126 and C=7.369e-6. Shielding [0,2]

and (-0.505388,0.10135236,3.271e-11).
The first fourth-order interval [0.038,0.028,0.020,0.014]
gives p=4.287980, R^2=0.99967760 and C=2.660e-2. The finer
fourth-order interval [0.027,0.021,0.016,0.0125] resolves the next
truncation term with p=4.156412, R^2=0.99983230 and C=1.574e-2.
Its separate absolute defect is 1.45645752e-10. The 17 Breit
second-order fits give p=1.841373..2.039653, minimum R^2=0.99906126 and

##### Four-component isotropic nuclear spin spectrum

Relativistic NMR spectra use the London-RMB shielding and the
electronic indirect nuclear coupling of one converged molecular
reference. The common isotope-spin Hamiltonian consumes the total
reduced coupling in atomic units and converts it to Hz using the
supplied signed nuclear gyromagnetic g factors. The spectrum retains
the first-order multiplet model and the exact finite spin Hamiltonian.
The exact model takes one spin specification per atom, one shielding
per atom, and the isotropic electronic couplings. The report includes
raw coupled residuals, ppm positions, integrated weights and exact
Hamiltonian eigensystem and area residuals.

For physical-c LiH with the diagnostic HF basis, the native shielding
values are [89.99126662267906,40.674837034386414] ppm at Li and H.
With signed g=[2.170951,5.5856946893] and twice-spin=[3,1], the
isotropic J is 637.8772777788078 Hz. A 400 MHz proton spectrometer
and a 30 ppm reference produce H first-order lines at
[-13.066876826056943,-11.472183631609923,-9.877490437162905,
-8.282797242715885] ppm, each with weight 0.25. The raw maximum
coupling response residual is 1.535184e-12. The first-order public
parity passes in native Python, both ASE unit modes and the CLI.

The initial exact heteronuclear profile difference is 1.31557092e-8
at the 1e-8 absolute gate. The common solver now retains a
dominant product-state carrier and small Rayleigh shift for each
eigenstate. The observed isotope's carrier cancels algebraically from
inter-block transitions. Applying this change to the electronic data
from the same four API calls reduces the maximum profile difference to
1.28630440e-12. The largest line-position difference is
4.07098355e-10 ppm. Four exact spin postprocessing regressions pass,
with independent dense mixed-spin discrepancy 1.97342143e-13 Hz.
The restored integrated build passes four warning-strict tests in
20.27 seconds, including the two four-component LiH API comparisons
and the pre-existing exact homonuclear and isotope-reference cases.

The four dominant exact H lines are
[-13.066873706163165,-11.472176351868612,-9.877483157437865,
-8.282794122838375] ppm, with weights between 0.249999999997 and
0.249999999999. Independent full eight-state nuclear diagonalization
confirms the dominant line positions and weights. Every adjacent
total-Iz transition is emitted, and the total area defect is zero.
The raw Coulomb spin Hamiltonian residual is 1.13686838e-13 Hz.
Native LiH Gaunt and Breit exact runs give J=638.0531952893963 and
638.0726609617088 Hz, respectively. Their H isotropic shieldings are
40.67549997571654 and 40.67546376666656 ppm. Both eigensystem
residuals are 1.49011612e-8 Hz and the maximum relative residual is
1.21874454e-16. Raw coupled residuals are 4.61446153e-14 and
3.08168201e-14, with zero area defects.

The molecular Faraday and collinear one-electron spin-orbit
providers now retain the complete complex electric susceptibility and
magnetic derivative at retarded frequency omega + i eta. The same
transported London density, response kernel and occupied-virtual
equations are used. With positive eta, the complex shifted paired
equations use the general Krylov solver. The report preserves the
historical imaginary tensors and adds their real parts, the complex
reference polarizability and the unscaled reference Fock defect.
The separate one-electron finite-field spectral tests measure the
independent component and gauge limits in `p316_causal_magneto_optics`.

The T148 [spinor orbital current](#coupled-periodic-spinor-orbital-current)
has a separate static, 3D Gamma-supercell response model. Its noncollinear
SVWN5 validation uses all nine independent output coefficients.

#### Covariant semilocal SCF on uniform-flux cells

The finite-Gamma and magnetic Bloch paths share the London quadrature.
The orbital and covariant momentum values generate all Pauli density,
gradient, kinetic-density and current descriptors. The semilocal energy
and Fock come from the same spin projection, with equal k weights on
the Bloch mesh. Spatial refinement compares independent quadrature
orders and checks the integrated charge against the analytical overlap.
Angular refinement is measured separately. The spatial grid is
retained for SCF reuse, while the XC descriptor workspace is processed
in blocks of up to 16,384 points. The angular defects in the public
report sum the measured block defects.

The initial unblocked BLYP calculation for a one-electron hydrogen
slab passed the CLI, native Python and ASE comparison on the
finite-Gamma sector. It uses a 9 by 9 Bohr square, a single
Gaussian exponent 0.7, and one normal flux quantum
`B_z = 2*pi/81` in atomic units. At final grid order 128 its energy
is `1.0956352242953038` Hartree, with spatial energy/operator defects
`5.854e-11` and `7.049e-11` Hartree and number defect `1.478e-12`
electrons. The orbital residual is `6.850e-18` Hartree. The same
unblocked fixture with M06-L exposed a roundoff failure in the
collinear empty-spin current projection. The bound on the residual
current now uses the density and kinetic-density scale, retaining
the separate density and kinetic cancellation checks.

The bounded-workspace BLYP run passes CLI, native Python and ASE on
both the finite-Gamma and `2 x 1 x 1` crystal Bloch slab. Both report
`1.095635224295` Hartree, spatial operator defect `7.054e-11`
Hartree and particle-number error below `2.3e-16` electrons. The
spatial number defects are `1.478e-12` and `5.491e-13` electrons,
and the orbital residuals are `6.476e-18` and `1.263e-18` Hartree,
respectively.

The skew 3D hydrogen cell with one flux quantum and a complex Hermitian
spin density tests all four independent Fock components against energy
differences. The centered stencil uses steps `0.040, 0.030, 0.020,
0.014` in the normalized AO density coefficients, a fixed spatial
quadrature order per fit, zero point-weight pruning and a `1e-7`
spatial convergence tolerance. In order, the rows describe the alpha
diagonal, beta diagonal, real coherence and imaginary coherence.

| XC | Fitted exponents | Minimum R² | Fitted coefficients in Hartree | Maximum error at 0.014 in Hartree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BLYP | 2.000721, 2.000730, 1.996018, 1.995736 | 0.99999963 | 0.05372, 0.07881, 0.04819, 0.05592 | 1.540e-5 |
| M06-L, tensor and atom-centered grids | 2.000818, 2.002708, 2.003119, 2.003483 | 0.99999975 | 0.04613, 0.1071, 0.04528, 0.05416 | 2.075e-5 |

Shifting the gauge origin by `(0.27, 0.16, -0.22)` Bohr changes the
BLYP Fock by `1.110e-16` Hartree. For the M06-L tensor grid the
energy and Fock defects are `1.110e-16` and `1.388e-17` Hartree.
For the first atom-centered grid they are zero and `5.551e-17`
Hartree. For the strengthened atom-centered grid they are zero and
`2.220e-16` Hartree, with the same fitted exponents to the precision
shown. The exponents measure truncation by the centered stencil.
Gauge invariance and spatial convergence are checked independently.

After the roundoff fix, M06-L on the slab reached the tensor-grid cap
of 128 on both routes. Its successive-order energy and operator
defects were `6.693e-6` and `2.170e-5` Hartree, above the
`1e-10` tolerance, with zero spin-angular defect. The orbital
residuals were below `6e-17` Hartree. The meta-GGA candidate now
uses the periodic atom-centered partition with unpruned radial and
angular refinement. Slab acceptance is tracked separately from the
tensor-grid derivative test.

The first atom-centered rules bring the one-electron slab Fock
defect down to `2.887e-10` Hartree in both the finite-Gamma and
crystal-Bloch models. At an 8 Bohr cutoff, the energy defect is
`1.678e-10` Hartree and the number defects reach `6.656e-10`
electrons. The finite-Gamma energy is `1.076537564181476` Hartree.
Increasing the cutoff to 12 and 16 Bohr reduces the number defect to
`3.908e-11` and `4.940e-13` electrons. The respective Fock defects
rise to `3.114e-9` and `2.090e-9` Hartree, so both runs remain
outside the original spatial tolerance.

A hydrogen molecule with bond length 1.4 Bohr in a skew 2D lattice
with in-plane vectors `(9, 0.13, 0)` and `(0.27, 9, 0)` Bohr
uses the same normal flux of one quantum and a primitive s orbital of
exponent 0.7 on each atom. M06-L reaches `1.939727501367301`
Hartree with an orbital residual of `1.718e-14` Hartree in two
iterations. The final spatial energy and number defects are
`7.666e-13` Hartree and `5.511e-11` electrons. The Fock defect
is `2.290e-3` Hartree, so the backend reports unconverged.

In a one-orbital spin channel, the same-spin M06 factor has the
physical boundary `tau_current_corrected = |grad(rho)|^2/(8*rho)`.
The clamped same-spin factor changes its derivative across that
boundary. The revised expression forms the kinetic ratio directly
and uses the derivative from the physical side for roundoff-sized
negative values. Across a `4 * EPSILON` relative shift of both
spin-channel kinetic densities to each side of the boundary, the
energy difference is `5.551e-17` and the maximum first-derivative
difference is `1.776e-15` in atomic units. The first derivatives
of the two densities, their squared gradients and the kinetic
densities pass separate physical-side one-sided fits at relative
steps `0.008, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001`. The six exponents range from
`1.978305` to `2.005023`, the minimum R² is `0.99998935`,
and the fitted coefficients in spin-component order are
`0.3050, 0.2374, 0.001302, 0.003768, 0.05863, 0.03555`.
The cross-spin gradient contraction has exactly zero dependence.
Full slab acceptance also requires the spatial rule to pass the
same residual thresholds.

The strengthened rule and iso-orbital correction leave the
one-electron slab above the `1e-10` gate in both magnetic models.
The final energy defects are `1.667e-10` Hartree, the Fock defects
are `2.827e-10` Hartree and the number defects are at most
`6.529e-10` electrons. The orbital residuals are below
`4e-18` Hartree. On the same skew hydrogen molecule slab the energy
is `1.939727501368526` Hartree and the orbital residual is
`1.793e-14` Hartree. The revised spatial defects are
`7.291e-13` Hartree in energy, `4.254e-4` Hartree in the Fock
and `5.463e-11` electrons in the number. These two one-electron
public tests and the hydrogen molecule calculation report
unconverged at the original tolerance.

Fixed-density probes separated two sources of error in the remaining
checks. On the one-electron slab, holding the Lebedev degree at 109
and increasing the radial point count from 256 through 352, 448 and
576 reduces the number defect from `6.520e-10` to `2.321e-12`
electrons. The Fock differences between the last three radial
rules are `2.334e-11` and `2.779e-12` Hartree. The 576-point
XC energy is `-0.4788560941446071` Hartree. The tested composite
Cartesian rules integrated the charge but left a Fock difference of
`2.668e-5` Hartree between 40 and 48 points per panel. The
atom-centered production rule therefore increases the radial count
to four times the reported order.

With the higher radial count and the kinetic-density correction below,
both one-electron M06-L slab cases pass the original `1e-10` spatial
gate and agree across CLI, native Python and ASE. The parameters are
the same single Gaussian exponent 0.7, 9 by 9 Bohr slab, one normal
flux quantum, 8 Bohr extent and initial magnetic grid order 48.

| Magnetic model | Energy (Hartree) | Spatial Fock defect (Hartree) | Spatial number defect (e) | Orbital residual (Hartree) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Finite Gamma | 1.076537563920671 | 8.934e-11 | 8.299e-11 | 1.233e-18 |
| Crystal Bloch, 2 x 1 x 1 | 1.076537563920678 | 8.933e-11 | 8.203e-11 | 1.233e-18 |

The energy difference among interfaces is zero at the stored precision
for each model. Both particle-number residuals are `2.220e-16`
electrons. The retested skew bulk M06-L Fock fits retain exponents
`2.000818` to `2.003483` and minimum R² `0.99999975`.

A separate two-AO one-point fixture gives a large M06-L Fock error
when a common local phase gradient is applied to the two orbitals.
The measured error before the correction is `1.899e4` Hartree at
an unchanged energy. The kinetic density and the flow term are
each much larger than their difference at the one-orbital boundary.
The numerical repair uses the arithmetic scale before subtraction,
enforces the von Weizsaecker value within that roundoff allowance,
and retains the derivative of the current-corrected kinetic density.
The two independent phase-gradient shifts then leave the energy
unchanged and give Fock differences of `4.955e-12` and
`9.369e-12` Hartree against a maximum Fock element of `1.899e4`
Hartree.

For the skew hydrogen molecule, the stationary density has diagonal
and bonding off-diagonal elements near `0.33256185325906` in
each spin block. The largest imaginary element is `5.536e-14`.
An independent fixed-density probe uses the normalized real bonding
orbital in both spin channels. Forming the descriptors from that
orbital's amplitudes and including its bond midpoint in the spatial
partition gives an XC energy of `-0.8868529391136624` Hartree and
a `3.273e-11` Hartree Fock change between 288 and 352 radial
points at angular degree 95. Computing the descriptors by
subtraction of AO contractions in a local zero-current frame on
the same rules gives a `1.274e-5` Hartree change. These probes
isolate the effect of AO contraction cancellation near the bond
center. Increasing the Lebedev degree from 95 to 109 at 352 radial
points changes the Fock by `1.560e-9` Hartree. Increasing the
radial count from 352 to 448 at degree 109 changes the Fock by
`1.184e-9` Hartree. Those independent refinements remain above
the production gate.

An isolated London-collocation probe tested evaluating orbital
values and all three momentum components in one pass over the
images. The skew-cell fixture has two primitives per shell for
`s` through `i` and 4,097 points. Across five alternating
one-thread pairs at matched optimization settings, the median
times for the four separate evaluations and grouped probe are
`1.976` and `0.719` seconds. The largest difference in any
real or imaginary element is `5.690e-16`.

The production magnetic SCF and current sampling now evaluate all
four channels in one pass. The shared evaluator contracts the Gaussian
radial value and slope once per shell image and applies the London
phase after the Cartesian-to-spherical transform. The test
`magnetic_collocation_matches_primitive_operator_through_i_shells`
compares individual primitive momentum operators with the full output
matrices for 31 points and 49 spherical AOs. The skew 3D fixture has a
nonzero magnetic Bloch wave and gauge origin. It samples a Gaussian
center, its translated image and generic off-axis points. Across all
6,076 complex entries, the largest deviations by channel are
`1.665e-16` Bohr^-3/2 for AO values and `3.331e-16`, `2.989e-16`
and `2.776e-16` Bohr^-5/2 for the Cartesian momentum components.
The original four-step spatial momentum checks pass for each
Cartesian channel at `[0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025]` Bohr. The
exponents are `1.999954961`, `1.999937620` and `1.999939764`,
with minimum R^2 `0.9999999997` and maximum Richardson defect
`2.140e-11` Bohr^-5/2. The closed current checks pass at all
three nuclear widths. The independent spin-curl fit on the same
steps gives `p = 1.999881618` and `R^2 = 0.9999999991`.

At angular degree 131, increasing the fixed-density radial count
from 448 to 512 changes the directly contracted Fock by
`3.381e-10` Hartree. The sphere of radius `1e-5` Bohr at the
bond midpoint contributes about `4.46932e-7` Hartree to a diagonal
Fock element and `-1.97733e-15` Hartree to the XC energy. A single
radial interval gives successive Fock differences of `1.338e-9`
and `4.429e-10` Hartree for 16, 32 and 64 Gauss points at degree
77. With logarithmically subdivided radii, the differences at 12,
24 and 48 nodes per interval are `1.102e-11` and `1.343e-12`
Hartree. Raising the angular degree from 77 to 109 at 48 nodes per
interval changes that sphere's Fock by `7.070e-13` Hartree.

The shared collinear meta-GGA evaluator factors each positive spin density
into occupied amplitudes with the original positive occupations.
It constructs the current-corrected kinetic density by completing
the square before integration. The variational AO matrix uses the
same analytic density, gradient, current and kinetic vertices.
The magnetic quadrature also includes Gaussian-product centers
from significant overlap images. The same points and weights are
used for cached and blockwise evaluations.

An orthogonal AO rotation of the near-stationary one-point test
changes the pre-amplitude energy by `1.334e-12` Hartree and the
transformed Fock by `1.060e-6` Hartree. After the change the
energy agrees exactly at the reported precision and the Fock
defect is `5.093e-10` Hartree. The reference phase-gradient
differences and the four-step skew bulk fits also pass.

On the same build and mesh, the one-electron finite-Gamma M06-L
slab gives `1.0765375639206711` Hartree with both the 2048 MiB

defects in both runs are `1.852e-11` Hartree, `8.934e-11`
Hartree and `8.299e-11` electrons. The managed peak is
`122,010,264` and `38,190,744` bytes, respectively. This one

With the combined London evaluation, CLI, native Python and ASE all
converge the same M06-L H2 slab after two iterations with either the
finite-Gamma model or the magnetic Bloch model on a `2 x 1 x 1` mesh.
The first H is at the origin and the second is at
`(0.82, -0.34, sqrt(1.4^2 - 0.82^2 - 0.34^2))` Bohr. The in-plane
rows and primitive exponents are those specified above. The field
normal to the plane is `2*pi / (81 - 0.13*0.27)` in atomic units.
The Gaussian nuclear widths are `0.3` Bohr. The overlap and grid
cutoffs are `5` and `8` Bohr, the reciprocal magnetic cutoff is
`14` inverse Bohr, and the open and spatial quadrature start at

The energy, density and orbital tolerances are `1e-13`, `1e-12`
and `1e-11`, respectively. Each run uses one thread and a 1024 MiB
managed limit.

All real and imaginary entries of the Fock and density matrices,
the magnetization, free energy and reported residuals agree at the
reported precision within each model. The unit maps agree across
interfaces, and the CLI emits the SCF iteration energy and residual
on stderr.

The common driver accepts explicit weighted XC on the two magnetic
SCF routes. On the same one-electron slab, a composition with weight
`0.60` for SVWN5 and `0.25` for HF gives
`1.233350183644643` Hartree at finite Gamma and
`1.179897987508517` Hartree on the `2 x 1 x 1` magnetic Bloch mesh.
The CLI, native Python and ASE report identical energy values in each
model. The fixture verifies the separate XC component and full
exchange weights through the pure end points at the same density.
Spatial operator defects are `7.379e-12` and `7.380e-12` Hartree,
and orbital residuals are `1.250e-18` and `1.287e-18` Hartree.
The CLI also emits the SCF iteration residual on stderr.

The explicit `reference` contract passes the finite-Gamma and magnetic
Bloch one-electron slab tests on CLI, native Python and ASE. The GKS
SVWN5, BLYP, M06-L and weighted recipes give energy parity at the reported
precision in each model. The direct Rust driver call on the SVWN5
magnetic Bloch case gives the same `1.125051820465661` Hartree per
magnetic cell and orbital residual of `1.048e-17` Hartree.
Explicit GHF with the HF provider gives
`1.300040170601815` Hartree at finite Gamma and `1.086231386057308`
Hartree on the `2 x 1 x 1` mesh. The suites also check named errors for
RKS, UKS, ROKS and GHF combined with a non-HF provider. The charged
Gaussian compensation case with explicit range exchange also gives
energy parity in both models with the default reference selection.

One paired BLYP run with one thread, a 2048 MiB managed limit and
the same final spatial order 128 measured peak RSS of

operator defect is `7.054e-11` Hartree after blocking. The managed
peak is `338,148,504` bytes for both runs. This pair measures the
workspace difference on the stated fixture. Timing repeatability
requires the separate repeated benchmark.

For molecular GKS, a complex eigensolver gave a globally rotated real
density imaginary AO Pauli entries of order 2.4e-16. Comparing each
imaginary entry to its own magnitude sent the PBE H₂⁺ reference into
angular integration. The common-axis check now measures the transverse
component against the charge and spin scales of the entire complex AO
entry. The check keeps the same 64-epsilon arithmetic bound and
establishes the axis before collocation. The exact collinear path takes
all 1000 sample points in the reproduced case. The independent
`p94_spinor_angular` gate verifies both the perturbed collinear and the
resolved noncollinear cases, including the retained angular failure at
an intentionally unattainable tolerance. Its three tests pass.

H₂⁺/STO-3G with axis [0.36, 0.48, 0.8] passes CLI/native/ASE spin-axis
covariance for SVWN5, PBE, omegaB97X-D and omegaB97X-V with the defining
VV10 term. The largest energy change against the z-axis case is
4.441e-16 Hartree. Five alternating PBE CLI pairs used one thread, a
1024 MiB memory setting, SCF grid level 0 with zero cutoff and two
release builds with the same profile. The five baseline trials timed
out at 8 s. The corrected trials took 0.0262–0.0492 s with median
0.0313 s and converged in two iterations at -0.5479296501879307 Hartree
with residual 3.625e-16 Hartree. The corrected peak RSS was
21104–21764 KiB and the managed peak was 272336 bytes. The baseline
RSS at termination was 21724–22448 KiB. Its completed runtime, final
residual and managed peak could not be measured with this time limit.

#### Generated one-electron SOC in molecular GKS

`spin-orbit` with `reference=gks` selects the full spin-covariant
molecular XC provider in the self-consistent spinor calculation.
The generated one-electron operator enters the same Fock builder
as other fixed spin/AO operators. The band-energy fields describe the
single diagonalization on the collinear starting state. The
`self_consistent_energies` and `self_consistent_orbital_residuals`
fields describe the relaxed spinor states, in Hartree per starting
axis. This route uses integer occupations and all-electron molecules.

The public-route check uses distorted H2O/STO-3G with oxygen and
hydrogens at `(0.14,-0.19,0.08)`, `(1.88,0.17,-0.36)` and
`(-0.77,1.45,-0.51)` Bohr. Main and VV10 grid levels are zero with
zero grid-weight cutoff. Each case reproduces the ordinary GKS
parent energy when all effective SOC charges are set to zero. The
canonical CLI, native Python and ASE agree on the relaxed energies.

| XC | Spinor energy (Hartree) | Change from zero SOC (Hartree) | Orbital residual (Hartree) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BLYP | -75.3039760267770362 | -1.193817e-6 | 1.674146e-13 |
| M06-L | -75.3721781997275855 | -1.149463e-6 | 1.110842e-12 |
| omegaB97X-D | -75.3265418933115569 | -1.139490e-6 | 1.558645e-12 |
| omegaB97X-V | -75.3087820206406064 | -1.140955e-6 | 2.541057e-12 |

`1.134478880838e-6` atomic units against a `1e-6` bound. With

`9.973060e-11` to `6.518995e-16` and `9.771049e-13`,
respectively. The regression specifies the tighter input controls
and retains its original tensor agreement bound.

The London-RMB core multiplies both components by the London phase. Acting
with `sigma.(p+A)` on the large component places the vector-potential origin
of each small component at its own Gaussian centre. Complex H and S enter
the same analytic positive-sector solver as kinetic balance.
[Magnetically balanced London orbitals](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3240198)

On the C1 ammonia fixture with one normalized s Gaussian per atom,
`B=(0.013,-0.019,0.011)` in atomic magnetic units, nuclear RMS radii in
Bohr `(4.84e-5,1.59e-5,1.59e-5,1.59e-5)`, `c=13.7` and phase order six,
the complex closed-form Gaussian overlap and Laplace-integrated finite
nuclear potential reproduce H and S to `5.329e-15 Hartree` and
`2.220e-16`. The electronic-sector trace is
`-49.85942190754065 Hartree`. Its normalized first and second Taylor
coefficients along `(-0.31,0.46,0.67)` are
`-0.004870114055843257` and `0.39434826796469835 Hartree`.
Rigidly translating all centres by `(1.31,-2.11,0.93) Bohr` changes
those trace coefficients by at most `2.487e-14 Hartree`.

All three first and six independent second derivatives of that trace agree
with separate generalized-eigenvalue calculations on the independent H/S
at four magnetic steps `[0.09,0.065,0.046,0.032]`. Central differences use
both source directions for the mixed terms. The first derivative is
`[0.01310931132050,-0.01763964612077,0.01090747711801]` in
Hartree per atomic magnetic unit. In order xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz the
second derivative is
`[1.082771893074,0.985609573803,1.048814037235,0.053145627609,0.004019703654,0.035855723176]`
in Hartree per squared atomic magnetic unit. The nine fits give
`p=1.986677..2.009539`, minimum `R^2=0.99999607`, and prefactors
`3.771e-4..1.449e-1` in the corresponding derivative units for atomic
field steps. The largest fourth-order extrapolation discrepancy at
`h=0.004` is `1.1054e-9` in the reported derivative units. The four
existing balanced Dirac integral regression cases also pass.

On the same geometry with STO-3G, physical c, zero base field and first

The fixed-band variational phase mode uses spin-summed occupations and
anomalous densities on the supplied bands. For uniform Z and reciprocal K,
it evaluates the Helmholtz functional with pairing interaction
`K/(1+Z)` and the quasiparticle entropy. Convexity of the entropy term in
the squared length `(1-n)^2+4*abs(chi)^2` gives a bound on the canonical
free-energy change about each candidate. The reported stability margin is
the smallest eigenvalue of the identity minus the weighted pairing map.
If the normal state has a negative margin, the leading normal mode seeds
the paired solve. A paired state must have lower free energy and a margin
at or above zero within the configured residual tolerance. The criterion
includes the global phase zero mode. Generated band-dependent mass,
normal-density/orbital/phonon feedback, general pair operators and
retarded response lie outside this phase-selection model.
[Quasifree BCS free-energy functional](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0703086)

Warning-strict Rust validation of the phase and onset leaves linked against
the frozen solver passes all 11 p164 tests, including the existing response
fits. At `kT=0.004 Hartree` a half-filled single band of weight 0.73 and
`Z=0.2` gives `abs(gap)=0.0100000000000000 Hartree`,
`F(paired)-F(normal)=-6.1650122795348875e-4 Hartree` and stability margin
`-2.220446e-16`. The raw gap and number residuals are
`1.735e-18 Hartree` and zero. At `kT=0.009 Hartree` the same model
selects the normal phase with margin `0.3450828`. A separate model with
unequal weights and a sign-changing three-band gap gives gaps
`[-0.0140,0.0098,0.0182] Hartree` up to the global phase,
`mu=-0.0020 Hartree`, and `F(paired)-F(normal)=-1.7149030383674982e-3 Hartree`.
Its raw gap and number residuals are `5.204e-18 Hartree` and `8.327e-17`.
A rigid band-energy shift of `0.123 Hartree` leaves the condensation
free energy invariant within `2e-14 Hartree`.
An additional cached-library replay compiles the common driver and passes
all 12 tests, including decoding the CLI-form controls and checking the
phase and energy unit in the report. The frozen executable, native
Python and ASE in atomic and physical units pass all five phase-selection
and linear-onset public comparisons. The paired single-band report has
`gap=0.01 Hartree`, `delta_F=-6.165012279534896e-4 Hartree`, gap residual
`3.469e-18 Hartree` and zero number residual. Its hot normal-state
margin is `0.34508278907349754` with zero gap and condensation energy.

The critical-temperature mode uses the normal-state limit of the band
gap equation and a fixed electron number. Each trial recomputes the
chemical potential from Fermi occupations on the fixed weighted bands,
then evaluates the selected K/Z provider at that temperature and chemical
potential. The onset is a bracketed crossing of the leading pairing
eigenvalue through one. The weighted symmetric eigensolve is checked
against the original gap map and the original linearized gap equation.
[Lüders et al., Eqs. (33) and (35)](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0408685)

The numerical tests distinguish the resonant and fractional-fill single
band limits, a weighted two-band characteristic equation, a dense
three-band nonsymmetric solve and generated LM2005 phonon K/Z. An
asymmetric four-band gap test at `k_B T=1e-4 Hartree` checks the
chemical potential against the weighted nearest-level limit even when
both thermal occupations round to their integer values. The canonical
number bisection compares the electron and hole tails in shifted
logarithmic form when the direct residual rounds to zero. The
finite-temperature electronic density response is a separate DFPT
observable. The normal-state linear pairing onset uses fixed bands and
phonons, including the existing DFPT adapter's supplied normal inputs
where available.

The focused corrected Rust kernel replay passes all nine p164 tests
against the fixed library and unchanged helper bodies. This includes

`0`, respectively. In the four-band underflow case,
`k_B T_c=9.9999999999999991e-5 Hartree` and
`mu=-0.12501682361183106 Hartree`, the weighted nearest-level oracle.
Its gap defect is `2.220e-16` and the raw number defect is zero.
The retained linear-space predecessor fails the four-band temperature gate
when both thermal tails round to zero. The original gates are preserved.
The corrected source also passes Clippy for the library and p164 with the
Python feature enabled and warnings treated as errors.
