#### Static microscopic Coulomb kernel

The commensurate electron-phonon adapter can build a reciprocal, electronic
RPA Coulomb kernel on the full thermal restricted 3D normal band space.
Each transfer q uses complex Gaussian Bloch plane-wave vertices and an
inversion of the microscopic dielectric operator. The thermal Gamma head is
the fixed-chemical-potential compressibility limit. The charge-neutral
alternative fixes electron number at Gamma, projects the associated density
kernel and removes the electrostatic zero mode. This alternative represents
a finite cell with a specified zero head. See
[the screening controls and equations](periodic.md#static-microscopic-scdft-coulomb-screening).

The independent LiH test uses a C1 triclinic cell with row vectors
`[[6.50,0.21,-0.13],[0.32,7.20,0.39],[0.27,-0.34,7.80]]` Bohr,
Li at `[1.21,0.80,1.10]` and H at `[3.68,1.48,2.00]` Bohr,
PBE/STO-3G, a `3 x 1 x 1` k mesh, `40000 K` electronic smearing,
reciprocal screening cutoff `1.05 Bohr^-1` and `grid_weight_cutoff=0`.
The elevated temperature resolves intra- and interband contributions in
this numerical test. Independent dense Fermi-density perturbations resolved
all 211 independent real microscopic density-response components over the
three transfer points, with 7, 9 and 9 reciprocal modes. The four central
steps were `[0.006,0.004,0.002,0.001]` Hartree for every component.
The exponents span `1.998187..2.000548`, minimum R² is `0.99999983`,
and fit coefficients span `5.394e-4..1.832` for these units.
All complex screened-interaction entries were also compared to an independent
pivoted inverse.

| Quantity | Measured |
| --- | ---: |
| LiH total energy (Hartree) | -7.778696037513283 |
| LiH normal chemical potential (Hartree) | -0.1718779797067559 |
| Thermal screened Gamma head divided by cell volume (Hartree) | 0.1257450831472863 |
| Normal thermal compressibility (Bohr^-3/Hartree) | 0.02694535 |
| Maximum pair element defect for either head convention (Hartree) | 1.943e-15 |
| Maximum microscopic screened-interaction defect (Hartree Bohr^3) | 2.842e-14 |
| Pair reciprocity defect (Hartree) | 2.331e-15 |
| Largest raw dielectric inverse residual | 6.661e-16 |
| Normal particle-number residual (electrons) | 0 |

The scalar tests recover the unscreened `4*pi/q^2` limit and a one-band
thermal Gamma value of `0.028 Hartree`. This all-component test links the
screening mathematics to a cached reference library. The scalar tests
also pass against the frozen integrated release archive. That release
passes the full public adapter replay on H2 in a 9-Bohr cubic
cell, with nuclei at `z=+/-0.7 Bohr`, PBE/STO-3G, restricted Gamma-point
DFPT, `3000 K` electronic temperature, grid level 1, shell 1, zero weight
cutoff, 4-Bohr overlap cutoff and `0.95 Bohr^-1` screening cutoff.
The charge-neutral six-mode Coulomb matrix in Hartree is
`[[0.14589942042346413,0.018329196097803573], [0.018329196097803573,0.14210305890214026]]`.
Its raw inverse residual is `1.3811938749883839e-17`, inverse Hermiticity
defect `3.825e-33` and pair imaginary defect `1.740e-32 Hartree`.
The raw number and pair reciprocity defects are zero. Canonical CLI,
native Python and ASE atomic/physical units agree within the respective
`1e-8` relative and `1e-11` Hartree absolute comparison tolerances.
The independently invoked public K/Z builder agrees within its
`1e-11` relative and `1e-12` absolute tolerances. CLI stderr carries
normal SCF iteration energies and final physical residuals. The first
public invocation used the molecular `reference="rks"` spelling and
was rejected by the periodic control parser. The successful replay uses
its supported `unrestricted=False` control.

The first elemental case is doubled primitive fcc Al at a conventional
lattice constant of `4.0495 Angstrom`. The restricted all-electron
PBE/STO-3G calculation uses Gamma sampling, `10000 K` electronic
temperature, a `6 Bohr` overlap cutoff, a grid with 12 radial and 9
angular settings, shell 1 and zero weight cutoff. The total energy is
`-479.31338196369097 Hartree` per two-atom cell, the chemical potential
is `0.5538448403291434 Hartree`, and the physical orbital residual is
`1.8680163242635308e-14 Hartree`. The screening run takes `933.38 s`
with one thread in the cache-linked reference environment.

| Screening cutoff (Bohr^-1) | Reciprocal modes | Thermal W00 divided by cell volume (Hartree) | First pair K00 (Hartree) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1.0 | 3 | 49.190916848 | 49.190916848 |
| 1.3 | 3 | 49.190916848 | 49.190916848 |
| 1.6 | 17 | 49.199885134 | 49.327028437 |

The largest K change upon adding the higher shell is
`0.13611244547688273 Hartree`. The normal compressibility is
`9.0728612093e-5 Bohr^-3/Hartree`. The number defect is zero and the
inverse and reciprocity defects are at most `5.551e-16` and
`1.110e-16 Hartree`, respectively. This Gamma mesh has no resolved
Fermi-level crossing, and the large thermal head and cutoff change show
why it is insufficient for a metallic material kernel or a prediction
of Al's pairing temperature. A separate 300 K finite-k normal reference
uses the same doubled cell with a `2 x 2 x 2` mesh and a `10 Bohr`
overlap cutoff. The PBE/RKS/STO-3G SCF converges in seven iterations and
`995.32 s` on one thread. Its internal energy is `-478.8216865711775`
and its Mermin free energy is `-478.8223286559802 Hartree` per cell.
The orbital residual and overlap-metric electron-count error are
`6.513074305417451e-11 Hartree` and `1.7763568394002505e-14` electrons.
The second iteration spent `125.215 s` building the Hartree field and
`2.474 s` on the XC field. Finite-k screening, cutoff convergence,
insulating head cell averaging and normal/pairing/phonon backreaction
remain open.

#### Retarded full Nambu probe response

The supplied full complex normal matrix, overlap and antisymmetric pairing
matrix define a fixed quadratic Nambu Hamiltonian. A Hermitian probe with
normal and pairing blocks enters that Hamiltonian as `+u_b(t) Q_b`. At
`z = omega + i*eta` with `exp(-i*omega*t)`, the collisionless density
variation solves `(z-ad_H) delta_R_b = [Q_b,R_0]`. The susceptibility is
`Tr(Q_a delta_R_b)/2`, where the factor of one half compensates particle-hole
doubling. Resolved quasiparticle occupations are held fixed from the
positive-temperature reference. As a result the collisionless zero-frequency
value and the equilibrium Fermi-density Taylor coefficient can differ. The
linear-response convention follows the commutator formula.
[Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570–586 (1957)](https://doi.org/10.1143/JPSJ.12.570).

The optional symmetric curvature `U` contributes induced fields
`U delta<Q>` around the supplied reference. The solver checks the
isospectral stability bound and solves `(I-chi0*U) chi = chi0` in the given
probe space. It reports the bare spectral defect, true relative coupled
residual, reference eigen/metric defects and dimensionless stability margin.
The returned complex `nambu_bare_susceptibility_*` and
`nambu_susceptibility_*` have axes frequency, observed probe, driven probe
and units inverse Hartree. Positive damping applies a frequency shift into
the upper half plane. An unresolved undamped transition raises a named error.
Generated normal and anomalous interaction kernels, moving metric or higher
derivatives of the frequency response, and conserving electromagnetic response
are separate work.

The asymmetric three-orbital fixture uses three mixed complex probes, a
complex positive overlap, `kT=0.083 Hartree` and `omega=0.047 Hartree`.
The independent finite-amplitude oracle diagonalizes two Floquet copies with
an external or separately iterated induced field between them and holds the
adiabatically identified reference populations fixed. The smallest undriven
copy spacing is `0.001105991131580275 Hartree`. The failed exploratory steps
`[0.004,0.003,0.002,0.001]` Hartree gave eigenvalue movements up to
`9.9597e-4 Hartree`, exceeding the common `4.9770e-4 Hartree` ordering
guard, and gave fitted p between `0.89280` and `1.39775`. These steps are
outside the resolved perturbation interval.

At the common steps `[0.0004,0.0003,0.0002,0.0001]` Hartree, the
warning-strict exact Rust solver matches the real-embedded Floquet reference
for all nine independent real components of each undamped susceptibility.
The independent complex NumPy replay gives a largest eigenvalue movement of
`2.1732e-5 Hartree`. The 18 central fits have p `1.952895..1.988673`,
minimum R² `0.99991647` and coefficients `7.178e4..9.975e5` in the stated
units. The independent bare `chi[0,0]` is `0.704352650745918` inverse
Hartree. The production induced value is `0.957713119211656` inverse
Hartree, with normal eigen/metric defects `6.889e-16` and `2.220e-16`.

At damping `0.009 Hartree` the production induced `chi[0,0]` at
`omega=0.047 Hartree` is
`-1.07377176819694 - 0.234836957534146 i` inverse Hartree. Across all bare
and induced complex elements at `[+0.047,-0.047,0]` Hartree the
largest independent Liouville defect is `6.214e-15` inverse Hartree.
Signed-frequency conjugation has zero defect, and the shared pairing-phase
rotation defect is `1.024e-15` inverse Hartree. The maximum bare and induced
equation residuals are `5.562e-17` and `5.223e-16`. The stability margin
is `1.0` for this curvature. A separate resolved `5e-10 Hartree` gap
has static susceptibility `-1.96594539481402` inverse Hartree, with zero
response in the conserved-number channel. The four causal tests and both
static-density regression tests pass with cache linkage to the exact
production Nambu leaves and warnings promoted to errors. The four causal
tests also pass unchanged against the complete frozen release archive.
The same production driver with decoded CLI flags returns
`-0.860938095335012 - 0.862522762056270 i` inverse Hartree for the
assembled two-orbital complex fixture at `omega=0.067 Hartree`,
`eta=0.008 Hartree`, `mu=-0.013 Hartree` and `11999.450942554537 K`.
The independent complex Liouville value differs by less than
`5e-15` inverse Hartree.

The frozen release passes both public causal tests with Python warnings
promoted to errors. The two-orbital fixture agrees across the canonical
CLI, dedicated and generic native Python, and ASE in atomic and eV units.
Every complex bare and induced element agrees with the independent
Liouville matrix at positive, negative and zero frequency. The largest
bare and induced equation residuals are `1.110e-16` and `2.072e-16`.
The reference eigen/metric defects are `3.840e-16` and `2.220e-16`.
The unstable-curvature check raises a named Python error and gives a
CLI exit code of 1.

For real LiH in the normal limit, use nuclei at the origin and
`[0.7,-0.5,2.9]` Bohr, restricted STO-3G, electronic temperature
`1800 K`, semilocal grid level 3 and zero weight cutoff. The
nonlocal VV10 grid uses level 2 and zero weight cutoff. The dipole probes
use the three laboratory Cartesian directions at `omega=0.037 Hartree`
and `eta=0.004 Hartree`. The physical polarizability is the negative
of the susceptibility to the `+E*r` electronic perturbation.

| Reference | SCF free energy (Hartree) | Chemical potential (Hartree) | Alpha zz (Bohr^2/Hartree) | Largest all-component orbital oracle defect (Bohr^2/Hartree) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| wB97X-D | -7.95912394644335 | -0.0907646534180331 | 6.391362763806 + 0.01208016091444 i | 7.105e-15 |
| wB97X-V | -7.94525613519177 | -0.104222037312667 | 6.141674710474 + 0.01058347104056 i | 5.329e-15 |

Both SCF runs converged in ten iterations. The maximum electron-number
defect is `4.441e-16` and the maximum bare spectral residual is
`1.111e-16`. The wB97X-V SCF includes its density-dependent nonlocal
term, `0.0177699115871623 Hartree` here. The listed free energies are
the SCF values before any empirical geometry-only term. The first
validation attempt assigned `1800` directly to the low-level
`kT` field and therefore used Hartree instead of Kelvin. Its
Mermin free energies near `-1.375e4 Hartree` failed the physical check.
The corrected fixture converts Kelvin through the shared Boltzmann
constant and checks the expected energy scale. This molecular acceptance
covers zero pairing and the independent-particle dipole response. The
paired supplied-operator response still requires separate material-level
validation.

Scope of the matrix: Static molecular moments use the common AO
integrals and tensor transformations for all four references. The
common-orbital solver supplies the ROKS density. The real scalar Pauli
component supplies the GKS spin trace. Derivatives retain their own
existing reference restrictions. RKS and UKS double-hybrid static
moments use the same orbital, amplitude and target response as the
correlated dipole, applied to the requested moment operators. Reports
give unweighted alpha and beta same-spin and opposite-spin PT2
contributions separately. The common-orbital and spinor correlated
moments require their corresponding PT2 providers.

Matrix evidence: `src/driver/molecular.rs`, `src/driver/gks.rs`, `src/response/mod.rs`, `src/response/nuclear.rs`, `src/response/field_path.rs`, `p314_electric_moment_references`.

The static moment acceptance separates HF, LDA (SVWN5), GGA (PBE),
meta-GGA (TPSS), the named global hybrid PBE0 and explicit weighted XC.
Each case uses the selected RKS, UKS, ROKS or GKS reference on a C1
four-center fixture with a finite electric bias. The independent
Gaussian-product oracle checks every monopole, dipole and Cartesian
quadrupole element. A translated origin checks the charged and neutral
tensor transformation and the Buckingham projection. Every dipole
component is also fitted against independently relaxed field energies.
Public checks for PBE0 and the explicit composition compare values,
units, origins and SCF residuals through native Python, CLI and ASE.

The named PBE0 global hybrid passes the static moment oracle and all
nine dipole fits for the RKS, UKS and ROKS cases. PBE/RKS passes its
three dipole fits. On field increments of 0.008, 0.006, 0.004 and 0.003
Hartree/(e Bohr), the PBE0 exponents range from 2.000204 to 2.043562
with minimum R2 0.99997848 and prefactors 1.454e-1 to 2.392e1. The
maximum PBE0 SCF orbital residual in these three base references is
6.258e-13 Hartree. At origin (0.23, -0.50, 0.42) Bohr and field
(0.002, -0.004, 0.003) Hartree/(e Bohr), PBE0/RKS has dipole
(-0.194713696, 0.056269820, 0.106969041) e Bohr and raw quadrupole
(-1.227526189, -0.079260443, 0.123781580, -0.945292106,
-0.040678322, -1.102791195) e Bohr² in (xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz) order.
The installed Linux wheel passes all eight PBE0 and weighted
dipole/quadrupole public parity cases across RKS, UKS, ROKS and GKS,
with warnings treated as errors. These public fixtures use the standard
GKS source. The independent noncollinear GKS PBE0, PBE and TPSS CLI
snapshots reached the 180-second observation limit. Their scientific
verification remains a separate gate.

T184 adds `multipole-polarizability` with `multipole_rank` from
one to five (default three). It shares the quadrupole request, operator
construction and existing collinear, common-orbital and spinor response
kernels. Its real Racah spherical moments and fields satisfy
`E_ext = -sum_m lambda_m M_m`, where
`M_lm = sum_A Z_A R_lm(R_A-origin) - Tr(P R_lm)`.
Mode order is 0, +1, -1, ..., +l, -l. The reported tensor
`dM_lm/dlambda_ln` has shape (2l+1) by (2l+1), with units
e^2 Bohr^(2l)/Hartree. The solid-harmonic coefficient matrix and
Cartesian powers make this normalization explicit. Unlike the separate
Buckingham quadrupole convention, this conjugate response has no extra
factor of three. The selected origin matters; translating a pure
rank-l field also produces lower-rank fields.
The default
`center_of_mass` origin is attached to the molecule and moves under
a rigid translation, so shifting the coordinate system leaves its
moments and response components unchanged. This removes dependence
on a laboratory coordinate offset, not the physical dependence on
the expansion centre. Permanent charged dipoles already illustrate
why arbitrary origin independence is impossible. The neutral RKS and
charged UKS/ROKS/GKS public translation tests check every moment
component through rank five and every static and retarded response
entry at ranks three through five.

Ranks three, four and five describe electric octupole, hexadecapole
and 32-pole moments, with 7x7, 9x9 and 11x11 response tensors.
These are linear responses to spatially varying multipole potentials;
they are distinct from nonlinear dipole hyperpolarizabilities. Signed
retarded and imaginary frequencies reuse the same one-body kernels.
The static RKS/UKS target and spin-resolved PT2 paths and the existing
common-weight static GKS PT2 path are connected at the required mode
counts. The new RKS/UKS causal perturbative PT2 path is connected but
independently unvalidated. Correlated GKS nonzero frequency and ROKS
remain named unsupported conditions. No field-gradient or relativistic/quantum-nuclear
capability is inferred from this new ordinary molecular entry.

passes the rank-one through rank-eight Racah addition theorem and

z = 0.08 + 0.012 i Hartree agrees with every ordered rank-three,
rank-four and rank-five complex response component within
2.7712e-13, 9.2372e-13 and 4.6044e-12 in their respective units.

static limit extrapolates from four positive imaginary frequencies
(1e-6, 2e-6, 4e-6, 8e-6) Hartree, retaining the signed defects at
each frequency. The largest extrapolated difference is

The largest recorded relative equation residual in the four-frequency
rank-four and rank-five replay is 9.936518e-11. The GKS static C00 is
125.351302286 e^2 Bohr^8/Hartree and 97.436930433 e^2 Bohr^10/Hartree

Its all-rank and functional-class acceptance gates remain open. The
separate eight-case public parity suite passed. A separate s-Gaussian
state sum compared 502 ordered complex entries across ranks three
through five at z=0.08+0.012i and z=1e-6i Hartree. Its maximum

The nonzero-frequency double-hybrid extension remains under development.
Its low-level `properties::pt2_response::Pt2FrequencyKernel` reuses
the existing Pauli-allowed spin-resolved pair action and stationary
denominators. Two labelled harmonics +z and -z retain the analytic left
and right coupling vertices and the moving-frame orbital connection.
Raw absolute and relative pair residuals are returned per harmonic and
spin. The exact frozen pair module passes four supplemental Rust tests
with warnings denied. An independent unique-determinant, three-harmonic
Floquet solve gives all 24 component/channel fits on h=(0.1,0.075,0.05,0.03),
with p=3.999757..4.000160 and R2=1.00000000 at the reported precision.
The fitted error is abs(D(h)-D_analytic), not its square; R2 is the
separate fit-quality statistic. The fourth-order error here follows from
zero-harmonic selection and four-corner parity. With independent +z/-z
amplitudes x and y, E=E0+a*x*y+b*x^2*y^2+c*x^3*y^3+... . The mixed
four-corner difference removes the even b term; the next term contributes
h^6/h^2=h^4. Ordinary central differences, including the assembled
cosine-field molecular oracle below, retain an h^2 error and use expected
order two. Existing fit-quality and order tolerances are unchanged.
The exact zero-frequency comparison over every ordered pair component
and SS-alpha/OS/SS-beta/weighted channel has maximum defect
1.1102230246251565e-16. Moving-frame phase covariance differs by at most
5.761815542251313e-16. The Pauli-forbidden pole, genuine driven pole
refusal and damped-pole checks pass. At z=0.51+0.039 i Hartree, the
prescribed-vertex weighted [0,0] response is
0.13338783719143835+0.0037832193855667157 i in the fixture's units.
This is a prescribed-vertex model, not a molecular result.
The supplemental harness includes production and test files verbatim
from source SHA-256
`1449d7a3f61f483f6ccefeb68217dd47572eff0932fdcf6732fd4a5ef418a090`,

The full-crate frozen-source test run remains separate. These prescribed-vertex tests alone are not molecular dynamic
polarizability acceptance. The assembled RKS/UKS driver now connects
parent +z/-z/zero-sum density and Fock paths, the distinct-target mixed
action, algebraically dual moving orbitals and the shifted SS/OS pair
equations. Dipole, Buckingham quadrupole and Racah multipole requests
share that driver. The model is a perturbative quasi-energy susceptibility
on an adiabatic parent, including residue corrections and unresummed
parent poles. It is not an excitation-energy-only correction.
The assembled static limit, signed-frequency identities, origin covariance
and installed API tests retain separate gates. Correlated GKS/ROKS nonzero
frequency and learned or nonlocal parent/target paths remain explicitly
unsupported.

The assembled finite-amplitude RKS HF-parent/SVWN5-target C1 dipole oracle
now passes its bounded immutable-library probe at omega=0.071 Hartree.
It solves a finite Sambe HF eigenproblem using direct four-index
Coulomb/exchange sums, evaluates the actual target energy on a time grid,
constructs finite polar orbital frames with their spectral connection,
and solves dense unique-pair Floquet equations. The oracle is independent
of production density derivatives, moving-frame jets and pair derivatives.
All six independent dipole components and seven energy/spin channels pass
on h=(0.0024,0.0018,0.0012,0.00075) atomic units: 42 fits, p =

2.9248302744924937) e^2 Bohr^2/Hartree. The [0,0] total, parent,
target correction and weighted PT2 entries are respectively
2.40223603815713, 3.4102623567079373, -0.2429466577307684 and
-0.7650796608200386 in those units. The unweighted SS-alpha, OS and

Initial finite-amplitude fixed-point oracles with mixing 0.55 and 0.12
failed the required root-overlap bound before derivative comparison.
Those failures are retained. An independently constructed, cached
zero-drive Sambe-projector Jacobian resolves that iteration failure with
Newton corrections, keeping the density threshold 2e-13 and root weight
greater than 0.5 unchanged. A larger-amplitude Newton interval and a
separate omega=0.11 attempt also failed and remain recorded; the measured
resolved interval is the four amplitudes above at omega=0.071.

The earlier UKS omega=0.071 intervals are retained as unresolved evidence.
Expanding the finite Sambe space to harmonics -3..3 resolves 40 of 42

T179 connects the electric quadrupole polarizability in five
orthonormal symmetric traceless field-gradient modes. The reported
Buckingham susceptibility is three times the response of the
energy-conjugate moment. Static, retarded and imaginary frequencies
reuse the existing collinear paired, common-orbital and full-spin
one-body solvers. The acceptance suite compares all 25 ordered
components against independently biased stationary states, and
checks frequency conjugation and the static limit. Collinear
double-hybrid permanent quadrupoles have their own first-order
energy tests for all six Cartesian entries and each PT2 channel.

The permanent quadrupole suite passes all 156 fits for named B2PLYP and
custom HF-parent/SVWN5-target RKS and UKS. Each reference uses synthetic
s Gaussians and an independent Gaussian-product quadrupole operator in
the displaced SCF. The second-order exponents span 1.907270 to 2.123509
with minimum R2 0.99980146 on the interval (0.004, 0.003, 0.002, 0.0015)
Hartree/(e Bohr²). B2PLYP/UKS opposite-spin yy has three retained
second-order failures. On the same four-step interval the fourth-order
stencil resolves it with p=4.000753, R2=0.99999998 and C=1.693e4.
The largest reference orbital residual is 1.447e-13 Hartree.
B2PLYP/RKS gives the raw quadrupole
(-1.840926829, -0.635289314, 0.327752372, -2.471576858,
-0.023137608, -1.056688511) e Bohr² in (xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz) order.

The corrected direct-reference suite passes all 125 ordered component

The static RKS/UKS double-hybrid extension uses the same second-order
fixed-geometry projector and PT2 amplitude path as the correlated
dipole polarizability with five field-gradient AO operators. The total,
parent, target and PT2 (weighted and separate unweighted spin
channels) are in e² Bohr⁴/Hartree. The response is constructed as a
symmetric energy Hessian. Stationarity and particle-number defects,
iterative residuals and Taylor amplitude residuals are reported
separately. Independent Gaussian field-gradient perturbations are
applied to the stationary parent for the component fits. The second
derivative is checked against differences of relaxed first-order
moments, including distinct row and column modes for mixed components.
The B2PLYP and custom HF-parent/SVWN5-target RKS and UKS fixtures
pass all 390 component and spin-channel fits. All cases use the same
four steps (0.004, 0.003, 0.002, 0.0015) Hartree/(e Bohr²), and no
alternate interval is required.

Maximum raw SCF orbital, second-order commutator, projector,
orbital-frame, particle-number and amplitude residual magnitudes
across the four cases are 1.447e-13 Hartree, 2.282e-10, 0,
2.351e-15, 2.843e-14 and 5.552e-16 in the reported coefficient units.
The custom HF-parent tensors agree with the direct HF RKS and UKS
results in the same fixtures to 1.510e-14 and 7.106e-15
e² Bohr⁴/Hartree respectively. The target and correlation tensors
supply the remaining response.
The audited Linux wheel passes the three quadrupole API cases with
Python warnings treated as errors. Both B2PLYP references agree across
the installed CLI, native Python and ASE for all seven tensors, raw
orbital and amplitude solve residuals, and ASE unit conversion.
The static spinor extension connects the common-weight generalized PT2
response to the same field-gradient Hessian. All 15 directional solves
reuse the fixed spinor reference, descriptor cache and spatial Coulomb
series. The report separates the parent, spin-complete unweighted PT2
and weighted correction. The spinor energy and diagnostics retain the
full complex orbitals and spin-flip substitutions. The independent
energy checks contract the stationary complex orbitals over distinct
occupied and virtual pairs and use mixed Gaussian field gradients for
the off-diagonal Hessian entries. For the asymmetric H5 HF-parent
fixture with a complex transverse source, a uniform electric bias and
a PT2 coefficient of 0.27, all 45 independent parent, unweighted
PT2 and total component fits pass on (0.008, 0.006, 0.004, 0.003)
Hartree/(e Bohr²). The exponent spans 1.991494 to 2.006127,
the minimum R2 is 0.99999877 and the fit C spans 0.3288 to 369.2.
The total energy is -1.569675193072060 Hartree. Unweighted PT2 is
-0.015104211018929 Hartree and agrees with the independently contracted
stationary spinor pair sum within 2e-12 Hartree. C[0,0] is
10.611479857520578 e² Bohr⁴/Hartree, with parent 9.949260442499442
and weighted PT2 correction 0.662219415021136. The raw SCF orbital
residual is 1.131e-15 Hartree. The largest relative orbital and pair
solve residuals are 3.001e-15 and 1.072e-16. The largest absolute
stationarity and particle-number coefficient defects are 9.070e-15
and 9.770e-15 in the reported Taylor units. In the installed wheel, the
closed-shell GKS limit agrees with RKS in the total tensor to 4.797e-14
e² Bohr⁴/Hartree and in total energy to 2.221e-16 Hartree. Global spin
rotation of the complex source changes the total tensor by at most
1.239e-12 e² Bohr⁴/Hartree and the energy by 1.111e-15 Hartree.
The installed HF-parent spinor case also agrees across CLI, native
Python and ASE for the four tensors and raw relative residuals.
The parent tensor agrees with the direct HF GKS quadrupole response
of the same H5 fixture within 4.092e-11 e² Bohr⁴/Hartree.
A distinct semilocal or hybrid target is evaluated on the same parent
density Taylor path. Its correction includes both the explicit
difference of the functionals on that path and the relaxed
second-order parent density. The target uses its own exchange kernel
and can have a range separation different from the parent's. The
full-spin PT2 amplitudes retain the parent energies and frame.
All 60 independent fits for the noncollinear HF-parent/SVWN5-target
H5 fixture pass on (0.008, 0.006, 0.004, 0.003) Hartree/(e Bohr²).
The four channels are parent, unweighted PT2, total and target.
They use separately displaced stationary energies and mixed field
gradients. Exponents span 1.990531 to 2.006127, minimum R2 is
0.99999847 and C spans 0.3288 to 969.6. All components pass on the
first interval. C[0,0] is 25.343798225144372 e² Bohr⁴/Hartree,
with parent 9.949260442499442, target 14.732318367623792 and weighted
PT2 0.662219415021136. The energy is -1.524043215033740 Hartree.
The SCF orbital residual is 1.130e-15 Hartree. The largest relative
orbital and pair solve residuals are 3.000e-15 and 1.071e-16.
The preceding installed wheel passes both HF-parent and distinct
SVWN5-target tensor, energy and raw residual checks across the
canonical CLI, native Python and ASE. The installed wheel with the
LDA endpoint optimization also passes the distinct-target tensor,
stationary energy, unit and residual parity test.

At regular LDA grid points the converged
spinor Taylor path now evaluates the spherical projection through
the two endpoints of the collinear spin density. The angular
integrand is the derivative of z times the collinear energy with
respect to z, so the average is the mean of the energies at the
two spin-density eigenvalue orderings. The density potential and
its derivatives follow from the same endpoint energy. The angular
evaluation remains available near zero spin and the minority-density
boundary. Explicit fixed-rule point evaluations keep their angular
meaning. The independent spin-density eigenvalue exchange oracle
passes all 60 potential, kernel and second-potential-derivative
fits with (0.016, 0.012, 0.008, 0.006) descriptor displacements,
p=2.000112..2.001504, minimum R2=0.99999996 and
C=0.004876..0.8951. The regular SVWN5 energy and potential
Taylor coefficients through second order agree with the 32-point
polar angular rule within 2e-12.

The LDA endpoint benchmark uses the preceding angular build and the
endpoint build with the same release settings, a biased H2/STO-3G
HF-parent/SVWN5-target GKS calculation, two threads and a 1024 MiB
managed-memory limit. Five alternating installed CLI trials give median
times 199.265 s and 4.123 s and time MADs 10.118 s and 1.773 s.
Median peak RSS is 51,011,584 and 51,232,768 bytes, respectively, and
the managed peak is 147,816 bytes in both builds. The runs share the
validation host with other jobs. Across all ten trials the maximum
energy, total tensor and target tensor differences are 4.441e-16 Hartree,
2.221e-16 and 3.331e-16 e² Bohr⁴/Hartree, respectively. Every trial takes
12 SCF iterations with orbital residual 8.376e-16 Hartree and maximum
relative response residual 8.289e-16.

The common driver accepts a weighted custom orbital parent with PT2
for the energy and the static dipole and quadrupole responses. The
clean-installed CLI, native Python and ASE agree for the noncollinear
H5 energy with 0.80 HF + 0.20 SVWN5 and a common PT2 coefficient of
0.27. The total energy is -1.562776338977913 Hartree and the weighted
PT2 energy is -0.005102851664798 Hartree. The unweighted pair energy
is -0.018899450610363265 Hartree and agrees with the independent
normalized-Gaussian integral and spinor pair contraction within
4.164e-17 Hartree. The absolute amplitude residual is 6.939e-18
Hartree and the SCF orbital residual is 1.291e-15 Hartree. Independent
component fits for the weighted-parent responses have their own gates.
Correlated frequencies, ROKS, nonlocal spinor correlation and unequal
spin coefficients remain separate coverage conditions.

The spinor dipole and quadrupole polarizabilities use the same stationary
full-spin PT2 Hessian and diagnostics. The dipole source is the electronic
Cartesian position operator, with a positive coupling in the Hamiltonian.
The report uses the negative second energy derivative and expands the six
independent entries into a 3 by 3 tensor in e² Bohr²/Hartree. The common
driver exposes this static GKS subset through Rust, the canonical CLI,
native Python and ASE. The asymmetric H5 HF-parent/SVWN5-target dipole
case passes all 24 independent fits for the six Cartesian components and
four energy channels. Independent normalized-Gaussian dipole sources and
mixed fields give p=1.996975 to 2.005450, minimum R2=0.99999953 and
C=4.372 to 62.47 on (0.008, 0.006, 0.004, 0.003) Hartree/(e Bohr).
All fits pass on the first interval. Alpha[0,0] is 6.419999128206088
e² Bohr²/Hartree, with parent 4.823542050357013, target correction
1.543750419664510 and weighted PT2 0.052706658184565. The raw SCF
orbital residual is 1.130e-15 Hartree and the largest relative orbital
response residual is 3.211e-15. A separate H3 fixture on an audited
wheel agrees across the installed CLI, native Python and ASE atomic and
physical reports. The zero-frequency alias returns the same tensor.
Its alpha[0,0] is 1.959849087793443 e² Bohr²/Hartree and the maximum
relative response residual is 8.951e-15.

The installed retarded quadrupole route also passes atomic and ASE-unit
parity at 0.02 Hartree with damping 0.005 Hartree for RKS/SVWN5, UKS/PBE
and ROKS/TPSS. C[0,0] is (16.866941077894 + 3.413615627134 i),
(19.672791516300 + 0.052324926688 i) and
(22.072525091838 + 0.041562778660 i) e² Bohr⁴/Hartree, respectively.
The largest relative response residuals are 4.869e-15, 8.180e-11
and 9.899e-16, respectively. The independent functional-by-reference
component matrix has a separate gate.

The existing correlated dipole polarizability shares the parent solver
across directions after the refactor. Five alternating before/after
installed CLI trials for B2PLYP/STO-3G water, grid level 1, one thread
and a 1024 MiB memory limit give 4.421 s versus 4.089 s (time MAD
0.157 s versus 0.054 s), managed peak 3,369,704 versus 1,780,656 bytes,
and peak RSS 49,750,016 versus 50,089,984 bytes. The tensor is identical
at reported precision, the SCF takes seven iterations in each trial,
and the maximum orbital and relative response residuals remain
9.353e-11 Hartree and 6.461e-16.

On an audited Linux 0.3.0 wheel, HF/STO-3G water gives static
C00 = 3.03894361189 and retarded C00 = 3.04441184821 + 0.001107525572 i
in e^2 Bohr^4/Hartree at z = 0.04 + 0.004 i Hartree. The
five-mode rotation defect is 3.02e-14 and the imaginary-frequency
static-limit defect is 1.20e-9 in the same tensor units. Signed
frequency conjugation and the absorptive positive-semidefinite check
pass. Native Python, the installed CLI and ASE agree at the reported
precision. The HF/cc-pVDZ water fixture gives static C00 =
8.346784749977127 in the same units. The two basis sets use the same
conventions and supply separate numerical cases.

The shared paired Casida action has an exact-zero block optimization candidate.
It skips the AO Coulomb/exchange/XC contractions only when every input amplitude
in a real paired block is exactly zero. Nonzero amplitudes, the complex frequency
coupling and the fresh full residual equation retain the existing path.
The full-column static/retarded comparison
`response::dynamic::tests::zero_block_action_matches_unscreened_casida_columns`
also covers purely imaginary and 1e-100 amplitudes. Numerical acceptance and
matched five-trial performance measurements are pending; no speedup is claimed.
`tools/bench.py` retains both real and imaginary quadrupole tensors for these
comparisons, together with raw residuals and memory statistics.
The live benchmark checks every retained observable against the first baseline
trial (or first candidate trial when no baseline executable is supplied).
Missing components, changed shapes and non-finite values fail acceptance.
The absolute and relative tolerances are explicit command-line settings, both
defaulting to 1e-8 in output units, and are saved with the result.
A failed numerical gate preserves raw trials, suppresses speed reporting and
returns a nonzero exit status. Eight warning-strict benchmark tests pass,
including an end-to-end failure with unchanged successful process exit codes.
The exact-zero Casida candidate passes warning-strict all-feature Clippy;
its numerical and matched performance gates remain pending.


Supplemental installed HF/6-31G HCN checks at a center-of-mass origin give
static C00 = 5.751671215338933 and retarded C00 =
5.8500583268790445 + 0.01669299599895186 i e^2 Bohr^4/Hartree at
z = 0.075 + 0.006 i Hartree. All 25 entries satisfy signed-frequency
conjugation with zero measured defect; the static imaginary part is zero.
Maximum retarded relative residual is 9.612911514617104e-11.
The earlier audit found an output-key failure. The corrected check
measures an invariant on the audited wheel. All-component derivative
acceptance has its own gate.

### R067 ground-state-properties-exports-relaxation-and-streaming

#### Molecular total-spin streaming

The molecular unrestricted and common-orbital solvers stream the
final `<S^2>` in units of `hbar^2`. The common-orbital determinant
uses `S(S+1)`. The unrestricted value uses the converged alpha and
beta density overlap and includes the Wick number variance for
fractional occupations.

The molecular GKS report gives `s_squared` in `hbar^2` and
`spin_expectation` in `hbar`. For a fixed-particle spinor determinant
it also gives `spin_sector_weights`, one normalized probability per
total-spin sector. The axis-resolved spin-up count distribution uses
the eigenvalues of the spin-up projector compressed to the occupied
space. A rotational average gives `q_M = sum(p_S/(2S+1), S >= |M|)`.
The adjacent differences recover the sector weights. Raw discrepancies
in normalization and in the reconstructed `<S^2>` accompany the
weights and appear in the log. Fractional-occupation runs report the
Wick expectation and a null sector distribution.

The same run-local logger flushes the stream and requested log file.
Independent two-electron tests pass the singlet, triplet and mixed
cases, including after a complex global spin rotation. The mixture
has weights `0.5, 0.5` for `S=0,1` and `<S^2>=1`. The
fractional-occupation independent ensemble at occupations `0.7,0.2`
gives `<S^2>=0.465`. CLI, native Python and ASE logging acceptance
uses a distorted ammonia cation and is staged.

independently reconverged energy oracle for the two finite-k VV10 force

#### Geometry-only dispersion with periodic common-orbital references

The field-free periodic ROKS driver assembles D2, D3(zero), D3(BJ), available
ATM terms, and the required CHG tail of omegaB97X-D from the same cell
used by the converged electronic reference in 1D, 2D and 3D. The correction enters the
total energy once. Its forces and strain derivative enter the total force
and stress. Forces use Hartree/Bohr. Stress uses Hartree/Bohr^d for
periodic dimension `d`, with raw ordered strain derivatives in Hartree
per cell. The stationary
electronic and nuclear energies remain separate report fields. The DOS
report includes the corrected reference energy and retains electronic
orbital energies for its spectrum. Gamma fixed-cell optimization includes
the same correction in the objective and gradient at every trial.

The staged LiH2 doublet omegaB97X-D acceptance uses a triclinic C1 cell,
zero grid weight cutoff, and 3.8 Bohr overlap and exchange radii. It
checks all nine Cartesian forces and nine ordered affine derivatives
against separately reconverged energies for Gamma and a 2x1x1 mesh.
The frozen CLI `d536ee66284cc7dd737c12ac5f9d49469ba3e0056b68174b30e21ff542ae07e0`
and native module `2d9c3be6c2f82af6d4893e75f0ffc82c8da8db43c6e5aa2f22c89c704d9fc35d`
passed all four public cases. Across the CLI, native Python and ASE the
energy, correction, forces, ordered strain, stress, pressure and orbital
residual agreed at an absolute tolerance of `1e-10` in their report units.
The tests used grid level 0, a 5.4 Bohr pair cutoff and SCF tolerances
`1e-13` Hartree for energy, `1e-11` for density and `1e-10` Hartree for
orbital residual. The corrected DOS reference energies agree with the
stress reports within `1e-12` Hartree and count eight spin-resolved states
per cell. The bulk Gamma fixed-cell objective decreased on the first
ionic step, and all four CLI cases emitted SCF residuals on stderr.

Twelve additional energy and dipole reports converged on the open-shell
OH doublet with UKS and ROKS. UKS spin-square was 0.75095346 to
0.75117089 and ROKS spin-square was 0.75. The working-tree records

reports. These checks establish the stated reference and observable
scope. Basis and grid convergence and derivative acceptance remain
separate.

The electronic DOS accepts the periodic axes and evaluates RKS, UKS,
ROKS or GKS spectra on their stationary SCF mesh. Bulk collinear DOS
also supports a separate frozen sampling mesh. ROKS diagonalizes each
physical spin Fock within the closed, open and virtual common-orbital
blocks. This preserves both occupied subspaces. GKS counts one state
per spinor and combines both spin components in its orbital projections.
Restricted collinear DOS counts two spin states per band. The integrated
DOS is in states per cell for wires, slabs and bulk. The raw per-channel
state count and exact Gaussian count in the requested window are
reported separately from the signed trapezoidal integration residual.
The orbital projections report their maximum sum-rule defect. The
closed-shell limit, independent semicanonical spectrum, state counts and
installed route comparisons have separate tests. Correlated spectra and
frozen sampling for the newly connected reference routes remain separate
models.

The Windows periodic DOS acceptance passes the two driver tests. The
closed-shell HF wire on a three-point mesh integrates to
4.0000000000000036 states per cell for RKS, UKS, ROKS and GKS.
The common peak is 13.2887825506315 states/Hartree per cell. Its energy
is -0.726187091967262 Hartree per cell. The independent open-shell
HF ROKS slab and HF UKS bulk fixtures each integrate to
4.0000000000000009 states per cell. Their peaks are 7.03400790752267
and 6.87106044412919 states/Hartree per cell. All cases pass the
1e-10 per-channel trapezoidal integration and Mulliken sum bounds.
The closed-shell curves agree within 1e-7 states/Hartree per cell.
The installed Windows wheel also passes GKS wire and ROKS slab DOS
comparisons across native Python, ASE and the CLI. These open-shell
fixtures have energies -2.421218382979283 and -2.421216684831667
Hartree/cell and each has four states per cell. The comparison
checks the total and Mulliken projected curves and raw sum rules.

Weighted molecular XC connects the common energy, analytic gradient and Hessian
reports to the sum of the declared XC operators on a single set of SCF
orbitals. The bounded path accepts semilocal and global exchange terms
and one common long-range exchange kernel. Multiple distinct long-range
kernels, required nonlocal terms, weighted Skala, PT2, higher-order
weighted nuclear tensors and weighted periodic response above first order
remain pending. The common-orbital ROKS
and complex spinor GKS drivers consume the same resolved operator for
energy, gradient and Hessian. Each reports the stationarity residual for its
reference. ROKS uses the active effective Fock elements from the accepted
SCF iteration and GKS uses the orbital residual of the spinor solution.
The initial asymmetric H4 fixture passed all 24 Cartesian fits with
`grid_weight_cutoff=0` on the RKS and equal-population UKS branches. The
steps were 0.032, 0.024, 0.016 and 0.012 Bohr, with exponents
1.998156 to 2.000229, minimum R2 0.99999994 and translation residual
7.295e-16 Hartree/Bohr on both branches. A unit-weight PBE0 energy matched
the ordinary PBE0 specification within 1e-12 Hartree. See
`tests/p313_weighted_xc.rs` and `python/tests/test_weighted_xc.py` for the
component and public route checks.

The follow-up fixture uses neutral RKS H4 and spin-polarized UKS H4+.
All 24 components pass at the same four steps, with exponents 1.998156
to 2.000256, minimum R2 0.99999994 and prefactors 4.889e-3 to 1.035e-1
for steps measured in Bohr. Translation residuals are 7.295e-16 and
5.055e-16 Hartree/Bohr. The maximum orbital-frame SCF commutator
elements at the two base geometries are 6.584e-16 and 3.744e-13 Hartree.
Every displaced SCF passes the 1e-10 Hartree residual check. A separate
TPSS/PBE0/SVWN5 point check combines independently evaluated term
energies with a signed weight and checks the full-range exchange
coefficient separately.

The periodic energy, Cartesian force and affine-stress routes also consume
the shared weighted specification. See [R026](#r026-stress-elastic-high-elastic)
for the periodic source and acceptance scope.

Measured periodic ROKS reference increment (2026-11-02):

the first two lattice vectors. Its analytic strain tangent enters the AO,
Becke and, where active, VV10 point terms. The initial co-rotating
SVWN5 test used the same triclinic He–H cell, level-4 angular pruning
and zero grid weight cutoff. At the centre it converged in seven SCF
iterations to −2.350908328358456 Hartree. The orbital residual was
2.614e-16 Hartree, the occupation defect was 8.049e-16 and the Coulomb
operator defect was zero. The grid integrated the electron count with a
1.5881461e-5 electron error against the 1e-5 gate, so both original
tests stopped before the displacements. Pruned levels 5, 6 and 7 gave
2.7523247e-5, 1.2362385e-5 and 1.8941247e-5 electrons, respectively.
With the level-4 angular rules and 200 radial nodes the error was
1.7367260e-5 electrons.

24 signed rigid rotations at 0.04, 0.02, 0.01 and 0.005 rad had maximum
energy defect 7.550e-15 Hartree and maximum raw torque 1.152e-15
Hartree. All nine ordered strain fits passed on the same four strain
steps from 73 SCFs, with p=1.99764945..2.00004236, minimum R²=0.999999681
and prefactors 3.319e-4..4.978e-1. The smallest-step absolute deviations
were 8.395e-9..1.2482e-5 Hartree. The maximum fresh orbital residual
was 1.223e-15 Hartree and the maximum grid number error was 2.714e-6
electrons. The unpruned centre energy was −2.350894088379315 Hartree.

#### Canonical finite-temperature molecular derivatives

The candidate uses the moving-geometry Taylor source and the canonical
Fermi response at fixed electronic temperature. The density law is
`D_s(t) = f((F_s(t) - mu_s(t) I)/(k_B T))` in the transported
orthonormal frame. The shared ensemble susceptibility determines each
new density coefficient and chemical-potential correction at fixed spin
population. The free-energy term `-T S` follows from integrating
`-Tr((F_s - mu_s I) dD_s/dt)` along the stationary path. The resulting
derivatives feed the existing nuclear and electric tensor assemblies.

The preserved baseline PBE/RKS/STO-3G tests on C1 NH3 at electronic
temperature 100000 K failed both the fourth electric free-energy identity
and the static beta/gamma test before numerical comparison. Separately
evaluated spin-source traces differed by roundoff, so the restricted
ensemble rejected unequal alpha and beta number shifts. The correction
uses the common restricted Fock and density at each order and keeps the
two spin targets identical. Numeric replay of the corrected candidate is
pending.

#### Molecular finite-temperature ROKS and GKS

The common `mermin-free-energy` and `free-energy` routes use the same
complex spinor SCF as `energy` for GKS and GHF. Its occupation equation
uses one chemical potential at fixed total electron count. The scalar
report gives `internal_energy`, `mermin_free_energy`, `entropy`,
`occupations`, a one-entry `chemical_potentials` array and raw orbital
and particle-number residuals. In this report, `entropy_term` has sign
`-T_e S_e`.

For ROKS and ROHF the common spatial orbital matrix is varied jointly
with two Fermi occupation vectors. Each chemical potential enforces its
spin's electron count. The residual comprises the occupation-weighted
sum of the two orbital commutators and the two diagonal Fock-level
equations in the common frame. The analytic first gradient uses the
symmetrized occupation-weighted Fock matrix as the overlap multiplier.
The higher-order path transports the common frame with the moving
metric and continues its rotations, occupations and chemical potentials
with the same residual Jacobian.

The GKS/GHF Taylor path transports the complex spinor frame with the
moving metric and solves the Hermitian Fermi density equation with a
trace constraint and one chemical potential. The energy expansion
integrates the entropy derivative in the orthonormal frame. At second
order only first-order density response is needed because the
second-order density contributions to energy and entropy cancel at
stationarity. Reports retain the raw orbital and response residuals,
Fermi or common-orbital stationarity defects and electron-count defects.
The new nuclear routes require compatible analytic integral, grid and
functional providers. Thermal PT2 and periodic ROKS/GKS nuclear
extensions remain open.

The two GKS cases use H2 in STO-3G with coordinates
`(0.13,-0.18,0.08)` and `(1.82,0.29,-0.17)` Bohr at
120,000 K to resolve fractional occupations. The main and VV10 grid
levels are zero, with zero grid-weight cutoff. The canonical Rust
CLI, native Python and ASE agree for both functionals. The regression
independently reconstructs the Fermi–Dirac occupations from the spinor
eigenvalues and chemical potential and computes the entropy from those
occupations.

CASSCF and MC-PDFT in the common driver require all-electron active-space
populations. With ECP, the seed SCF uses valence populations and the
active-space driver returns a named capability error. Nuclear derivatives
in a finite uniform electric field also have a separate capability error
until the active-space path includes the electric one-electron and
nuclear energy terms.

On a clean replay of the original LiH/FT-PBE CMS-PDFT public check,
the second state differed by `3.1003e-10` Hartree between CLI and
native Python at the unchanged `1e-10` Hartree gate. The ordinary
active-space energies agreed to roundoff and the orbital residuals
were both `6.91725e-9` Hartree. The summed Coulomb localization
objective agreed at the printed precision, while the optimal rotation
angle differed by `5.8036e-8` radians. The original golden-section
comparisons lose the rotation well before the objective loses digits.
The analytic pair search writes the two rotated densities as
`A ± (B cos(2 theta) + C sin(2 theta))`. The pair objective has
only a constant and the two harmonics of `4 theta`, so the maximum
is a single quarter-angle `atan2` from three Coulomb contractions.

The rebuilt CLI, native extension and ASE pass the original parity
gate with CMS-PDFT energies `-7.916417749232416` and
`-7.764631143234748` Hartree and angle
`-0.296503538848499` radians. Native, generic Python and atomic ASE
agree bitwise. The CLI differences are `1.78e-15` Hartree in
the state energies, `5.33e-15` in the Coulomb terms, `1.33e-15`
in the on-top terms, and `8.88e-16` in the effective Hamiltonian.
The p230 and p232 Rust suites pass 9 and 1 tests on the rebuilt library.
The p230 coverage includes explicit zero-field derivative compatibility
and capability errors for ECP populations and finite-field nuclear paths.
The four existing CLI/native/ASE cases, including the state-specific
gradient and Hessian reports, pass with warnings treated as errors.

Five alternating CLI samples per build use the same LiH input,
one thread, a 256 MiB setting, release optimization level 1 and
128 codegen units. The baseline median and interval are
`0.2089 [0.1289, 0.2440]` seconds. The candidate's are
`0.2154 [0.1541, 0.2655]` seconds. Peak RSS medians are
`23437312` and `23719936` bytes. The managed peak of
`172184` bytes, eight CASSCF macroiterations and raw final orbital
gradient of `6.91725200903381e-9` Hartree agree across all runs.
The timing intervals overlap.

The original cross-API fixture round-trips to the same nuclear
coordinate bits. A separate LiH probe changing the distance by one
ULP rotates the transverse p part of the state density, with
its lithium p-block eigenvalues fixed to roundoff. The second
state eigenvalues remain approximately `[0, 0.0022131836582,
0.5584932187103]`. The CAS energies and summed Coulomb objective
remain stable within `1e-14` Hartree while finite on-top quadrature
of the differently oriented density changes. At grid levels 3 and
5 the minus-one-ULP probe changes the second CMS-PDFT energy by
about `1.1e-4` and `2.0e-5` Hartree, respectively. This degenerate
orbital orientation sensitivity remains outside the exact-coordinate
CLI parity subset.

#### Molecular Dirac–Coulomb Kohn–Sham

T193 selects the molecular `dirac-dks` driver. It forms the full
four-component restricted-kinetic-balance Dirac core and fixes its positive
electronic sector at the field-free nuclear core. Every SCF step contracts
the Coulomb, hybrid exchange and XC terms with the full balanced density.
The functional uses the existing noncollinear charge and spin descriptors
of the large and small components. This is a no-pair Dirac–Coulomb model
with a finite Gaussian charge distribution for each nucleus.
[Four-component relativistic Kohn–Sham theory](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.10066)

The numerical solve uses the nuclear-core eigenvector chart of the positive
sector. Its energy terms agree with the spin-orbit X2C formulation in the
same finite basis if all the operators and the density use the same change
of picture. The fixed-sector electric response uses the same SCF kernel,
and reports each source residual. The model accepts an isolated
all-electron even-electron reference, with semilocal, hybrid or supported
weighted XC and the provider's required VV10 or CHG.
[Exact decoupling](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2137315)

Raw diagnostics include the reference orbital residual, metric defect,
particle-number error, Dirac sector gap and response residuals. A first
frozen native run on LiH at 1.596 Å with omegaB97X-D/STO-3G, Gaussian RMS
radii (4.62e-5, 1.59e-5) Bohr, physical speed of light and grid level zero
gives -7.955763826143945 Hartree and bond-axis dipole -1.902512063434630
e Bohr. The CHG term is -0.000350870137313650 Hartree. The raw orbital
residual is 3.513e-15 Hartree after eleven iterations. The sector gap is
37554.203236637666 Hartree, the metric defect is 3.331e-16 and the
embedding residual is 1.245e-13 Hartree.
The canonical CLI, native Python and ASE reproduce that LiH result,
energy terms and raw orbital residual within 3e-10 in atomic units.
ASE also passes the energy conversion with radii supplied in Angstrom.
The native omegaB97X-V result on the same geometry gives
-7.944384110647571 Hartree, bond-axis dipole -1.891291416091749 e Bohr
and raw orbital residual 1.449e-14 Hartree after eleven iterations.
Its self-consistent VV10 term is 0.01775398782810467 Hartree. The same
CLI, native Python and ASE value, term, residual, and unit gates pass
for this second LiH reference.

The same frozen source `b6c445edab23d5d0c19fa84716723765ba3716c125f59a4f03ea7c7ac8f4eaa7`
passes the direct positive-sector versus X2C test for hydrogen fluoride
at 1.7325 Bohr, with STO-3G and nuclear RMS radii (5.47e-5, 1.59e-5) Bohr.
Total and individual core, Coulomb, exchange, XC, VV10 and empirical
dispersion terms agree within 3e-10 Hartree. The four-component results
are:

| XC | Energy (Hartree) | Bond-axis dipole (e Bohr) | Orbital residual (Hartree) | SCF iterations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| omegaB97X-D | -98.99924199526464 | 0.487669844926456 | 4.932e-15 | 10 |
| omegaB97X-V | -98.98801233367452 | 0.479253540195953 | 4.746e-15 | 11 |

The CHG term is -5.934774364792494e-7 Hartree for omegaB97X-D and
the variational VV10 term is 0.04387666783982315 Hartree for
omegaB97X-V. The sector gap is 37523.84495003656 Hartree, the metric
defect 4.475e-16 and the embedding residual 2.584e-13 Hartree for both.
The Coulomb-only frozen build returns a named error and status 1 for an
explicitly requested Breit operator or UKS reference. Both additional
hydrogen-fluoride public interface replays pass. Full Cartesian finite-field
fits are in progress. Relativistic nuclear and magnetic derivatives,
open-shell references and periodic cells remain outside the validated coverage.

The candidate accepts `dirac_interaction` values `coulomb`, `gaunt` and
`breit`. For the two current interactions, the energy is the Coulomb
Kohn–Sham energy plus `Tr(P (J_current[P] - K_current[P]))/2`.
The explicit determinant term uses unit direct and exchange weights,
independent of the Coulomb hybrid coefficients. The XC provider continues
to evaluate its Coulomb functional. The same current integral contraction
acts on the trial density in the Fock and on the density variation in the
electric response. The energy report gives the signed current direct and
exchange contributions and the raw Hermiticity defect in Hartree.
This fixed-sector model uses the static two-electron current interaction.
Its first acceptance tests compare the no-pair HF limit, all static dipole
and polarizability entries in a C1 geometry and the public routes. The
current-dependent numerical gates are recorded separately from the
Coulomb results above.
[Two-electron Gaunt and Breit mean-field terms](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6CP01222A)

##### Uniform magnetic Dirac–Coulomb reference

With `dirac_integrals="london-rmb"` and `magnetic_field` in atomic units,
the nuclear-core positive sector follows the selected field. The
Hamiltonian and overlap, scalar Coulomb, full and range-separated
exchange, density gradients, kinetic density, current and electric
dipole all use the same London-RMB basis. The covariant basis gradient
uses the local vector potential after the orbital phase is
differentiated. VV10 uses the same magnetic density and gradient. The
finite-field driver reports the plane-wave truncation degree up to
eight. A phase refinement is required for substantial fields. The
field-dependent Gaunt and Breit vertices are pending.

At zero field on the C1 ammonia shell fixture used by R049, the full
four-component London direct and exchange matrices agree with the
original RKB matrices to `1.388e-17` and `2.776e-17 Hartree`. At
`B=(0.013,-0.019,0.011)` and `c=13.7`, the independent Fourier-Gaussian
pair integrals reproduce the energies of a fixed Hermitian large-component
density for full Coulomb and long-range `omega=0.32 Bohr^-1`. All 36
first and second energy derivative components pass steps
`[0.10,0.075,0.054,0.039]`, with `p=1.992587..1.999208`,
minimum `R^2=0.99999901` and `C=2.165e-6..7.718e-3`.
Fourth-order absolute defects at
`h=0.0038` are at most `5.638e-11` and `3.619e-11` in the corresponding
derivative units. This test differentiates the pair integrals at fixed
density. The coupled magnetic field susceptibility has a separate gate.

H₂/STO-3G at `[0.12,-0.24,0.31]` and `[1.45,0.06,-0.11] Bohr` with
physical c, radii `1.59e-5 Bohr`, `B=(0.004,-0.003,0.007)` and
phase order three gives `-1.1510387328111373 Hartree` for PBE
(grid level zero, zero weight cutoff) and `-1.1157723634845071
Hartree` for Dirac–Coulomb HF. Orbital residuals are
`8.725e-16` and `3.133e-16 Hartree`. The field-free Gaunt and Breit
public regressions continue to pass.

LiH with positions `[0.13,-0.22,0.14]` and `[2.91,0.48,-0.82] Bohr`,
Gaussian radii `[4.62e-5,1.59e-5] Bohr`, physical c, and a
normalized three-s Gaussian diagnostic basis (Li exponents 5.25,
0.1562 and H exponent 0.61) passes `omegaB97X-D` CLI, native Python and
ASE tests at `B=(0.0054,-0.0031,0.0078)` and phase degree three.
Its energy is `-5.705532236242765 Hartree`, dipole
`[-2.122174793414,-0.534360587979,0.732837326786] e Bohr`
and orbital residual `8.368e-14 Hartree`. The field-free limit is
`-5.705605907041192 Hartree`. Phases of degree three and four change
the energy by `-1.240e-10 Hartree`. Gauge-origin and field-sign replays
pass. This small basis verifies the field and API contracts.

The same LiH field, basis and charge-radius input with `omegaB97X-V`,
semilocal and VV10 grid levels both zero and zero weight cutoff, gives
`-5.664618673809680 Hartree`. Its VV10 energy is
`+0.0180344186417823 Hartree` and the dipole is
`[-2.090098333800,-0.526283754500,0.721760575129] e Bohr`.
The field-free energy is `-5.664694059136116 Hartree`. Degree-three
and degree-four phase energies differ by `-1.409e-10 Hartree`.
The orbital and pair Hermiticity residuals are `7.370e-13` and
`1.665e-16 Hartree`. The single CLI calculation uses 11 SCF steps and
72.67 s on one thread. Native Python, CLI, ASE atomic and physical-unit
results, the common-gauge replay and the field reversal all pass. The
complete parity test takes 491.43 s. Grid convergence is separate.
With the default VV10 grid level three the same public tests also pass.
That field energy is `-5.664592945373402 Hartree`, the field-free
energy is `-5.664668332675607 Hartree` and the dipole is
`[-2.090029980199,-0.526266543233,0.721736970978] e Bohr`.
Here the orbital residual is `7.359e-13 Hartree` and the phase
change is `-1.409e-10 Hartree`. The public suite with the default
nonlocal grid and both functionals takes 1553.21 s.

The finite Gaussian magnetization vertex uses
`A_mu=(mu cross grad_R(erf(omega*r)/r))/c^2` in the Dirac Hamiltonian
with its own nuclear magnetic RMS radius. An isolated normalized s
Gaussian (`alpha=0.849 Bohr^-2`, magnetic radius `0.354 Bohr`,
`c=11.7`) gives an atomic contact entry
`4.982538071596901e-3` in atomic magnetic moment units.
The independent radial formula matches all complex large-small,
small-large and uniform-field coefficients to `8.674e-19`.

The existing `dipole`, `polarizability`, `dynamic-polarizability`,
`quadrupole-polarizability` and `multipole-polarizability` entries select
the same molecular Dirac–Coulomb KS provider with
`relativistic_method="dirac"`. A shared dispatch selects the observable
once for Rust, the CLI, native Python and ASE. Unknown provider/property
combinations give a named unsupported error. Every electric source is
projected from large and small kinetic-balance components into the same
positive sector. One SCF density and kernel serve all sources in a request.

Quadrupole polarization returns Buckingham moments in e Bohr^2 and their
response to all five traceless electric field-gradient modes in
e^2 Bohr^4/Hartree. The dipole/gradient and field-conjugate-moment/dipole
blocks use e^2 Bohr^3/Hartree and report both orientations. Multiply the
field-conjugate moment response by three for the Buckingham scale.
`electric_field_gradient` supplies the five finite SCF perturbations in
Hartree/e/Bohr^2. The stationary energy adds the positive electron
operator and the negative nuclear source moment. The report provides
relative solve residuals for every source and the selected origin.
The base Dirac sector is generated at zero field. The retarded response
uses the same stationarity kernel with its signed frequency and damping.
General harmonic modes reuse the same projection and support Racah ranks
one through five. The C1 static finite-field fits and retarded LiH
interface checks are staged.

##### Four-component indirect nuclear spin coupling

`spin-spin-couplings` with `relativistic_method="dirac"` takes an
explicit Gaussian magnetic RMS radius in Bohr per atom. The source
moments have unit Hartree per atomic unit of magnetic field. The
nuclear-core positive sector follows the nuclear magnetic sources in
the fixed AO basis at the selected uniform field. Its analytic first
and second coefficients include the negative-energy complement. The
variational KS density responds within that sector. The report gives the
electronic indirect coupling, its explicit-sector and orbital-relaxation
tensors, and raw sector, stationarity and response residuals. Optional
g factors give isotropic J in Hz. The independent SCF energy oracle uses
`nuclear_magnetic_moments` and `nuclear_magnetic_rms_radii` on
`dirac-dks`.

The C1 hydrogen dimer uses HF/STO-3G with test `c=6.8`, charge RMS radii
`[0.09,0.083,0.075,0.088] Bohr` and magnetic radii
`[0.08,0.10,0.115,0.094] Bohr`. For the pair [0,2] the analytic tensor is
`[[-0.001677908516508,0.000146959718728,0.000083949919141],
[0.000172082546387,-0.001762300418459,0.000172608415186],
[0.000108585661616,0.000182466615199,-0.001868329792884]]` in atomic
coupling units. Its sector metric, sector operator and largest coupled
residuals are `1.998e-15`, `2.710e-15 Hartree` and `5.018e-12`.
Independent reconverged mixed-field energy differences pass all nine
components at `[0.32,0.24,0.16,0.12]` with
`p=1.973476..1.979118`, minimum `R^2=0.99998859` and
`C=1.195e-5..3.180e-4`. The separate absolute gate of `2e-9`
initially fails with a fourth-order error of `5.37881187e-9` at
`h=0.06`. The same stencil at `h=0.035` gives `6.24426630e-10`.
Error reduction by a factor of 8.614 agrees with the fourth-order
prediction 8.636.

The full Breit and two-component matrix above retains its pending

T189 connects a molecular fixed-picture SCF with exact one-electron X2C,
second-order Douglas–Kroll–Hess and finite-basis matrix ZORA. The X2C
electronic projector is anchored to the orthonormal large-component chart
by its positive polar factor. A covariant operator is changed to
`B† O B` and the contravariant density is lifted with `B P B†`.
The Sylvester recurrence for the principal metric square root and the
whole-sector projector retain factorial-normalized coefficients through
order four. [Kutzelnigg and Liu](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2137315)

DKH2 expands the free-particle rotated core through second order in the
external nuclear potential. Its approximate transformed orbitals use
the normalized graph through that order. Matrix ZORA eliminates the
small coefficients with the electron energy set to zero in the
denominator and uses normalized restored spinors for property and
density operators. The finite-basis inverse differs from quadrature of
the reciprocal local potential. The unscaled ZORA core and its restored
spinors have different metric conventions, recorded by the raw
`decoupling_residual`. [Reiher and Wolf](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1818681)
[Matrix regular approximation](https://pure.rug.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/67391170/1.1844298.pdf)

All three routes use the same lifted density for the balanced Coulomb
operator, full and erf long-range exchange, and the semilocal density,
gradient, kinetic density and current descriptors. The resolved provider
supplies its required nonlocal terms. VV10 uses the lifted total charge
and charge gradient variationally, and CHG contributes a classical
geometry-only energy. Static and retarded electric response use the
same Fock kernel and the field-free picture. The permanent dipole
includes the classical finite Gaussian charges. Numerical acceptance
for the first molecular tests is in progress.

### R076 multicomponent-nuclear-positron-photon-dft

The nonrelativistic molecular driver now routes signed `frequencies` and

position-constraint rows act on the time-even amplitudes. The report

per driven field. Zero frequency is included in the comparison with the

### R080 molecular-medium-optics

- **Status**: Electric dipole constitutive and anisotropic slab models connected, including the first-order orbital Faraday dielectric for a weak magnetic bias.
- **Scope**: Homogeneous slab with an explicit molecular number density, line width, thickness, orientation and lossless isotropic exterior indices.
- **Entry**: `driver::run(molecular-medium-optics)` and `response::medium_optics`
- **Tests**: `src/response/medium_optics/tests.rs`, `p315_molecular_medium_optics`, `p316_causal_magneto_optics`, `python/tests/test_molecular_medium_optics.py`

The molecular retarded electric dipole tensor is evaluated at positive photon
energy with the requested imaginary shift in the frequency. An explicit proper orthogonal orientation
rotates it into slab axes. The default orientation is an isotropic average.
For number density N in Bohr⁻³ and atomic polarizability alpha, the dilute
model has relative permittivity I + 4 pi N alpha. The Lorentz cavity solves
(I − 4 pi N alpha / 3) P = N alpha E for the macroscopic polarization.
The reported local-field residual is the largest absolute entry of this
equation in dimensionless susceptibility form.

The slab normal is +z and the incidence plane is xz. The field convention is
exp(−i omega t), with unit relative permeability. The normal-axis indices
are the square roots of the transverse dielectric eigenvalues after
eliminating the normal electric field. The corresponding intensity
attenuation coefficients are 2 omega Im(n) / c. Tangential electric and
magnetic fields match across each interface. A scaled Maxwell propagator
is composed in scattering form for oblique incidence, including evanescent
exit waves. Jones rows and columns are outgoing and incoming s and p
amplitudes. Positive s and p amplitudes have positive tangential E_y and
E_x in both propagation directions. Power reflectance, transmittance and
absorptance are returned per incident polarization. The largest interface
and scattering connection solve residual and the exterior flux balance
are reported separately.
[Anisotropic Maxwell propagator](https://web.njit.edu/~sirenko/SiMM_web/Bereman%20Original%20Propagator.pdf)

Required controls are `frequency`, `medium_number_density` and
`slab_thickness`. Optional controls are `frequency_damping`,
`medium_local_field` (Lorentz or dilute), `medium_orientation`,
`incidence_angle` and the two exterior refractive indices.
The optional `medium_magnetic_field` is a slab-axis vector in atomic units.
The driver carries the molecular response model and residuals alongside
the medium diagnostics. The magnetic model adds the causal molecular
d alpha / dB contracted with the bias to the electric polarizability
before the local-field solve. Aligned molecules rotate the rank-three
tensor and isotropic orientation uses its axial Haar average. Independent
boundary solutions at opposite biases give the odd part of the reflected
ellipse orientation and ellipticity in radians. The circular Stokes term
is twice the imaginary part of the conjugated co-polar amplitude times
the cross-polar amplitude. The angles are undefined
at zero reflected intensity, and the orientation is undefined for a
circular reflected state. The bulk permeability, electric–magnetic
constitutive tensors, spatial dispersion and higher bias powers of the
molecular susceptibility remain open. The magnetic slab path inherits the
orbital Faraday reference and functional capabilities. The molecular
spin-orbit tensor has its own response entry.

Four standalone kernel tests pass the scalar Lorentz closed form, oblique
isotropic Fresnel and Airy formulas, rotated anisotropic mode mixing with a
longitudinal field, thick absorbing layers and evanescent exit waves.
The isotropic Lorentz fixture has relative permittivity
1.260833543806665 + 0.025879111092678 i and two equal indices
1.122927568719866 + 0.011523054475446 i. The local-field equation
residual is zero at printed precision. The oblique isotropic film
has s/p reflectance (0.040193055829223, 0.013207111567559) and
transmittance (0.959806944170767, 0.986792888432439). Its maximum
exterior flux residual is 1.952e-16. A fifth kernel test agrees with independent circular-channel Fresnel
reflection from a gyrotropic half space. The s/p Kerr rotations are
(+0.008315320609264, -0.008315320609265) rad and the ellipticity angles
are (+0.042383547052898, -0.042383547052898) rad. The maximum exterior
flux residual is 1.111e-16.

A clean-installed wheel passes the H2/HF aligned dielectric case through
the CLI, native Python and ASE atomic and physical units. The normal
complex indices are (1.007739570148546 + 1.679792443665252e-5 i, 1).
The s/p reflectances are (0.035570332409975, 0.018942954815116)
and transmittances (0.964429667590027, 0.981055523528983).
The largest exterior flux, boundary and molecular response residuals
are 2.329e-16, 1.571e-16 and 2.427e-16. The magnetic molecular and
standalone Rust SCF-to-slab integration cases have separate gates.

### R081 relativistic-quantum-nuclear-response

- **Status**: public fixed-sector Dirac-Coulomb HF energy, uniform-electric dipole and static/retarded response for distinguishable quantum nuclei have validated subsets.
- **Scope**: Finite-nucleus relativistic electronic and selected quantum nuclear sectors with compatible ECP and external fields.
- **Entry**: multicomponent, `multicomponent::relativistic::JointNoPairSystem::solve`, `multicomponent::relativistic::JointNoPairModel::solve`
- **Tests**: `balanced_quantum_coulomb_reciprocity_convolution_and_all_centre_fits`, `joint_no_pair_coulomb_scf_matches_independent_variational_energy`, `joint_no_pair_coulomb_two_electrons_and_two_quantum_nuclei`

Reuse balanced Dirac integrals and the differentiated electronic-sector
projector from R075 and the multicomponent variational residual and
perturbation assembly from R076. The joint model needs a common energy
with transformed electronic density and coupled particle response.

`integrals::dirac::electron_quantum_coulomb` supplies the field-free
electron–quantum-nucleus Coulomb coupling for a complex four-component
electronic density and a real nuclear density. It accumulates both
potential matrices from the same shell quartet and retains the scalar
and spin terms of the kinetically balanced small components. A finite
intrinsic nuclear radius convolves the nuclear density with a Gaussian.
The routine reports both contractions and their raw difference.

In `balanced_quantum_coulomb_reciprocity_convolution_and_all_centre_fits`,
the two contractions both give -0.6471486781352320 Hartree and their
difference is 0. The small-component contribution is
-0.0009815874699008421 Hartree. An independent finite Gaussian attraction
matches the total and checks inverse-square speed-of-light scaling of
the small-component term. All nine centre gradients and all 18 mixed
electronic/nuclear centre derivatives pass the four steps
(0.06, 0.04, 0.03, 0.02) Bohr. Exponents span 1.910294 to 2.022696,
minimum R2 is 0.99974651 and prefactors span 1.407e-4 to 1.640e-1.
The fixed-sector `NoPairSpace` and `NoPairBackend` now lift the trial
density to the full balanced basis and project its variational Fock
back into the positive-energy sector. The generating one-electron
operator fixes that sector throughout the SCF. With a supplied
electronic energy provider and a prepared real nuclear core and metric,
`multicomponent::relativistic::JointNoPairModel::solve` alternates the
complex electronic SCF with a normalized orbital solve for one
distinguishable quantum nucleus. Both species use the same Coulomb
energy. The inner electronic residual, nuclear orbital and density
residuals, particle-number defects, reciprocity and projection
residuals are exposed at the stationary point.

The one-electron finite-Gaussian fixture uses c=11.7 in atomic units,
nuclear mass 19 electron masses and a specified spin splitting to
isolate the occupied level. It converges in 21 iterations at
-0.1454781795735447 Hartree. The independent Gaussian-product
attraction and nuclear orbital minimization gives
-0.1454781795735448 Hartree. The electronic one-species, nuclear
one-body and interspecies Coulomb terms are -0.2172762921946986,
0.6968569662810105 and -0.6250588536598564 Hartree. The electronic
and nuclear orbital residuals are 2.090e-16 and 3.356e-12 Hartree.
The nuclear density residual is 2.960e-11. The raw reciprocity and
projection residuals are 2.220e-16 and -2.220e-16 Hartree.
These values come from the Windows test harness compiling the new
modules against the existing SCF and integral library.

`multicomponent::relativistic::JointNoPairSystem::solve` accepts a
slice of prepared quantum nuclei and applies the same SCF through
the single-nucleus compatibility entry. Each nuclear pair is evaluated
once with both intrinsic Gaussian charge variances and supplies both
conjugate potentials. The electronic–nuclear and nuclear–nuclear terms
each enter the common energy once. The tests include all six
independent nuclear-pair density derivative components against
closed-form Gaussian products on (0.06, 0.04, 0.03, 0.02).
Exponents round to 2.000000, minimum R2 rounds to 1.00000000 and
prefactors span 0.2074 to 0.4001.

The prepared two-electron, two-quantum-nucleus fixture uses the full
scalar Dirac–Coulomb HF provider, c=11.7 atomic units and quantum masses
19 and 27 electron masses. It converges in 25 iterations at
-0.3930746099982820 Hartree. Exchanging the two nuclei in the input
reproduces the energy and permutes their density matrices. Electronic,

The uniform electric field keeps the same fixed projector and uses

### R082 molecular-magnetic-quadrupole

- **Status**: bounded models connected; zero-bias UKS NO2 strict-unit and origin covariance checks pass; finite-bias GKS omegaB97X-D ammonia passes all five modes
- **Scope**: Electronic symmetric-traceless tensor Q = -dE/dG for a source-free field B(r) = B0 + G(r-O). The common Poincaré gauge uses A = (B0 cross r)/2 + ((G r) cross r)/3 with r measured from O. Includes orbital and g=2 Pauli spin terms and the current-invariant meta-GGA convention.
- **Entry**: `driver::run(magnetic-quadrupole)`, `dft-rs magnetic-quadrupole`, `magnetic_quadrupole`, `get_magnetic_quadrupole`
- **Tests**: `tests/magnetic_quadrupole.rs`, `python/tests/test_molecular_methods.py`

Target T178. Orbital, spin and total magnetic quadrupoles, magnetic dipole and raw SCF residual. Magnetic quantities use atomic units. Origin defaults to the centre of mass in Bohr. Connected zero-bias RKS/UKS/ROKS and finite-bias GKS all-electron moments. At changed expansion origin the spin tensor mixes with the spin dipole, and finite common-gauge basis orbital values retain gauge dependence. ECP and PT2 magnetic-gradient operators are pending.

The five reported mode components use normalized Cartesian matrices. The
diagonal modes are proportional to `diag(1,-1,0)` and `diag(1,1,-2)`; the
remaining modes are symmetric xy, xz and yz matrices. The finite-bias
orbital derivative includes both the linear momentum operator and
`A_bias dot A_mode`. The spin tensor transforms under an origin change by
subtracting the symmetric-traceless projection of the outer product of
the magnetic dipole and origin displacement.

### R083 constrained-density-functional-theory

- **Status**: C1 ammonia RKS multiplier fits, omegaB97X-D and omegaB97X-V water fragment gradients, and omegaB97X-D relaxation and static electric fits pass. The repaired omegaB97X-V static electric fits remain open.
- **Scope**: Charge and spin constraints on variational integer determinants with explicit AO operators or symmetrized Mulliken fragment projectors. The dual uses L = E + sum lambda (Q - target) and an analytic multiplier Jacobian. Moving projectors supply analytic nuclear forces and the multiplier response keeps populations fixed under static electric perturbations.

- **Tests**: `tests/constrained_dft.rs`, `src/scf/constrained_tests.rs`, `python/tests/test_molecular_methods.py`

Target T185. Physical energy, dual Lagrangian, multipliers in Hartree,

in inverse Hartree. The common route also assembles first nuclear
derivatives and static electric response of the constrained determinant.
The variational correlated PT2 density and its constrained derivatives

The locally built current CLI and Python extension pass native Python,

omegaB97X-D and omegaB97X-V. The same eight-case test also covers
