Each `density_constraints` object takes `target` and either `atoms` with
`kind=population` or `kind=spin-z`, or an explicit AO matrix
`operator_alpha` and optional `operator_beta`. A GKS request additionally
supports `spin-x` and `spin-y` fragment operators and Hermitian full spin/AO
matrices `operator_real` and `operator_imaginary`. Atom and orbital indices
start at zero. The fixed-geometry operators are dimensionless. Dependent
or unreachable constraints and a nonconcave multiplier response raise a
named diagnostic. The derivative of physical constrained energy with
respect to the target is minus the converged multiplier.

For fragment populations, `electrons` is an alias for the target
expectation. A single `atoms` list may span any number of atoms. The
projector is `(WS + SW)/2`, where `W` selects the fragment AOs and
`S` is the current AO overlap. For `gradient=true`, the biased SCF
supplies the Pulay term and the explicit projector derivative is
contracted with its converged multiplier and charge or spin density.
Explicit matrix operators are treated as constant AO coefficients
in the moving basis. `optimize_geometry=true` uses the same
gradient in molecular L-BFGS,
rebuilding and solving the constraints at each trial geometry.
`constraint_electric_response=true` holds the targets fixed under
the electric perturbation. The collinear response uses the Schur
complement of the multiplier susceptibility and the full spinor
response projects out the constraint directions in the orbital solve.

### R084 car-parrinello-molecular-dynamics

- **Status**: real-reference water trajectories, off-shell C1 derivatives and installed parity pass. The GKS trajectory and its independent component tests are connected
- **Scope**: Microcanonical propagation of nuclear coordinates and occupied electronic orbitals in the instantaneous symmetric Löwdin frame. The fictitious electronic kinetic energy uses the Euclidean coefficient metric in that frame. RATTLE enforces orthonormality and tangent velocity. The analytic moving metric contributes to the off-shell nuclear force.

Target T186. Trajectory, forces, both kinetic energies, extended energy
drift and constraint defects. Time and velocities are atomic units.
Masses are electron masses, positions Bohr and energies Hartree.
Real RKS/UKS/ROKS trajectories have executed acceptance. The complex
GKS route uses the same integrator with Hermitian constraints, a
full-spin Fock and an explicit moving-AO derivative plus the
Löwdin metric covector. Distorted-water GKS trajectories pass for
omegaB97X-D and omegaB97X-V. Their initial energies are
-75.31979238771551 and -75.30181515450867 Hartree, their maximum

are 4.448419153868510e-9 and 4.299094635840106e-9 Hartree/Bohr.
The independent complex off-shell component sweep remains open.
Correlated off-shell PT2 forces,
thermostats and alternative kinetic metrics remain open.

The electronic coordinates are the occupied columns of `Q` with AO
coefficients `C=S^(-1/2)Q`. Nuclear gradients at fixed `Q` include the
matrix-function derivative of the symmetric orthogonalizer. The SCF
initializes `Q`; its fictitious velocity is initially zero. One common
frame is propagated for RKS and ROKS, and separate frames for UKS.
The propagator reuses the molecular density/Fock and analytic gradient
assemblies. Its off-stationary overlap term belongs to the moving
Lowdin frame. The trajectory driver owns that state and propagation.
`md_timestep`, `md_steps` and `fictitious_mass` specify the integrator.
`nuclear_velocities` defaults to zero and `nuclear_masses` to standard
atomic weights in electron-mass units.

### R085 near-edge-xray-absorption-fine-structure

- **Status**: bounded CVS-TDA and per-hole relaxed-ion models connected; eight RKS water spectra and polarization/broadening checks pass, broader references and installed parity pending
- **Scope**: Polarization-resolved finite-basis electric dipole absorption with explicit occupied spin orbital lists or K-edge absorber indices. CVS-TDA evaluates unshifted response poles. The relaxed-core-ion model solves one ion per selected spin/core hole and uses its virtual energies and a projected, nonorthogonal determinant transition dipole.
- **Entry**: `driver::run(nexafs)`, `dft-rs nexafs`, `nexafs`, `get_nexafs`
- **Tests**: `tests/nexafs.rs`, `python/tests/test_molecular_methods.py`

Target T187. Lines and Cartesian oscillator-strength tensors, Gaussian or Lorentzian spectrum and core-hole tracking residuals. Energies and full widths are Hartree, dipoles e Bohr and oscillator density inverse Hartree. Connected collinear all-electron CVS-TDA and per-hole relaxed-ion models. Complete continuum, spin-orbit-split edges, state-specific neutral relaxation, common-orbital and spinor response remain open.

The relaxed-ion threshold and virtual orbital energies come from the
same hole calculation. No separate frozen-orbital correction is added.
The empty orbital that most strongly overlaps the selected initial core
orbital is excluded as the refill state, and both its overlap and the
occupied-space tracking weights are reported. The determinant transition
moment is projected against the initial state so a shift of the electric
dipole origin cancels. For a unit polarization `e`, the strength is
`e^T (2 omega d d^T) e`; isotropic strength is one third of the trace.

The molecular checks use explicitly prescribed, unoptimized geometries.
The water O K-edge fixture has O at the origin and H coordinates
`(1.809,0,0)` and `(-0.452,1.752,0)` Bohr, representing the approximate
gas-phase bond length and angle. STO-3G and 6-31G are finite orbital
bases without a continuum representation. The spectrum test measures
line energies, normalized polarization projections, integrated Gaussian
oscillator density and translated relaxed-ion determinant strengths.

The water test passed both models for wB97X-D/STO-3G and 6-31G, and
wB97X-V and wB97M-V/STO-3G. Grid levels were 0 and weight cutoffs were
zero. The first CVS lines span `19.0521962..19.1711375` Hartree and
the first relaxed-core-ion lines `19.7283482..19.8603379` Hartree.
The total isotropic oscillator strengths span `0.1134167..0.4015254`.
The largest raw projected TDA residual was `2.0766e-14` Hartree and
the largest core-ion occupation-selection residual `7.5328e-10`.
The smallest reported occupied-subspace tracking weight was
`0.9412630872`. The 6-31G basis substantially increases the integrated
strength relative to STO-3G. These levels document finite-basis model
behavior and basis sensitivity.

### R087 molecular DFT+U

- **Status**: fixed-geometry molecular Hubbard energy and stationarity connected for integer RKS, UKS, ROKS and complex GKS
- **Scope**: The variational site correction enters the reference energy and Fock. Fixed-projector Hubbard kernels are available for the real collinear and complex spinor occupations. Moving-projector derivatives, periodic cells, correlated parents and property-level Hubbard response remain open.
- **Entry**: `driver::run("dft-plus-u", ...)`, `scf::hubbard::run_collinear`, `scf::hubbard::run_roks`, `HubbardModel::evaluate_spinor`, `HubbardModel::response_spinor`
- **Tests**: `tests/hubbard.rs`, `tests/hubbard_spinor.rs`, `python/tests/test_strong_correlation.py`

Target T190. Each `hubbard_sites` entry contains ordered, zero-based spherical
AO indices in `orbitals`. All interaction parameters use Hartree. An AO may
occur in only one site. Site AOs are symmetrically orthogonalized within the
site and retain overlaps with other sites. For AO overlap `S` and site
indices `I`, the reported spin occupations are `W^T P_s W` in electrons,
where `W = S[:,I] (S[I,I])^(-1/2)`. This choice makes the correction
dependent on the specified correlated subspace and basis.

Optional `hubbard_pairs` entries add intersite terms to this driver. A pair
gives two distinct zero-based entries in `hubbard_sites` as `sites` and
one coupling as `v`. Specify each unordered pair once. The molecular
fixed-projector implementation evaluates
`-V_IJ sum_s ||W_I^T P_s W_J||_F^2` for collinear references and includes
all spin blocks in the spinor norm. The Fock and fixed-projector kernel
differentiate the same quadratic energy. The report gives each pair's
interaction, double counting and net correction, plus the sum as
`hubbard_intersite_energy`. Native inputs use Hartree. Default ASE input
units convert pair `v` from eV. Independent component and public acceptance
for the new path are tracked separately from the on-site tests below.
[Campo and Cococcioni](https://doi.org/10.1088/0953-8984/22/5/055602)

- A Dudarev entry has `model="dudarev"` (the default) and `u_eff`.
  Its site `interaction` is the combined term
  `u_eff/2 sum_s Tr(n_s - n_s^2)`. The separate `double_counting` field is zero.
  [Dudarev et al.](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.57.1505)
- A Liechtenstein entry has `model="liechtenstein"`, fully localized
  limit averages `u` and `j`, and the complete real chemists' Coulomb tensor
  `integrals` in row-major `(a,b,c,d)` order in the orthogonalized site basis.
  The caller specifies a consistent tensor and averages. The reported
  `interaction` contains projected direct and same-spin exchange terms.
  Its `double_counting` is
  `u N(N-1)/2 - j sum_s N_s(N_s-1)/2`.
  [Liechtenstein et al.](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.52.R5467)

For GKS the same spatial projector acts on every block of the complex
spinor density. The site output gives `occupations_real` and
`occupations_imaginary` in spin-major order and in electrons. Dudarev
uses `u_eff/2 Tr(n - n^2)` over the full spin-site matrix. Liechtenstein
contracts the same input tensor with the spin-traced direct density and
with every exchange spin block. Its spin-covariant fully localized
double counting is `u N(N-1)/2 - j (Tr(T^2) - N)/2`, where
`T_st = sum_a n_(sa,ta)` and `N = Tr(T)`. Global spin rotations transform
the site potential with the density and preserve the energy. The complex
SCF report gives a separate Hubbard contribution and the raw spinor
orbital residual in Hartree.
[Binci and Marzari](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.108.115157)
[Bousquet and Spaldin](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.82.220402)
[Ryee and Han](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-27731-4)

The total `hubbard_energy` is the sum of site interaction energies minus
double counting and is included in the electronic and total energies.
The ordinary parent dispersion and SMD terms use the shared additive
energy path. `scf_orbital_residual` in Hartree is the maximum absolute physical
Fock-density commutator in the final MO frame for RKS/UKS. For ROKS it is
the raw common-orbital residual in the closed, open and virtual frame.

The warning-strict release run passes all three Hubbard tests. The fixed
AO-density derivative tests use a nonsymmetric noncoplanar H4 geometry,
STO-3G, and grid weight cutoff zero. The independent scalar oracle uses
a closed-form two-by-two metric inverse square root and expanded
polynomials for the direct, exchange and double-counting energies.
All 20 Fock and 400 ordered density-kernel entries per model pass on
`[0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01]` in density coordinates, with
`p=2.000580` and minimum `R²=0.99999998`. The oracle chart has unit
tangent and an independent cubic term. This gives a finite error for
the identically zero mixed-spin Dudarev entries without changing
the derivative at the origin. The fitted coefficient ranges
are `[0.02736, 0.4369]` for Dudarev and `[0.01634, 0.2905]`
for Liechtenstein. All four zero-U results agree with their respective
ordinary parent energies. Setting J to zero and using the isotropic
Coulomb tensor also recovers the Dudarev energy and potential.

### R088 molecular PZ-SIC

- **Status**: real integer UKS fixed-geometry orbital minimization implemented
- **Scope**: Parent electronic energy and each occupied orbital's self-Hartree and self-XC terms use shared integral and XC providers. Occupied–occupied and occupied–virtual stationarity are both tested in the solver. Other reference manifolds, complex orbitals, descriptor optimization and physical response remain open.
- **Entry**: `driver::run("pz-sic", ...)`, `scf::sic::run_pz`
- **Tests**: `src/scf/sic_tests.rs`, `python/tests/test_strong_correlation.py`

Target T191. For each occupied orbital in each spin, the solver subtracts
the Hartree and XC energies of its normalized one-electron density. It
retains the parent's full- and long-range exact exchange, semilocal and
VV10 terms in the subtraction. Independent orthogonal rotations optimize
both spin orbital frames from the parent UKS determinant. The largest
absolute derivative with respect to a rotation is the raw residual in
Hartree. A converged result is a local stationary point in the real
unrestricted manifold. [Perdew and Zunger](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.23.5048)

In the canonical CLI at STO-3G, grid level 0, weight cutoff zero,
the H2+ one-electron limit is `-0.5782730664298588` Hartree.
wB97X-D with its empirical tail disabled and wB97X-V with
its defining VV10 term both reproduce the one-electron orbital
Hamiltonian limit within `1.2e-16` Hartree. Their orbital residuals
are `1.2350e-17` Hartree, and their self-interaction corrections
are `+0.010383557047673` and `+0.006324970314035` Hartree. The
wB97X-V one-electron self-XC includes `+0.004578204637200` Hartree
from VV10. JSON units and stderr iteration logging pass.
Rebuilt native Python, CLI and ASE agree within `1e-10` Hartree
for the two H2+ energies, corrections and residuals. The default
ASE mode also passes the eV conversions at their stated tolerances.

The optimized test build passes all ten independent occupied–occupied
and occupied–virtual orbital-gradient components for a nonsymmetric
noncoplanar H4 PBE/STO-3G fixture, grid level 0 and weight cutoff zero.
The independent oracle rotates each pair with a trigonometric rotation
and contracts its rank-one densities directly. The first four-step
interval `[0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005]` radians passes unchanged.
The fitted exponent is `1.948419..2.004521`, minimum `R²=0.99951585`,
and prefactor interval `[5.123e-4, 2.999e-2]`.

The initial multielectron scan gives `-7.93475162449544` Hartree
for LiH with wB97X-D/STO-3G and orbital residual `9.4703e-6`
Hartree after 41 iterations at the `1e-5` gate. At the same gate,
the unpreconditioned distorted NH3 wB97X-D/STO-3G calculation
ends iteration 150 at residual `7.227e-2` Hartree. Its orbital
objective starts at `-55.371087038379` and ends at
`-55.533252114353` Hartree. All steps decrease the objective.
The last ten reduce it by `0.002907709279` Hartree. The failure
is orbital stationarity while the objective is still decreasing.

With the same geometry, parent and stopping conditions, using current
parent orbital gaps for occupied–virtual rotations and smaller
curvature for occupied rotations gives a residual of `9.945e-4`
Hartree at iteration 50, compared with `8.794e-2` Hartree without
the preconditioner. The calculation reaches iteration 140 with
raw orbital residual `8.91467712726605e-6` Hartree. The orbital
objective is `-55.543980998159` Hartree. The reported total is
`-55.5440506149571` Hartree including `-6.96167985436179e-5`
Hartree empirical dispersion. The self-interaction correction
at the final orbitals is `+0.207590267884441` Hartree.
The complete iteration histories and binary hashes were retained
with the private numerical audit.

Preconditioned LiH/STO-3G at the `1e-5` Hartree orbital gate
gives `-7.934751624562014` Hartree in 29 iterations for wB97X-D,
with residual `6.9862e-6` Hartree. Its total differs from the
unpreconditioned value by `6.6574e-11` Hartree. With wB97X-V and
its defining VV10, the LiH total is `-7.9492816799889185` Hartree
in 28 iterations with residual `8.2596e-6` Hartree.

#### Fixed-descriptor Fermi-Lowdin SIC

Target T192 uses a converged real integer UKS determinant on a fixed
molecular geometry. Each `fod_alpha` or `fod_beta` row is one Cartesian
Fermi-orbital descriptor in Bohr. Supply one row per occupied orbital
in that spin channel. The AO spin density is preserved when the
normalized Fermi orbitals are symmetrically orthogonalized. The
existing PZ self-energy evaluator supplies each localized orbital's
self-Hartree, exact exchange, semilocal XC and explicit VV10 terms.
The geometry-only dispersion is applied once outside the orbital
subtraction. [Fermi-Lowdin construction](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4869581)

The report separates the parent orbital residual in Hartree from the
dimensionless occupied and localized metric defects and the AO density
defect. Descriptor spin densities use electrons/Bohr³. The independent
two-orbital case had a maximum coefficient deviation of `5.5511e-17`,
an occupied-frame rotation deviation of `1.1102e-16` and a metric
residual of `3.3307e-16`. Rust H₂⁺ and distorted H₄ and public H₂⁺
tests are tracked separately from the new optimization and complex routes.
On the frozen fixed-descriptor public routes, H₂⁺/STO-3G with grid level
zero and zero weight cutoff gives `-0.5758728702150192 Hartree` for
wB97X-D and `-0.5758716156232605 Hartree` for wB97X-V. The respective
SIC corrections are `+0.009739532476444879` and
`+0.005722317545749492 Hartree`, and parent orbital residuals
`1.882e-16` and `1.591e-16 Hartree`. The canonical CLI, native Python
and atomic ASE match within the predefined `1e-10 Hartree` gate.

`fod_gradient=true` evaluates the analytic derivative of the energy with
respect to each descriptor at a fixed occupied subspace. The localized AO
orbital derivative is contracted with its own self-interaction potential.
The derivative of the Löwdin factor uses a polar-decomposition Sylvester
equation whose denominators are sums of positive singular values. This
avoids eigenvector derivatives in degenerate positive eigenspaces.
`fod_optimize=true` applies L-BFGS to the correction with the parent
subspace fixed. `flo_self_consistent=true` also rotates the occupied
subspace against the virtual orbitals. Its orbital residual includes the
parent Fock matrix, the individual localized-orbital SIC potentials and
the derivative of the localized orbitals through the occupied subspace
in the descriptor values. The two raw residuals are reported separately
as `flo_orbital_residual` in Hartree and `fod_gradient_max` in Hartree/Bohr.
[Self-consistent variational framework](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.95.052505)

All 12 real FOD components of the C1 H₄ PBE/UKS/STO-3G calculation
pass independently displaced energy comparisons, grid level zero
and zero weight cutoff. For steps `[0.012,0.008,0.005,0.003] bohr`,
the fitted `p` ranges from `1.973836965` to `2.000418964`,
minimum `R^2=0.999967686` and `C=7.21449e-6..2.05697e-3`.
The maximum fourth-order central discrepancy at `0.002 bohr` is
`3.186e-13 Hartree/bohr`. The base energy is
`-2.213702365504417 Hartree`. FOD-only relaxation reaches
`-2.2140054948454155 Hartree` and a `5.666e-7 Hartree/bohr`
residual in three iterations at the `1e-6 Hartree/bohr` threshold.
The first joint search lowers the energy to `-2.2148620567683617 Hartree`
but reaches its 200-cycle limit with orbital and descriptor residuals of
`1.509e-4 Hartree` and `1.299e-4 Hartree/bohr`. Alternating descriptor
L-BFGS minimization and updates from the occupied–virtual SIC residual
converges in nine cycles and 35 evaluations at the same `1e-6`
thresholds. The final energy is `-2.214866064776698 Hartree`, with
orbital residual `6.407326e-8 Hartree` and descriptor residual
`5.450993e-7 Hartree/bohr`.

Supply `fod_alpha_imaginary` and/or `fod_beta_imaginary` for the complex
descriptor evaluator. It analytically continues the Gaussian AOs, applies
an exponent offset shared within each descriptor and performs the same
Löwdin calculation in a real embedding with a measured consistency defect.
The orbital density used for the self-energies is
`Re(c_i c_i^H)` in the real AO basis; single-orbital exact exchange uses
the corresponding self-Coulomb integral. The complex FOD gradient contains
three real-coordinate components followed by three imaginary-coordinate
components. The fixed-parent optimizer supports both sets of coordinates.
An imaginary starting displacement can explore the complex branch.
The reported descriptor densities are logarithms relative to
`1/bohr^3`. Fully self-consistent complex orbital optimization and other
reference families remain pending. The N₂ PBE/UKS/STO-3G public-route
test at `2.072 bohr`, grid level one and zero weight cutoff, passes the
zero-imaginary limit and compares the nonzero-imaginary case across CLI,
native Python and ASE in atomic and physical units. The real and complex
descriptor energies are `-107.902568100057` and `-107.922767684161 Hartree`,
respectively. The complex correction is `+0.00335177421450994 Hartree`
and the maximum AO density defect is `1.5543e-15`. The eight FLO-SIC Rust
unit tests also pass. For the C1 H₄ complex descriptor test, all 24 real
and imaginary derivatives pass over `[0.012,0.008,0.005,0.003] bohr`
with `p=1.999059..2.033423`, minimum `R^2=0.99995694` and
`C=1.115e-5..4.938e-3`. The corresponding energy is
`-2.213622334017 Hartree`, with AO-density defect `1.665e-16`.
All eight real occupied–virtual derivatives also pass over the
same dimensionless rotation steps with `p=1.978885..2.003080`,
minimum `R^2=0.99997219` and `C=1.836e-2..8.148e-2`.
[Complex descriptors](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0091212)

The independent algebra check uses three complex descriptors, Gaussian
point values and distinct orbital-specific quadratic energies. A complex
SVD supplies the displaced Löwdin factors. All 18 real and imaginary
components pass the four steps `[0.008,0.004,0.002,0.001]`, with
`p=1.99725759..2.00054832`, minimum `R^2=0.999999548` and largest
Richardson discrepancy `1.562e-10`. This is separate from the molecular

### R090 Molecular IGMH

- **Status**: Molecular SCF point and affine-grid fields connected. Spatial derivatives, four public reference cases and an explicit two-functional mixture verified.
- **Entry**: `driver::run(igmh)`, `properties::igmh::analyze`.
- **Tests**: `tests/p329_igmh.rs`, `python/tests/test_igmh.py`, `python/tests/test_igmh_visualization.py`.

IGMH samples the converged spin-summed density `rho`. The neutral
proatom density `rho_A_free` comes from the existing spherical atomic HF
SAD in the molecular basis. The weight is `w_A = rho_A_free / sum_B rho_B_free`.
The published map convention uses `v_A = w_A grad(rho) - rho grad(w_A)`
as defined in the erratum. With `igmh_gradient=hirshfeld`, the sign of the
second term is positive and `v_A` is the derivative of `w_A rho` itself.
[Original article](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.26812).
[Authors' erratum](https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-g1m34).

The total field is the sum of norms of the atomic vectors less the norm
of their sum. The interfragment field groups vectors by fragment before
taking norms. The intrafragment field is the sum of atomic norms less the
sum of fragment norms. With no assignment, all atoms share one
fragment. The colouring field is `sign(lambda_2) rho`, using the
ascending middle eigenvalue of the molecular density Hessian. Its six
independent Cartesian entries are reported in xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz
order. Densities are in electrons/Bohr³, gradients and delta-g in
electrons/Bohr⁴ and the Hessian in electrons/Bohr⁵. Raw diagnostics include
the SCF orbital residual and maximum density and gradient partition
closure defects over all points. Exact collapsed tails are counted as
vacuum points.

The isolated, all-electron driver supports RKS, UKS, ROKS and GKS.
GKS contracts the scalar Pauli density with the real spatial AOs.
Supported shared SCF controls include semilocal and hybrid providers
and non-PT2 `xc_terms`. Spin-covariant Skala requires the corresponding
GKS provider. ECPs, ghost centres, relaxed double-hybrid densities
and periodic IGMH are outside the connected driver scope. With `igmh_atom_details=true`,
the point-major output includes the atomic densities and the vectors
used in the selected convention.

For a noncoplanar water dimer at PBE/RKS/STO-3G with SCF grid level 1
and zero weight cutoff, the total reference energy is
-150.4657342911233 Hartree. At Bohr coordinates [0.31, -0.19, 3.13],
the published total, interfragment and intrafragment fields are
0.05421468511224952, 0.05352892174981882 and 0.0006857633624307025
electrons/Bohr⁴. The signed density is -0.03859666787143953
electrons/Bohr³. Raw closure defects are 6.939e-18 electrons/Bohr³
and 8.674e-19 electrons/Bohr⁴.

The independent direct AO value contraction fits all 3 density
gradient, 6 symmetric density Hessian and 36 atomic vector
components in the two conventions at [0.036, 0.027, 0.019, 0.013]
Bohr. Mixed directions use all four displaced corners. The
exponents span 1.996325 to 2.092021 and minimum R² is 0.99985509.
The fit coefficients span 6.175e-7 to 2.834e-1 in the corresponding
atomic units. The largest independent fourth-order absolute error
at 0.0015 Bohr is 4.912e-11 across the field components.
The independent primitive-pair formula for isolated hydrogen agrees
through the density Hessian to 2.220e-16 in atomic units. All three
interaction fields vanish exactly in the one-atom limit.

## TPSSloc zero-gradient reference investigation (2026-10-31)

The numerical definition is TPSS exchange (independent ID202) plus TPSSloc
correlation (ID247), with PySCF 2.14.0 and reference library 7.0.0. Point10
is (rho-a,rho-b,sigma-aa,sigma-ab,sigma-bb,tau-a,tau-b) =
(0.31,0.22,0,0,0,0.37,0.21), atomic units. Tau contains one-half of the
orbital-gradient norm squared. The kernel differentiates energy per volume
rho*epsilon, not energy per particle. Direct native calls reproduce the
original huge values exactly, excluding a Python-wrapper explanation.
Native packed sigma order is (aa/aa,aa/ab,aa/bb,ab/ab,ab/bb,bb/bb): packed
entries0 and5 map to full-kernel diagonal indices2 and4. The generator's
mapping is correct.

| Entry | Original raw reference | Independent physical inward limit | Absolute error of earlier finite proposal |
|---|---|---|---|
| X sigma-aa/sigma-aa | 1.4642734346580563e+22 | -0.028203103069422734445 | 8.2248e-14 |
| X sigma-bb/sigma-bb | -9.2700395509038186e+21 | -0.109459099115612441869 | 7.4912e-14 |
| X+C sigma-aa/sigma-aa | 1.4642734346580563e+22 | -0.023705184855672024483 | 5.0255e-15 |
| X+C sigma-bb/sigma-bb | -9.2700395509038186e+21 | -0.104961180901861731907 | 1.1522e-13 |

### Independent exchange derivation

[TPSS equations (3)--(10)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0306203) give,
for one spin channel with s=sigma-spin, p=A*s and z=B*s after exact
spin scaling. A=1/[(3*pi*pi)^(2/3)*(2*rho-spin)^(8/3)] and
B=1/(8*rho-spin*tau-spin). Therefore the apparently singular factor
sqrt(((3*z/5)^2+p^2)/2) is C*s on the physical s>=0 side, where
C=sqrt(((3*B/5)^2+A^2)/2). Its second s derivative is exactly zero.

Writing q=q0+q1*s+q2*s^2+..., u=10/81, v=146/2025, w=73/405 and
L=sqrt(e), the numerator coefficients derived from equation (10) are
N0=v*q0^2,
N1=u*A+2*v*q0*q1-w*C*q0, and
N2=v*(q1^2+2*q0*q2)-w*C*q1+(u^2/kappa)*A^2+2*L*u*(9/25)*B^2.
The c*z^2*p and e*mu*p^3 terms begin at cubic order. Division by
(1+L*A*s)^2 gives x0=N0, x1=N1-2*L*A*N0 and
x2=N2-2*L*A*N1+3*L^2*A^2*N0. The required kernel is the spin-LDA
energy density times
2*x2/(1+x0/kappa)^2-2*x1^2/[kappa*(1+x0/kappa)^3].
All q coefficients are independently differentiated from equation (7),
with alpha=(2*tau-spin-s/(4*rho-spin))/tau-uniform(2*rho-spin).

### Independent correlation derivation and domain

For fixed density and tau let S=sigma-aa+2*sigma-ab+sigma-bb,
t^2=D*S, D=1/(4*phi^2*ks^2*rho^2), beta=b0+b2*t^2,
b0=0.0375 and b2=0.08*(1-exp(-rs^2)). The PBEloc logarithm has
quadratic S coefficient phi^3*(b2-b0^2/(2*gamma))*D^2; its auxiliary
PBE A parameter first contributes at cubic order. The revPKZB part
adds [C0*epsilon0-(1+C0)*sum-spin(rho-spin/rho*epsilon-tilde-spin)]
/(64*rho^2*tau^2). Multiplication by 2*rho gives the same finite
correlation sigma diagonal for both spins,
0.00449791821375070996172. The d*z^3 term and variation
of C with xi begin at cubic order and cannot affect these diagonals.

The spin-only versus full correlation max branches are separated by
0.0327713 and 0.0341255 Hartree per particle here. Tau and density floors
are inactive. The Fermi-hole sigma caps are 0.9176 and 0.3696, far from
the tested origin; toggling enforcement on a private native object leaves
the relevant results unchanged. Thus no max/cap branch switch explains
the four huge entries. The physical Gram cone requires nonnegative
sigma-aa/bb and sigma-ab^2<=sigma-aa*sigma-bb. The derived polynomial
on that cone gives unique inward partials at fixed positive rho/tau;
six physical directions, including parallel, antiparallel and interior
spin gradients, agree to at most 7.076e-27.
This is not a claim of two-sided differentiability at negative sigma,
nor of a unique joint limit with tau approaching zero.

### Numerical mechanism, evidence and limits

The installed native library clamps spin-diagonal sigma to the square
of a small threshold. Its actual default threshold is
1.0000000000000027e-20, giving sigma=1.0000000000000052e-40.
The unsimplified square-root second derivative contains cancelling terms
proportional to 1/sigma. In the official 7.0.0 generated polarized FXC
operation graph, ordinary floating-point replay is unstable while
120-digit replay at positive sigma=1e-40 recovers the finite exchange
limits above. Native threshold sweeps likewise change the huge values;
even replacing the default threshold by the nearby double literal1e-20
changes their signs/magnitudes although the physical change in input
is negligible. This establishes catastrophic cancellation in reference
evaluation, not physical divergence. The independent replay does not
claim to reproduce compiler long-double/FMA choices bit for bit.

An independent Decimal evaluator imports neither Rust nor a numerical
XC library. Analytic series at 80/120/160 digits agree; 120-versus160
differences are below 2.5e-120 for the fixed documented constants.
Direct original-form energies and nine-point forward second derivatives
give two four-step positive sequences per target: eight fits,
p=6.992551--6.999696, minimum R-squared
0.99999979. Their maximum final-step error is
3.369e-19. This precision
agreement measures numerical evaluation, not physical parameter accuracy
or a formal interval certificate; about fifteen significant digits are
appropriate for double-precision conventions.

The TPSS primary PDF was retrieved and hashed. Publisher access to the

table3](https://doi.org/10.1002/qua.25224), and the explicit official7.0
definition. No relevant equation-changing erratum was found in the
targeted search, which does not prove that none exists. Installed wrapper,
native binary and downloaded generated-source hashes are retained; exact
binary compiler options are not recovered from the version string.

## Collisionless thermal electric response

`dynamic-polarizability` accepts the explicit common control `thermal_response="collisionless"` (CLI `--thermal-response collisionless`). Python `dynamic_polarizability` and the ASE getter forward this control. The default `integer` preserves integer-projector validation. The new opt-in requires a converged positive-temperature real collinear canonical Fermi reference. Its population-weighted Liouvillian retains all ordered unequal-population pairs and both spin channels. Reference populations remain fixed: diagonal occupation relaxation and chemical-potential response are absent, so its zero-frequency limit differs from static isothermal Mermin response.

Rust `response::thermal_dynamic::{ThermalSolver, polarizability}` exposes the parent local/GGA plus exact-exchange kernel. The common driver rejects correlated composite, spinor and constrained common-orbital extensions; kinetic/meta, nonlocal and continuum kernels are also excluded by the core capability checks. A resolved parent functional alone does not encode external correlation metadata. No causal PT2 contribution or public real-time integrator is implied.

Reports include all nine complex tensor entries, residuals, iterations, the actual reference occupations, electronic temperature and spin chemical potentials in Hartree, and per-axis/per-spin response particle-number defects in electrons*e*bohr/Hartree. `population_defect` measures consistency with the reference Fermi populations. Thermal `reference_projector_defect` describes physical non-idempotency rather than a convergence error. Full compiled-artifact acceptance is recorded separately from metadata compilation and independent test-oracle checks.

For MCD, `faraday_a_terms` provides the canonical coefficient of the line-shape derivative in observation frequency, while `a_terms` preserves the legacy signed first-line-moment representation: `faraday_a_terms=-a_terms`. `b_terms` includes the ground-state permanent-dipole subtraction. Complete degenerate levels must be summed; orientation and circular-helicity prefactors are not already applied. Returned `mcd_convention` and unit labels state these distinctions explicitly.

## Constrained static electric tensors

The existing `static-spectroscopy`, `beta` and `gamma` common-driver entries
accept `reference="roks"`/`"rohf"` and `reference="gks"`/`"ghf"`.
`static-spectroscopy` with `electric_order=2` or `3` returns all nine Raman
or twenty-seven hyper-Raman entries for the supplied nuclear direction.
`beta` returns all 27 first-hyperpolarizability entries; `gamma` returns all
81 static second-hyperpolarizability entries. Each ordered slot is assembled
by analytic scalar-energy polarization. Identical homogeneous path
coefficients, including exact reversal parity, are reused; tensor slots are
not filled by symmetry. `tensor_assembly="projector"` and `"energy"` select
this stationary contraction. The separate collinear three-solve
`"variational"` shortcut is not inferred for constrained references.

Rust `response::nuclear::open_shell_molecular_energy_taylor` and
`SpinorNuclearContext::molecular_energy_taylor` consume
`MolecularDirection { nuclear, electric }`. Their energy coefficients are
factorial normalized through order four; public tensors are actual
derivatives without factorial factors. The common-orbital closed/open/virtual
flag and full complex spin/AO density respectively obey the physical
stationarity and metric constraints. GKS retains both density parts through
the same physical core, Hartree, full/range exchange and spin-covariant
density/gradient/tau/current XC providers. Its cached kernel is used only at
its exact expansion center. No functional-name response branch is added.
`SpinorNuclearEnergyTaylor::reference_energy_defect` is the retained
zeroth-order energy minus the input SCF energy, in Hartree; it accompanies
the existing Fock, projector, solved-order and angular diagnostics.

All surfaces use `driver::run`: Rust, canonical `dft-rs static-spectroscopy`
or `beta`/`gamma`, native `static_spectroscopic_derivative`/`beta`/`gamma`,
and ASE `get_static_spectroscopic_derivative`/`get_beta`/`get_gamma`.
Native paths use Bohr, fields Hartree/(e Bohr), and tensor units
e^r Bohr^r/Hartree^(r-1): r=2/3 for contracted Raman/hyper-Raman, r=3/4
for beta/gamma. ASE converts paths, fields, fixed Hermitian spinor sources
and reports through the shared unit registry. The calculator forwards its
SCF `guess` and preserves configured response tolerance/iteration controls;
explicit call controls take precedence. An absent `guess` delegates the
reference-family default (molecular SAD,
periodic core); explicit guesses are forwarded. The native legacy summary falls
back to the authoritative tensor unit label when no duplicate summary exists.
Raw response, projector, stationarity, reference and accumulation diagnostics
remain available; no compatibility wrapper constructs an alternate reference.

Local, full-exchange and range-exchange providers are connected generically.
The measured subset below is biased molecular HF/STO-3G in a C1 geometry,
not all functional classes. Nonlocal, learned, continuum, fractional,
periodic and dynamic combinations retain their separate capability checks
and validation status. Constrained PT2 is rejected until matching amplitude
and orbital providers are connected; no parent-only double-hybrid tensor is
returned. RKS/UKS correlated support remains a separate measured subset.

## Reference-independent harmonic analysis

`driver::run("frequencies", ...)` and `driver::run("gibbs-free-energy", ...)`
now delegate to the same analytic `hessian` provider for ROHF/ROKS and
complex GHF/GKS references. This is a harmonic/RRHO postprocessor, not a
second SCF or response implementation. Its functional, occupation,
Hamiltonian and correlated-reference limits are exactly those of the
selected Hessian provider. No functional-name branch is added.

`vibrational_projection=auto` removes rigid translations/rotations for a
free molecule. A nonzero fixed `field`, `reference_field`, `bfield` or
additional GKS AO operator instead retains all 3N Cartesian modes, including
zero and unstable modes. Explicit `eckart` assumes a free-molecule internal
mode model; `cartesian` always retains all 3N. No small eigenvalue is floored
or discarded. Frequencies use cm^-1, Hessians Hartree/Bohr^2 and Cartesian
normal-mode patterns 1/sqrt(amu). An absent atomic polar tensor gives null
IR intensities, never a fabricated zero; available intensities use km/mol.

RRHO requires Eckart internal modes, a converged electronic/nuclear report,
strictly positive internal frequencies and positive temperature/pressure.
With a fixed laboratory source, a saddle/zero internal mode or zero nuclear
temperature, frequencies remain available with warnings and null
thermochemistry; `gibbs-free-energy` refuses the inapplicable RRHO model.
The electronic degeneracy is an explicit positive integer, defaulting to
multiplicity for a collinear state and one for a fixed spinor state. No
spin quantum number is inferred from a general spinor. `temperature` is K,
`pressure` Pa and `symmetry_number` dimensionless. Gibbs energy includes
pV=k_B T per molecule, in Hartree per molecule. A positive electronic
temperature requires the provided electronic entropy and thermal Hessian;
the Mermin entropy is included once and the equilibrium temperatures agree.

The permanent `p311_reference_vibrations` and
`python/tests/test_reference_vibrations.py` acceptance files cover this
adapter. In an isolated exact-body Rust check over an accepted electronic
library, four checks pass: all 12 dense Cartesian frequencies, all 12 IR
intensities and every mode-projector element match a closed oracle; all 6
internal C1 ROHF and genuinely complex GHF frequencies match the same full
analytic Hessian; atomic ROHF/GHF Gibbs degeneracy changes match
-k_B T log(2) to 1.290200585258e-17 Hartree; and all 144 C1 spring-Hessian
entries pass independent four-step fits. For h=[0.04,0.02,0.01,0.005] Bohr,
p=1.999434523225..2.001666048898, minimum
R2=0.999999814175. No failed spring interval or error floor
is used. The spring model does not validate electronic derivatives.

The full warning-strict library, canonical CLI and portable-artifact audit
also pass. Its rlib SHA-256 is
`8e615f7010b817db89d442b66a80a3f677dd6ac73e50f136c6109aea1e0c6bb0`.

SCF/gradient/Hessian kernels without changing their physical formulae.

migration work. The API documents describe exact limits.

- The spinor forced route unnecessarily constructed a complete XC Hessian

Earlier saved-model controls separate one large ten-candidate inversion:
the Cl-minus-Me error of 251.472574 kcal/mol consists of 234.618548 from
the fixed-neutral-density proton interaction, 0.003607 from grid transfer
and 16.850419 from electronic relaxation. The physical same-AO frozen
response changes the Cl-minus-Me result by only +0.032922 kcal/mol, so
omitted frozen relaxation does not explain that large error. The raw
mapped neutral Me/Cl active densities initially capture 25.964478/25.871372
electrons and have lifted frozen overlaps 0.031223/0.140463. Their model
orbital residuals are 0.294988/0.775288 Hartree; retained identical-AO Fock
defects are 0.073862/0.424694 Hartree. This is evidence for neutral action
and metric/Pauli transfer errors, not a unique attribution to operator
fitting. Those diagnostic normalized densities are not a silent production
fix. The new B versus A+B neutral Et maximum Fock-fit defect decreases
from 0.204556 to 0.024954 Hartree, despite the failed target ranking.

The exact common chart fixes reference-space and frozen-orthogonality
inconsistencies, but the runtime model still replaces the internal action
with a static linear operator. It does not retain the complete scalar
E_Hxc[T P T^T + P_B]-E_Hxc[P] or its internal-density response away from
the neutral reference. A neutral fit alone cannot establish that response.
The next controlled comparison, deferred at this stopping checkpoint, is
full scalar frozen protonation in the identical union/common chart versus
the static fitted action. This separates frozen response from compression
and nonadditive-energy error before any new fit. The earlier tBu-minus-Me
frozen-response contribution (+10.663715 kcal/mol) is near the combined
relative error (+10.009596), but comes from a different reference space;
that resemblance is a hypothesis, not a quantitative decomposition.

If the matched control supports it, reuse the existing frozen scalar
evaluator with dual chart maps for a density-dependent correction and then
test any low-rank internal response. Expand a common operator dictionary
only after that separation; retain fixed dimension/electron count and
test untouched scaffolds without fitting their protonation energies.
For derivative diagnosis, a future independent displaced-SCF energy
difference should avoid subtracting approximately 133-Hartree totals and
include the actual semilocal XC difference. That oracle is not implemented
here. Current experiments are terminal; no additional remedy or chemistry
work remains active after this requested checkpoint.

### R089 molecular post-SCF dispersion and nonlocal kernels

#### Molecular D1 energy and nuclear tensors

With `dispersion="d1"`, supply `dispersion_free_c6` (Hartree Bohr^6),
`dispersion_free_radii` (Bohr), and the dimensionless
`dispersion_energy_scale` in molecular atom order. The geometry-only
pair energy uses the harmonic C₆ mean and the original steepness 23.
It enters the total energy and the stationary nuclear gradient,
Cartesian Hessian, cubic and quartic force constants for the applicable
RKS, UKS, ROKS, and GKS electronic paths. The Taylor coefficient is
added before the mixed Cartesian tensor is assembled. Geometry derivative
units are Hartree/Bohr^n for order n. A named provider with its own
required nonlocal energy cannot be combined with the explicit D1 model.
The C1 ammonia Cartesian derivative test passes 12, 78, 256 and 636
nonzero components from first through fourth order, with 837 structural
zeros. All 982 fits pass the first interval, 0.018, 0.012, 0.008 and 0.005
Bohr. The exponent range is 1.998813 to 2.007135, minimum R2 is
0.99999829 and prefactors span 6.203e-10 to 1.310e-3. The D1 term for
this fixture is -6.312135461008352e-6 Hartree. The separate BLYP/RKS
ammonia energy case gives a D1 term of -6.182386304421e-5 Hartree and
total -55.71609127540 Hartree. Its CLI, native Python and ASE comparison
passes with maximum total energy defect 2.842e-14 Hartree. The PBE/RKS
LiH cubic block passes across the same public interfaces. Its selected
Cartesian entry is 0.07577246609000098 Hartree/Bohr^3 after adding
the -4.927098926216233e-6 Hartree/Bohr^3 D1 term. The raw orbital
residual is 6.872e-10 Hartree. The LiH quartic public check also
passes. The selected quartic entry is 1.153515484957932 Hartree/Bohr^4
with a -1.338495801972428e-5 Hartree/Bohr^4 D1 term, at the same
reference residual. The frozen public group passes all three cases.
[D1 equations](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.20078)

#### Periodic D1 and analytic dispersion derivatives

Periodic D1 accepts the same explicit `dispersion_free_c6`,
`dispersion_free_radii` and `dispersion_energy_scale` inputs as the
molecular energy. Specify atom references in primitive-cell order. Atoms
of the same element use the same free-atom reference, including in
replicated cells. The pair cutoff `disp_cutoff` is in Bohr. The ordered
image sum uses the published harmonic C₆ mean and steepness 23.
Raw D1 force and strain enter the common periodic energy and stress drivers.

The Rust dimensional dispersion tensor uses the same radial function
and a fixed reference image list for all Cartesian nuclear derivatives
from first through fourth order in 1D, 2D and 3D. The 3D phonon and
elastic paths use the same D1 model when they request a geometry-only
term. The independent image-sum test covers the canonical Cartesian
entries and checks the structural zeros involving three atoms and the
raw permutation and acoustic residuals. The frozen source manifest
`9f64dd269aa8ddc667ddf3b59d49c6488e168e1c58cf49cff607b22a44f1f76b`
passes all 1,575 nonzero four-step fits and all 567 structural zeros.
Each dimension covers 9, 45, 138 and 333 fitted components at orders
one through four. The Cartesian steps are 0.018, 0.012, 0.008 and
0.005 Bohr. The exponent range is 1.871462 to 2.055491, minimum R2 is
0.99930908 and prefactors range from 4.543e-9 to 0.2678. The largest
fourth-order permutation and acoustic defects are 2.168e-17 and
3.307e-18 Hartree/Bohr^4.

At PBE/RKS and the [2, 1, 1] mesh, the LiH wire with a 6.4 Bohr pair
cutoff gives -6.693805570730705 Hartree per cell, a D1 term of
-1.881414633334844e-5 Hartree per cell and xx stress of
-0.01395727313640888 Hartree/Bohr. The raw orbital residual is 2.010e-13
Hartree. CLI, native Python and ASE agree to 1e-10 in atomic units;
the energy, force and strain changes reproduce the separate D1
contributions to 1e-12 in their respective atomic units. Lower-dimensional
total electronic fourth derivatives remain open. TS, MBD@TS, MBD@rsSCS,
VV09 and the vdW-DF family
still require periodic energy and analytic derivative routes.

The common molecular `energy` driver applies `dispersion="ts"`,
`dispersion="mbd-ts"`, `dispersion="mbd"` or `dispersion="vv09"` to a
converged reference density.
RKS, UKS and ROKS use their total collinear AO density. GKS uses
the scalar density; for VV09 it also supplies all three Pauli spin
densities. The corrected report includes the post-SCF term in
`energy_components.dispersion` and `dispersion_energy`, in Hartree.
The SCF diagnostics still refer to the parent energy and orbitals.
The correction is available through the ordinary molecular energy routes.
Analytic derivatives, periodic calculations, ECPs, ghost centers, PT2 and
functionals that already include a defining nonlocal term are outside
this path.

TS and MBD@TS share a Hirshfeld partition with spherical neutral
all-electron free atoms in their molecular orbital basis. In atom
order, supply `dispersion_free_polarizabilities` (Bohr³),
`dispersion_free_c6` (Hartree Bohr⁶) and `dispersion_free_radii`
(Bohr). Also supply the positive dimensionless `dispersion_radius_scale`,
the TS parameter `s_R` or the MBD parameter `beta`. Native Rust and
Python use atomic units; ASE accepts these controls in the calculator's
unit system. In the CLI, use the same setting names with hyphens,
and pass the atom arrays as quoted JSON lists. The report returns
the dimensionless `dispersion_volume_ratios` and effective
polarizabilities, C₆ and radii in those same units. MBD@TS also
returns the bare and coupled oscillator frequencies in Hartree and
`mbd_minimum_squared_frequency` in Hartree². Nonpositive coupled
modes return a named stability error. These empirical models use
the caller's documented parameterization.
[TS equations](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.073005),
[MBD@TS equations](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4865104).

VV09 requires a single unscaled original PW92 local correlation,
for example `xc="spw92"`. It evaluates the original Thomas–Fermi pair
kernel, with finite coincident-point values and a local spin factor
from the magnetization magnitude. It reports the correction separately
from the reference PW92 energy. The variational nonlocal potential
and analytic response remain open.
[VV09 equations](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.063004).

At an asymmetric NH₃ geometry, the PBE/STO-3G reference used
12,536 grid points with zero weight cutoff and converged in eight
SCF iterations. Its energy was `-55.68017199433405` Hartree. TS at
`s_R=0.94` gives `-2.349426974852503e-6` Hartree, against
`-2.349426974852506e-6` Hartree from separate AO density, proatom
and pair contractions. Its volume ratios in N, H, H, H order were
`[1.042565326225477, 0.870344528040556, 0.873056310617884, 0.871017471871528]`.
MBD@TS at `beta=0.81` gives `-5.441802024525322e-4` Hartree,
against `-5.441802024390457e-4` Hartree from an independent
imaginary-frequency log-determinant integral. The minimum squared
oscillator frequency is `0.1768771371360374` Hartree².
The molecular fixture uses individual H/N C₆ values 6.5 and 24.2
Hartree Bohr⁶ and radii 1.64 and 1.77 Å from the original TS paper.
The hydrogen polarizability is the 1s value 4.5 Bohr³. The nitrogen
polarizability of 7.4 Bohr³ is the neutral-atom reference already
used by the library. [Static atomic polarizabilities](https://doi.org/10.1080/00268976.2018.1535143).
The corresponding SPW92/STO-3G reference used 2,548 points and eight
iterations, with energy `-55.26238659639` Hartree. Its VV09 term
is `+0.04026627842653` Hartree, versus `+0.04026627842649` Hartree
from independently integrated angular and spatial terms. The VV09
correction can be positive because its short-range subtraction
avoids double counting the local PW92 contribution. The separate
H/H MBD@TS check reproduces the six closed-form modes and approaches
`C6=6.500000245546` Hartree Bohr⁶ at 30 Bohr for an input of `6.5`.

The original D1 correction uses the harmonic C₆ mean and damping
slope 23. For the molecular energy, supply `dispersion_free_c6`
(Hartree Bohr⁶), `dispersion_free_radii` (Bohr), and the dimensionless
`dispersion_energy_scale` for `s6`. A compiled element/functional
dataset is pending.
With explicit test parameters on the NH₃ geometry the correction
was `-6.182386304421459e-5` Hartree, equal to the separate pair
formula at the reported precision.
[D1 equations](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.20078).

Molecular MBD@rsSCS (`dispersion="mbd"`) solves screened uniform
responses, integrates the frequency-dependent local polarizabilities
for C₆, rescales the effective radii and diagonalizes the coupled
long-range oscillator Hamiltonian. Use the same atom input and `beta`
controls as for MBD@TS. The default imaginary-frequency quadrature
uses `mbd_quadrature_nodes=64` and `mbd_frequency_scale=0.8` Hartree.
The report includes the dimensionless minimum short-range screening
eigenvalue and normalized residual, the effective screened parameters
and the unscreened polarizabilities, C₆ and radii in atomic units.
The published PBE fits use `beta=0.81` for MBD@TS and `beta=0.83`
for MBD@rsSCS. The following screened fixture uses an explicit
`beta=0.81` to isolate the effect of screening at the same damping.
At 4.2 Bohr and `beta=0.81`,
the H/H dimer gave `-8.773399179068386e-5` Hartree, compared with
`-8.773399179062835e-5` Hartree from independent longitudinal and
transverse screening and angular-transform Casimir–Polder quadrature.
The screened atomic polarizability was `4.516824420417` Bohr³ and
C₆ was `6.531144469792` Hartree Bohr⁶. Over 24, 48, 96 and 128
quadrature nodes, the smallest screening eigenvalue was
`0.9126455935699` and the maximum screening residual was `4.415e-16`.
The H/H results check the Rust primitive. The corresponding molecular
D1 and MBD@rsSCS shared-driver checks use NH₃ and the explicit
parameter settings described here.
[Range-separated screening](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4865104),
[Screened radii](https://doi.org/10.1039/C5SC03234B).

For the PBE/STO-3G NH₃ density, screened MBD at `beta=0.81` gives
`-5.828671022547749e-4` Hartree. Integrating the log determinant
at the same screened parameters gives `-5.828671023482546e-4` Hartree.
The minimum short-range eigenvalue is `0.3434030313009`, the raw
screening residual is `1.537e-15` and the minimum squared long-range
oscillator frequency is `0.2051726914618` Hartree².
Using the published PBE value `beta=0.83` at the same density gives
`-5.124703828978117e-4` Hartree versus
`-5.124703829851487e-4` Hartree from the log determinant. The short-range
minimum is `0.3428138355236`, the screening residual is `1.776e-15`,
and the minimum squared long-range frequency is
`0.2054444949878` Hartree².

#### Fixed-density molecular vdW-DF family

Set the parent `xc` to a semilocal functional such as `spw92` and specify
`dispersion="vdw-df"`, `"vdw-df2"`, `"optpbe-vdw"`, `"optb88-vdw"`,
`"optb86b-vdw"`, `"vdw-df-cx"` or `"rev-vdw-df2"`. The driver replaces the
parent XC energy at its converged density with the selected outer exchange,
PW92 local correlation and the corresponding nonlocal kernel integral.
This route accepts unpolarized all-electron molecular RKS with integer
ground-state occupations. It reports `vdw_df_parent_energy`,
`vdw_df_parent_xc_energy`, `vdw_df_exchange_energy`,
`vdw_df_local_correlation_energy`, `vdw_df_nonlocal_correlation_energy`,
`vdw_df_xc_energy` and the parent `scf_orbital_residual` in Hartree.
The common controls `vdw_df_radial_order`, `vdw_df_angular_degree`,
`vdw_df_table_points` and `vdw_df_momentum_cutoff` default to
`32, 17, 96, 72`, respectively. The radial mapping scale is 1.1 Bohr
and the effective vacuum density threshold for nonlocal integration is
`1e-8` Bohr⁻³. Analytic response, self-consistency, spin-polarized
references and periodic XC integration remain open.

```sh
dft-rs energy molecule.xyz --xc spw92 --reference rks --dispersion vdw-df --format json
```

For native Python, call
`dft_rs.energy(numbers, positions_bohr, xc="spw92", reference="rks", dispersion="vdw-df")`.
For ASE, use
`DftRs(xc="spw92", reference="rks", dispersion="vdw-df").get_energy_report(atoms)`.
In Rust, supply the same controls to `driver::run("energy", &system, &controls)`.

The shared vdW-DF/DF2 Rust pair kernel uses composite momentum
quadrature for the published plasmon formula. The original and revised
internal inverse lengths at `rho=0.04` Bohr⁻³ and
`|grad rho|²=0.021` Bohr⁻⁸ are `1.546450535425` and
`1.904100889596` Bohr⁻¹. They coincide for zero gradient.
At momentum cutoff 192, the direct kernel and separately evaluated
unfactored equations agree within `5.25e-12` Hartree for the
dimensionless pairs (0.25, 0.8), (2, 3) and (5, 7). At cutoff 768,
the (18, 24) pair gives `-1.944813471347520e-7` Hartree against
the far-field asymptote `-1.944792659975414e-7` Hartree.
The spatial rule integrates the logarithmic coincidence with the
radial Jacobian. For a manufactured Gaussian density with constant
internal inverse length, the independent autocorrelation integral is
`2.027957592855e-3` Hartree. At 12, 18, 26 and 36 radial nodes, the
errors are `8.780e-7`, `4.731e-9`, `2.138e-10`, and `1.359e-10`
Hartree. An initial point-cache test failed because the Legendre nodes
were presented in descending order. Sorting the test cache resolved
the comparison. The generated logarithmic table is checked against
direct momentum quadrature. For 26, 43 and 64 nodes, the maximum
interpolation defects across the five pairs are `1.098e-4`,
`9.505e-6`, and `3.498e-6` Hartree. The direct evaluator handles pairs
outside the table.
[Original kernel](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.246401),
[Revised inverse length](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.82.081101).

For 384 dimensionless pair inputs from 0.105 to 16, five alternating
single-thread runs at momentum cutoff 72 and panel order 8 give
median times of 287.643 microseconds per direct pair and 0.075965
microseconds per tabulated pair. The 96-node table on [0.09, 18]
took 1.5014 seconds to construct and stores 37,248 bytes of
triangular kernel entries. Its maximum absolute pair error was
`5.05408e-7` Hartree. Times describe the kernel on this input set.

For asymmetric NH₃ on the SPW92/STO-3G RKS density, the reference
spatial and momentum fixture uses level 0 with zero grid weight
cutoff, radial order 14, angular degree 9, 72 table points, and
momentum cutoff 48 with panel order 6. Each column is Hartree.
The common-driver totals use the same geometry and outer grid with
momentum panel order 8 and density threshold `1e-8` Bohr⁻³.
